title: story: with no adapter installed, core run-variant returns :status :pass with zero assertions and no frame — rf2-c9t52 closed this only at the story-mcp layer
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b). Verified at source by the mayor; the probe is the reviewer's, re-measure at tip.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1250-1265 (handle-run-error! :else branch resolves (record-result-map {:variant-id variant-id} start-ms)), :357-384 (record-error! swallows the dispatch into a non-existent frame), :595-723 (record-result-map assembles from a nil app-db); frames.cljc:664-669 (the comment that names this class).

EVIDENCE (JVM probe, no rf/init!):
    A_SETUP_THROW  status= :pass lifecycle= :pre-mount exception-records= 0 total-assertions= 0
      frame-ids after run: #{}
Mechanism: rf/make-frame throws :rf.error/no-adapter-installed before any frame exists -> handle-run-error! -> record-error! dispatches ::append-assertion into a frame that does not exist -> caught at 371-383 (debug breadcrumb only) -> record-result-map {:variant-id ...} -> aggregate-status [] [] -> :pass. rf/app-db-value returns nil for an unknown frame (core.cljc:2101-2108), so nothing throws. The existing test story_runtime_test.clj:1631-1647 with-redefs run-phase-2! to throw AFTER the frame exists, which takes the frame-bound branch; it does not cover this.

WHY IT MATTERS: rf2-c9t52's close reason scopes its fix to story-mcp's run-variant/preview-variant handlers, so the core verb, the one the tutorial and any clojure.test user calls, still answers a success-shaped non-run. It is the first thing a JVM/REPL user hits.

SMALLEST CHANGE: in handle-run-error!'s :else (and db-seed) branch, when (nil? (rf/app-db-value variant-id)) resolve a frame-free {:status :error :lifecycle :error :assertions [<exception record>]} (the plan-error-result shape) instead of record-result-map. One JVM test: run-variant with no adapter -> :status :error.

GATE: jvm-tools-story.

ALREADY-COVERED CHECK: rf2-c9t52 (closed 2026-09-01) and rf2-2ktuc are story-mcp only by their own close reasons; not fixed at trunk for core.
notes: FENCE DISCHARGED BY CLUSTERING 2026-09-13 01:15:25 AUSEST (mayor): this bead is dispatched to rtfix-a in ONE PR with rf2-3okc, rf2-poty, rf2-izz5 and rf2-9ppq, in the reviewer's order (3okc, then poty, then izz5, then 9ppq). The fence existed only to keep a second worker out of the same file, and one worker now holds all four, so the ordering it protected is kept inside the PR. Title prefix struck in the same act.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9723 (branch worker/rtfix-a), with rf2-3okc, rf2-izz5 and rf2-9ppq in one PR.

Fix: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc now routes every run-chain failure through one assembler, run-error-result, which never throws. When there is no live frame ((rf/app-db-value variant-id) is nil, because make-frame threw :rf.error/no-adapter-installed before registering the frame), it resolves a frame-free result instead of recording onto a missing frame and assembling from a nil app-db. That result is {:status :error :lifecycle :error} with ONE record: :rf.error/exception at :phase-0-setup, carrying the exception, with :error :data :rf.error/id :rf.error/no-adapter-installed. This is the plan-error-result shape; both now share frame-free-error-result. The inline path (story/run with a map, run-inline-plan's fail!) had the same vacuous :pass and now goes through the same assembler. A variant that genuinely ran with no assertions stays vacuously green. The plan-construction-error? docstring claimed no-adapter errors land after the frame exists; that was wrong and is corrected.

Evidence: a JVM probe in a process with no rf/init!, before at cfe0559ded and after on the branch.
- Registered run: :status :pass, :lifecycle :pre-mount, 0 assertions, frame-ids #{} before; :error/:error with 1 exception record after.
- Inline run: :pass with 0 assertions before; :error/:error with 1 record after.
- Control, same process after rf/init!: :pass :ready both times.

Tests: story_runtime_test.clj gains no-adapter-installed-run-is-an-error-not-a-pass. It covers both the registered and the inline run, uses a REAL :rf.error/no-adapter-installed through a scoped with-redefs of re-frame.substrate.adapter/adapter-lifecycle-state, and has a with-adapter control. title: story: dispatched?/effect-emitted/no-warnings read the frame's whole epoch ring, so a same-id rerun inherits the previous run's facts (false PASS)
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b). Verified at source by the mayor; the probe is the reviewer's, re-measure at tip.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:126-135 (frame-tape = (rf/epoch-history frame-id) unfiltered), :157-164 (dispatched-events), :192-200 (emitted-fx), :202-208 (warnings). Contrast runtime.cljc:607-626, which baseline-filters the RESULT tape precisely because "the epoch ring remains frame-owned across runs"; implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:175 (histories is a defonce atom outside the frame-state partitions); frames.cljc:1145-1155 (reset-state! overwrites app/runtime partitions only); runtime.cljc:829-831 (ensure-fresh-frame! resets in place).

EVIDENCE (JVM probe, re-frame.epoch loaded, plain-atom adapter):
    C1 first run:  {:script [[:dispatch [:probe/ok]] [:assert [:rf.assert/dispatched? [:probe/ok]]]]}
                   status= :pass  verdict= [[:rf.assert/dispatched? true]]  run-tape= 4  full-ring= 6
    C2 SAME id re-registered with {:script [[:assert [:rf.assert/dispatched? [:probe/ok]]]]} (no dispatch)
                   status= :pass  verdict= [[:rf.assert/dispatched? true]]  run-tape= 3  full-ring= 11
    C3 CONTROL fresh id, same assert-only script
                   status= :fail  verdict= [[:rf.assert/dispatched? false]] run-tape= 3
    C'2 effect-emitted on a same-id rerun with no emit: record true; run-level :cannot-run
run-tape (the baseline-filtered result slice) is 3 while the handler read 11: the handler is not run-scoped. For effect-emitted the unified verdict is rescued by the post-run evidence-slot validator (requirements/validate-run-evidence), but the assertion record itself is a false true; for dispatched? nothing rescues it.

WHY IT MATTERS: the in-place reset is the shell's hot path (every cell-override edit, mode toggle, substrate switch, hot-reload re-prepare, the stepper's prepare-variant) and the clojure.test recipe in spec/Tutorial-CLJS-Unit.md runs one variant twice. A script that stops dispatching an event keeps passing.

SMALLEST CHANGE: give the three handlers the same :epoch-baseline the result uses. run-phase-0! already computes (runner-events/last-epoch-id variant-id); stash it per frame (a defonce map keyed by frame-id, evicted in clear-state!/destroy!) and have frame-tape drop records with :epoch-id <= baseline. Add the C1/C2/C3 shape as a JVM test.

GATE: jvm-tools-story.

ALREADY-COVERED CHECK: rf2-96qsjr / rf2-4u5zl4 (closed) fixed the result-side baseline and truncation; the handler side was in neither.
notes: FENCE DISCHARGED 2026-09-13 01:15:25 AUSEST (mayor): PR #9717 merged as ac36ed93bd (rf2-b2mt + rf2-jjhy). Title prefix struck in the same act. Dispatched in wave 2.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9723 (branch worker/rtfix-a), with rf2-poty, rf2-izz5 and rf2-9ppq in one PR.

Fix: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc now keeps a per-frame run baseline (set-run-epoch-baseline! / clear-run-epoch-baseline!). frame-tape, which feeds dispatched? / effect-emitted / no-warnings and the loaders' :loaders-complete-when vector form, keeps only the epochs committed after it. runtime.cljc's phase 0 (stamp-epoch-baseline!, on both the registered and the inline path) records the SAME :epoch-baseline the run-result tape uses. record-result-map and frame-tape share one run-slice rule, so a verdict and the evidence slots read one run. An inline frame clears its baseline on teardown. The bead suggested evicting the baseline in canonical.cljc's drop hook; I did not, because that file is outside the fence. It is not needed for correctness: :epoch-id is globally monotonic and never reset (re-frame.epoch.state/epoch-counter is a private defonce with no reset), so a baseline a destroyed registered frame leaves behind sits below every later epoch and is inert. Registered entries are bounded by the variant-id set.

Evidence: a JVM probe (clojure.main on the :test classpath, live epoch tape, plain-atom adapter), before at cfe0559ded and after on the branch.
- C2 (same id re-registered with no dispatch): :pass/true before, :fail/false after.
- C3 control (fresh id): :fail/false both times.
- C1 (first run): :pass/true both times.
- E2 (same-id re-run emitting nothing): effect-emitted record true before, false after.
- W2 (clean same-id re-run): no-warnings :fail/false before, :pass/true after. The W1 control (a run that warns) is :fail with warnings slot 1 both times.

Tests: story_assertions_test.clj gains dispatched-assertion-reads-only-the-current-run and effect-emitted-and-no-warnings-read-only-the-current-run. Gate: jvm-tools-story (cd tools/story && clojure -M:test), captured exit 0 on the rebased head cf9ae3c050: 1939 tests / 7169 assertions, 0 failures (1938 / 7163 before the rebase). title: [bug] trunk red: uix-adapter recipe test still requires the template to pin com.pitch/uix.dom, which rf2-j908 deliberately dropped
description:
TRUNK IS RED FOR ONE JOB RIGHT NOW. `Diagnostic skip-ok JVM uix-adapter classpath probe` fails at
`implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj:157`, whose
`testing` block reads "the template pins both UIx coordinates":

    expected: (some? dom-ver)      actual: (not (some? nil))
    expected: (= core-ver dom-ver) actual: (not (= "1.4.4" nil))

4 tests / 34 assertions, 2 failures, 0 errors.

THE CAUSE IS RULED DESIGN, NOT A MISTAKE. [[rf2-j908]] (PR #9543) migrated the UIx template scaffold
onto the adapter's `client-root` + `render!` and DELIBERATELY dropped `com.pitch/uix.dom`: the Root is
minted by the shared spine via `react-dom/client`, so the coordinate is not a day-one dependency. That
PR also added `com.pitch/uix.dom` to `retired-coords`, precisely because `view-lib-coords` is a
PRESENCE check and merely deleting a row asserts nothing. Verified at tip: the template's `_uix/deps.edn`
pins `com.pitch/uix.core {:mvn/version "1.4.4"}` and no `uix.dom`.

**So the TEST is the stale artefact, not the template.** The fix is to make
`uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj` assert the ruled shape — uix.core pinned, uix.dom absent and
RETIRED — rather than requiring both coordinates at equal versions. Do not restore `uix.dom` to the
template; that reverts a ruled migration and re-teaches the superseded boot.

## WHY IT REACHED TRUNK, AND THE PROPERTY WORTH KEEPING

PR #9543's own classifier armed `template_expensive` and nothing else, so this probe read **SKIPPED**
on that PR — measured directly on its rollup. It only surfaced on PR #9550, whose diff armed the
uix-adapter surface for unrelated reasons. **The merge criterion cannot catch this class**: clause 2
accepts passed-OR-SKIPPED, so a diagnostic that would have caught the break is admitted precisely
because the classifier did not schedule it. That is structural rather than an error by any author or
reviewer, and it is the second time a template change has been graded by a job set that excluded its
own consumer (rf2-j908's fence had to be widened mid-flight for the same reason, to
`skills/re-frame2-setup/**`).

Record that property; do NOT build a gate for it under this bead, and do not widen the classifier
here. Whether the uix-adapter probe should be armed by `tools/template/*` is a separate question worth
its own bead if anyone wants it.

## SCOPE

One test file. Do not touch the template, `retired-coords`, `view-lib-coords`, the setup skill, or the
classifier. Also check — and fix if present — the STALE COMMENT at `_uix/deps.edn:4`, which still
explains what `uix.dom` is for although the coordinate is gone; that is one line and in the same
family, but if touching it arms a different surface, say so and leave it.

## GATE

The failing job itself: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/adapters/uix`. It must go from 2 failures
to 0. Quote the captured exit code and the test/assertion counts both before and after, because a
green run that skipped the namespace is not the same as a green run that executed it.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in PR #9553 (`27b274d7d6` on trunk after fast-forward), merged at band 87 on all five clauses.

Grading re-measured this tick: band 87 across the five previously merged PRs; #9553's rollup 87
distinct; 0 failure-or-cancelled; 0 non-terminal; all four workflow runs completed at the full
40-character head oid 265e85af39f77590c4c6a3618abeaa8a8ee2a1a1; workflow diff against merge-base =
0 lines / 0 job keys; `git merge-tree --write-tree` rc=0.

TRUNK IS NO LONGER RED. `Diagnostic skip-ok JVM uix-adapter classpath probe` goes 2 failures -> 0.
This also unblocks PR #9550, whose only two failures were this probe and the `All required checks
passed` aggregator that `needs:` it.

The test now asserts the RULED shape — `uix.core` pinned, `uix.dom` absent — rather than requiring
both coordinates at equal versions. The absence is asserted POSITIVELY (`(nil? dom-ver)`), not by
deleting the assertion, which would have asserted nothing.

## THE ASSERTION COUNT FELL 34 -> 33, AND THAT IS CORRECT

The brief named 34 as a floor. It was wrong to do so and the worker flagged the shortfall rather
than padding it. The arithmetic is exact: `(some? core-ver)` survives, `(some? dom-ver)` becomes
`(nil? dom-ver)`, and `(= core-ver dom-ver)` is DELETED with no replacement — a lockstep check
BETWEEN TWO COORDINATES cannot survive the second coordinate's removal, and asserting it against
nil is a contradiction rather than a check. Padding the count back to 34 with a filler assertion
would have been the wrong repair.

What distinguishes this from a silently skipped namespace is the sabotage run, not the count:
planting an equality assertion against a unique token gave exit 1 with `4 tests / 33 assertions, 1
failures` naming that token. The token exists nowhere else in the repo, so a run that had wandered
into a sibling worktree would have come back green; the 33-assertion line proves the namespace
executed. Restored and verified by git BLOB hash
872cdf7fd8cfd0ff935b446fdad440d9f4ef8896, identical before plant and after restore.

## THE BRIEF'S SECOND SCOPE ITEM DID NOT HOLD — CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE

I briefed `_uix/deps.edn:4` as a stale comment "still explaining what `uix.dom` is for". That is
FALSE at tip. The comment explains that `uix.dom` is NOT a dependency and why — PR #9543
(`606414f7b2`) rewrote it as part of the migration and `bca094d97b` trimmed it for the leaf byte
ceiling. It currently states that `uix.dom` is not direct because the adapter's `client-root` /
`render!` own the React Root, which is exactly the post-migration truth. Editing it would also have
armed `template_expensive` for no gain. Nothing is owed here and no follow-up bead is warranted.

Minor: the `testing` block sits at source line 157 but its failures report at 159/161, which is
where the `is` forms are.

Ratchets swept from the workflow job lists rather than nominated from memory:
`check_require_alias_dialect.py`, `check_test_lane_bijection.py`, `check_jvm_lane_rosters.py`,
`check_retired_spellings.py` all 0, each with its own `--self-test` control also 0; clj-kondo 0/0.
The one needing thought was `re-frame.observation-render-law-drift-test` — zero tolerance, and it
does NOT strip docstrings or comments, so the new prose about `render!` and a React spine was
squarely in its subject; checked with its own patterns plus a control string the expression does
match, 0 hits.

AI-attribution trailers declined on both commit and PR body.

Follow-up filed separately for the classifier gap that let this reach trunk.

title: TRUNK RED: compile-node-test zero-warning gate fails on two :uix.linter/interop-ref-read warnings from 570d07d286
description:
TRUNK IS RED. Reported INDEPENDENTLY by two workers within an hour on 2026-09-05, on files byte-identical to origin/main, and confirmed by the mayor at source.

THE FAILURE. `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` exits 1 on two `:uix.linter/interop-ref-read` warnings under a zero-warning gate:
  implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120
  implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:139
Both are `(.-current ref)` inside a `uix/use-effect` body. The linter's message: "use-ref hook in UIx returns Atom-like ref, use `@` instead of `.-current`".

IT IS THE COMPILE STEP, NOT THE TEST STEP. The node test step is GREEN. That distinction matters because it is why this was not caught at merge and why it presents confusingly: the tests pass, the compile that produces them does not.

PROVENANCE, established at source: commit `570d07d286` (2026-09-05 14:14:05 +1000, "fix(uix): the imperative effect recipe follows its frame (rf2-tug6)") added the 251-line test file carrying both reads. It IS an ancestor of origin/main. Both reporting workers confirmed the file is byte-identical to origin/main in their branches, so this is trunk state and not any worker's diff.

BLAST RADIUS. This reds `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and `npm run test:cljs` LOCALLY for any diff. In CI the `cljs_node_test` job is surface-gated by the classifier, so a PR that does not arm the CLJS surface gets it SKIPPED — and a skip counts as passed in the rollup, which is exactly why PRs kept merging green all afternoon while this sat on main. A PR that DOES arm the surface will red on it, through no fault of its own.

WHY P1: multiple workers are live on CLJS surfaces right now, every one of them will hit this, and each will spend time establishing that it is not their fault. Two already have. The fix is two lines.

THE FIX, on the merits. The linter is telling the truth: UIx's `use-ref` returns an atom-like ref, so `@ref` is the idiomatic read and `.-current` is interop reaching through the abstraction. Change both reads. BUT VERIFY THE SEMANTICS BEFORE CHANGING THEM — read UIx's own `use-ref` implementation and confirm `@` and `.-current` return the same thing here, because these two sites read a DOM node out of the ref inside an effect body, and a test that silently starts reading something else would be worse than the warning. If they are not equivalent at these sites, say so and STOP: that would make this a real defect in `570d07d286` rather than a lint.

CHECK WHETHER OTHER SITES CARRY THE SAME PATTERN. Two token axes, line-oriented AND whitespace-collapsed, with a control that shares the target's shape. If the same read appears elsewhere under the UIx adapter and is NOT flagged, establish why before assuming the gate is inconsistent — the linter may be scoped to hook bodies.

DO NOT SUPPRESS THE WARNING. Adding an ignore, lowering the gate, or excluding the file are all wrong: the zero-warning gate is the thing that caught a real idiom violation within hours of it landing, which is the gate working.

ACCEPTANCE: `node implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` (or whatever the real entry point is — read it) exits 0 on the tree, and the node test step still reports its full count with zero failures. Quote both captured exit codes and both counts. Confirm the tests still assert what they asserted: a green suite after changing what a test READS is not evidence unless the counts hold and a fault plant still bites.
notes:
--- worker uixlint-a, 2026-09-05, PR #9293 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9293) ---

REPRODUCED FIRST, captured exit code. `node implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs
node-test out/node-test.js` (the real entry point; `npm run test:cljs` is that,
`&& node out/node-test.js`) exited 1 on the unmodified trunk file:
`node-test compiled 1901 of 1902 files with 2 WARNING(S)`, both
`:uix.linter/interop-ref-read` at lines 120:24 and 139:24. The node test step was
green in the same tree. AFTER the two-line change: exit 0, `Build completed.
(1903 files, 72 compiled, 0 warnings, 43.20s)`.

SEMANTICS VERIFIED AT SOURCE BEFORE CHANGING THE READS — they ARE equivalent, so
this is a lint and not a defect in 570d07d286. `com.pitch/uix.core` 1.4.4,
`uix/core.cljs` `use-ref`: it returns `(specify! #js {:current value} IDeref
(-deref [this] (.-current this)) IReset ... ISwap ...)`. `-deref` is LITERALLY
`(.-current this)` — the same property read on the same object, no coercion, no
second indirection. That object is also what `($ :div {:ref ref})` hands React,
so React assigns the DOM node into the very `.current` both forms read.

CENSUS, two token axes (line-oriented + whitespace-collapsed) with a
shape-sharing fixed-string control that returned non-zero. Both axes agree:
3 `.-current` hits under `implementation/adapters/uix/` — the two fixed sites,
plus `adapters/uix/README.md:61`. Repo-wide there are 18 more across
story/xray/bench/core/hicasso. NONE of the others is flagged, and the reason is
at source rather than gate inconsistency: `uix.linter/interop-ref-read?` requires
the `.-current` target's LOCAL BINDING INIT FORM to be a `use-ref` call, and
`lint-body!` is reached only via `uix.linter/lint!`, which `uix.core` calls from
`defui` and `uix.core/fn` alone. So the rule is scoped to UIx component bodies.
`hicasso/test/.../imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test.cljs` carries `.-current` on
Hicasso refs (its only `use-ref` occurrence is the KEYWORD `:use-ref` in a
hook-ledger assertion), and README.md is markdown the compiler never sees.

THE NODE LANE DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE TWO TEST BODIES — worth recording, because
it is what would make a green node suite worthless as evidence here. Both
deftests self-gate on `(browser?)` and no-op under `:node-test`, contributing one
trivial `(is true ...)` each; a namespace-scoped run reads `Ran 2 tests
containing 2 assertions`. The ns docstring states this. Behavioural coverage is
the `:browser-test` lane (ns-regexp `-dom-cljs-test$`).

COUNTS HELD, measured same-base (only the two lines differing):
  before  Ran 11253 tests containing 57131 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.
  after   Ran 11253 tests containing 57131 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.
The final-base figure is 11256/57172 purely because trunk gained tests in flight
(PR #9284 extended realworld_cljs_test.cljs; PR #9286 added
ssr/presence_truthiness_cljs_test.cljc) — neither touches this file.

FAULT PLANT, done in the BROWSER lane because that is where the behaviour lives.
Line 120's `@ref` replaced by a freshly created detached element, rebuilt so the
runtime observed it (3 files recompiled), browser suite went RED exit 1 with three
failures ALL inside `imperative-effect-follows-the-frame-across-a-provider-swap`
— the one test whose component was planted — while
`omitting-the-frame-dep-keeps-dispatching-into-the-previous-frame`, still reading
`@ref`, stayed green. Restored and verified by GIT BLOB HASH against the
committed object (16a1e70e99f5fca3db56a31ab8aff7c1642970c3, exact match), not by
reading a diff. Clean browser control run: exit 0, Ran 786 tests containing 4311
assertions, 0 failures 0 errors.

NOTHING SUPPRESSED. `compile-node-test.cjs` and every linter/gate configuration
are untouched; no ignore comment, no threshold change, no exclusion.

CI SURFACES ARMED, from `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` on the
changed PATH: implementation_jvm, cljs_node_test, adapter_diagnostic,
cljs_browser, examples_compile, cljs_prod, bundle_isolation,
adapter_testbed_smokes, tools_jvm, template_expensive, mcp_conformance, mcp_live.
Both the job that was red (cljs_node_test) and the lane that exercises these
tests (cljs_browser) are armed. NOTE for whoever runs that classifier next: it
takes PATHS, not revisions — handed `origin/main HEAD` it reports EVERY surface
false, which is a false all-clear indistinguishable from a genuinely unaffected
change. Caught here by exercising it against a control path.

RATCHETS: check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose exit 0 (2794 files, 10867 edges,
2446 non-canonical, every surface at or under its floor) — grades IMPORT EDGES and
this diff adds no file and no require, so honest but uninformative.
check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose exit 0 (zero 'lease' residue in tracked
content or paths) — this one does grade the edited lines and the file's prose.

REAL WORK FOUND OUTSIDE THE FENCE, deliberately NOT done here to keep the P1 to two
lines: `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:61` carries the same `(.-current ref)`
in the canonical outer/inner imperative-lifecycle recipe — the very recipe this test
transcribes ("The README's canonical imperative-lifecycle recipe, compiled."). It
reds nothing, because markdown is never compiled, but it is the source the next
transcription copies, and copying it re-creates this exact trunk-red. Worth a
follow-up bead.

--- gates re-established on the FINAL base after two further rebases ---
Trunk moved three times during this work. The spine's exit 0 was measured at base
c4d8d49f; trunk then gained core.cljc and others, so the branch was rebased again
and the two headline numbers re-run rather than carried over:
  compile-node-test.cjs node-test   captured exit 0 — Build completed.
                                     (1904 files, 1004 compiled, 0 WARNINGS, 87.67s)

                                     base c4d8d49f.
No trunk commit has touched this file since the original base (git log <base>..

The two spellings are interchangeable at these sites; the linter's preference is idiom.

BUT THE NODE LANE DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE TWO BODIES AT ALL: both deftests self-gate on `(browser?)`, and a namespace-scoped run reports "Ran 2 tests containing 2 assertions". So a green node suite proved nothing about the behaviour. The worker planted in the BROWSER lane where the behaviour lives — line 120 replaced with a detached element, rebuilt so the runtime saw the plant — and got exit 1 with three failures ALL INSIDE the planted component's test, while the sibling test still reading `@ref` stayed green. Restore verified by git blob hash 16a1e70e99f5fca3db56a31ab8aff7c1642970c3, exact match.

That asymmetry is why PRs kept merging green all afternoon while this sat on main, and why two separate workers independently reported it as "not mine" while establishing it was not theirs. AN INSTRUMENT FINDING WORTH CARRYING: `report-changed-surfaces.sh` takes PATHS, not revisions. title: story: Step Debugger Start runs the script before step 1
description:
## Finding

The Test-mode Step Debugger does not start from pre-play state for the normal/default `:script` shape. `re-frame.story.ui.test-mode.stepper-state/begin!` says it re-allocates the frame "so the run starts fresh," but at `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state.cljs:104-147` it calls `(rf.story.runtime/reset-variant variant-id)` and waits for that promise before calling `begin-stepper!` and publishing cursor 0. `reset-variant` is deliberately a full rerun: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1715-1728` destroys the frame and delegates to `run-variant`; `run-variant` enters `run-phase-4!` (`runtime.cljc:979ff`, `:1260ff`), where `auto-runnable-plays` executes the script. Bare `:script` defaults `:auto-run?` to true (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner.cljc:324-356`). `begin-stepper!` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc:366-385`) then merely seeds the complete script into `:remaining`; it does not restore setup state. The UI therefore says "ready · N steps" with cursor 0 while app-db already reflects all N mutating steps.

This is reproduced against current production JVM primitives at HEAD `2c61dafd702db9672163ee9d2028db34c70c978d`, not inferred from prose. A registered variant with `:setup [[:probe/seed 0]]` and three default-auto-run `[:dispatch-sync [:probe/inc]]` steps, followed by the same `reset-variant -> begin-stepper!` sequence used by the CLJS UI, printed:

`{:after-reset {:count 3}, :frame-db {:count 3}, :stepper {:remaining [inc inc inc], :ran []}}`

The existing prepare-only lifecycle proves the expected shape is already available: the same probe through `runtime/prepare-run!` (documented at `runtime.cljc:1364-1378` as phases 0-2 "WITHOUT executing the play script") printed:

`{:prepared-frame-db {:count 0}, :stepper {:remaining [inc inc inc], :ran []}}`

The repository's own exemplary `:story.counter/clicked-three-times` makes the user-visible failure concrete (`tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs:353-375`): setup seeds 0 and the script increments three times. Pressing Start first advances it to 3 while displaying cursor 0; pressing Step once advances it to 4 while displaying "step 1". Rewind restores the incorrectly captured post-script epoch (3), not the specified initial state (0). This contradicts `tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md:462` (`begin!` re-allocate + prime), `:465`, `:482`, and `:498-501` (rewind restores the pre-play state), plus `tools/story/README.md:28-34` (canvas reflects each step's app-db).

## Impact

This is not a cosmetic counter mismatch: the debugger repeats every default-auto-run interaction and side effect before the programmer can inspect step 1. State mutations, HTTP stubs/effects, DOM gestures, and assertions may execute twice, and displayed cursor/outcomes describe a different run from the frame being debugged. A debugging tool that changes the program before presenting its initial state is actively misleading to both SPA authors and agents.

## Bounded recommendation

Make Step Debugger Start allocate/prepare the variant only through the pre-play lifecycle (loaders/setup, phases 0-2), then capture that epoch and seed `begin-stepper!`; do not call a full `reset-variant`/phase-4 run. Reuse the existing prepare-only runtime path or extract the narrow shared primitive it already embodies rather than duplicating lifecycle logic. Keep `reset-variant`, ordinary shell auto-run, and `:auto-run?` semantics unchanged.

Non-goals: redesigning the stepper controls or script DSL; changing normal run/reset behavior; changing the default `:auto-run?`; solving multi-play selection; a broad runtime ownership rewrite.

## Acceptance

1. Add a CLJS/browser regression using a mutating default-auto-run script: immediately after Start, cursor is 0 and frame app-db is setup state (for example count 0), not post-script state (3).
2. The first Step executes exactly the first script step once (count 1); subsequent steps remain 1:1 with cursor, and Rewind returns to setup/pre-play state (count 0).
3. Assert no script checkpoint, effect, or terminal phase-4 work runs as part of Start itself; failures in preparation still return the section to an honest inactive/error state.
4. Existing `run-variant`/`reset-variant` full-run behavior and ordinary on-mount auto-run remain unchanged.
5. Exercise `begin!` itself (or the Start DOM path), not only a directly seeded local slot.

## Why the current gates miss it

`tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state_cljs_test.cljs:25-27` explicitly seeds slots "without going through begin!" and has no begin test. The only live Start probe is `tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs:829-881`; it uses `:story.counter/loaded`, whose script is assertions only (`stories.cljs:340-346`), and checks controls/progress but never frame app-db. Thus the full `clojure -M:test` suite is green (1889 tests, 6959 assertions, 0 failures/errors) while this path is wrong.

## Duplicate and history check

Targeted `rg` against `.beads/issues.jsonl` found no title/body occurrence of `stepper-state`, `step-debugger`, `play stepper`, `begin-stepper!`, `pre-play epoch`, or `step-by-step run`; broader title scans for reset/auto-run/debugger found no matching Story issue. Git history shows the reset-before-begin sequence dates to the feature's original commit `c5f6ca44c15` / rf2-ulw5m (#1390). That commit advertised a full Start -> Step -> Back -> Rewind -> Stop browser flow but deliberately used `:story.counter/loaded`; later `c438c6cfaf` / rf2-4e545l fixed step-back epoch indexing while continuing to assume `begin!`'s seed was truly pre-play. No commit fixes or tracks this start-state defect.

## Uncertainty

The CLJS browser lane was not run because this dedicated review worktree has no `node_modules` and the review assignment forbade creating a link. The exact production lifecycle composition reproduces on the JVM, and the CLJS `begin!` calls those same cross-platform runtime/play functions around a JS Promise. The implementation worker should choose the cleanest way to carry the current shell run context into the existing prepare-only seam, but that integration choice does not affect the demonstrated phase-4-before-cursor bug.

## Posture fit

This is one high-leverage correction to a marquee programming tool, using an existing lifecycle split. It removes deception and friction without adding author-facing API or general machinery.
notes:
Post-merge audit — PR #9214 (completeness + correctness): `prepare-variant` promises to REJECT for a throwing loader / `:setup` handler, and `stepper-state/begin!` relies exclusively on that rejection (`.catch`) to leave the debugger inactive. The reused phase machinery deliberately does not throw for normal re-frame pipeline failures: `run-events!` / `run-loaders!` capture handler/cofx/interceptor exceptions into `:rf.story/assertions` and return, after which `prepare-variant` resolves `nil`. Deterministic probe against remote-main commit 64ba267e10: a variant whose sole `:setup` handler throws produced `{:settled :resolved, :value nil, :lifecycle :ready, :assertions [{:assertion :rf.error/exception, :phase :phase-2-events, :passed? false} ...]}`. Therefore `begin!` enters its `.then`, calls `begin-stepper!`, and publishes an active cursor-0 slot over a failed preparation, contradicting this bead's acceptance criterion 3 and the new §Start semantics. The new failure witness covers only an unknown variant, which throws during plan construction and misses the captured-handler class already pinned by `event-throwing-projects-as-assertion` and the loader-rejection E2E test. Bounded correction: preserve `run-variant`'s gather-the-full-picture semantics, but make `prepare-variant` expose a failing prepare outcome that `begin!` actually branches on (reject or a typed result), then add direct Start witnesses for captured `:setup` and loader failures. No stepper redesign is needed.

Under the default :rf.egress/local-redacted, a sensitive setup/loader exception therefore leaves no assertion for prepare-variant to see. Start still resolves and publishes an active cursor-0 stepper over failed setup.

Confirmed by a deterministic JVM probe of the production prepare-variant -> begin-stepper! composition using this PR's own reset-all! and begin-outcome helpers. A first setup event returns :db plus :sensitive [[:auth :password]]; the next uses {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:auth]]]} and throws ex-info. No synthetic trace injection, no mocks of the changed seam. The ordinary control uses the identical handler and omits only the classification effect:
  ordinary: {:start-branch :catch, :stepper-present? false, :failure-records 2, :suppressed 0, :observed-failures [{:operation :rf.error/handler-exception, :sensitive? nil}]}
  sensitive: {:start-branch :then, :stepper-present? true, :failure-records 0, :suppressed 6, :observed-failures [{:operation :rf.error/handler-exception, :sensitive? true}]}
Captured probe exit 0; audit-pr9252-re-frame2-1.log/.exit, invoked from this checkout's tools/story with the test source loaded by absolute path. The positive ordinary-failure control proves the new rejection path is live; privacy classification alone makes the identical failure read as success. Existing sensitive_trace_cljs_test.cljc:271ff intentionally asserts that sensitive handler exceptions never reach the display pending-exceptions buffer, corroborating the source behavior.

This is the same exact acceptance-3 residual, so reopening rf2-k6y2 rather than filing another issue. Keep the title, original criteria and prior fixes. Bounded repair: carry the fact that THIS preparation failed independently from the redacted display records (for example a phase-local presence flag at the existing exception-capture boundary), then reject Start with privacy-safe evidence. Keep sensitive payloads/messages suppressed; do not turn on local-raw, treat every suppressed event as a failure, or change run-variant's gather-the-full-picture behavior. Add setup and loader witnesses with real sensitive path classification, plus healthy sensitive-event and ordinary failure controls. Start should remain inactive on both failures without exposing their private details. No debugger or privacy-system redesign is needed.
FIX for the REOPEN audit note (PR #9272, draft->ready 2026-09-05). Every cited site verified at source; line numbers re-derived at tip fbbec30b2e: captured-prepare-failures runtime.cljc:1735-1766 CONFIRMED; capture-phase-errors' suppress branch runtime.cljc:107-149 (the drop is at :131-135, the note said :130-148) CONFIRMED; the play.cljc site is at :143-155 and its function is named listener-for-frame, NOT make-trace-listener — the note's only inaccuracy, and the mechanism it describes is exactly right.

No synthetic trace injection, redaction never turned off. Pre-fix focused run captured exit 1, 6 failures: (= :catch branch) read :then and the stepper slot was live over failed setup, while BOTH preconditions passed — display path empty AND suppressed-count positive, so the witness is the redaction mechanism and not section (5)'s ordinary case.

Redaction is NOT weakened — nothing author-owned crosses. Suppression alone is never a refusal: the record keys on a suppressed pipeline EXCEPTION, not on suppressed-count, so a healthy privacy-classified variant stays step-debuggable. Cleared at phase 0's fresh-frame boundary and evicted on frame teardown beside pending-exceptions. run-variant / prepare-run! unchanged.

The healthy-sensitive control was checked against the over-broad repair the note warns about rather than assumed: planting readiness-keyed-on-suppressed-count turned it red; plant reverted and revert verified by sha256 of the file bytes (identical).

title: surface-review(template): collapse the generator to one small runnable SPA contract
description:
## Scope

Reduce `tools/template/**` to one deliberate product contract: scaffold a small client-side counter SPA that a programmer or agent can read, run, test, and replace. Keep the Reagent default and the UIx substrate selector because that choice changes authored source and adapter wiring. Remove feature/style modes and the generated policy/toolchain bundle. Update the generated resources, hook API, tests, and normative spec together; touch directly coupled template release-gate assertions only where the smaller contract requires it.

## Findings

1. The default Reagent scaffold is not minimal. Before compiled output or `node_modules`, it emits 20 files, 75,816 bytes, and 1,579 lines. The generated README alone is 677 lines; `events.cljs` is 232 lines for two tiny handlers; `deps.edn` is 76 lines. The actual counter cycle is a handful of forms.
2. The default installs decisions the app has not made: schemas, a git-pinned Xray tool plus `@xyflow/react` and `elkjs`, a trace error sink, a whole-app-db schema, a long commented HTTP handler, CSP and production-hosting policy, GitHub Actions, Lefthook, cljfmt, clj-kondo, `dev/user.clj`, and a REPL scratch namespace. These are useful recipes, not requirements for the first SPA.
3. The generator exposes three feature/style flags (`:include-story?`, `:include-ssr?`, `:css`) on top of the substrate axis, yielding eight accepted output cells and mutual-exclusion/capability machinery. `hooks.clj` is 774 lines; the template tests are 5,608 lines; the spec is 3,295 lines. Much of the suite pins explanatory prose, badges, CSP snippets, Xray layout details, and variant combinations instead of the first-run contract.
4. The shared README teaches Story even when Story was not requested. The generated source teaches HTTP, privacy/egress, production schema elision, Xray, and deployment hardening before the reader has replaced the counter. This makes both humans and agents distinguish essential code from a framework handbook on their first edit.
5. The public descriptions have already drifted under the matrix: `template.edn` advertises Story but omits the live SSR and Tailwind modes; Principles P3 says React and ReactDOM are the only npm dependencies while the default Reagent path injects Xray's two additional npm packages. The canonical Clojure name `acme/my-app` is copied verbatim into `package.json`; npm 11's bundled `validate-npm-package-name` rejects that unscoped slash form.
6. History shows accretion, not an intentional current baseline. The initial scaffold at `2313a8d85a` emitted 10 files / 8,966 bytes / 272 lines. Subsequent commits separately added the dev bundle (`d9830dc2fc`), cljfmt (`3cdc6f3b26`), Lefthook (`bfe4aa3ee8`), Xray's predecessor (`efbdd60a94`), CSP/production hardening (`f61b816163`), best-practice demos (`f6f770bfc0`), and CI (`b04c304614`). Correct later fixes hardened that accumulated shape, but no product pass re-asked what belongs in a starter.
7. Public distribution is a separate known blocker: `.github/workflows/template-release.yml` states that it rewrites emitted framework coordinates to local roots and that the advertised public template coordinate is not yet usable. Existing publication beads own that. Adding another invocation mode or a `:minimal?` flag would compound both problems.

## Recommended Action

- Make the template emit one SPA shape per supported view substrate. `:name` remains required; `:substrate :reagent|:uix` is the only template-specific option, with Reagent as the obvious default.
- Delete `:include-story?`, `:include-ssr?`, and `:css` from the hook API, resources, errors, docs, and matrix tests. Story, SSR, and Tailwind remain learnable through their focused examples/guides; do not replace the flags with a wizard, profiles, or separate compatibility modes in this task.
- Emit only the files needed to run, test, release, and understand the counter: `.gitignore`, a short README, `deps.edn`, `package.json`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, the HTML/CSS shell, `core.cljs`, `events.cljs`, `subs.cljs`, `views.cljs`, and one focused event-flow test. Remove generated CI, hook-manager/editor/formatter/linter configs, REPL scratch scaffolding, and schema source.
- Keep direct dependencies to the runnable counter: Clojure/ClojureScript, re-frame2 core, the selected adapter and view library, shadow-cljs, React, and ReactDOM. Do not preload Xray or pull schemas/tool coordinates into every Reagent app.
- Keep comments local and brief. Preserve the measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` lifecycle, but move HTTP, schema, privacy, CSP, production-host, Xray, Story, SSR, migration, and tooling tutorials to existing public docs and link to them from a compact next-steps section.
- Derive an npm-valid package name from the Clojure project coordinate instead of copying `acme/my-app` verbatim.
- Replace prose- and combination-heavy tests with a small black-box contract: exact emit manifest, parseable/valid manifests, compile/test/release, real browser boot and 0→1 counter interaction for both substrates, and absence of retired files/dependencies/options. Keep history in git rather than carrying completed migration/validation reports as live normative surface.

## Evidence

- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:37-66` enumerates the 20-file default; lines 364-712 assert the generated handbook, CI, Xray host, CSP, privacy, schema, and HTTP prose.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md` is 677 lines and includes Hot reload, Story, Production hardening, REPL, schemas, privacy/egress, HTTP, migration, and future skill-install sections.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/events.cljs` is 232 lines; the counter handlers occupy only the small initialisation/increment blocks, while the rest is an error sink and commented HTTP exemplar.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn` adds schemas, Xray, cljfmt, clj-kondo, and tools.namespace around the base app; `_shared/package.json` injects Xray npm packages and uses `{{name}}` as the npm name.
- `tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:179-291,321-643,655-741` owns the flag gate, coercions, capability-conditioned substitution prose, and file-selection matrix.
- `tools/template/spec/000-Vision.md`, `API.md`, `001-Substrate-Variants.md`, and `002-Generated-Shape.md` claim a minimal counter while specifying the larger matrix and tooling bundle.
- `.github/workflows/template-release.yml:114-129,257-273` explicitly says the release smoke masks unresolved consumer coordinates; this task must not invent a second distribution route around that separate owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The documented template API has exactly one template-specific selector: optional `:substrate` with Reagent default and UIx alternative. The removed Story, SSR, and CSS keys fail as unknown; there are no aliases, deprecation warnings, reserved gates, or compatibility shims for them.
2. Reagent and UIx emit the same small project manifest apart from `core.cljs`, `views.cljs`, and required dependency differences. The emitted tree contains the run/test/release essentials named above and does not contain `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `lefthook.yml`, `.cljfmt.edn`, `.clj-kondo/`, `.editorconfig`, `dev/`, `schema.cljs`, Story files, SSR files, or Tailwind overlays.
3. The default direct dependency graph contains no Xray, Story, SSR, schemas, machines, cljfmt, clj-kondo, or tools.namespace coordinate and no Xray-only npm package. `package.json` has an npm-valid name derived deterministically from both qualified and bare Clojure project names.
4. Each substrate's generated app parses, compiles, runs its focused test, builds an advanced release, opens its real generated page, paints the counter, and moves 0→1 on click. The correct one-time init plus `^:dev/after-load` re-render lifecycle from `rf2-r0kk7` remains covered.
5. Generated source contains the counter dataflow and the lifecycle facts needed to edit it, without embedded HTTP/schema/privacy/security/tooling tutorials. The generated README gives the run, test, release, and guide/docs links without conditional sections for modes that were not emitted.
6. Template tests assert the behavioral and manifest contract, including red witnesses for a retired flag, an advanced dependency/file reappearing, an invalid npm name, and a broken browser boot. They do not pin badges, prose paragraphs, server-specific CSP snippets, or removed variant cells.
7. Normative template docs and metadata describe the same reduced surface. Completed migration/validation records are removed from the live contract or clearly historical; no document advertises a mode the generator no longer accepts.

## Non-goals

- No new wizard, `:minimal?` switch, profile system, second template, prompt sequence, or replacement feature flag.
- No compatibility layer for pre-alpha Story/SSR/Tailwind invocations; git history is the migration record.
- No runtime, adapter, Xray, Story, SSR, Tailwind, schema, HTTP, or security-policy redesign.
- No Hicasso substrate addition.
- No operator-owned repository split, coordinate rename, Clojars verification, tag, or publication work. The reduced scaffold must compose with that work when it lands, not duplicate it.
- Do not delete the focused examples or guides that become the on-ramp for advanced capabilities.

## Related beads

- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed): established the correct generated hot-reload lifecycle; preserve its behavior while shrinking the prose.
- `rf2-48rk3` (closed): made feature capability selection fail closed; most of that machinery becomes unnecessary when feature modes are retired, while the substrate registry can remain small.
- `rf2-8urba` (deferred): proposed a future Hicasso template variant; distinct and explicitly outside this minimal-contract change.
- `rf2-uelji` (deferred) and `rf2-fo4ng` (deferred): own verified-group/public-coordinate work; this task does not bypass or duplicate them.
- `rf2-k5r9t` (open): adapter-owned client-root work may later shorten generated Reagent boot code, but is not a prerequisite for removing template ceremony.

*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** TRIAGE 2026-08-30 22:10:05 AUSEST (read-only agent at d0aabeb73a): premises HOLD (spec drifted to 3,337 lines/11 files). == 2. HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED ==

THE DOSSIER AUTHOR (§Recommendation): "Affirm the collapse and strip both." Grounds: pre-alpha, elegance over accumulation, trust the programmer; a starter's job is to be read, run and replaced in one sitting, and today's scaffold hands a newcomer a 719-line handbook and five installed decisions before their first edit; Xray and Story each have a copy-paste attach recipe surfaced from the README's next-steps and from the setup skill at the moment the user wants it. Option B was called "the only defensible keep", tipped against by mechanics rather than aesthetics: the preload drags in a sha-pinned monorepo git dep and two npm packages, keeps the substrates asymmetric, and couples the template to the tools' release cadence. Reversible: re-adding one preload line later is a smaller act than carrying the machinery meanwhile.

THE REVIEWER (§Codex Recommendation): AGREES on every point that matters — "Affirm the collapse and strip both the default Xray wiring and the `:include-story?` generator flag. Make `:substrate` the only template-specific choice" — and says it reached that "from the current resources, hooks, tests, tool dependency graphs, documentation, and git history rather than from the bead's findings." It ADDED four things the dossier did not carry, all adopted here: (i) the strongest keep-Xray argument named at source — tools/template/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §9 ("Xray on by default", rf2-y9zqc) treats immediate runtime feedback as part of the first-run experience, and a devtools preload never enters an advanced release — answered by "'no production bundle cost' is narrower than 'no scaffold cost'", with the scaffold cost itemised (git-pinned coordinate, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a preload, a layout host, CSS, CSP qualifications, README material, and the lockstep tests at version_lockstep_test.clj:227-251) and Xray's own dependency graph (tools/xray/deps.edn:15-100 reaches epoch, routing, flows, schemas, resources, machines, Hicasso, machines-viz, reagent-slim, Reagent, Editscript and zprint, and records that Xray cannot publish while Hicasso lacks a coordinate); (ii) Story is "even less suitable as the one surviving flag" — the flag selects a 123-line routing/lifecycle entry point, a separate 102-line deps.edn and a 76-line registration example, and Story hard-depends on Reagent, machines, HTTP and Xray (tools/story/deps.edn:14-75); (iii) an explicit warning, adopted verbatim as a non-goal: "Do not replace the removed Xray wiring with an `:include-xray?` flag: that would immediately recreate the option matrix this decision is trying to eliminate"; (iv) the concrete test shape — explicit ABSENCE assertions for Xray/Story coordinates, npm packages, preloads, hosts and variant files, and the README's Xray and Story links kept as TESTED escape hatches.

WHERE THEY DIFFERED, in the reviewer's own words: "The real tradeoff is discoverability. A new Reagent user will no longer see the project's most distinctive devtools automatically, and some users will never follow a next-steps link. That is a product-marketing loss, not a runtime correctness loss, and it should be acknowledged rather than hidden behind the word 'minimal'. If the desired front door is a showcase rather than a neutral starter, then keeping Xray only is the coherent fallback; keeping Story or adding more flags is not. I would revisit default-on Xray only after there is evidence from first-run testing that auto-opening the panel materially improves successful onboarding, preferably once it has a stable consumer coordinate and can mount on every supported default substrate." The dossier called the same loss "the one real ergonomic loss" and mitigated it by the next-steps link; the reviewer weighted it higher and named the fallback. This ruling sides with both on the outcome and ADOPTS THE REVIEWER'S REVISIT CONDITION AS THE RECORDED ONE: default-on Xray is reconsidered only on first-run evidence, only once Xray has a stable published coordinate (`xray-v*`), and only if it can mount on every default substrate — today it cannot mount on UIx (rf2-p6f6u; Xray's mount refuses that adapter kind by name), and its Reagent-only preload is exactly the asymmetry that would force AC2/AC3 here and rc0yh's AC3 to be reworded around an exception. The front door is a neutral starter, not a showcase; the showcase is the docs, the testbeds and the setup skill, each of which teaches the tool at the moment the reader wants it.

WHY THE RULING WENT THIS WAY, in one paragraph: everything in the bead except the taste question is machinery removal, and both opinions plus the 2026-08-30 triage and the 2026-09-01 backlog reread hold it settled. On the taste question the two opinions converge from different evidence bases; the only dissent is about how loudly to acknowledge a discoverability cost; and that cost is reversible in a one-line PR, while the machinery a keep would retain (a git-pinned monorepo coord in every newborn app, lockstep npm pins, `xray?` substitutions in four hook slots, a permanent manifest asymmetry, release-cadence coupling) is exactly the class of coupling this surface review exists to cut. Posture applies in full: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, trust the programmer to paste four lines when they want a panel.

description:
Named by rf2-qrjr5's census during PR #10108 and correctly NOT edited (018 was spoken for). Verified independently by the mayor at trunk cbaa181303.

TWO SITES IN tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md DESCRIBE THE VIEWS TAB AS THE UNBUILT THREE-GROUP LAYOUT, and one of them is the canonical tab-inventory table:

- 018:634, the L3 tab inventory row: "| 3 | **Views** | `v` | `:views` | Per-view rows: mounted / re-rendered / unmounted groups; each row lists subs used + sub return values; cluster-large-grids; isolation-scoped to selected frame | [`012-Views.md`](012-Views.md) |"
- 018:2283, a reference-list row: "- [`012-Views.md`](012-Views.md) — Views tab three-group layout (mounted / re-rendered / unmounted); nested subs; cluster-large-grids."

WHY BOTH ARE FALSE, measured at source by the mayor:

tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md:1-14 is a SUPERSEDED banner, and it disclaims precisely these words:

  "SUPERSEDED by 021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §3 (rf2-ee38b.2, 2026-05-23). The shipped Views panel implements 021 §3.2's left-to-right reactive flow graph (app-db -> Level-1 subs -> derived subs -> views), followed by unmounted-view and destroyed-subscription lists and the unchanged-sub disclosure. Earlier table layouts are superseded. The richer surface this document describes below -- three TEMPORAL groups (mounted / re-rendered / unmounted), subs nested under views with inline return values, >=50 grid clustering, a component/sub group-by toggle, a right-click component-filter chip, per-component inline drilldown (props-diff + Fiber metadata), and the five-state sub-status glyph taxonomy -- is NOT implemented and is not the destination."

So 018:634 lists THREE of the disclaimed items as the tab's content -- the three temporal groups, subs-with-return-values nested per row, and cluster-large-grids -- and cites 012 as its authority, when 012 exists to deny them.

THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS THE FLOWS-INTO-VIEWS ROWS CORRECTED THIS WEEK (rf2-qvczv in 018, rf2-exv5x in 007, rf2-qrjr5 in 000/019): a spec describing a PROPOSED surface as though it shipped. It is worse in one respect -- 018:634 is the L3 TAB INVENTORY, the table a reader consults to learn what a tab IS, so a wrong row there misinforms every reader of the page rather than one paragraph's.

WHAT IS TRUE AND SHOULD REPLACE IT: 021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §3.2 owns the shipped Views panel -- a left-to-right reactive flow graph (app-db -> Level-1 subs -> derived subs -> views), then unmounted-view and destroyed-subscription lists, then the unchanged-sub disclosure. 021:552 records that "(rerendered)" survives only as a PER-NODE LABEL on a View node, never as a group. rf2-qrjr5's landed correction at 019:821 states this correctly and is the wording to match rather than re-invent.

OUT OF SCOPE: do not edit 012-Views.md (its superseded banner is correct and deliberate); do not rewrite 021; do not touch the Flows rows already corrected; do not renumber the inventory table or change its column count. If the reference row at :2283 should simply be re-pointed at 021 rather than reworded, say so and do that.

VERIFY THE TABLE RENDERS: 018:634 is a markdown table row and nothing in CI checks column counts or rendering. Count the pipes before and after and say so.

GATES: check_doc_slugs.py covers tools/*/spec and is the live gate; measure whether its green is vacuous for the lines you edit (the discriminator is whether those lines carry a link or an anchor -- both these rows DO carry links, so it is likely live, but measure rather than assume). mkdocs build --strict stages only spec and migration, never tools/ -- wrong gate. check_readme_links.py --ci excludes tools/*/spec/ entirely. Nothing grades whether the prose is TRUE; that is resolved by hand against 012's banner and 021 §3.2.

FENCED: 018-Event-Spine.md is held by open PR #10110 (rf2-uwvpi) at filing. Re-derive both line numbers at the trunk of the day -- 018 has taken several PRs this week and these numbers will move.

## THE FIX, AND WHY THE BOUNDARY IS HONEST

A `bounded-vec` helper beside `bounded-count*`, sharing its `counted?` dispatch: `counted?` (vector,
list, `IntegerRange`) realises whole, because `diff-pair-count` reports their FULL count; NOT `counted?`
(`LazySeq`, and the `Range` an unbounded `(range)` returns) takes `count-bound`, because those are the
only shapes that can be endless and are exactly the ones `bounded-count*` already stops at.

That split was READ OUT OF THE CLOJURESCRIPT SOURCE rather than assumed (cljs 1.12.145 `cljs/core.cljs`):
`Range` and `LazySeq` implement no `ICounted`; `IntegerRange` does. So `counted?` separates "can be
endless" from "finite by construction" exactly.

**Honest** is therefore structural, not cosmetic: the header number and the rendered row count are the
same number in BOTH directions, because both are computed by the same `counted?` test —
`diff-pair-count` via `bounded-count*`, the body via `bounded-vec`. A blanket `(take count-bound ...)`
would have been finite but DISHONEST, rendering 1001 rows under a header saying 1050; `children-of`'s
own docstring already refuses that direction, and this brings the diff entry path into line with it.
That is also how "preserving ordinary finite diffs" is satisfied.

truncation drops a suffix of each; for every k inside the bound the k-th survivor on each side is still
the k-th, and `bi->ai` pairs it exactly as it did unbounded. Bounding one side only would slide that zip
and strike the wrong element — the very defect rf2-vu42n fixed. Pinned by a 1050-element vector (longer
than the bound) with a scattered mid-vector removal: 1050 rows, the struck row is the genuinely-removed
member and not a shifted survivor, before-order reconstructed exactly, survivors past the removal
carrying their shifted after-index. That test PASSES ON TRUNK by design — its job is to refuse a WRONG
FIX, not to catch the current defect.

assertion alone is green against `(take count-bound (vec after))`, which bounds the OUTPUT while still

mechanism being fixed, so a worker trusting the number lands somewhere plausible and is NOT alerted. The
real site is `:1457-1458` (+7). The caller cited at `:2705-2706` is mid-comment; the call is at `:2713`
(+7/+8). Anyone re-dispatching against this file should re-derive rather than inherit.

## CENSUS — ONE UNBOUNDED SITE, AND IT IS THE ONE FIXED

29 `(vec ` lines in the file, two independent instruments agreeing (ripgrep and a Python multi-pass).
Passes: line-oriented 29, whitespace-flattened 29, `;;`-comments-stripped 29, string-literals-dropped 28
— the single difference being one DOCSTRING prose hit, "(vec of segments)". Control taken FROM the
target (`sequential-diff-children`: 4 line-oriented, 2 after comments stripped = the `defn` and the one
call site); nonsense needle `zzqqx-not-here` reads 0 at every pass. Every other `(vec ...)` is a finite
path vector, map `keys`, a set, or already bounded. Call sites, `git grep` over tracked src only:
`children-of-pair` exactly twice (the fallback inside `sequential-diff-children`, and the
non-sequential diff arm), `sequential-diff-children` exactly once.

## GATES — CAPTURED EXITS, NEVER PIPED, NEVER GLOBBED

Node lane, split so the run phase is gated on the compile's own captured exit: baseline clean trunk
`COMPILE_EXIT=0 RUN_EXIT=0`, 12315 / 61768, 0 failures 0 errors -> after `COMPILE_EXIT=0 RUN_EXIT=0`,
**12318 / 61783, 0 failures 0 errors**. Delta PREDICTED FROM THE DIFF BEFORE ANY LOG WAS OPENED as
+3 tests / +15 assertions; actual +3 / +15, EXACT — which is the evidence the branch was compiled, a
namespace grep of a green log being incapable of it under this tree's quiet reporter.

**This is the ONLY gate that grades this code**, measured not assumed: all TEN tracked `edn_inspector*` /
`edn_widget*` test files are `.cljs`, ZERO are `.cljc`, so no `clojure -M:test` invocation compiles a
line of it.

clj-kondo via `python scripts/lint_kondo.py` (CI-pinned 2026.04.15, twelve `--lint` roots):
**errors 0 / warnings 1957 / exit 0 before and after — zero delta.** Plain form on the two changed files:
errors 0, warnings 2, exit 2, both pre-existing — linting the TRUNK BLOB of the same file yields the
identical two at trunk lines 2197/2264, mapping to 2240/2307 under this change's +43-line insertion.
Positive control: the plain form exits 3 on a planted unresolved symbol that `--fail-level error` reads
as 0. NOT APPLICABLE and stated rather than skipped: `check_doc_slugs.py` (roots `docs`, `spec`,
`skills`, `migration`, `tools/*/spec` — this change is outside all of them), `mkdocs build --strict`
(stages only `spec` and `migration`, never any `tools/` tree), `check_readme_links.py --ci` (no markdown
touched).

Line endings: both files `i/lf w/crlf`; CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0 before and after, all three numbers
taken with Python on the bytes.

## rf2-jh12f DOES NOT COLLAPSE INTO THIS — STATED EITHER WAY, AS ASKED

Verdict: SEPARATE, and the `counted?` dispatch was chosen partly so it would stay that way. This item
was "the bound is never reached"; rf2-jh12f is "the bound lies". A blanket `(take count-bound ...)` here
would have IMPORTED jh12f's defect onto the live path — 1001 rows under a 1050 header — and then the two
genuinely would have had to be fixed together. Dispatching on `counted?` instead makes this item's
boundary self-consistent without touching any of jh12f's three named functions.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR rf2-jh12f, named precisely so its worker inherits a map rather than a
surprise: `children-of-pair`'s own sequential branch at `edn_inspector.cljs:1363-1364` still caps a
`counted?` sequence at `count-bound` while `diff-pair-count` reports its FULL count, so an ADDED 1200-
element vector (before side `::missing`, hence `b-vec` nil, hence the fallback) still renders 1001 rows
under a header saying 1200, with no continuation marker. That path is reached through this function's
fallback at `:1464`, which is why the two items read as entangled. Also left: the `bounded-count*`
one-element lookahead recorded above, and the same header/body mismatch between `child-count` and
`children-of` for a `counted?` `:list` over 1001. None of these were touched.

Out of scope and untouched: `estimate-chars!` (rf2-re7dn), `render-protocol-node` (rf2-et4l0).

## LANE

Taken ~15:58 AUSEST after verifying free by effect (6 node/java rows machine-wide, no path filter, 0
empty command lines, 0 lane-bearing). Four runs. Released 16:28:51 AUSEST, re-verified by effect: 6
rows, no path filter, 0 empty command lines, 0 lane-bearing, 0 under this worktree; PIDs 80140/87380
(rf2-azxt5) untouched, Codex CLI and MCP servers untouched. `npm ci` from the lockfile in the worker's
own worktree — NO junction — and the mayor's `node_modules` read 103 entries before and 103 after, via
`find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` rather than a bare `ls`, which omits dotfiles including `.bin`.

Entered no other worktree; touched no queued sibling's code. AI-attribution trailers declined in all
three commits and in the PR body, per CLAUDE.md Git Conventions, which overrides the harness reminder.
