# Senior review: xray-reactive-diff

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has written structural-diff engines and dependency-graph visualisers; hunts the classic bugs (move reported as delete+add, stale edge after re-registration, "changed" badge on an equal-but-not-identical value, per-trace allocation on a hot path).
Tree: xray-review-sep17 worktree, trunk 9555881fe3
Scope read: PARTIAL (stopped by the coordinator to conserve budget; no runtime runs were made). ALL 20 source files read in full (7,972 lines): tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc (1233), chart/timing_waterfall.cljc (204), panels/reactive_panel.cljs (152), reactive_panel_view.cljs (771), reactive_panel_subs.cljs (719), reactive_panel_events.cljs (19), reactive_flow_graph.cljc (247), derivation_graph.cljs (594), derivation_graph_helpers.cljc (337), module_view.cljs (332), app_db_diff.cljs (325), app_db_diff_state.cljs (583), app_db_diff_subs.cljs (312), app_db_diff_events.cljs (87), app_db_diff_format.cljs (120), app_db_diff_helpers.cljc (686), app_db_segment_inspector.cljs (422), image_view_reads.cljs (356), image_view_helpers.cljc (268), local_render.cljc (205). Tests skimmed: diff/engine_cljs_test.cljc (partial), chart/timing_waterfall_cljs_test.cljc (full), app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs (partial). NOT READ: no file in scope is unread; see "Not yet examined" for the spec sections and runtime checks left open.
Owning specs consulted: tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md (end to end); 025-Derivation-Graph-Panel.md (end to end); 026-Module-View-Panel.md (end to end); 021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §3 and §4 only (:446-1146) -- remainder NOT READ; spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §Subscription input producers (:1027-1107) and §Subscription topology vs subscription tracking (:2186-2222) only; spec/Tool-Pair.md :618-651 and :884-895 only; tools/xray/spec/014-Registry-Catalogue.md :398-430 and :720-767 only; 008-Embedding-Contract.md :240-275 only; DESIGN-RATIONALE.md grepped for segment/show-me-when/waterfall/pinned (no ruling on any of them).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. `[N∆]` chip counts positional shifts as changes and never counts vector removals  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc:765-768 (`container-paths-from-leaves` removes only `:same`), :1084-1095 (`:same-shifted` ops are injected into `path-ops`), :933-936 and :971-980 (vector `:-` edits go to `:vector-removals`, never `path-ops`); tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:2097-2100 (chip = `engine/change-count-at`).
- What: prepending one element to a 100-element vector paints `[100∆]` on the parent (1 added + 99 shifted), and removing one element paints `[N-1∆]` from the shifts alone while the removed element itself is not counted.
- Evidence: traced by hand through `project`: `[:a :b :c :d] -> [:a :NEW :b :c :d]` yields path-ops `[1] :added` + `[2] [3] [4] :same-shifted`, so `change-count-at []` = 4; `[:a :b :c :d] -> [:a :c :d]` yields two `:same-shifted` entries and one `:vector-removals` entry, so the chip reads 2 for one removal. `flat-rows-from-path-ops` (:829-848) already excludes `:same-shifted` -- the flat lens got this right and the container count did not. Existing tests pin the ops (`r6-vector-insert-with-shift`, engine_cljs_test.cljc:68) and the map-case count (`r3-change-count-chip-input`, :166) but never the count after a shift or a removal.
- Action: in `container-paths-from-leaves` also `remove` `:same-shifted`; add each parent's `(count removals)` from `:vector-removals` to that parent and its ancestors; pin both with a vector case beside `r3-change-count-chip-input`.

### 2. The App-DB segment-inspector popup is mounted, installed and catalogued, but nothing opens it  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift] [size: M]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:108 (`:rf.xray/open-segment-inspector` reg-event); shell.cljs:3202 (mounted at root); registry.cljs:1266 (installed); panel_enum.cljc:105; panels.cljs:572-580 (`mount-segment-inspector!`); app_db_diff_state.cljs:374-379 (App-DB opts out of `:popup-affordance?`).
- What: `:rf.xray/open-segment-inspector` has zero dispatchers in `tools/xray/src` -- the only hits are its own `reg-event` and a docstring table (panels.cljs:108) -- and the edn-inspector dispatches nothing but `[:rf.xray/app-db …]`/`[:rf.xray/handler …]` site ids, so the "click any path segment" affordance spec 004 :429-488, :552-560 and :646-648 ("That is the whole list") describes cannot be reached; ~420 lines plus mount/registry/enum rows are dead surface.
- Evidence: Grep `open-segment-inspector` over `tools/xray/src` -> 2 hits (reg-event, docstring). Controls: `close-segment-inspector` is dispatched at 3 sites in the same file; `:rf.xray/reactive-toggle-unchanged` at reactive_panel_view.cljs:647; the same grep over `tools/xray/test` -> 28 hits across 5 files, so the popup is exercised only by tests. Spec 014 :414-425 and spec 007:1980 also list it as live. (The predecessor's "unreferenced" zero was wrong on the namespace -- it is required and mounted -- and right on the gesture.)
- Action: decide: A -- wire an opener (the inspector's key click or the rf2-h71e0 zoom gesture dispatches `[:rf.xray/open-segment-inspector path]`), or B -- delete the ns, the shell mount, the registry install, the panel_enum row and `mount-segment-inspector!`, and strike spec 004's three sections plus the 014/007 rows; zoom-into-node already covers "inspect at a prefix" in place, so B is the smaller and more honest change.

### 3. A changed sensitive slot now shows NOTHING in the App-DB tab; the framework still stamps the count the pruned chip was meant to render  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: privacy] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:24-43 (rf2-p53m2 pruned `:rf.xray/selected-epoch-redacted-modified-count`); implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:191 and :336 (`:rf.epoch/redacted-modified-paths-count` computed and stamped on every record); diff/engine.cljc:358 (`(= before after)` -> `:same`, so `:rf/redacted` vs `:rf/redacted` emits no row).
- What: under the `:rf.egress/local-redacted` default (finding-free, see the cross-slice note below) both sides of a declared-sensitive path read `:rf/redacted`, the engine classifies `:same`, and spec 004 :562-635's separate-from-diff chip -- the one designed signal that "something changed in a redacted slot" -- was pruned, so the operator sees an unchanged tree.
- Evidence: Grep `redacted-modified` over `tools/xray/src` -> only the two prune docstrings (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:27, app_db_diff.cljs:53); the same grep over `implementation/*/src` -> 5 hits in assembly.cljc, so the producer is live and the consumer is gone. Spec 004 :592-612 says "Xray reads it directly from the record".
- Action: read `(:rf.epoch/redacted-modified-paths-count record)` into `:rf.xray/app-db-current+diff` and render one muted chip on the TOP card header when > 0 (the record is already in hand at app_db_diff_subs.cljs:221); or strike the spec section and say why. The former is ~15 lines.

### 4. Per-epoch App-DB diff is O(whole db) even for a no-op epoch: `user-domain-db` defeats the engine's identity short-circuit and `mark-wholly-changed` walks the entire tree regardless of diff size  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: perf] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:377 (`(into {} (remove …) db)` -- always a fresh map, for both `:top` and `:before-top` at :564-567); diff/engine.cljc:884 (`identical?` guard), :735-740 (`walk-containers` over the ENTIRE after tree and the entire before tree), :682-688 (`check-uniform` calls `collect-leaves` over the whole subtree at EVERY container -- O(N x depth)); views/edn_inspector.cljs:3346-3354 (memo keyed on `identical?` of both inputs); app_db_diff_subs.cljs:214-218, :296-297 (`:rf.xray/app-db-state` recomputes on every epoch-history change).
- What: with the App-DB tab open and following head, every dispatch rebuilds `top`/`before-top` as non-identical maps, misses the inspector memo, and runs `engine/project`, whose `mark-wholly-changed` walks every container of the whole user-domain db twice even when the edit script is empty; spec 004 :9 names 1-50 MB app-dbs and calls this "the single most-used Xray surface".
- Evidence: Editscript's own entry guards `(when-not (= a b) …)` (editscript 0.6.5 a_star.cljc `diff`, read from the jar), so the A* is cheap on a no-change epoch; nothing guards `mark-wholly-changed`. The rf2-4spyl comment at app_db_diff_format.cljs:46-52 shows identity preservation was deliberately built for exactly this short-circuit, and `user-domain-db` sits between it and the engine. Not measured (no browser run); the cost model is from the code, not a profile.
- Action: (a) `user-domain-db` returns `db` unchanged when no key satisfies `reserved-namespace-key?` (its own docstring says that is the normal post-EP-0001 case); (b) `mark-wholly-changed` returns `#{}` when no leaf in `path-ops` is `:added`/`:removed`, and otherwise walks only the ancestor chains of those leaves. Open question for the successor: whether `re-frame.elision`'s walker returns `v` identical when the frame declares nothing (the `walk-tree` body was not located); if it rebuilds, every section pays and the fix is framework-side.

### 5. Derivation graph reassembles on every coalesced trace tick and `summarize` `pr-str`s every live value in full to keep 80 characters  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: perf] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph.cljs:535-538 (`:rf.xray/derivation-graph` inputs include `[:rf.xray/trace-buffer]`), :541-549 (`summarize-graph` on each recompute); derivation_graph_helpers.cljc:209-212 (`(pr-str v)` of the whole value, then `subs … 80`); trace_collector.cljs:260-272 (one `:rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer` per `next-tick` with any host activity); registry.cljs:1121-1124 (`(vec buffer)` copy per sync).
- What: with the Graph tab mounted in `:live` mode, every event-loop tick that saw a host trace re-derefs every cached subscription (`re-frame.subs.tooling/sub-cache-algebra-view`, `:value` = current deref) and serialises every node's `:value`/`:params`/`:query`/`:state` (`value-bearing-node-keys`, re-frame.derivation.egress:83-84) in full -- a 10k-entry sub value is printed end to end per tick to show its first 80 characters.
- Evidence: this settles the predecessor's cadence question: the trace-buffer write is task-coalesced (`compare-and-set!` + `next-tick`, rf2-wq6gx), so it is per tick, not per trace event; the graph sub is the consumer that re-derives on every such tick. Static mode is registry-only and cheap. Not measured.
- Action: bind `*print-length*`/`*print-level*` (or use a bounded printer) inside `summarize`; consider keying the static graph on a registry-change signal rather than the trace buffer. Both S.

### 6. "Show me when this changed" survives as a sub + event + walker with no renderer, so the embedding contract's `:path` focus is a no-op  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:138-147; app_db_diff_events.cljs:30-36; app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:600-686 (`path-touched?`, `path-exists?`, `op-at-path`, `event-of-epoch`, `epochs-touching-path`); focus.cljc:200-219 (spec 008 `:path` -> `[:rf.xray/focus-slice-path path]`).
- What: app_db_diff.cljs:6-7 says the affordance was dropped (rf2-okvit), yet spec 004 :763-783 describes it as the "high-leverage right-click affordance", spec 014 :410-423 and spec 008 :259 list it live, and a host that sends `:path` through `focus!` changes an app-db slot nobody reads.
- Evidence: Grep `show-me-when-this-changed-result` over `tools/xray/src` -> the reg-sub only; no `subscribe`/`rf.fresco/sub` of it anywhere (control: `:rf.xray/app-db-state` is sub'd at app_db_diff.cljs:221). Same sweep: `partition-reserved`/`triple-path`/`reserved-path?`/`reserved-app-db-keys` (helpers :75-105, :229-258) have no `src` caller either.
- Action: decide: delete the pair, the walker, the four orphaned helpers and the spec 004/014/008 rows (and drop `:path` from `focus!`), or build the list view spec 004 sketches. Either way the spec must stop promising it.

### 7. The 400 ms diff-flash is promised by the spec, defined as keyframes, and applied to nothing  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs:446-450 (`@keyframes rf-xray-diff-flash`); theme/tokens.cljc:709 (`:flash-duration-ms 400`); panels/app_db_diff.cljs:137 (comment: the keyed remount "replays the diff-flash CSS animation").
- What: spec 004 :31-32 and :394-396 promise a 400 ms yellow-to-transparent flash on touched slices with a reduced-motion variant; no element in `tools/xray/src` carries `animation … rf-xray-diff-flash`, so the keyframes are dead CSS and the remount replays nothing.
- Evidence: Grep `rf-xray-diff-flash` over `tools/xray/src` -> global_styles.cljs:446 only. Control: the sibling `rf-xray-fade-in` keyframe declared four lines later IS applied at shell.cljs:2782.
- Action: add the animation to the per-epoch keyed section (one style entry, `calc(400ms * var(--rf-xray-motion-scale, 1))` per the motion seam at global_styles.cljs:374-390), or delete the keyframes, the token and the two spec sentences.

### 8. The waterfall drops the producer's own zero-duration `:issued` phase, so every synthesised waterfall renders one bar  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/chart/timing_waterfall.cljc:77 (`(pos? ms)` filter), :128 (`:issued` colour branch); panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:427-430 and :445-448 (synthesise `[[:issued 0] [:elapsed N]]` for HTTP-without-native-timing, WebSocket, machine-invoke, SSR and flow); managed_fx_template.cljs:371 (`waterfall/render wire`).
- What: the producer and the renderer disagree about zero: the two-phase waterfall the helpers deliberately build ("the panel can always show today") collapses to a single `elapsed` row, and the dedicated `:issued` accent fill is unreachable. A genuine 0 ms phase (cached DNS, reused connection) will vanish the same way once native timing lands.
- Evidence: `normalise-phases-drops-non-positive` (timing_waterfall_cljs_test.cljc:43) pins the drop of `[:b 0]`; `render` then uses `(max 1 …)` for bar width (:168), so a zero-width bar was already handled.
- Action: keep `(and (number? ms) (>= ms 0))`, drop only negative/non-numeric; keep `slowest-phase` on `pos?`; update the one test.

### 9. Spec 021 §3/§4 and the reactive/app-db code disagree on five load-bearing sentences  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md :897-903, :909-915, :970-972, :990-993, :1128-1131, :866; code: implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:337, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs:244-263 and :320-363, :635-645, reactive_panel_view.cljs:331 and :396, app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:593-597.
- What: (a) §3.5 constraint 2 says `:rf.view/rendered` "carries no deref-subs list … spec'd, absent in the current build" -- the framework stamps `:rf.view/deref-subs` (views.cljs:337) and the panel's shared-sub edges are built from it; (b) §3.6 says a sub row jumps to App-db -- both node kinds open the editor; (c) §4.2 says every reserved area renders even when empty and shows a `SYSTEM-IDS` section -- rf2-jcdvo filters empties (pinned by the "no placeholder card" test) and no such area exists; (d) §4.7's changed-path-row navigation is not implemented; (e) §3.5's "seed-path resolution from the epoch's diff" reads `:rf/changed-paths`, which nothing in `implementation/*/src` stamps (grep -> 0; control: the same grep found `redacted-modified-paths-count`), so `:seed-paths` is always `[]` and is not rendered.
- Evidence: as cited; the spec side is right for (a) only in the sense that it is stale -- the code is right in every case.
- Action: one doc PR correcting the five sentences; delete `seed-paths` (reactive_panel_subs.cljs:635-645, :681).

## Spec drift by chapter
- tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md: DRIFTS. spec :31-32/:394-396 promise the 400 ms diff-flash; code applies no animation (finding 7); code is right to have none until wired. spec :398-427 promise `[fx :db]`/`[flow …]`/`[mixed]` path-origin chips read from `:writer` markers; no code (grep `path-origin|flow-writes|\[mixed\]` -> 0 in src; control: `redacted-modified` found the prune docstrings); code side is where the tree is, strike or file. spec :429-488, :552-560, :646-648 describe the clickable-segment popup as the panel's one gesture; nothing opens it and the real gestures are expand/collapse and zoom (rf2-h71e0) (finding 2). spec :544-550 promise the `:rf/machines` row jumps to the Machines tab with a soft cue; no code. spec :562-635 promise the redacted-paths-modified chip; pruned (finding 3). spec :763-783 promise the right-click "Show me when this changed"; no renderer (finding 6). spec :785-797 claim diff caching per `[frame-id epoch-id]`, head/tail slice virtualisation and a popup resolved against the LIVE db -- the caches were pruned (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:24-59), the inspector memo is per-mount by identity (edn_inspector.cljs:3330-3354), no head/tail virtualisation exists (grep `more entries|children-cap|max-entries|virtual` -> 0), and :793-797 contradicts :444-467 inside the same chapter (the popup sub at app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:98-103 follows the focused epoch, so :444-467 is the true half). spec :73-81 "every :diff-lens consumer (App-DB panel …) converts each row to `[path before after op]`" -- the App-DB `:diff` lens retired with rf2-vv3m6 (app_db_diff.cljs:107-115); `partition-reserved` has no caller. spec :803-807 empty-state prose differs from the rendered "app-db has no user-domain keys yet." (app_db_diff_state.cljs:446). MATCHES on: diff semantics :83-116, empty-collection/set/vector engine rules :130-336 (read against engine.cljc in full), removed-slot rendering :338-384, the reserved-keys table :513-519 vs `runtime-areas`, the local-render egress contract :671-761 vs local_render.cljc + app_db_diff_subs.cljs:296-312 (including "reveal not wired": `raw?` is never passed true).
- tools/xray/spec/025-Derivation-Graph-Panel.md: MATCHES. Checked the five-family contributor map (:116-161 vs derivation_graph.cljs:113-135 incl. `:selector-targets`), the two modes and their sources (:72-101 vs :486-493), the section order (:103-114 vs `panel-tree`), the registry table (:274-292 vs `install!`/`install-test-overrides!`), and the egress delegate (:179-272 vs helpers :262-274).
- tools/xray/spec/026-Module-View-Panel.md: MATCHES. Checked the single FRAMES section, the demand-gated caption, the `:rf.xray/image-view` sub, the seam names (§8.3/§8.4 vs image_view_reads.cljs), and that requiring `re-frame.live-frame`/`re-frame.image`/`re-frame.image-assembly`/`re-frame.trace` directly is ruled in §8.4 (so not a Tool-Pair crossing); `image-view-frames` exists (live_frame.cljc:259). One nit: §2's `caps` line and `frame-row`'s `capabilities` branch are both dead since EP-0026 removed `:rf.frame/capabilities` (image_view_helpers.cljc:148-150).
- tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §3 and §4: DRIFTS (finding 9). Remainder of 021: NOT READ.

description:
# Senior review: schemas-flows

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has shipped a malli/spec/zod-class validation integration (dev/prod elision, pluggable validator, stable schema digest) and a derived-state/dataflow layer with a dependency graph.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/schemas/src (schemas.cljc, schemas/{cache,malli,digest,validator,storage,walker,validate}.cljc — 4082 lines, all in full); implementation/flows/src (flows.cljc, flows/{registry,topo,tooling}.cljc — 1826 lines, all in full). Tests skimmed: both late_bind_missing_test.clj, schemas/digest_parity_fixtures.cljc, plus greps over the rest of both test trees (46 schemas test files, 34 flows test files) for what is and is not pinned. Cross-checked consumers outside the slice only where a finding needed them: core/late_bind.cljc (get-fn-cached), core/fx.cljc (reserved :rf.fx/reg-flow / clear-flow bodies), core/trace.cljc + trace/tooling.cljc (listener isolation), core/identity.cljc (canonical-bytes domain), core/frame.cljc (frame-slot-value), ssr/hydrate.cljc + ssr.cljc (digest consumer), epoch/assembly.cljc (digest consumer).
Owning specs consulted: spec/010-Schemas.md (whole), spec/013-Flows.md (whole), spec/Ownership.md rows 54 and 60.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Schema digest is neither process-stable nor cross-host-stable for any schema carrying a function, and diverges JVM↔CLJS on whole-number doubles  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:103-119 (`compute-edn-print` — `pr-str` over the canonicalised form) and :82-101 (`canonicalise-schema-form` passes every non-collection through unchanged); implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/digest.cljc:93-97 (`digest-line` hashes `run-printer`'s bytes).
- What: the per-schema serialisation step is `pr-str`, so a Malli schema that contains a predicate fn (`[:map [:n pos-int?]]`, `[:fn pred]`, `[:and :int [:fn …]]`) prints with the JVM's per-process identity hash, and a props map carrying `1.0` prints as `1.0` on the JVM and `1` on CLJS — which makes the digest change when nothing semantic did, and makes the two consumers that compare digests across processes/hosts fire falsely.
- Evidence: ran `clojure -M -e '(pr-str pos-int?)'` from the scratchpad → `#object[clojure.core$pos_int_QMARK_ 0x4c6daf0 "clojure.core$pos_int_QMARK_@4c6daf0"]` (identity hash; differs every JVM start); `(pr-str 1.0)` → `1.0` on the JVM, where CLJS prints `1` (JS numbers). Spec 010:495 requires the digest to be "cross-runtime reproducible … byte-for-byte" and :512 "equal iff their {path → schema-value} maps serialise byte-for-byte identically"; spec 010:501 itself prescribes `pr-str` for the CLJS reference's default. Consumers that compare across a process or host boundary: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:568-576 emits `:rf.ssr/schema-digest-mismatch` with reason "Deploy drift — server and client are running different schema sets" (a JVM ring server vs a CLJS client will disagree on EVERY hydrate for such a schema set), and implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:92-109 feeds the epoch-restore schema-mismatch trace (a JVM restart between record and restore reads as drift). The tree already knows `pr-str` is not a cross-host identity — digest.cljc:78-92 moved the PATH key off `pr-str` onto CEDN-1 `canonical-bytes` for exactly this reason — but the schema VALUE still goes through it. `canonical-bytes` is not a drop-in for the value: implementation/core/src/re_frame/identity.cljc:245-258 and :359 reject floats and fns outright (throw), so routing schema values through it would turn every such registration into a digest-time throw. Control on the test corpus: schemas/test/re_frame/schemas/digest_parity_fixtures.cljc pins only keyword / vector / props(int,string,bool) forms — no fn, no double — so the parity gate passes while this is live (Grep `pos-int\?|int\?|\(fn |:fn ` over the fixtures: 2 hits, both in the harness helper, none in a schema). The repo's own on-ramp invites the shape: docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:126 recommends `[:fn pred]`; testbeds/schema_violation/core.cljs:92 and tools/xray/testbeds/standard_epochs/core.cljs:471 use `pos-int?` in schemas (event schemas there, but the same idiom on an app schema hits the digest).
- Action: decide: (A) make the printer stable per host — in `canonicalise-schema-form` map a `fn?` value to a stable token (JVM `(.getName (class f))`, CLJS `(.-name f)`, falling back to a constant `#fn`) and print doubles via a fixed-format encoder (e.g. the CEDN-1 rule: integer-valued doubles print as integers) — then add two parity fixtures (a `pos-int?`-bearing map, a `{:min 1.0}` props map) so the gate pins it; cross-host fn digests still differ under `:advanced` name munging, so also (B) emit a once-per-process dev warning at `reg-app-schema` when the schema contains a fn, naming the consequence ("digest is host/process-specific; the SSR and epoch digest checks will report drift"). (A)+(B) is ~25 lines; (B) alone is the trust-the-programmer minimum and still worth doing, because today the false "Deploy drift" warning sends the reader to compare bundles that are identical.

### 2. The sensitivity walker cannot see a Malli local `{:registry …}` and does not fail closed on it, so `:sensitive?` slots declared inside one leak verbatim on a validation failure  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:226-232 (`walk-flags` reads the props map only for the flag key; a `:registry` value is never descended), :511-516 and :540-555 (`opacity-child-schemas` classifies `:schema` / `:map` / `:and` … as fully walkable, so `schema-has-opaque-child?` answers false), :821-822 and :1150-1157 (`align-in-path` falls back on the `:schema` wrapper and `schema-sensitive-at?` then tests only the leftover and the consumed prefix — both empty of declarations).
- What: a vector-form schema such as `[:schema {:registry {::user [:map [:pw {:sensitive? true} :string]]}} ::user]` (Malli's documented idiom for local/recursive schemas; the same holds for `[:map {:registry …} [:u ::user]]`) walks to `{}` for both flags, is classified NOT opaque, and so every value-bearing slot (`:value` / `:explain` / `:explain-humanized`) of a failure at `[:pw]` ships the secret verbatim, with no `:sensitive?` stamp and no `:rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque` nudge at registration.
- Evidence: traced end to end — `walk-flags`: op `:schema`, `schema-properties` = `{:registry …}`, `declaration-from-properties :sensitive?` → nil, children `[::user]` → keyword → acc `{}`; `schema-has-opaque-child?` → `schema-opaque?` false, `opacity-child-schemas` → `:schema` ∈ `opacity-bare-ops` → children `[::user]` → `opaque-nested-tail?` keyword → false; `schema-sensitive-at?` with Malli's `:in [:pw]` → `align-in-path` hits `:else` → `[:fallback schema []]` → `schema-has-sensitive?` false, `opaque-nested-tail?` false, no ancestor declaration → false; `whole-sensitive?` (nil path) → false. Spec 010:439 promises "Compiled / opaque schemas fail closed" so that the "register the vector form so per-slot flags are visible" nudge is never a silent privacy hole — this IS the vector form and it is still a hole. The documented tradeoff (walker.cljc:14-16, spec 010:439) covers bare keyword registry refs (indistinguishable from primitives) — it does not cover a registry that is sitting in the schema's own props as plain data. Control: Grep `:registry` over implementation/schemas (src + test) → 0 hits; Grep `:sensitive\? true` over implementation/schemas/test → 218 hits in 13 files, so the walker's sensitivity surface is heavily pinned and this shape is simply absent from it.
- Action: fail closed, matching the existing posture — in `opacity-child-schemas` return `::opaque` when `(contains? (schema-properties schema) :registry)` (so both the redaction and the registration warning treat a local registry as unintrospectable; ~3 lines), and add `:local-registry` to `maybe-warn-walker-opaque!`'s `:schema-kind` so the nudge names the cause. Walking the registry values instead is not worth it: a registry entry's app-db path depends on where it is referenced, and over-redaction is the documented acceptable direction. Pin with one test in schemas_sensitive_test (a `{:registry …}` schema failing at a sensitive slot must redact `:value`).

### 3. A malformed flow `:schema` masquerades as a value failure on every recompute, because the boundary seam erases the malformed/failed distinction the dev seam keeps  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:116-128 and :143-145 (`validate-output!`); implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1295-1317 (`validate-with-registered-fn` coerces a validator throw to `false`) and :1319-1330 (`explain-with-registered-fn` coerces the same throw to `nil`).
- What: a flow registered with a structurally bad schema (`:schema [:vector]`, an unknown op, a `:schema nil` under the default Malli validator) emits `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :flow-output` with `:explain nil` and the reason "Flow :x output failed schema [:vector]." on every drain that recomputes it — telling the programmer their VALUE is wrong when their SCHEMA is, with no explanation to disagree with.
- Evidence: `validate-with-registered-fn` `(catch … false)`; `explain-with-registered-fn` `(catch … nil)`; `validate-output!` branches only on `valid?` and builds its reason from `(pr-str schema)`. The dev-time seam does this right for event/fx/sub/app-db: validate.cljc:600-614 `validate-entry-result` returns `[:malformed ex]` and :713-735 / :914-944 emit the distinct `:rf.error/malformed-schema` with the validator's message, which spec 010:100 requires "so the throw can never masquerade as a clean validate". Spec 013:364-378 routes flows through the boundary seam deliberately (optional artefact), so this is the seam's contract shape rather than a flows bug. Control: Grep `malformed` over implementation/flows/test → 15 hits, all registration-shape / opts / classification-mark tests (flows_test.clj:382-767, flows_direct_clear_settle_cljs_test.cljc:268-298, flows_topo_test.clj:35); none exercises a malformed flow `:schema`, so the masquerade is unpinned. The same seam serves machine `[:schemas :data]` and `:sub-override` (out of slice) — the fix below covers them for free.
- Action: publish one more seam beside the two, `:schemas/validate-entry-result` → `validate-entry-result` (already private, returns `true` / `false` / `[:malformed ex]`), have `validate-output!` prefer it when bound and emit `:rf.error/malformed-schema` (with the validator's message and the flow's structural tags) on the vector case. ~15 lines; the boundary seam's existing true/false contract stays for `re-frame.spec`.

### 4. Spec 010 promises a "different source coords" warning on app-schema re-registration; nothing emits one  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:613-623 (re-registration path: swap, then only `:rf.schema/violation` when the LIVE VALUE fails); spec/010-Schemas.md:141.
- What: spec 010 §Multiple schemas at the same path says "Tooling warns when the new source coords differ from the previous registration — a same-form re-register (hot reload) is benign; a different-source re-register at the same path is probably a bug", and the storage layer emits no trace for a replacement at all (neither `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` nor anything else), so two feature modules registering `[:auth]` from different files silently last-write-wins.
- Evidence: read `reg-app-schema` end to end — the only re-registration diagnostics are `maybe-warn-validator-unavailable!`, `maybe-warn-walker-opaque!`, `maybe-emit-schema-violation!`; the prior entry's source coords (`:ns`/`:file`/`:line`, stamped at :603-605) are never compared. Control: Grep `handler-replaced` over `{schemas,flows}/src/**/*.cljc` → schemas 0, flows 3 (registry.cljc:717-745 emits `:rf.registry/handler-replaced {:kind :flow …}` on a shape change, deduped per frame slot) — so the flows sibling implements exactly the pattern the schemas spec promises.
- Action: decide: (A) mirror the flows shape — in `reg-app-schema`, when `prior-known?` and the coords-stripped shape or the `:file`/`:ns` differ, emit `:rf.registry/handler-replaced {:kind :app-schema :id path :frame frame-id :different-source? …}` inside the existing `debug-enabled?` block (~10 lines), or (B) strike the sentence from spec 010:141. (A) is cheap and is the diagnostic that would have caught the feature-module collision the spec is worried about.

### 5. Late-bound seam census for the sibling's failure class: every schemas seam reachable from a callback or commit path fails SOFT and matches spec 010; the one loud/soft asymmetry is `[:rf.fx/reg-flow …]` vs `rf/reg-flow`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:53-64 (default validator soft-passes when `:schemas/malli-validate` is unbound); implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:116-118 and :130-148 (`:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn` / `:schemas/explain-with-registered-fn` / `:schemas/redact-validation-tags` — nil → pass / nil-explain / tags verbatim); implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:943-952 and :954-962 with :428-444 (reserved `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` bodies — out of slice, cited because it is the asymmetry).
- What: unlike the http reviewer's `classify-decoded` (fails loud with `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing` inside an async callback), no schemas seam consumed from a commit path or callback throws on an absent artefact: the router's `:schemas/validate-app-schema!` / `validate-event!` / `validate-fx!` / `validate-sub!` are nil-skipped, the flows output validator soft-passes, the redaction seam passes tags through (safe, because with no validator there is no failure trace to redact), `:schemas/app-schemas-digest` answers nil to SSR/epoch which suppress their compare. That is spec 010 claim 4 (recommended soft-pass) and spec 013:366 ("an app that omits the schemas artefact … pays nothing"). The ONLY loud schemas seam is the `rf/reg-app-schema` façade macro (`:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing`, pinned in schemas/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:50-80), which is synchronous registration, never a callback — so this slice carries no http-class hazard. The asymmetry worth a decision is on the flows side: `rf/reg-flow` fails loud (`:rf.error/flows-artefact-missing`, flows/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:50-78) while the reserved effect `[:rf.fx/reg-flow …]` silently no-ops when the flows artefact is absent AND still gets a uniform `:rf.fx/handled` trace from `handle-one-fx` — the same registration, two doors, one of which reports success for work it did not do.
- Evidence: fx.cljc:945 `(when-let [f (rf.late-bind/get-fn :flows/reg-flow)] …)` and :421-422 "When a hook is unregistered … the body-fn is a no-op"; flows.cljc:155 `true` on nil validate hook; validator.cljc:62-64. `get-fn-cached` (core/late_bind.cljc:153-178) does not cache nil, so a later-loaded schemas artefact is picked up by the flows validator — no stale-nil hazard.
- Action: decide: leave the reserved-fx posture as documented ("matching every other frame-scoped reserved fx"), or emit a once-per-process dev warning from the reserved body when the hook is unbound (`:rf.warning/flows-artefact-missing`, ~6 lines in core/fx.cljc — outside this slice; file it against core if wanted). No change is needed in schemas or flows for the sibling's class.

## Considered, left alone
- flows.cljc:337-371 — the `:output-write` `try` is wider than the install: it also wraps `pass-set-flow-last-inputs!`, the `:rf.flow/computed` emit and `validate-output!`, so a throw from any of those would be reported as "re-frame could not install that value … do not go looking in the :derive fn" (spec 013:307 claims the two phases are discriminated purely structurally). No measured route reaches it — per-listener throws are swallowed at core/trace/tooling.cljc:1012-1014, the validator/explainer seams catch, `elide-wire-value` only throws on bad opt keys — so left alone; narrowing the `try` to the `assoc-in` is a 10-line tidy if the phase claim is ever pinned.
- walker.cljc:475 vs :573 — a ROOT fn schema (`(reg-app-schema [:n] pos-int?)`) is `schema-opaque?` (fires the walker-opaque warning, fail-closed redaction on every failure) while the same fn NESTED is provably flag-free; a root fn has no enclosing entry either, so it is flag-free too. Over-redaction is the documented acceptable direction; one-token fix (`(fn? schema)` in `schema-opaque?`) if the warning annoys anyone.
- storage.cljc:512-520 — `maybe-emit-schema-violation!` reads `frame-app-db-value`, which is nil for an unknown/destroyed frame (core/frame.cljc:1645-1654), so a hot-reload re-registration against a not-yet-allocated frame (Story registers pre-allocation by design, storage.cljc:310-312) validates `nil` and can emit a spurious `:rf.schema/violation {:mismatching-value nil}`. Dev-only trace, indistinguishable from the spec'd "slot not seeded yet" case; guard on `frame-incarnation-token` if Story reports the noise.
- topo.cljc:108-168 + registry `run-flows-on-db*` — the dependency graph is rebuilt (O(n²·k) `rf.path/prefix?`, each normalising both paths) on every drain of every frame. Spec 013:250 sanctions the unmemoised sort explicitly at "a handful of flows"; no hot path measured.
- spec/010-Schemas.md:117 still says the bulk form's `:frame` default "is `(current-frame-id)`" while :100/:447 and the code require an explicit frame or a carried scope (`require-current-frame!`, storage.cljc:48-49). Doc-only; fold into whichever spec edit lands first.

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C … rev-parse --short HEAD` → d89a41e057.
- Read tool, every source file of both artefacts in full (schemas 4082 lines, flows 1826 lines); spec 010 and 013 in full via two paged reads each.
- Bash `clojure -M -e` (read-only, no test lane) from the scratchpad: `(pr-str pos-int?)` → identity-hashed `#object[…]`, `(pr-str 1.0)` → `1.0`; the CLJS half (`1`) is by JS number printing, not run here — a `{[:x] [:double {:min 1.0}]}` parity fixture would pin it.
- Grep `pos-int\?|int\?|\(fn |:fn ` over digest_parity_fixtures.cljc → 2 hits, both harness `(fn [` helpers, zero inside a fixture schema (control: the same pattern over the repo's testbeds/how-to → 83 hits in 32 files, including `pos-int?` schemas at testbeds/schema_violation/core.cljs:92).
- Grep `:registry` over implementation/schemas (src+test) → 0; control `:sensitive\? true` over implementation/schemas/test → 218 hits / 13 files.

title: review(core-reactive): senior-developer findings, 5 ranked, trunk d89a41e057 (2026-09-16)
description:
# Senior review: core-reactive

Reviewer persona: senior engineer on reactive/signal runtimes (Reagent / MobX / Solid class) — derivation graphs, glitch-freedom, memo correctness, cache invalidation, ref-count teardown.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/core/src/re_frame/ subs.cljc (2669, full), subs/{memo,cache,tooling,override_schema}.cljc (1913), substrate/{spine.cljs (4482, full), adapter.cljc, plain_atom.cljc, atom_container.cljc} (1588), derivation/{graph,node,egress}.cljc (1391), views.cljs + views/* (1993), adapter/{context,use_frame,sub_override_context}.cljs (611), core_reg_view_macro.cljc (294). ~14.4K lines. Tests skimmed: sub_cache_test.clj (deftest roster), sub_dispose_trace_test.clj, sub_arg_fragmentation_warn_test.clj (full), adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/sub_dispose_view_cljs_test.cljs (full), spine_dispose_cljs_test.cljs (roster). Also read: stock Reagent 2.0.1 `ratom.cljs` `dispose!` (from the local Maven jar) and reagent-slim `reagent2/ratom.cljs` `dispose!`.
Owning specs consulted: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §Host value model / §Value-keyed cache-key contract (870-891), §Cache shape, §Lookup algorithm, §Invalidation algorithm, §Subscription input producers (1027-1106), §Reference counting and disposal + §Disposal guarantees (1108-1156), §Render-phase provisional acquisition (1157-1172), §subscribe-once / §unsubscribe (1174-1230), §Lifetime contract (1232-1248), §Adapter disposal lifecycle (314-383), §What happens when a sub references an unknown sub (1719-1737), §Sub-cache wiring (Reagent realisation) (1856-1925); spec/002-Frames.md §Subscriptions composing (1548-1569); spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue rows for `:rf.error/sub-cycle` (1998) and `:rf.warning/sub-arg-cache-fragmentation` (2083); spec/API.md rows 200-202; spec/Ownership.md rows 26-31, 43-46.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The cache-fragmentation guardrail warns about a hazard the cache cannot have  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness (of a diagnostic) + spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:621-762 (block comment, `fragmenting-arg-state`, `maybe-warn-fragmenting-arg!`), call site :1682; spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2083; docs/core/subscriptions.md:125-134; implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_arg_fragmentation_warn_test.clj:2-20, 98-159.
- What: The dev warning `:rf.warning/sub-arg-cache-fragmentation` fires exactly when a query-vector arg is `=` to the previous one but not `identical?`, and its hint says "The sub-cache keys by identity, so every render mints a NEW cache entry: the cache grows unbounded" — but the sub-cache is a persistent map (`:sub-cache (atom {})`, frame.cljc:2510) keyed by the query vector under `=`, so an `=`-equal fresh map/vector arg is a cache HIT, not a new slot; the warning can never correspond to real fragmentation, and the only args that DO fragment (fresh closures, JS objects — not `=` to anything) are the ones the heuristic deliberately never flags (subs.cljc:651-654, 713-714).
- Evidence: Spec 006 §Value-keyed cache-key contract (lines 874-876) states the opposite of the warning verbatim: "Two subscriptions whose query vectors are `rf=` — regardless of allocation identity … resolve to one cache entry", and names CLJS's persistent-map keying as the reference mechanism (880). The code's own comment conflates the two ("keys … by query-vector identity (`=`)", :623), as does the Spec 009 row and the test docstring. The test pins only that the warning fires; it never counts cache entries (control: grep `equal|dedup|distinct|one entry` over sub_cache_test.clj → 0 while `ref-count` → 20+ hits, so no test in the slice asserts either way). Also a false positive by construction: two components each holding a hoisted-but-distinct `{:filter :a}` alternate renders → warn, one slot. Cost paid per subscribe in dev: a `swap!` plus a full `=` walk of the arg, and the last arg per sub-id retained for the process lifetime.
- Action: Delete the guardrail (the two fns, the `defonce`, the late-bind enrolment at :691-697, the call at :1682), its test file, the Spec 009 row, and the "rookie mistake" paragraph in docs/core/subscriptions.md:125-134; replace the paragraph with one sentence stating the cache is value-keyed so inline `=`-equal args are fine and only non-`=` args (closures) miss. Under "trust the programmer" this is a nagging diagnostic that is also wrong — the AI reading the docs today learns a false model and hoists args for nothing.

### 2. On the Reagent adapter, a real component unmount emits NO `:rf.sub/dispose` — the trace stream's "dispose" half is silent on the default substrate  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift + test-gap]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1459-1484 (the on-dispose closure: releases inputs + identity-guarded `dissoc`, no emit); subs/cache.cljc:137-144 (`emit-dispose!` is reachable only from `dispose-entry-now!`, `invalidate-frame-subs!`, `clear-sub-cache!`, `dispose-all-for-frame-destroy!`); stock Reagent 2.0.1 `reagent/ratom.cljs:481-494` and reagent-slim `reagent2/ratom.cljs:436-460` (`dispose!` removes watches BEFORE firing on-dispose callbacks); spine.cljs:1706-1767.
- What: The production teardown path for every `reg-view` component on Reagent is: render reaction disposed → its watch on the sub Reaction removed → the sub Reaction auto-disposes (`-remove-watch`, slim ratom.cljs:314-320) → `dispose!` first removes ITS watches on its inputs (so each input auto-disposes and its slot is dissoc'd by its own callback, no emit) → then the parent's callback runs `release-input-ref!` against already-absent slots (identity guard → no-op) and dissoc's its own slot, no emit. Zero `:rf.sub/dispose` events for parent or inputs. Spec 006 §Reference counting (1114) and §Disposal guarantees (1140) promise the emit "at the eviction site", and Spec 009 makes dispose the fourth leg of the created/run/skip/dispose lifecycle Xray reads.
- Evidence: The Reagent-adapter test file stands its "view-unmount" up with explicit `rf/unsubscribe` (sub_dispose_view_cljs_test.cljs:85-89, 115, 180, 240) and, in the rf2-b2bxk "reaction-disposal" test, derefs the reaction OUTSIDE a reactive context (so it watches nothing) and then says outright "no emit for the parent on this path" (:327-330); the input emits it asserts exist only because that reaction held no watches. No test mounts a real component (or drops a watcher on an outer reaction) and asserts the emit. Second silent site: the spine's adapter-teardown walk `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` disposes BEFORE `reset!` (spine.cljs:1762-1766) and emits nothing, so under UIx teardown inputs emit a misleading `:no-more-derefers` via the cascade and parents emit nothing — the rf2-awhtpc double-emit reasoning that made `clear-sub-cache!` reset-first (cache.cljc:473-496) was not applied here.
- Action: (a) In the on-dispose closure (subs.cljc:1481-1484) emit `:rf.sub/dispose` with `:no-more-derefers` iff the identity-guarded `dissoc` actually removed the slot — every cache-driven eviction site removes the slot BEFORE disposing, so this cannot double-emit there, and it makes Reagent's auto-dispose path emit for parents and inputs alike. (b) Make `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` take its snapshot with `reset-vals!` first and emit `:cache-clear` per key (mirror `clear-sub-cache!`, keeping the injected disposer). (c) One CLJS test on the Reagent adapter: outer reaction with a watcher derefs the sub, `remove-watch` the outer, assert the emits.

### 3. `:ref-count` is a render counter on Reagent, but tooling reports it as the live reader count  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1799-1810 (hit path bumps on every `subscribe`); subs/tooling.cljc:179, 447-449 (`sub-cache-snapshot` / `sub-cache-algebra-view` document `:ref-count` as "the live consumer ref-count … the lifecycle evidence the entry is kept alive by its readers").
- What: A Reagent component body calls `subscribe` on every render (the `@(rf/subscribe …)` idiom; `build-frame-aware-view` at views.cljs:534-679 wraps the render and pairs no `unsubscribe`, and the adapter never decrements), so after N re-renders the slot reads `:ref-count N` while exactly one reader exists; eviction there is driven by Reagent's watcher count, not this integer. On the React-hook spine the count is exact (balanced round trips, spine.cljs:3225-3230). Xray shows the number.
- Evidence: grep `unsubscribe|ref-count` over adapters/reagent/src → 0 (control: `make-reaction|add-on-dispose` in the same file → 6 lines); grep `unsubscribe|dispose-entry|subs.cache` over core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs → 0 (control: `add-on-dispose` → 3). Spec 006 §Per-host notes (1259) already concedes "Reagent's Reaction handles … ref-counting" itself.
- Action: decide: A) label it honestly in the two tooling docstrings and Xray ("subscribe calls since materialisation; reader count only on the React-hook substrates") — one-line change; or B) leave the number and accept that it means nothing on the default adapter. No runtime change is warranted; nothing evicts on it there.

### 4. `(unsubscribe query-v {:frame f})` is a silent no-op that leaks the reference — and a test pins the silence  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics (fail-open)]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2502-2520; frame.cljc:211-223 (`frame-target->id` returns a non-frame value UNCHANGED); implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_cache_test.clj:346-372 (`unsubscribe-did-NOT-gain-an-opts-map-form`); spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1209-1218; spec/API.md:202.
- What: `subscribe`'s explicit-frame form is `[query-v opts]` while `unsubscribe`'s is `[frame-id query-v]` (ruled, rf2-bfadc6 / rf2-csbbwu). Writing the subscribe shape for the teardown — the shape an AI copies from the row directly above it in API.md — resolves `[:v]` as a frame id, `(rf.frame/frame [:v])` is nil, and the call returns nil having released nothing. The test asserts exactly that the live entry survives.
- Evidence: Traced end to end through `frame-target->id` (a vector is neither a keyword nor a frame value, so it passes through) and the `when-let` at :2516. The spec's justification ("never a hot in-view call an author reaches for by muscle-memory") does not cover a code-generating reader; the spec's "missing frame is not an error" (1225) is about a destroyed frame, not a call-shape error.
- Action: decide: A) keep the ruled frame-first shape but refuse a first arg that is a vector (a query-vector shape can never be a frame target) with a thrown `:rf.error/*` naming `(unsubscribe frame-id query-v)` — five lines, fail-closed, no new arity; or B) keep the silence as ruled. A costs nothing on the correct path and turns a leak into a loud call-site error.

### 5. Spec 006's Reagent-realisation pseudocode delivers a single static input as a scalar, contradicting the normative delivery rule and the code  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1895-1901 vs :1035-1042; implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1405-1411; subs/memo.cljc:683-686.
- What: The illustrative `compute-and-cache` block reads `:static (case (count inputs) 0 nil 1 @(first inputs) (mapv deref inputs))` — zero inputs → `nil`, one input → the bare value — while §Subscription input producers says a declared list "arrives as a vector, at every count" (ruled rf2-kuky.45) and the code hands `[v0]` / `[]`. The block is the section a non-CLJS implementor is told to port from.
- Evidence: Read both spec sections and both memo wrappers; `make-layer-n-single-input-memoised-body` passes `[v0]` as `body-arg`.
- Action: Replace the `case` with `(mapv deref inputs)` for the `:static` arm (and drop the `:parametric` duplicate — same arm). Spec-only edit; the code is right.

## Considered, left alone
- Unknown-sub recovery reaction (subs.cljc:1198-1241, 1578) has no inputs, so a component that subscribed before a lazy-loaded `reg-sub` stays `nil` until something else re-renders it; Spec 006 §unknown sub (1737) rules "observed by the next subscribe", and re-checking the registrar would add a mechanism.
- `maybe-validate-sub!`'s `(catch _ true)` (memo.cljc:113-114) looks fail-open but is dead for the registered validator: `run-validation` (schemas/validate.cljc:616-661) catches a throwing schema itself, emits `:rf.error/malformed-schema`, and returns false.
- `:rf.error/sub-cycle` is diagnostic-only and the subscribe path hands back a never-cached nil reaction (subs.cljc:1567-1578) — Spec 009 row 1998 rules it diagnostic like `:rf.error/flow-cycle`; consistent.
- `compute-sub` on a `:frame-state` sub given a bare app-db map passes the bare map through as the whole frame-state (subs.cljc:2010-2017); test-only surface, documented arity.
- `acquire-cache-reaction!`, `*acquire-recovery*`, `*disposal-cause*` retained at zero callers — ruled rf2-63t1i (subs.cljc:2341-2354, cache.cljc:92-125); not re-litigated.

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C … rev-parse --short HEAD` → d89a41e057.
- Grep (ripgrep) `sub-arg-cache-fragmentation|fragmenting-arg` repo-wide → 4 files (src, test, Spec 009, docs); control: the src file itself is among them.
- Grep `:sub-cache\s+\(atom` in core/src → frame.cljc:2510 `(atom {})`.
- Grep `equal|dedup|distinct|same slot|one entry|one cache` (-i) in sub_cache_test.clj → 0; control on the same file: `ref-count` → 20+ lines, `deftest` → 38 rows.
- Grep `unsubscribe|ref-count` in adapters/reagent/src → 0; control: `make-reaction|add-on-dispose|auto-run` in adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs → 6+ lines.
- Grep `unsubscribe|dispose-entry|subs.cache` in core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs → 0; control: `add-on-dispose` → 3 occurrences.
- Grep `no-more-derefers|rf\.sub/dispose` under implementation/adapters → hits only in adapters/reagent/test (the file read in full for finding 2).
- Grep `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` under implementation → 5 files (spine src, spine dispose test, live_frame comment, test-react and reagent-slim walk tests); `rf.sub/dispose|emit` in the reagent-slim walk test → 0 (control: `deftest` → 3).
- Grep `clear-all-frame-sub-caches!` → 3 files (defined in cache.cljc, called by test-react); plain-atom's `dispose-adapter!` is a no-op, which Spec 006:383 permits for headless.
- `unzip -p ~/.m2/repository/reagent/reagent/2.0.1/reagent-2.0.1.jar reagent/ratom.cljs | grep -n -A 16 "dispose! \[this\]"` → watches removed at :488-489 before on-dispose at :490-494; reagent-slim `reagent2/ratom.cljs:436-460` same order.
- Grep `defn frame-target->id` in frame.cljc → :211-223, non-frame values returned unchanged.
- Grep `defn validate-sub!` / `run-validation` in implementation/schemas → validate.cljc:1192, :616 (read for the left-alone item).
- No `clojure -M:test` run was used; no shadow-cljs, no browser, no writes outside this file.
notes: CROSS-REFERENCE (recorded 2026-09-16 by the worker in Mike's session): finding 2 here (a real Reagent unmount emits no :rf.sub/dispose) and finding 3 (:ref-count is a render counter on Reagent) are the SAME MECHANISM the adapters review rated HIGH as its finding 1 on rf2-pk4i6.12: ratom substrates retire sub-cache slots through watcher auto-dispose, bypassing the ref-count / dispose path spec 006 and the tooling describe; Reagent and reagent-slim share it identically, UIx takes the spec path, so the three adapters disagree on what :ref-count and the dispose trace mean. description:
RULING (Mike, in chat 2026-09-15: "rule a"). The follow-up to the rf2-ia2if visual-review experiment (PR #9835) is option (a): a documented recipe. The rejected options were (b), a story:visual npm script; (c), nothing; and (d), a nightly-gated sample.

WHAT TO BUILD

1. docs/story/08-snapshot-identity-and-sharing.md: a recipe section for local visual review.
   - The runner is Playwright toHaveScreenshot over the :test-tagged variants.
   - Each case is keyed by snapshot identity: variant id plus theme, viewport and browser.
   - The sample script and config are trimmed from tools/story/spec/findings/parity-2026-09/fable/visual-review.pw.cjs and visual-review.config.cjs.
   - Baselines stay out of the repository. Not in CI.
   - It carries the three measured lessons:
     (i) Never skip a capture because the content hash is unchanged. A CSS-only change diffed 10/10 while the hashes stayed unchanged.
     (ii) Pin threshold 0. Playwright's default 0.2 missed PR #9827's heading colour change (0/10). Threshold 0 caught 10/10, with 0 false diffs over 130 comparisons.
     (iii) Approve new baselines only with -u.
   - No gate runs the sample, so the recipe names the Story hooks it depends on: dev-build globals, Story's DOM test hooks, the share-URL variant and modes params, and the help overlay's localStorage key.
   - Chapter 08 already says Story hands the pixel service a stable key. The recipe completes that thought.

2. tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md, in the :rf.assert/visual-snapshot paragraph (about :2991-3001).
   - Replace "A local capture-and-compare experiment is rf2-ia2if" with the settled position.

- The trimmed sample runs as written against the login-form dev server.

title: Repair Resources tutorial as one runnable authenticated app and test path
description:
The Resources tutorial does not currently describe one application that a new consumer can build and test through all five chapters. Repair the existing guide as a coherent path; no new Resources API or implicit cache-scope rule is needed.

Verified against research pin 22b2e9951979fb87271f6f2304e628d5aceea454 and current f680007c6b7dcb63cf4dd4bdd7b39f83d8c4c9d4. All 160 source files in the research manifest remained unchanged at final validation.

Concrete defects:

1. docs/resources/tutorial/02-server-data.md:19-26 instructs adding both Resources and managed HTTP, but the dependency map omits day8/re-frame2-http. The namespace at line 60 requires re-frame.http.managed. A detached consumer with exactly the shown dependencies fails to require it; adding only the HTTP artifact succeeds. Preserve the compiler and development alias from setup when showing additive dependency changes, and show the registration namespaces' boot-loading path.
2. Parts 2 and 4 leave article/list/detail reads global after introducing authentication; Part 4 populates the global detail from an authenticated favorite reply. Anonymous readability does not imply viewer-invariant favorited/following/content visibility. Use the reference Conduit's viewer resolver and correct transition/replan/clear behavior when adding auth. Do not classify the correctly scoped reference implementation as broken. A separate deliberately global browser registration reproduced reuse of a prior viewer's synthetic marker after switching to Bob, with no second request.
3. Part 5 says the earlier registration namespaces contain no browser code and can be renamed to .cljc. Part 3 contains unguarded js/globalThis and js/JSON interop. An isolated literal interop form fails JVM compilation with "No such namespace: js". Part 5 also tests :auth/flow, :auth/state and :auth/error machinery not constructed in Part 3, which teaches direct auth handlers. Make the tests exercise the application actually taught, on their stated target, including the view test's namespace/target.
4. The tutorial's .io API base differs from the current official .show API. Provide a concrete local-demo route as well as current hosted configuration. This finding does not assert the old endpoint's live availability.

Acceptance: from a clean consumer, follow the revised setup through a read, refresh failure, authenticated viewer change and favorite mutation, then run the tests taught for that same app. Record every necessary dependency/require, visible state and command outcome. A docs-site build alone cannot establish snippet compilation or runtime behavior. Keep the repair focused on continuity and current idioms rather than converting every small editorial issue into a separate task.

Evidence in the mayor checkout: ai/findings/Resources/astra/report.md and sibling-review.md; evidence/consumer-literal-re-frame2-1.log (exit 1), consumer-repaired-re-frame2-1.log (exit 0), facade-portability-re-frame2-1.log (exit 0 for asserted counterexample), scope-counterexample.json, and local-source-manifest.json. title: spec + SSR test still register the strict submission schema at the draft path; skill was fixed in PR 9773 and will be re-broken by the next derivation
description:
FILED 2026-09-13 by the mayor, routed out of PR #9773 (skillsc-a, rf2-fzbj.16 F1). That PR fixed the SKILL leaf. This bead is the SPEC and IMPLEMENTATION half, and it matters because the spec is the artefact and the skill is downstream: leave this and the next derivation restores the bug the skill just lost.

THE RULE THAT IS BEING BROKEN. A form has TWO schemas. The DRAFT path takes a STRUCTURAL schema (every key present, loose values) because a blank first render and a half-typed field must both be valid. The strict SUBMISSION schema is the argument to an explicit `validate-against` call, and is registered NOWHERE. `reg-app-schema` rejects a failing candidate WHOLE — `:db` AND `:fx` — so a strict schema at a draft path does not merely warn: it silently discards the whole event, including the request the handler meant to fire. PR #9773 added a "§The two-schema rule" section to `skills/re-frame2/patterns/forms.md` stating this; that wording is the reference.

THREE SITES, VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the mayor at trunk a8c33f1bc8 unless marked.

SITE 1 — `spec/Pattern-Forms.md`, about line 55 (VERIFIED). It registers the strict submission schema at the draft path:

    (rf/reg-app-schema [:auth :login]              FormSlice)
    (rf/reg-app-schema [:auth :login :draft]       LoginForm)            ;; or via the slice's :draft path

`LoginForm` is `[:map [:email [:re #".+@.+"]] [:password [:string {:min 8}]]]` — strict. This is the exact registration PR #9773 removed from the skill. NOTE the surrounding paragraph already says these registrations are "a development tripwire, not the form's validation" and are elided from production builds; that nuance is TRUE and does not save it, because the whole-candidate rejection bites in development, which is where the tripwire is supposed to help.

SITE 2 — `spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:57` (worker-reported, RE-VERIFY). Carries the same defect for `AddToCartFields`.

SITE 3 — `skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md:40` (worker-reported, RE-VERIFY). Strict `AddToCartFields` (`[:string {:min 1}]`, `[:and :int [:>= 1] [:<= 99]]`) registered at `[:cart :add-form :draft]`, while the handler's failure arm at `:157` writes the rejected submission back into that same draft — the write the page itself calls "what makes the no-JS path honest". So the page's own headline promise is what the registration refuses.

AND A VACUOUS TEST THAT IS PART OF THIS BEAD, NOT A SEPARATE ONE. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_doc_example_form_action_test.clj:427` pins the faulty registration (`(is (= 'AddToCartFields draft-schema-sym))`), and its anti-regression assertion at `:431` is VACUOUS on the point it claims to defend:

    (is (m/validate fields (assoc drafted :quantity 1)) ...)

It patches the offending field to a valid value BEFORE validating, so it asserts nothing about the `{:item-id "sku-1" :quantity 0}` the arm actually writes and which its own comment claims the schema "can accept". Fix the assertion to validate what the arm really writes, against the structural draft schema.

WHAT LANDS. All three sites move to a structural draft schema plus an explicit `validate-against` at submission, matching the skill's new §The two-schema rule; the SSR test moves with them and its vacuous assertion becomes real.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS. A `check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` rule refusing a strict schema at a `:draft` path was the obvious guard and could not be taken: any formulation tight enough to catch the pre-fix `forms.md` also fires on `form-action.md`, so it would land red. Once this bead lands it is a few correct lines. Adding it is IN SCOPE here if it stays small.

NEITHER SPEC PAGE IS A HOT ZONE (checked against CLAUDE.md § Workflow's list). `spec/002-Frames.md` and the rest are — do not drift into them.

GATES. `jvm-ssr` for the test, `npm run test:cljs`, `check_doc_slugs.py` (nominated by PATH — `spec/` is one of its roots), and `python -m mkdocs build --strict`, which DOES cover `spec/` because mkdocs_hooks.py stages it into docs_dir. Nothing validates prose or the EDN inside a fence; check those by hand and say so.

Site 2, spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:57: strict AddToCartFields at [:cart :add-form :draft], whose failure arm writes the rejected submission back into that draft. The strict schemas are registered nowhere and stay the argument to the handler's own validation. One paragraph per page states the rule; the skill links forms.md §The two-schema rule.

title: reply: preserve explicit nil frame in trace-summary
description:
Preserve an explicitly supplied `:frame nil` when building reply trace summaries. Seed the reply's carried `:rf.frame/id` only when the options map omits `:frame`. The current nil test overrides an explicit no-governing-frame request and returns wire values under the carried frame's policy; the same option correctly redacts through the shared walker and public `project-egress` boundary.

Ownership: implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc:628-638,658-662 (primary). Security-review provenance: implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:109-152. Related regression home: implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:239-291. Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 22d46508a9e1ab8e9ebbe433a52b0cf1a9b30824. These paths and the examined runtime producers were unchanged from baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Contract and current callers

`trace-summary` documents that explicit `(:frame opts)` wins when given, otherwise the reply's carried stamp supplies policy. The actual machine and routing trace helpers explicitly document that `opts` is forwarded to the walker: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/reply.cljc:645-656 and implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/reply.cljc:238-248. They delegate to this core function unchanged. The walker contract at implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1218-1234 reads `:frame` by KEY PRESENCE: explicit nil says no frame governs and fails closed; absence alone permits fallback. The neighboring public projector implements that same key-presence rule. This finding concerns the documented helper option, not an added privacy policy.

Concrete source-loaded JVM witness

With the plain-atom reset fixture, create a live empty-policy frame :security-review/carried. Supply a canonical, `reply/valid-reply?`-accepted partial envelope:

    {:status :partial
     :value {:token "security-review-explicit-nil-sentinel"}
     :error {:kind :rf.http/server-error
             :detail "security-review-explicit-nil-sentinel"}
     :correlation {:token "security-review-explicit-nil-sentinel"}
     :meta {:token "security-review-explicit-nil-sentinel"}
     :rf.reply/work-id [:rf.work/http :review 1]
     :rf.reply/work-kind :http
     :rf.reply/work-status :failed
     :rf.frame/id :security-review/carried}

Call `reply/trace-summary`, `machines.reply/trace-reply`, and `routing.reply/trace-reply` with that envelope and `{:frame nil}`. All three return the entire input unchanged, including the sentinel in all four wire slots. In the same process, `elision/elide-wire-value` and `rf/project-egress` of the value with `{:frame nil}` return `:rf/redacted`.

Controls: an explicit unknown non-nil frame redacts all four reply slots; an explicit named live frame and omitted options correctly preserve the value under the carried frame. The trusted raw opt-out preserves it, and forced wire redaction still overrides the raw opt-out. The observed difference is specifically explicit nil being treated as absence. No raw-sensitive opt-in was supplied.

Expected: every present wire slot is `:rf/redacted` for explicit nil unless the caller deliberately enables sensitive inclusion; reply identity stays unchanged. Actual: `(nil? (:frame opts))` at reply.cljc:660 seeds the live carried frame over the caller's nil before the correctly implemented walker receives the options.

Impact and limit: a caller using the documented frame override to request a frameless summary cannot obtain that result and can receive raw values instead. This is confirmed on the actual shared helper and the two family wrappers. The review did not find or execute an asynchronous completion path that naturally supplies nil while carrying a different non-nil frame, and does not claim an observed external transmission or adversarial application exploit. P2 is for the concrete egress-option inconsistency, not a broad secrecy guarantee.

Suggested repair

Replace only the seed predicate with `(not (contains? opts :frame))`, retaining the existing carried-stamp presence check. Preserve omitted-options self-summarization and the explicit non-nil override. Keep classification fail-open behavior for unclassified values under a known frame and the trusted raw opt-in.

Acceptance criteria

- With a valid reply carrying a live frame, `{:frame nil}` redacts every present wire slot and preserves all identity facts, including under a different live ambient frame.
- Absent options still use the carried frame; a live explicit override uses its own policy; explicit unknown/destroyed frames continue to fail closed.
- Explicit nil with `:rf.egress/include-sensitive? true` retains the deliberate raw opt-out; forced wire redaction still wins.
- Cover the core helper with CLJC assertions and retain actual machine/routing wrapper coverage. Run focused JVM and CLJS reply/security tiers during remediation.

Validation and provenance

Fresh cached-dependency JVM security tier: 92 tests, 725 assertions, zero failures/errors, runner exit 0. The run printed the correct gate root and security source resource. Evidence: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_security/probe-impl_security-1.clj, gate-impl_security-1.log and .exit.

The controlled, valid-envelope witness is probe-impl_security-4.clj with same-name .log/.exit in that directory, exit 0; it asserts the current incorrect behavior, its legal envelope, and the stated controls. Both core source resource URLs resolve to this checkout. Attempt 2 was exploratory and used an invalid :ok envelope with :error; attempt 3 corrected the fixture; attempt 4 retains that valid-envelope assertion and adds the named-live-frame, trusted-raw and forced-redaction controls, and is the authoritative witness. No source edits, dependency install, compilation, shared build, server or transport occurred; the JVM processes exited.

No normative decision is being reopened. Live all-status searches for nil/reply/egress and descriptions containing trace-summary found no dedicated open owner of this defect. Known rf2-gwye.11, .18 and .60 are separate schema, SSR redirect and Story assertion causes. This is a fresh independent finding under rf2-gwye, not a split of a fenced aggregate; no prior status or notes were altered and no fixer is dispatched.

title: Cells: reuse settled dependencies to avoid exponential evaluation
description:
Bound Cells evaluation by the dependency graph instead of recursively recomputing the same settled cell at every reference. A 21-cell sheet of ordinary addition formulas currently expands one displayed value into 2,097,151 evaluate-cell calls. Add snapshot-scoped completed-value reuse while retaining the path-local cycle guard and the deliberately simple whole-map subscription design.

Ownership and review identity
- Slice: examples_core. Owner: examples/core/seven_guis/cells/core.cljs; teaching explanation also at examples/core/seven_guis/README.md:32.
- Baseline: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Revalidated current source in the 2026-09-13 read-only review; no source edits.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Split from finding 1 of rf2-fzbj.18, which remains unchanged. The title fence is retained: remediation is held until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This issue is an independently dispatchable review deliverable, not authorization to fix or dispatch.

Evidence and trigger
- core.cljs:270-325: evaluate-ast eagerly mapv-evaluates every argument at line 285; each cell reference invokes evaluate-cell at 280-281; evaluate-cell 319-324 has a visited-path cycle guard but no completed-value reuse.
- core.cljs:383-393: every displayed :cells/value subscription starts its own evaluation over the current cell map. Equality deduplication of the final subscription value happens after these calls.
- Enter 1 in A1, =(+ A1 A1) in A2, =(+ A2 A2) in A3, and continue through A21. Then edit A1. These are valid, in-bounds references and short formulas, without a cycle.
- Expected: A21 yields 1048576 for A1=1, with each distinct dependency settled once within its root/snapshot evaluation.
- Actual fresh source-extracted measurements: 9 cells = 511 calls; 13 = 8191; 17 = 131071; 21 = 2097151. The corresponding final values are 256, 4096, 65536, and 1048576. An equal-depth control with each cell adding one previous-cell reference and literal 1 performs 21 calls and yields 21.
- The call recurrence is T(n)=2*T(n-1)+1. The numbers count only the last cell's evaluation, before all the other mounted subscriptions run. The 21-cell instrumented Babashka probe took about 1.47 seconds; that is not a CLJS/browser timing claim. The exact repeated-call count and reachable source path are the evidence.

Impact
A small valid sheet can monopolize the UI thread and prevent the user from editing the formulas that caused it. The teaching claim at core.cljs:15-21 that recomputation is cheap because the grid is small and result values are deduplicated obscures this separate exponential cost.

Suggested repair
Keep the sparse app-db, parser, typed errors, whole-map input subscription, and cycle semantics. Reuse completed cell values in a cache scoped to one immutable cells snapshot/evaluation; either an internal per-root cache or a derived value table is sufficient. Distinguish visiting cells from completed cells. Do not use a process-global cell-id-only cache or reject valid formulas through arbitrary limits. Update the explanation of evaluation cost to describe the implemented bounded rule.

Acceptance criteria
1. The 21-cell duplicate-reference chain returns 1048576 with a deterministic operation-count regression that fails the old exponential evaluator.
2. Editing A1 recomputes dependents from the new snapshot; a prior snapshot's cached results cannot leak.
3. The single-reference control, self/two-cell cycles, parse-error propagation, arithmetic, and empty-cell behavior remain correct.
4. Extend implementation/core/test/re_frame/seven_guis_cells_parser_cljs_test.cljs. Examples intentionally have no spec.cjs or per-example tests (rf2-8cevm); do not add them.

Validation and limits
Freshly executed bb C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/ai/surface-review-20260913/examples_core/probe-examples_core-1.clj. Exit 0; absolute source-root banner verified. Probe, log, and exit file are ignored and uniquely named. The script reads/evaluates the actual parse-error?, evaluate-ast, and evaluate-cell forms, constructs the valid ASTs emitted by the inspected parser, and instruments recursive visits process-locally. It substitutes Babashka parse-double only for CLJS parsing of literal 1. Current parser and framework regression source were inspected; no compiler, broad gate, browser, or server was run. The probe passed by confirming the defect, not by demonstrating a repair.

Duplicate disposition
Live all-status title searches for Cells and description searches for evaluate-cell and the owned source path find only rf2-fzbj.18 for this behavior; its latest three history entries preserve the fence and open status. It contains two independent findings, so does not substitute for this individual issue. Existing cycle/grid-bound/error-marker regression coverage addresses different outcomes and remains intact.
notes:
REMEDIATED — PR #9762 (branch worker/excore-a), 2026-09-13. This is finding 1 of rf2-fzbj.18; both beads are closed by the same change. Re-verified at tip before fixing: core.cljs still evaluated every reference eagerly with no completed-value reuse, exactly as filed.

THE FIX. `evaluate-cell` / `evaluate-ast` in examples/core/seven_guis/cells/core.cljs now thread a `settled` memo of finished cells beside the path-local `visited` cycle guard. The two sets answer different questions — `visited` is "on the path right now", so meeting it again is still :error/cycle; `settled` is "done, reuse it" — so reuse never stands in for cycle detection. The memo is created per top-level call over one immutable cell map, so a prior snapshot's results cannot leak and there is no process-global, cell-id-keyed cache. Untouched: the parser, the sparse app-db, typed error values, the path-local cycle semantics, and the deliberately broad whole-map `:cells/all-cells` subscription. The public 3-arity signatures of both fns are unchanged; the memo rides a 4-arity. No formula is rejected and no input-size cap was added.

1. The 21-cell duplicate-reference chain returns 1048576 in exactly 21 cell reads, counted through an ILookup that tallies every lookup the evaluator makes — a deterministic operation count, not a wall clock. It fails against the old evaluator at 2,097,151.
2. Editing A1 moves A21 to 2097152 while the original snapshot still reads 1048576 — no leak in either direction.
3. The equal-depth single-reference control still reads 21 in 21 visits, and the file's existing cycle, parse-error, arithmetic and empty-cell cases are unchanged and green. A chain closed into a loop still reads :error/cycle, now in 21 reads rather than two million.

TEACHING TEXT updated as the finding asked: the cost claim in the Cells namespace docstring, its subscriptions comment, and the Cells row of examples/core/seven_guis/README.md now describe the bounded rule (one visit per cell depended on) instead of "the grid is small".

NOT BUILT, deliberately: the suggested whole-snapshot derived value table. The per-evaluation memo already bounds the work at one visit per dependency, and a value-table sub would change the one-input subscription topology this finding explicitly says may remain.
