title: Resources RealWorld: refuse departed article-delete navigation
description:
Make a Resources article-detail delete navigate home only while the initiating article still owns the active route. The current completion unconditionally overrides the reader's later navigation.

Remediation fence: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. Independently implementable Resources detail-delete part of confirmed finding 4 in rf2-fzbj.21, revalidated under rf2-gwye. Editor paths are separate issues. Review/issue creation only; implementation remains held.

Ownership: examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:188-212, the :ui/delete-article/:ui/article-deleted pair. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; inspected HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879.

Trigger/reproducer: on an owned article alpha, click Delete and hold the successful mutation response. Navigate to article beta or profile/eve, then release alpha's response.

Expected: alpha is deleted and cache invalidation remains valid, while the chosen beta/profile route stays active. Actual: :ui/delete-article supplies :reply-to [:ui/article-deleted] with no originating route/slug argument, and :ui/article-deleted always dispatches home navigation on :ok. Neither releasing alpha's route-owned read nor moving to a new route retires the independently executing mutation.

Suggested repair: carry alpha's slug (and/or existing committed route identity) in the continuation target, and gate navigation on the current route being :realworld.article/show for that same initiating article. The HTTP twin's comments.cljs:159-172,625-642 article-route-for-slug? is a small working precedent. Mutation-instance cleanup is a separate obligation and should remain scoped to the completed operation; do not suppress legitimate server/cache reconciliation or turn this into a general navigation manager.

Acceptance: held mutation sequences alpha -> beta and alpha -> profile/eve both retain the newer route after old success. A success while still on alpha still clears the completed delete instance and navigates home. Verify the failure path and later navigation remain usable. Add coverage in existing framework-owned realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs, keeping examples test-free.

Validation performed: source-probe.clj evaluates the actual current :ui/article-deleted function with runtime route profile/eve and a successful alpha delete reply. probe-examples_real_apps-1.log/.exit: exit 0, correct SOURCE_ROOT banner; result contains mutation-instance clear and unconditional home navigation. Inspected the real call-site target, route resource ownership and mutation success continuation path. No browser/full transport or CLJS compile was run.

Remediated in PR #9758 (branch worker/realworld-a), which fixes all four confirmed findings of rf2-fzbj.21 together. Every finding was re-verified at tip before the fix; all four still held.

1. rf2-gwye.33 (HTTP optimistic comment) — realworld_http/schema.cljs gains DurableComment: the wire ws/Comment with :id widened to [:or :int [:re #"^temp-"]], derived from ws/Comment rather than restated. title: mcp-base: replace record extension keys during dedup walks
description:
Rebuild transformed record extension keys with replacement semantics in both dedup walks. Escaping or expanding a dynamic key currently adds its replacement without removing the original, so normal record data gains an extra entry. This is the independently actionable split of rf2-fzbj.9 finding 2; its remediation fence remains in force until Mike rules who owns remediation.

Ownership and revision: tools_mcp_base, tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc, baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Revalidated at 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879; owned paths unchanged from baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source: side-walk line 384 and decompress-cache line 537 reduce transformed entries into the ORIGINAL record. The escape pass at line 480 transforms dynamic keys, but conj/assoc does not remove the old key. The inverse repeats the same mistake when removing the escape prefix. This differs from ordinary maps, rebuilt into an empty map.

Reproducer (real JVM Clojure 1.12.0):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.mcp-base.dedup :as d])
(defrecord ReviewRecord [x])
(let [shared {:v [1 2 3]}
      payload {:record (assoc (->ReviewRecord shared)
                              :de-dupe.cache/cache-1 77)
               :a shared}
      wire (d/dedup-value payload true)]
  (d/expand (:rf.mcp/dedup-table wire)))
```

Expected record keys: :x and :de-dupe.cache/cache-1. Actual record keys additionally include :de-dupe.cache/!cache-1, also carrying 77. Equality with the original payload is false. The encoded record already contains both spellings. The unrelated shared subtree forces a real multi-slot wrapper; the ordinary-map control round-trips exactly, and disabled dedup preserves identity. Record type itself remains intact in the observed bad result.

Impact: dynamic extension entries in normal persistent records gain data during the default wire transform. Story tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:127-161 consumes the in-memory result through dedup-value, so records can reach the shared codec. Host-side corruption is proven; a distinct JSON alias failure is not claimed without executing that seam.

Repair: snapshot original entries and rebuild transformed extension entries so changed keys replace originals rather than coexist. Apply the same semantics forward and inverse; avoid overwriting an entry before reading its original value. Preserve declared record fields and record identity where supported. Keep the existing reference grammar and deliberate sorted-collection lowering; no generic serialization redesign is needed.

Acceptance: add a .cljc record fixture with dynamic colliding keyword, symbol and string keys, force a genuine wrapper, and assert exact entries and record type after expansion. Assert the original spelling is absent from the encoded record when escaped, and the escaped spelling is absent after expansion. Include ordinary-map, real-repeat and disabled controls. Add a focused Story apply-dedup integration pin for matching text and structured data.

title: SSR streaming install! Usage mounts before readiness and recommends payload polling
description:
Replace streaming.client/install!'s Usage example with a readiness-driven bootstrap that seeds and hydrates only from :on-ready. The current example immediately renders into the streaming root and suggests polling for the payload, directly contradicting the shipped streaming lifecycle contract above it.

Ownership: impl_ssr; implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming/client.cljs:766-783 (Usage example), :735-753 (:on-ready contract), :667-705 (finalization). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Concrete trigger: an application author copies the public install! docstring's "streaming-aware Reagent bootstrap" as the host sequence. It calls (streaming-client/install! {:frame :app/main}), then immediately (rdc/render react-root [rf/frame-provider ...]), and tells the reader a host "typically polls / observes for __rf_payload" before reconciling later. It supplies no :on-ready callback and never shows the required ordinary hydrate-root adoption.

Actual sequence: the streaming consumer initially materializes <rf-suspense> transport wrappers and only removes them in finalize! when the canonical payload arrives. The sample therefore invites the client renderer to own/mutate the root while the observer still owns protocol DOM; its polling suggestion can race finalization even after __rf_payload appears. The function's own option documentation explicitly forbids this ordering. Spec 011:1689-1690 requires finalization to consume pending chunks, unwrap mounts, disconnect, then invoke readiness; both ssr/hydrate! and adapter hydrate-root run from :on-ready, never a timer or DOM poll. Readiness can fire synchronously inside install! for a buffered response.

Expected: the executable guidance demonstrates the supported host ordering. Initialize the adapter and create the live target frame first; pass :on-ready that installs the final payload and calls the supported adapter hydration entry point; initialize callback-captured root/container values before install!, because the callback may be synchronous; retain the stop function only if illustrating early abandonment. Keep Reagent/adapter imports and APIs consistent with the chosen supported substrate. No immediate render/create-root or polling branch belongs in this example.

Impact: developers and coding agents using API documentation can build a bootstrap that destroys server-painted content or hydrates mismatched transport wrappers. This is a documentation repair to the shipped correct lifecycle, not a request to redesign the runtime or revisit the progressive-paint protocol.

Acceptance:
- A self-consistent minimal example follows Spec 011's sequence and handles both incrementally arriving and already-buffered payloads.
- The advertised mount/hydrate API exists for the selected adapter, and the frame creation/provider contract is explicit enough to paste into a host.
- Validate the extracted recipe in an existing streaming DOM fixture (or manually in the real streaming host) with a delayed final payload: no root ownership before readiness, exactly one seed/hydration after wrappers disappear; buffered payload boots once without relying on a later tick.

Validation performed: inspected actual install!/finalize! source and the browser test no-mounts-and-no-readiness-before-the-payload at implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_hydration_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:529-553, which explicitly asserts wrappers remain before readiness; also inspected the already-buffered once-only callback fixture at :502-525. Tests were read, not executed or claimed green. Separate production-JVM probes verified continuation render failure falls back and emits no delta, projector throw returns sanitized generic 500, root hash survives a keyed fragment, and request teardown clears storage (probe-lifecycle-impl-ssr-1.log/.exit, exit 0). They do not execute this CLJS recipe. No browser build, source edits, or broad suite ran.

Deduplication: current all-status streaming/SSR titles plus all-status description search for on-ready found no dedicated issue. Prior rf2-fzbj.10 contains only redirect/claim defects, not this recipe. Closed rf2-6r9j.191 renamed streaming locals and preserved callback contracts; its closure is not evidence this stale Usage block was corrected. This is newly identified executable-guidance drift, independent of the two prior aggregate findings.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9747. The install! Usage block is replaced with a readiness-driven Reagent-slim recipe: the frame is made first, the container is bound before install!, and ssr/hydrate! then reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root run only from :on-ready, with no create-root and no polling. Two tests in re-frame.ssr.streaming-hydration-lifecycle-dom-cljs-test (cljs-browser) execute the recipe, for a live stream and for a buffered response. A planted fault reddened exactly those two tests. The held note is cleared by the 2026-09-13 ruling. The full verdict is in the notes.

title: Incomplete: rf2-pjay still crashes on computed :variants inside a literal reg-story body
description:
Merged-PR audit #9719, 0b25036b321c6685ed9fa1812d24f8012b54c103. The new reg-story* runtime desugaring works, but the rf2-pjay authoring-input correction remains incomplete for a normal Form-B call with a literal outer metadata map and a computed :variants value.

Reproducer (public re-frame.story API, isolated JVM):
  (def vs {:v {:setup []}})
  (story/reg-story :story.audit-symbol {:variants vs})
  (story/reg-story :story.audit-merge {:variants (merge vs {:other {:setup []}})})
The symbol form fails during macro expansion with IllegalArgumentException: Don't know how to create ISeq from: clojure.lang.Symbol. The merge form fails with UnsupportedOperationException: nth not supported on this type: Symbol. In the same probe, (story/reg-story* :story.audit-program {:variants vs}) and (story/reg-story :story.audit-body (assoc {} :variants vs)) both register their /v variant successfully. This is a real load/compile failure, not a stale-comment-only finding.

Cause: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/macros.clj:165-183 classifies only the OUTER metadata as literal. Any truthy :variants form is then peeled off and traversed by the macro's for, even when it is a symbol or an expression. It never reaches the runtime fallback newly fixed by #9719. Conventions.md's registration pair uses the same body shape, and #9719's new registrar docstring describes macro peeling for a LITERAL :variants map.

Minimal correction: only macro-desugar a literal variants map. Forward the full metadata form unchanged to reg-story* when its :variants value needs runtime evaluation, so the existing runtime desugar/validation handles it. Preserve literal-map expansion into independent variant registrations, source-coordinate binding and production elision. Update the now-adjacent obsolete helper-drops-variants comment as part of this correction. No new public API or validation mechanism is needed.

Verified both expand-reg-story and the public macro through isolated JVM probes (captured exit 0; failures deliberately caught and reported), with positive literal/computed-body/programmatic controls. The loaded macro/registrar resource paths point at C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2, and those source files plus schemas.cljc match the landed PR after normalizing checkout line endings. Searched all 58 literal-open Beads by full title/description/criteria; no exact computed-variants macro defect and correction exists.
acceptance_criteria: The public reg-story macro accepts a literal outer body with :variants supplied by a def/let-bound symbol and by a merge expression; all entries register under the expected story IDs with the macro's source coordinates. Retain literal Form-B expansion and computed-whole-body/programmatic controls. A regression must fail on the current macro expansion and pass through actual registration after the change. Run the existing Story JVM authoring suite and relevant CLJS compilation lane; preserve elision and do not change existing Bead statuses.

title: surface-review(story-mcp): preserve valid run results and isolate the stdio lifecycle
description:
Recommendation: keep ordinary Story execution usable over MCP by isolating application stdout and projecting supported callable values before success results reach JSON encoding. Also release the CLI-owned executor at EOF so a completed session does not linger for one minute. This review confirms two P2 defects and one P3 finite shutdown delay. Keep this single report OPEN for remediation; no production fixes are included.

Scope and revision
- Owned slice: tools_story_mcp, all 39 tracked paths under tools/story-mcp/**, as partitioned for parent rf2-fzbj.
- Reviewed source baseline: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f.
- Final observed HEAD: 1b285ba9a841a336dd6f54f81f77aaee3150253b. git diff --exit-code BASELINE -- tools/story-mcp returned 0: owned source remained identical despite concurrent tracker checkpoints.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Coverage and exclusions
Inspected the JVM stdio boot/dispatch/read/write flow in server.cljc and protocol.cljc; descriptor assembly, input schemas, argument normalization and per-tool filtering; write gating and object/EDN body coercion; docs/list/cursor handlers; registered Story run/preview/identity guards and execution; success/error envelopes, dedup/cap ordering and egress helpers; deps.edn and README launch instructions. Read relevant spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md, spec/002-Tool-Registry.md, spec/API.md passages and neighboring Story authoring/schema/lifecycle sources. Sampled tools_test.clj, wire_encodability_test.clj and the stdio-roundtrip.js harness to compare what tests execute with the paths below. Coverage is focused, not a claim that every test, descriptor sentence, documentation renderer or CLJS provider was exhaustively inspected.

Executed actual current source with Clojure 1.12.4, Java, Node and an existing cached classpath, made absolute to this checkout. The cache includes schemas and other development dependencies; this is NOT a hermetic published-jar or runtime-dependency completeness proof. No dependency resolution/install, compilation output, shared framework service, browser or external network request was used. The root explicitly authorized the bounded real -main subprocess witness. Those subprocesses used synthetic in-process stories and piped stdio only, and exited normally. All probe processes and unified-exec sessions are finished. No broad test/build gate was run, and there is no passing-suite claim.

Finding 1 — P2: an ordinary event-handler println corrupts the MCP stdout stream

Locations
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:281-284 dispatches the handler and writes its reply without rebinding application *out*.
- server.cljc:397-399 builds the JSON writer directly over System/out, then runs that same unisolated dispatcher.
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc:178 runs Story in a future which conveys the caller's dynamic bindings, including *out*.
- tools/story-mcp/spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md:7-13 reserves stdout for one JSON frame per line and stderr for diagnostics.

Trigger/reproducer
Preload a valid CLJC/JVM story namespace (as the README supports), installing plain-atom and registering:

    (rf/reg-event :review-mcp/log
      (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
        (println "APPLICATION-LOG-SENTINEL")
        {:db (assoc db :executed true)}))
    (story/reg-story :story.review-mcp {})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review-mcp/logging
      {:setup [[:review-mcp/log]]})

Launch the actual re-frame.story-mcp.server/-main, send initialize, tools/call run-variant for :story.review-mcp/logging, then ping. The probe uses :dedup false and :max-tokens 0 so compression/budget behavior cannot conceal the wire observation.

Measured actual behavior
- The successful run reports status "pass" and app-db.executed=true.
- stdout contains FOUR lines for THREE requests: initialize response, the bare APPLICATION-LOG-SENTINEL line, run result, ping response.
- JSON parsing that second line fails. The same observation was first confirmed with run-loop! using one StringWriter for the response writer and bound *out*, then independently confirmed through actual -main/System.out; it is not an artifact of a mocked dispatch path.
- A no-print variant through the in-memory loop produces exactly three valid JSON response lines.

Expected: application diagnostic output emitted during an invoked Story handler should reach stderr, while stdout contains only protocol frames. A normal println in behavior under test must not invalidate the transport.

Impact: the shipped stdio test/client's own stdout parser rejects malformed lines; ordinary diagnostic logging in app events can therefore break the agent session even though the scenario executed successfully. This is not malicious output and does not require raw System.out writes or a custom logging backend. README.md:161-163 already warns about LOAD-TIME printing before the server starts; this finding is specifically runtime printing under the server's own handler dispatch after initialization.

Repair: at the server-owned dispatch/execution boundary bind application *out* to *err*, while preserving the explicit protocol writer for JSON replies. Clojure future binding conveyance will carry that redirect into run-variant-blocking. Keep server log! on stderr. Do not require every application event handler to know about MCP, and do not globally rewrite System.out for unrelated library users. The pre-main loading caveat may remain: code already run by clojure.main init-opts is a distinct ownership boundary.

Acceptance: an actual stdio test registers and runs a variant whose setup or script handler printlns a unique marker; all stdout lines parse as JSON, the marker appears only on stderr, the run returns its expected app-db/verdict and a following ping succeeds. Include a quiet control and a throwing handler that prints before failing. This test must call a real registered run; the present stdio-roundtrip.js only previews an unknown variant and never reaches the lifecycle worker.

Finding 2 — P2: a supported predicate assertion makes four successful tools fail JSON encoding

Locations
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/result.cljc:173-187 edn-result puts the raw value in structuredContent and uses pr-edn/pr-str for text. Only caught exception data passes through wire-safe-value/wire-safe-ex-data (result.cljc:50-156).
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:119-124 (get-variant), 389-393 (explain-variant), 406-409 (variant->edn) send the valid registered body/plan directly through that success envelope.
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:124-200 carries the real run's assertion/evidence values into the same envelope through egress/result-with-indicators.
- protocol.cljc:312-319 JSON-encodes the raw payload; server.cljc:283-291 catches the encoding throw outside the tool and replaces the entire reply with -32603.
- Supported authoring trigger: tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md:516 explicitly accepts [:assert-db path :pred fn-or-sym]; tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc:539-591 accepts that script, and Story's direct run executes it successfully.

Executed fixture

    (story/reg-variant :story.review-mcp/predicate
      {:db-seed {:count 1}
       :script [[:assert-db [:count] :pred pos?]]})
    (:status @(story/run-variant :story.review-mcp/predicate))
    ;; => :pass

For each of get-variant, variant->edn, explain-variant and run-variant, send a tools/call through actual server/run-loop! over in-memory JSON streams, with the registered id, :dedup false and :max-tokens 0. No handler, registrar, plan, runner, envelope or encoder is stubbed.

Actual: all FOUR replies are JSON-RPC errors with code -32603 and message beginning "Server fault: Cannot JSON encode object of class: class clojure.core$pos_QMARK_". The message includes the live object's identity suffix. The predicate reaches ordinary successful body/plan/run data; it is not exception ex-data, so the existing error-only encodability projection never sees it. A control changing only the assertion to [:assert-db [:count] 1] succeeds through all four tools, and its run result reports "pass".

Expected: a supported Story assertion should remain inspectable and its passing run verdict should cross the MCP wire. Callable values cannot be reconstructed by raw JSON or EDN printing, so the wire must represent that limitation explicitly without discarding all surrounding author data or run evidence as a server fault.

Impact: the advertised author/refine/test loop breaks for the documented predicate form. Even catalog reads and explain fail, and a completed passing run loses its entire verdict/evidence response. Disabling dedup or raising the token cap does not help. The strict round-trippable EDN prose is also false for a raw closure: pr-str emits #object, not a reconstructible function.

Repair: introduce one explicit success-value projection before both text and structured payload construction (and before dedup/cap), reusing/extracting the existing shape-only opaque-value policy where appropriate. Preserve plain data and surround a callable with a stable, honest non-reconstructible-value marker or supported callable descriptor. Keep the rest of the body and run evidence, including its actual status. Do not blindly call wire-safe-ex-data on author data: its special treatment of :explain and :rf.error/id belongs to exceptions, and would reinterpret literal application keys. Align the round-trip contract with the actual callable representation; do not remove supported predicate assertions or claim a closure round-trips losslessly. Source-based callable reconstruction is not required to repair this boundary.

Acceptance: the exact predicate fixture must remain :pass through direct Story and return a valid MCP result for all four tools, with useful surrounding body/plan/evidence preserved and explicit representation of the callable. Exercise the real JSON encode/decode boundary with default dedup and dedup=false. Retain the equality-only control and the existing exception-ex-data encodability tests. Assert no raw #object identity/address escapes, and ensure literal author keys named :explain or :rf.error/id are not renamed by the new projection.

Finding 3 — P3: the CLI lingers for the executor's 60-second idle timeout after EOF

Locations
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc:178 creates a Clojure future for every actual run/preview.
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:399-408 returns from run-loop!/run-stdio!/-main after EOF without shutting down the CLI's future executor.
- tools/story-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js ends with child.kill(), so its success does not prove graceful EOF process exit; it also never executes a registered variant.

Measured actual-command witness
The Node probe launches java with the existing absolute source classpath, clojure.main -i <synthetic-prelude> -m re-frame.story-mcp.server. It waits for a final ping response, closes child stdin, records the "stdin closed; exiting" stderr signal and observes the CHILD PROCESS close event (no kill on the successful path).
- Same prelude, initialize + ping, no lifecycle call: exit code 0, stdin-to-exit 71 ms; EOF log after 3 ms.
- initialize + successful run-variant + ping: exit code 0, stdin-to-exit 60,021 ms; EOF log after 0 ms.
- The separate in-memory probe finds an alive, non-daemon clojure-agent-send-off-pool-0 thread in TIMED_WAITING after run-loop! returned :eof.

Expected: after the CLI has finished its work and stdin closes, the process should release its own execution resources and exit promptly. Actual: the read loop and -main return, but the cached future executor keeps the JVM alive until its finite idle timeout. This is a measured ONE-MINUTE DELAY, not an indefinite hang or claim that the read loop failed to see EOF.

Impact/severity: slower agent-host restart/shutdown and temporary orphaned JVMs after sessions that actually run stories. The host can terminate the child and the idle executor eventually exits, so this is P3 rather than a blocking/infinite resource leak.

Repair: make process-level cleanup explicit at the actual CLI entry point, e.g. use a finally around boot/run with shutdown-agents when -main owns this process, or use a narrowly owned executor with explicit shutdown. Do not put global shutdown-agents in reusable run-loop! or each tool handler: embedded callers and later requests must remain usable. Preserve the existing timeout covering synchronous Story work.

Acceptance: a spawned real -main session performs a real registered run, receives its result and a ping, closes stdin, and exits 0 within a short post-EOF bound (for example 2 seconds after the already-running process sees EOF) without test-driven kill. Keep the no-run control and a library-use control proving run-loop! does not globally shut down Clojure execution resources. A timeout/cancellation case should still free the CLI promptly.

Overlap and prior-history checks
- rf2-fzbj.3 owns Story's raw-versus-compiled effective-args defect. This review additionally executed an MCP consequence: a child with {:extends :story.review-mcp/base}, whose parent supplies {:args {:inherited 7}}, rejects snapshot-identity :cell-overrides {"inherited" 8} as story-mcp-unknown-cell-override-key with :allowed []. tools/args.cljc:115-123 derives its allowlist via the same raw rf.story/resolve-args path. Treat this as a consumer acceptance case for rf2-fzbj.3, not a fourth independently counted defect or duplicate repair owner. Its inherited/composed loader findings likewise remain owned there.
- rf2-fzbj.9 owns shared dedup metadata collisions, record extension keys and list/vector pooling. Those are not refiled here. Finding 2 explicitly disables dedup and fails at Cheshire, independently of that codec.
- rf2-cfq8a (closed) and rf2-c9t52 (closed) cover project preload launch instructions and missing-adapter false passes. Read current notes/closures and the latest cfq8a history snapshot; their repairs are present. The load-time stdout note is not a runtime redirect, and the probes deliberately install the required adapter.
- rf2-sw1d and rf2-49o8 (closed) address unknown run identifiers and nested override-key alignment. Their guard code is present; the inherited-key consequence above is caused by the separate Story resolver issue.
- The source-cited rf2-ia904/rf2-2z9u3 error-encoding work is visible in current code/tests and commit ecc6f65d500c59327fb04abde409ee54bd59fda7. bd show could not find those old IDs (nor rf2-j538f7.31), so their full tracker histories were unavailable. The inspected commit explicitly fixes caught EX-DATA projection; finding 2 concerns valid success data and does not ask to redo that repair.
- Searched current all-status Story-MCP titles and relevant full title/description/notes in the exported issue data; also checked live bd search for stdout/encoding terms and relevant source history. No current bead owning these three concrete defects was found. Missing old tracker records limit the history claim; they do not weaken the current executable witnesses.

Evidence and validation limits
All evidence is gitignored, unique to tools_story_mcp, and attempt-numbered under ai/surface-review-20260912:
- probe-tools_story_mcp-1.clj/.log/.exit: real in-memory dispatcher/writer, application-output witness, quiet control, post-EOF non-daemon thread observation and inherited-override overlap. Exit 0.
- prelude-tools_story_mcp-2.clj plus probe-tools_story_mcp-2.cjs/.log/.exit: actual -main/System.out, finite EOF timing and no-run control. Exit 0; both children exited normally.
- probe-tools_story_mcp-3.clj/.log/.exit: direct passing predicate run, four real encoded MCP counterexamples and four equality-only controls. Exit 0.
These exits mean assertions reproduced the reported CURRENT DEFECTS and controls, not that correctness gates passed. In-memory probes call shutdown-agents to dispose their own resources; the CLI witness deliberately did not and measured natural exit. No CLJS/browser, SDK integration suite, remote host configuration, timeout-interruption stress test, published packaging, full test suite, rendering or docs gate was executed. The practical transport failure follows from the actual non-JSON stdout line and the inspected shipped client's parser; no claim is made that a particular external host was run.

title: pilots: the two counted-pilot briefs carry stale instructions that would contaminate a run (no-website read fence, commit-move upgrade, Xray manual barred)
description:
Found by the rf2-hic-063 ruling pass and verified that tick. rf2-hic-063 owns these files
but is now titled "[HELD GATE - nothing to pick up]", so a dispatcher will skip it and this
repair - which can and should be done BEFORE publication - becomes invisible.

THE DEFECT, two parts, both measured:

1. STALE "no website" INSTRUCTION. The briefs tell the pilot the docs have no published
   website and to read the checkout copy instead - `brief-realworld.md:52-54`. The docs
   site is LIVE (probed 200; controls 404 and 200). Left unflipped, this instruction sends
   a COUNTED pilot into a source checkout, which is precisely the contamination the
   published-artefact gate exists to eliminate. A pilot that followed it would invalidate
   its own run.

2. STALE UPGRADE STEP. Both briefs still prescribe a commit move for the upgrade outcome -
   `brief-realworld.md:143`, `brief-linearlite.md:169` - rather than a released-version
   move. Outcome 7 requires an upgrade across a release candidate, so a commit move does
   not satisfy it.

NOT A CONTRADICTION IN THE FRICTION LOG: `friction-log.md:50` resolves the pin-substitution
case coherently. The defect is that the briefs were never flipped to match it.

WHY IT IS PRE-PUBLICATION WORK: neither repair needs a tag, a coordinate or a Clojars
group. Both are doc edits that make the briefs correct for the moment the gate opens. Doing
them now removes a landmine; doing them later risks a counted pilot running on stale
instructions.

RELATED, DO NOT DUPLICATE: rf2-i6ug covers `16-diagnostics.md` resolving Xray from a
checkout. Outcome 5 has TWO independent causes - that one, AND the briefs' read fence
barring the public Xray manual (`brief-realworld.md:67`) where the operator page admits it
(`workspace.md:49`). Fixing rf2-i6ug alone leaves outcome 5 blocked; this bead covers the
fence half.

WORK: flip both briefs to (a) direct the pilot at the published docs site, (b) prescribe a
released-version upgrade move, (c) permit the public Xray manual in the read fence,
consistent with `workspace.md:49`. Verify against `friction-log.md:50` rather than
re-deciding it. Sequence BEFORE the pilots run; independent of rf2-uelji / rf2-fo4ng /
rf2-kmqx3.

title: [examples/real-apps] Both RealWorld settings replies restore credentials after logout
description:
Snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Relevant sources unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

The supported Update Settings -> Logout sequence can restore the logged-out user's credentials when the earlier save completes. This is not a requirement for generic defensive input validation: both actions are simultaneously enabled in the shipped UI, and the real demo intentionally delays replies.

Evidence (examples/real-apps/realworld_http):
- settings.cljs:321-334 issues PUT /user, success target [:settings/submit-success], with no request owner/session identity carried to that handler. While submitting, only the form fields and submit button are disabled. The form Logout remains enabled at 463-466; core.cljs:189-194 also exposes enabled navbar Logout.
- auth.cljs:364-368 handles the auth machine's :clear-session action with [:auth/clear-session], token persistence removal, and navigation home. clear-session:158-162 sets user and token nil. No pending settings request is aborted or invalidated here.
- settings.cljs:345-358 unconditionally uses auth/store-session-db with the returned user, then navigates to that user's profile. store-session-db is auth.cljs:128-131 and writes both :auth/:user and :auth/:token.
- The frame is reused on logout, so frame-incarnation reply fences do not reject this outstanding managed reply. There is no intervening request under a stable settings request ID which could supersede it.
- routing.cljs:159-163 treats non-nil auth user as authenticated for protected route entry; core.cljs:320-325 injects auth token into real HTTP. The auth machine stays :idle after logout, so its header :auth/authenticated? can also disagree with these newly resurrected credentials.
- The built-in fake backend freezes a reply before deferred delivery: realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:571-581 transitions its state then delegates to canned success with :after-ms reply-delay-ms. The README also supports replacing the stub with a real backend.

The same defect is independently present in examples/real-apps/realworld_resources (added by that separately scoped surface review, not a duplicate issue):
- settings.cljs:111-127 dispatches :rf.mutation/execute for :realworld/update-settings with stable instance :settings/save and reply-to [:settings/replied], without session ownership captured in the continuation.
- settings.cljs:129-151 unconditionally stores the success reply's user/token and navigates to its profile. Logout is still available at settings.cljs:207-209 and core.cljs:112-114.
- auth.cljs:237-261 clears user/token and dispatches concrete resource clear-scope operations for the former session/viewer; logout's auth action at 424-428 also persists nil and navigates home. These operations do not retire the pending settings mutation.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2073-2140 clear-scope walks resource entries and cancels their live read work/timers, not mutation rows. This follows its settled concrete-resource-scope contract; changing that generic contract is not the proposed repair.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:284-316 defines update-settings without session-owned continuation invalidation. mutation_events.cljc:1569-1571 reaches reply_handlers.cljc:93-99 live-slot checking frame/work/generation; logout keeps the same frame and the mutation's live instance, so the success can still reach settings/replied.
Thus this is the same application-level settings-completion ownership gap in both siblings, despite different request engines. The resources extension is a source-only causal trace; the executed reducer probe below is specifically the HTTP example.

Normal reproduction in either example: sign in; edit Settings; Update Settings; click either Logout while the save reply is parked; let PUT /user succeed. Expected user/token remain nil and navigation stays where logout took the user. Actual old user/token return and the late settings handler navigates to that user's profile.

Bounded probe executed actual source forms in a fresh bb process, not copies of their algorithms: read auth.cljs/settings.cljs forms, eval auth/store-session-db, the fn at :auth/clear-session and the fn at :settings/submit-success (alias auth to the isolated namespace). Essential inline sequence:
```clojure
(let [before {:auth {:user {:username "alice"} :token "token-A"}}
      logged-out (:db (clear-handler {:db before} [:auth/clear-session]))
      late-result (success-handler {:db logged-out}
                    [:settings/submit-success
                     {:status :ok :value {:user {:username "alice" :token "token-A"}}}])]
  (prn {:after-logout (:auth logged-out)
        :after-late-save (:auth (:db late-result))
        :late-effects (:fx late-result)}))
;; after-logout {:user nil :token nil}
;; after-late-save {:user {:username "alice"} :token "token-A"}
;; late-effects dispatch settings submit-succeeded and navigate profile/alice
```
Exit 0 (~1 second). This directly validates the reducer sequence; React clicks, the managed timer, CLJS compilation and full tests were not executed. Existing settings tests in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:610-685 settle a canned request synchronously, so never perform logout between submission and completion.

Smallest repair: give settings completions explicit session ownership and refuse both success/error side effects after that ownership is retired by logout/account change; optionally cancel the actual pending request on logout as cleanup, but cancellation alone must also handle an already queued reply. Keep ordinary settings success for the still-current session. No global concurrency scheduler or auth API redesign is needed.

Focused acceptance in both examples: park actual example settings request/mutation, logout through :auth/flow, deliver success and failure; auth user/token remain nil and no stale profile navigation/form settlement occurs. Also cover an old account's reply after a new account signs in, and retain same-session settings success. Test in the existing adapter/example harness, not examples/.

Dedupe: active+closed searches settings logout, realworld session, logout and settings found no matching issue. Read the returned logout memory merged-pr-audit-pr-9323 fully; it is the settled concrete-only resource clear-scope API audit, not this managed settings completion. No resource scope policy change is proposed.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9374 (2026-09-07), landed 111d371cd436ee3095290f220ce3443e8794a6d6: reopen this exact session-completion owner for the remaining resources-twin account-switch path. The new guard reads CURRENT settings-form/session-owner (:settings/replied, settings.cljs:166), and :settings/load overwrites that field with whichever user owns the newly seeded draft (:87-89). The actual /settings route runs that load on entry (routing.cljs:138-145). The request still captures no owner in its continuation: :settings/submit emits :reply-to [:settings/replied] at :139.

Reproduction: Alice starts a parked settings save; logs out; Bob signs in; Bob opens Settings before Alice's reply arrives; Alice's success is then delivered. Bob's route entry has changed both the current auth username and the current draft owner to bob, so owns-session? compares bob with bob and accepts Alice's old User/token. It overwrites Bob's auth with Alice and navigates to Alice's profile. Merely switching accounts without opening Settings is correctly rejected, which is all the new account-switch regression exercises.

Executed an isolated bb probe over the exact landed source FORMS (not a rewritten algorithm): auth/store-session-db, session-owner, owns-session?, settings/draft-from-user, settings/load, settings/submit, and settings/replied. With no Bob settings re-entry, the old reply yields no db write (control). Add the real load handler before the same reply and the result writes username alice plus its synthetic token and emits profile navigation; assertions pass, exit 0. Evidence: ai/pr-audit-9374/probe-session-owner-re-frame2-1.clj and gate-session-owner-re-frame2-1.log/.exit. This is a reducer/continuation seam reproduction; full browser, auth-machine and managed transport execution are not claimed. Source separately confirms the supported route triggers that seam and clears resource reads without retiring this mutation.

Smallest completion: bind immutable issuing-session ownership to each settings reply/continuation, independent of the mutable page draft; preserve the ordinary same-session detour/rename behavior and reject departed-session success/error consequences. Add Bob's actual Settings route/load between account switch and delivery in the existing parked-request regression. The original owner's acceptance also requests logout through auth/flow and both success/failure in both twins; current additions deliver success after direct auth/clear-session only. Retain those existing criteria rather than rewriting them. No generic scheduler, new auth API, or resource clear-scope policy change. Original title/description/criteria and notes are preserved; no duplicate Bead.

title: [examples/capabilities/resources] Linearlite loses edits made before a new card receives its server ID
description:
Snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Source unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Linearlite's newly optimistic cards expose title and status controls before their temporary IDs have been reconciled. A user can move/edit a new card during the intentionally delayed create, but the app sends the temporary ID to a server which knows only its server ID. The follow-up write reports success while doing nothing; creation's accepted reply replaces the temporary card and loses the visible follow-up change.

Concrete path in examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:
- create event at 503-511 mints tmp-N and create optimistic patch at 256-263 inserts the clickable card. Request at 280-283 sends only title (not that ID).
- Real demo stub apply-write! at 389-418 immediately creates srv-N, and returns that row; http-stub at 460-464 delays delivery by demo-reply-delay-ms=220 (353-358).
- issue-card at 582-618 computes pending? only for a badge/class. Title on-click at 612-614 and status-picker at 572-580 remain enabled on tmp-N.
- These handlers invoke edit-title/change-status, whose request URLs at 305-308 and 330-333 use the supplied ID verbatim, e.g. PUT /api/issues/tmp-1.

title: [implementation/core/events] Path-focused events without a db effect let flows overwrite the root app-db
description:
## Problem and impact

A legal path-focused event that emits no `:db` effect can replace the entire app-db with its focused subtree when flows are loaded. Returning `nil`, `{}`, or `{:fx []}` all reproduce. This can erase unrelated application state during an ordinary no-op or effect-only action. The event need not register, clear, or otherwise change any flow.

Surface: implementation/core/events, specifically the standard path interceptor and the router's flow integration. Reviewed snapshot: `7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd`. The relevant router, standard-interceptor, and flow-evaluator files have no diff against mayor main `e4d949e8e87893ad638ed97e3d087fda1f62f0d4` checked before filing.

## Expected behavior and existing contract

The handler receives its focused slice, while the framework's outermost flow pass evaluates against the complete app-db. A focused event that produces no state effect must preserve the full root and all sibling state. Existing root flows should remain materialized from their actual root inputs.

`spec/002-Frames.md:2070` explicitly says flows read full-app-db input paths. The standard-path rules at `spec/002-Frames.md:2573` say that no handler `:db` effect must not create a synthetic path write. The persistent memory `event-pipeline-atomicity` confirms the full-app-db flow input and one deferred install. These contracts compose without any new public API or application workaround.

## Reproduction

Executed in a fresh isolated Babashka process with the actual `implementation/core/src` and `implementation/flows/src` on its classpath, using the plain-atom adapter. No copied evaluator or mock flow hook is involved:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
         '[re-frame.flows :as flows]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as pa])
(rf/init! pa/adapter)
(rf/reg-event :review/unfocused (fn [_ _] {}))
(rf/reg-event :review/focused
  {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:cart]]]}
  (fn [_ _] {:fx []}))
(rf/make-frame
  {:id :review/frame
   :initial-events
   [[:rf/set-db {:cart {:items [1]} :counter 2 :sibling :keep}]]})
(flows/reg-flow :review/derived
  {:frame :review/frame :inputs [[:counter]] :output-path [:derived]}
  (fn [n] (or n 0)))
;; Direct reg-flow correctly waits for the next ordinary drain.
(rf/dispatch-sync [:review/unfocused] {:frame :review/frame})
(rf/app-db-value :review/frame)
;; => {:cart {:items [1]}, :counter 2, :sibling :keep, :derived 2}
(rf/dispatch-sync [:review/focused] {:frame :review/frame})
(rf/app-db-value :review/frame)
;; ACTUAL => {:items [1], :derived 0}
;; EXPECTED => {:cart {:items [1]}, :counter 2, :sibling :keep, :derived 2}
(rf/destroy-frame! :review/frame)
```

The bounded control probe ran the same sequence on four separate frames. `nil`, `{}`, and `{:fx []}` handler results each lost the root exactly as above. Returning an explicit focused `{:db {:items [1]}}` preserved the full root and `:derived 2`. Both probe processes exited 0 and took approximately 2-4 seconds; exit 0 means the observation scripts completed, not that the defective behavior passed an assertion. No build, shared test suite, CLJS runtime, or production bundle was executed. The involved event/path/flow branches are shared `.cljc` code; CLJS behavior remains to be verified by the fixing worker.

## Exact causal path

1. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc:175` replaces `[:coeffects :db]` with the `[:cart]` slice.
2. Its `:after` at lines 177-204 pops the saved full-db/slice pair. It widens `[:effects :db]` only when that effect exists and never restores `[:coeffects :db]`. Thus a no-db result leaves the coeffect focused.
3. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1787` selects the pending app-db: without a `:db` effect, line 1789 reads the final context's still-focused `:coeffects :db`.
4. The actual `run-flows-on-db` invocation at router line 1875 receives `{:items [1]}` as the root. `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:295` reads root input `[:counter]` as nil rather than 2. The dirty check therefore recomputes; its output write at line 335 yields `{:items [1], :derived 0}`.
5. Router lines 1907-1908 stage that new map as a root `:db` effect, and `commit-frame-effects!` installs it into the app partition. No path widening remains after the outermost flow interceptor, so the sibling keys are gone.

The existing `flow-reads-full-db-under-path-scoped-handler` regression in `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1913` exercises only handlers that return `:db`; its path widening succeeds and cannot expose this fallback branch.

## Smallest repair and acceptance

Ensure the no-db fallback into the outermost flow transform is the complete pre-event app-db, preserving path focusing for the handler. Restoring the saved coeffect during path unwind or retaining an unambiguous root snapshot for the framework are possible small repairs; select the one consistent with interceptor composition. Do not make callers add a redundant `:db` return, skip the ordinary flow pass, add a second install, or introduce a public flag.

- The reproducer preserves every root key and the correct derived value for `nil`, `{}`, and an actual effect-only return.
- The effect-only case executes its effect once and sees the intact committed root; the flow does not derive from fabricated nil root inputs.
- Nested path references preserve the same behavior; existing path `:db` widening and identical-object no-op behavior remain intact.
- With no pending flow changes, a no-db focused event does not manufacture a root state write.
- A focused CLJ/CLJS integration regression exercises the actual router plus flows; maintain one deferred app-db commit and existing flow-failure atomicity.

## Duplicate and decision review

Searched open and closed tracker entries by focus/path/interceptor/flow terms, then searched the full all-status issue JSON locally across descriptions and notes for path-scoped and focused-flow integration. No issue owns this no-db root replacement. Related closed `rf2-kh73v` concerns automatic settling and ordering of flow lifecycle effects; `rf2-g1zb` concerns direct clear-flow; `rf2-f3yl` preserves deliberate direct-reg-flow deferral. Their relevant descriptions, notes, and close rulings were read. This issue preserves all three decisions. `event-pipeline-atomicity` was read in full and supports the expected full-root input. The duplicate search and exact source comparison happened before filing.
acceptance_criteria: No-db and effect-only path-focused handlers preserve full root app-db and correct flow inputs, including nested paths; focused db writes and identity no-ops remain intact; actual router-plus-flows CLJ/CLJS regression covers the fallback without a new API or second install.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9384 (0dd38947d4319422903e0ac61c8a828918e49cfe, merged 2026-09-07T13:04:37Z). The path unwind repair restores the original full db object before the outer flow pass, including nested paths, and the normative rule now says so. Reopening only the original integration-acceptance remainder; no additional runtime defect asserted.

All new bw76 tests are in interceptor_test.clj, so the new actual-router-plus-flows nil/empty/effect-only/nested cases run on the JVM only. The existing CLJC interceptor_runtime_complete_cljs_test path-no-db-effect-emits-no-synthetic-db case has no registered flow, and its nested test emits :db; neither reaches the root-input fallback with a live derived flow. Searches of the CLJS/CLJC core and flows corpus found no equivalent focused no-db-with-flow case. The PR's claim that CI will exercise the two new CLJC test namespaces does not apply to this .clj namespace.

The original acceptance also asks for an ACTUAL effect-only return whose effect runs once and sees the intact committed root. The new :bw76/fx-only handler returns {:fx []}, which tests the no-db shape but executes no effect, so it cannot witness that ordering/count. Port or add the small actual router/flows regression to the existing CLJC test surface, covering nil, {}, one real effect, and nested focus; assert root-derived value, sibling preservation and the effect's single post-commit observation. Keep existing focused-write/identity/failure-atomicity controls and one deferred install, without a new API or alternate flow model. Preserve the original criteria.

Actual CI 34123467697 passed core JVM 2264/11699, core production 1985/8493, Node 11377/57394 and browser 815/4466, all zero failures/errors. All eight changed code/test blobs match CI and landed; the ninth path, Spec 002, differs only by #9375's separately reviewed Hicasso additions at integration. These greens establish the runtime repair's existing coverage, not the missing CLJS/real-effect acceptance. No new local suite run.
close_reason: Delivered by PR #9395 (worker feat-b), merged at e2d1981990. The premise does NOT hold as a live runtime defect at tip and that is recorded rather than glossed: the rule-6 unwind (assoc-in [:coeffects :db] original-db) is present and correct in std_interceptors.cljc, landed by the earlier PR the audit note names. What the merged-PR audit reopened this bead for was the ACCEPTANCE remainder, and both halves of that were genuinely outstanding, verified at source rather than assumed: every existing rf2-bw76 test sits in implementation/core/test/re_frame/interceptor_test.clj, a .clj namespace that is JVM-only, while the event/path/flow branches are shared .cljc — and the two existing CLJC path cases cannot reach the fallback at all (one registers no flow, the other emits :db, whose widening succeeds). {:fx []} pinned the no-:db shape but executed nothing, so nothing witnessed the ordering the acceptance asks for. New implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_path_focused_no_db_cljs_test.cljc: 4 deftests / 11 assertions over nil, {}, {:fx []}, a nested focus, and an actual effect that must run once and observe the intact committed root, plus the focused-write widening control and an identical? control proving no synthetic root write and one deferred install. It lives in the flows artefact because core's test tree cannot require re-frame.flows, and is named *-cljs-test.cljc so shadow's :node-test discovers it AND the cognitect JVM runner runs it. FAILING-FIRST: with rule 6's restore reverted to original-slice, exit 1 with 6 of 11 assertions failing, reproducing this bead's recorded ACTUAL verbatim — {:items [1], :derived 0} against the expected full root — which is the confirmation that the originally executed Babashka reproduction still describes pre-fix behaviour. Post-fix exit 0. Restore verified by git blob hash 2defad0db9c3a99a49c8e5b5111d4cf11202f08d, identical before and after.

=== ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (2026-09-05, STALE AS TO THE FIX) ===
FOUND BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 while chasing rf2-2qa7, which expected the first Windows CI leg to run at merge. It did not run, and this is why.

## What is established, by measurement

Run 33946468214 of `.github/workflows/post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml`, on merge commit `73ac28b7af` (PR #9276, which edited `expensive-tests.yml`). Its runtime output, read with the ANSI command-echo lines filtered OUT (the echo lines are the script's source, not its output — my first read matched those and told me nothing):

    dispatching: expensive-tests.yml
    could not create workflow dispatch event: HTTP 422: No ref found for: 73ac28b7af7fbdce3d8a07cacb3e030cb1aa191f
      (https://api.github.com/repos/day8/re-frame2/actions/workflows/277358356/dispatches)
    WARN: gh workflow run failed for expensive-tests.yml (non-fatal)

**Job conclusion: success.** The run is `completed/success`.

## The mechanism

`post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml:200` is `gh workflow run "$f" --ref "${{ github.sha }}" || { echo "WARN: ..."; }`.

Two independent halves, and both need fixing:

1. **`--ref` takes a REF, not a commit SHA.** The Actions dispatch endpoint resolves `ref` as a branch or tag name; a 40-character commit id is not one, hence 422 "No ref found for". `${{ github.sha }}` is always a commit id, so this argument can never succeed as written.
2. **The failure is swallowed by `||` and the job goes green.** So the workflow whose ENTIRE PURPOSE is to close a 24-hour feedback gap on workflow edits reports success while having dispatched nothing. This is the fail-open shape: a green that means "we tried", read by every reader as "it ran".

## What is NOT established — do not overstate it in the fix

I checked the last TEN sanity runs. Only ONE of them attempted a dispatch at all (the other nine printed no dispatch lines — most pushes change no workflow file). So the measured record is **1 attempt, 1 failure**, not "always broken". `expensive-tests.yml` does have 5 `workflow_dispatch` runs among its last 60, so the endpoint has succeeded at some point — plausibly from manual `gh workflow run` with a branch name. **Establish the real history before writing a claim into the file**: search sanity runs further back for `dispatching: ` lines and report how many attempts there have been and how many succeeded.

## Consequence right now

`expensive-tests.yml` has not run since 2026-09-04T15:25:53Z. PR #9276's `mcp-live-windows` job — the repo's first Windows leg — has therefore **never executed**. Its first opportunity is the scheduled nightly at 15:17 UTC. rf2-2qa7 (read the first two nightly runs) is the live path, and rf2-hhw6's close reason has been corrected to say so.

## The fix, on the merits

The obvious repair is `--ref "${{ github.ref_name }}"` (or literally `main`), which dispatches the workflow at the branch tip. **Note the semantic change and decide it deliberately rather than by accident**: dispatching at the branch tip is not the same as dispatching at the merge commit, and if two workflow-editing merges land close together the second dispatch covers both. For this workflow's purpose — "does the edited workflow still run" — the tip is arguably the RIGHT target, since that is what tonight's nightly will use. Say which you chose and why.

The `||` is the other half. A dispatch that fails is not a non-fatal condition for a workflow that exists to dispatch: at minimum it must fail the step, or set a job-level annotation that is visible without opening the log. Weigh `set -e` semantics against the file's own stated reason for the `||` (read the surrounding comment before removing it — the comment at :35 says none of the excluded workflows declare `workflow_dispatch`, so there may be a case the `||` was protecting). If the `||` is genuinely load-bearing for a case the loop already skips, narrow it rather than deleting it.

## Verification is the hard part and the deliverable

A fix you cannot exercise is a guess. `workflow_dispatch` behaviour cannot be proven from a PR branch, because the workflow that runs is the one on the DEFAULT branch. State plainly what you verified and what you could not:
- You CAN verify the argument shape against the API contract and against a manual `gh workflow run expensive-tests.yml --ref <branch>` from your own checkout — do that and quote the result.
- You CANNOT verify the merged behaviour until a workflow-editing commit lands on main. Say so, and note that THIS PR is itself such a commit, so the next sanity run after it merges is the natural witness — name that as the acceptance check and leave the bead for the mayor to close on the evidence.

## Fence
IN: `.github/workflows/post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml`.
OUT: every other workflow file. `.github/workflows/*` is hot-zone and sequential — no other bead may touch that directory while this is live.

title: api(boot): init! throws :rf.error/adapter-already-installed when a different adapter is already seated
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from boot.md (ref boot.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`rf/init!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2660-2697`) seats an adapter only when none is seated — line 2682: `(when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter) (rf.substrate.adapter/install-adapter! adapter-map))`. A second `init!` with a DIFFERENT adapter — `(rf/init! reagent/adapter)` then `(rf/init! uix/adapter)` — returns `nil`, leaves the first adapter seated and emits nothing. That is the shape `spec/Conventions.md:1149-1160` §No silent swallow forbids: a recognised input the runtime cannot honour MUST signal. The owning-namespace `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` (`substrate/adapter.cljc:124-175`) already throws `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` on any second call; the facade's front door hides it.

## Evidence (tip 3fbd3a9ede)

- `core.cljc:2682` — the `when-not (current-adapter)` guard; no identity or kind check.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/boot_test.clj:74-97` `init-is-idempotent` asserts the SAME map twice (`identical?` on `current-adapter-spec`); `:99-125` `install-adapter-rejects-double-install` covers the owning fn only; `:423` covers `destroy-adapter!` → `init!` with a different adapter. No test covers `init!` → `init!` with a different adapter.
- `substrate/adapter.cljc:728` `same-adapter?` — the discriminator already exists and is public: two maps carrying the same canonical `:rf.adapter/*` `:kind` are the same adapter even across a copy / `assoc` / re-evaluation (stable token, rf2-dkl5z1); otherwise object identity, so two custom adapters are never conflated; nil-safe. Used by `route-hook!` and by test-react's mount guard (`adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:457`).
- Hot reload decides the discriminator. Every adapter Var is a plain `def` (`adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:185`, `reagent_slim.cljs:108`, `uix.cljs:228`, `hicasso/substrate.cljs:137`, `core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc:145`, `ssr/substrate.cljc:68`), so a reload re-evaluates the map with fresh fn identities — and 30 of the 40 files under `examples/` + `tools/template` that call `(rf/init! …)` call it from a `^:dev/after-load` fn. An `identical?` / `=` rule would throw on every reload; `same-adapter?` does not.

## Target API

```clojure
;; before — core.cljc:2682
(when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter)
  (rf.substrate.adapter/install-adapter! adapter-map))

;; after — one line; the throw stays in the owner and is never duplicated in the facade
(when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/same-adapter? adapter-map
                                               (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter-spec))
  (rf.substrate.adapter/install-adapter! adapter-map))
```

Semantics: nothing seated → install. Seated and `same-adapter?` (same canonical kind, or the identical custom map) → idempotent no-op exactly as today. Seated and different → `install-adapter!` throws `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` (`:where 'rf/init!`, `:extra {:installed <seated> :attempted <arg>}`, `:recovery :no-recovery`) and the seated adapter is untouched. Update the reason string at `adapter.cljc:155` so it also names this path ("a second `init!` / `install-adapter!` with a different adapter and no intervening `(rf/destroy-adapter!)` …"). The three registrar re-seeds (`:2687-2696`) run as before. `init!`'s docstring (`:2661`) gains the rule and the hot-reload sentence from Risks.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area (fable boot doc), but codex's cross-check independently endorses this slice: "really does ignore a different adapter map once one is installed. Correcting that is worthwhile independently of name pruning. Define idempotence against the installed adapter specification — not merely `:kind` … decide explicitly what hot reload means … Keep the actual seating, generation and rollback logic in the existing adapter owner; do not duplicate it in the facade." `same-adapter?` is that definition (canonical-kind token, identity fallback), hot reload of a canonical adapter is the same-adapter no-op, and the throw stays in `adapter.cljc`.

## Deletion list

None.

## Consumers to migrate

None change. All 34 example boots, both template scaffolds (`tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:38`, `_uix/core.cljs:40`) and the ssr-ring host call `init!` with one canonical adapter per process; the after-load re-calls are same-adapter no-ops. `skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs:78-100` re-inits a different adapter only after `destroy-adapter!` — unaffected.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` (HOT-ZONE): §Adapter selection at boot `:2066` — state the `init!` rule beside the `install-adapter!` sentence; `:2242` "Re-installing after frames exist is an error" — add "or `init!` with a different adapter".
- `spec/API.md` (HOT-ZONE): `:866` `init!` row — "idempotent boot" → "idempotent for the seated adapter (same canonical `:kind`, or the identical custom map); a different adapter raises `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` — `destroy-adapter!` first to swap".
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT-ZONE): `:2250` `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` row — add the `init!` path; while there, fix its stale `dispose-adapter!` (the public verb is `destroy-adapter!`, `Conventions.md:1390`).
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:748-764` `init!` entry (hand-written page, not generated).
- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:224` scenario — add the `init!`-with-a-different-adapter variant (optional, not hot-zone).
- Tests — `boot_test.clj`, new `init-rejects-a-different-adapter` beside `init-is-idempotent`: (1) `init!` plain-atom, then `init!` a distinct map with a different kind (e.g. `(assoc rf.substrate.plain-atom/adapter :kind ::other)`) → throws with `:rf.error/id :rf.error/adapter-already-installed`, `:installed` identical to the seated map, seated identity unchanged after the throw; (2) hot-reload CONTROL: a structural copy of the seated canonical map (`(assoc rf.substrate.plain-atom/adapter :doc "reloaded")`) → no throw, seated identity unchanged; (3) two distinct kind-less custom maps → throws (identity fallback). `same-adapter?` is `.cljc` and already exercised on CLJS by `react_shared_suite`; a CLJS mirror is optional.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: no row change; run the drift check anyway (`cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check`).
- Migration README: no v1-era name changes. Conformance corpus / mcp-conformance: not affected (no boot fixtures).

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches `API.md`, `006`, `009` → serialise with @boot.2 (`API.md`, `009`), @boot.3 (all three) and any open bead on those files. @boot.4's implementation bead 1 (delete facade `install-adapter!`) is BLOCKED BY this bead: the facade must throw on a different adapter before the throwing door is removed. Related: rf2-uimu (lifecycle-verb roster has no `install-*`) — unaffected here.

## Risks

Low. The only behaviour change a production app can meet converts a silent misconfiguration into the error the runtime already owns. One honest cost: a CUSTOM adapter whose `:kind` is not under `:rf.adapter/*` (or has none) falls to the identity comparison, so re-evaluating its Var on hot reload and re-calling `init!` throws — the remedy is `defonce` on the custom adapter Var, or `destroy-adapter!` in the after-load fn; write that sentence into 006 §Adapter selection at boot and the `init!` docstring. Every shipped adapter carries a canonical kind and is unaffected.

description:

Each is a dated review, each says so, and none has been re-read since the surfaces it scores were retired or its findings were corrected. A reader who takes a checkpoint page as a statement about the CURRENT tree is misled, and three of the four pages invite exactly that by writing their rows in the present tense.

1. checkpoint-4-coverage.md's newest amendment is dated 2026-08-15. The required-result amendment that scopes mismatch attribution landed as 137bd927db (PR #8646) on 2026-08-21 and this page has never read it: a search of the page for 8646, 137bd927db, r3dgc, 0brem, vwo53 and 6cc52f60fb returns nothing at all. Its conjunct B still enumerates HS-21 among the ids that fail the exit.
2. checkpoint-4-coverage.md:384 records rf2-s52w as 'open' and its cause as 'A missing door; the ledger row is open too, and the door is the operator's call'. The tracker reads rf2-s52w closed; the ledger row reads resolved; and the ledger's own 2026-08-21 amendment records that BOTH clauses of that stated root cause are now wrong — re-frame.hicasso.server/render landed as 30317bfe0e on 2026-08-14, and the two named SSR suites were retargeted onto it.

What is wanted is the cheapest possible currency statement — a dated banner at the head of each page naming the tip it was last reconciled to and the events since that its rows do not reflect — plus correction of the five cells above beside themselves, in the convention those pages already use.

title: Make implementor skill trigger description validator-safe
description:
## Scope

Repair the frontmatter description in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md` so
the skill-creator validator accepts the shipped skill. Keep the public skill
directory, frontmatter name, trigger behavior, exclusions, and all body/reference
content unchanged except for the invalid trigger-example placeholder wording.

## Finding

The description contains the trigger example `implement re-frame2 in
<language>`. The required `quick_validate.py` validator rejects any `<` or `>`
in frontmatter descriptions, so the current skill fails validation before any
normal skill routing can occur.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:16` contains the literal trigger text
  `implement re-frame2 in <language>` in the YAML `description`.
- `C:\\Users\\miket\\.codex\\skills\\.system\\skill-creator\\scripts\\quick_validate.py`
  rejects descriptions containing `<` or `>`.
- Running the validator against the current package returns exit 1 with
  `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is a frontmatter-description clarity/validator-compatibility fix only.
Preserve `name: re-frame2-implementor`, the eight-host scope, the three trigger
concepts (port re-frame2, implement re-frame2 in a host language, conformance
corpus), all do-not-use routing, allowed tools, eval fixtures, filenames,
references, package/plugin metadata, and skill body semantics. Do not rename the
public skill or directory, alter invocation policy, or change any spec/conformance
terminology. No Phase-1 vestigial/removal target is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The frontmatter description contains no angle brackets or unfinished
   placeholders and still clearly triggers on porting re-frame2 to a host
   language and on conformance-corpus work.
2. `quick_validate.py` run against the absolute skill directory exits 0 and
   prints `Skill is valid!`.
3. A planted angle-bracket trigger placeholder in a temporary validation copy
   makes `quick_validate.py` exit 1 with the expected diagnostic; restoring the
   clean skill returns exit 0.
4. `git diff --check` is clean and the diff is limited to the one frontmatter
   description phrase.
acceptance_criteria: Validator clean pass; planted angle-bracket control red; restored clean pass; exact one-phrase diff and no routing/public-name changes.
notes: 2026-09-03 landing verification (worker skillval-a): the fix IS on main. Commit d9055f01c1 'fix(implementor-skill): make trigger description validator-safe' landed during this session; git merge-base --is-ancestor d9055f01c1 origin/main exits 0. skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md line 17 now reads 'implement re-frame2 in a language' - the '<language>' angle brackets are gone. Measured: description 1003 chars before AND after (the substitution is length-neutral, 10 chars for 10), no angle brackets, well inside the portable 1024 ceiling. Independently re-ran the gates on a worktree cut from post-fix origin/main: quick_validate.py against the absolute skill dir exits 0 printing 'Skill is valid!'; check_skill_description_budget.py --verbose --ci exits 0 (re-frame2-implementor resolved 996, headroom 28) and --self-test exits 0. NOTE for anyone reading this bead's history: at the moment this worker started, origin/main was 4fcb998b4e and STILL CARRIED the angle brackets - i.e. the bead was closed before the fix merged, the standard closed-does-not-mean-landed gap. It has since closed. No further work needed.

title: test(story): stop treating the no-op reg-variant row as a browser probe
description:
Finding

`tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs` classifies the `reg-variant` coverage row as a live browser `probe`, but its body only prints `SKIP` and returns. The replacement CLJS test named by the comment already landed, so this is a stale migration shim that makes the feature-load coverage report falsely claim execution.

Evidence

- The file's coverage contract at lines 28-49 defines `kind: 'probe'` to mean the function actually exercises the named feature, says a non-probed row must be `kind: 'owned-by'`, and explicitly says never wire a probe whose body does not exercise the feature.
- The `reg-variant` row at lines 1185-1219 is `kind: 'probe'`, but its `_page` body ends in only `console.warn('SKIP: reg-variant scenario · migrating to CLJS unit per rf2-8awk1'); return;`. It performs no browser or product operation. A repo-wide search finds this as the only unconditional `SKIP:` in Story source/tests/testbeds.
- The row comment says this is temporary until `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/panels_e2e/reg_variant_e2e_cljs_test.cljs` is merged. That replacement exists and says it replaces the Playwright probe; it covers the four named variants plus registration shape. Git commit `c47f1925c3` (2026-05-20) added the CLJS replacement and converted the browser row to the no-op in the same landed change, so the temporary state has already outlived its condition.
- `validateCoverageMatrix` at lines 1538-1575 checks only that a probe is a function. `assertCoverageMatrix` at lines 1578-1596 awaits the no-op and records only `owned-by` rows as declared out-of-scope. Thus the row completes green as if directly exercised, and verbose output does not disclose it among ownership skips (apart from an easy-to-miss warning inside the fake probe).
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:82` still lists `test:story-feature-load` as an owning gate and promises selecting every sidebar variant, including post-burst verification. The same file's helper table at line 425 still binds `assertMatrixVariant` to the `reg-variant` row, although this row never calls it. The separate live `Sidebar navigation` probe deliberately skips `clicked-three-times` and owns navigation, not the no-op row's claimed lifecycle/state contract.
