title: xray: a dead ^{:key ...} on a call form in epoch/view.cljs — discarded on BOTH substrates, inside a for
description:
A `^{:key ...}` ATTACHED TO A CALL FORM, SO THE KEY IS DISCARDED AND NEVER REACHES REACT --
inside a `for`, which is precisely where sibling keys matter.

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk b6441eaddf, with a nonsense control reading absent:

    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:3683
        ^{:key (str "cascade-row-wrap-" (:step row))}
        (cascade-row-view machine-meta row)

    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:3507
        (defn- cascade-row-view

`cascade-row-view` is a plain `defn-`, so the reader metadata rides the LIST FORM and is gone
the moment that form is evaluated -- the returned hiccup vector carries none of it. React
therefore receives no key for these siblings and reconciles the cascade rows BY INDEX.

=== THIS IS THE rf2-hxfy CLASS, AND IT IS THE DEAD-ON-BOTH-SUBSTRATES MEMBER ===

Distinguish it carefully from rf2-twil's finding, which is the OPPOSITE member of the same
family and is why the two must not be merged into one item:

  - rf2-twil / `trace.cljs`  -- `^{:key ...}` on a VECTOR LITERAL. Reagent reads metadata then
    props, so the key DOES reach React today; it dies only when that panel becomes a Fresco
    boundary. Latent.
  - THIS one -- `^{:key ...}` on a CALL FORM. It reaches React on NEITHER substrate and never
    did. Not latent: dead now.

So this is not blocked on the Fresco migration and can be repaired independently.

=== THE REPAIR ===

Move the key into the returned hiccup's attribute map, which satisfies both substrates because
Reagent reads meta then props -- the standing direction, and the same repair rf2-hxfy took.

=== HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND THE CENSUS FIGURE ===

Reported by the rf2-4bsq worker (keyxing-a) while working an unrelated repair, and correctly
NOT swept -- it is outside that bead's two files. Its census read 59 `^{:key` hits across 26
files against the mayor's independent count; of those, this is the one real call-form hit, two
further candidates were the worker's own regex artefacts, and ZERO were in its two in-scope
files (both of which use `[:<> {:key ...}]`, which is correct).

=== A TRAP FOR WHOEVER TESTS THIS ===

Do NOT assert with `(meta ...)`. `rf.test-helpers/expand-tree` rebuilds nested vectors with
`mapv`, which STRIPS reader metadata, so a probe navigating through it reads a FALSE `nil`.
Worse, `(meta ...)` reads `nil` at a REPAIRED site too, because the key then lives in the
attribute map -- so a metadata assertion is hollow in BOTH directions, green on the broken code
and red on the fixed code. Assert at the renderer that React actually receives the key.
notes:
=== WORKER FINDING (epochkey-a, PR #9626) — THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED, THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT ===

CONFIRMED: `^{:key (str "cascade-row-wrap-" (:step row))}` at view.cljs:3683 sits on the
`(cascade-row-view machine-meta row)` CALL FORM; `cascade-row-view` is a plain `defn-` at 3507,
so the metadata rides the source list and is discarded on evaluation. It contributes nothing on
any substrate. That half of the bead is exactly right.

REFUTED, AND MEASURED IN THE WORKER TREE: "React receives no key for these siblings and
reconciles the cascade rows BY INDEX." React was already receiving a distinct key for every row.

WHY: `cascade-row-view`'s own returned root div carries `:key (str "cascade-row-" step)` in its
ATTRIBUTE MAP (view.cljs:3535). `git log -L` puts that line in `4d3ccc12f8` (rf2-u69j7) — THE
SAME COMMIT that introduced the dead metadata. So the repair the brief prescribes ("move the key
into the returned hiccup's attribute map") was already in place before the bead was filed; the
reader metadata was a DECOY SITTING OVER A WORKING KEY, not a lost key.

ALL THREE RENDERERS HONOUR THE PROPS SPELLING — read at source, not inferred:
  - stock Reagent 2.0.1 (what tools/xray/deps.edn pins): `convert-props` copies every props
    entry into jsprops, `key` included — no filtering — and `make-element` hands that to
    `createElement`, which extracts it.
  - reagent-slim (reagent2/impl/template.cljs, `react-key-from-meta-or-props`): its own
    docstring states the rule — meta wins, "failing that, the props map's `:key`".
  - Fresco codec: `codec_cljs_test.cljs` pins a props-map key landing on the element.

THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT (renderer-level, not metadata): a new gate reads `.-key` off real React
elements via `r/as-element` over a raw meta-preserving walk.
  - Against UNMODIFIED trunk view.cljs, dead meta still present: PASSES, React receives
    ["cascade-row-1" "cascade-row-2" "cascade-row-3"].
  - With the attribute-map `:key` deleted and everything else left alone: FAILS [nil nil nil],
    3 of 4 assertions, row-count precondition still passing.
That second row is the hollow-gate check the brief demanded and it is the regression this gate
actually guards: a future editor deleting the props `:key` on the belief that "the key is at the
call site" is the live hazard, which is precisely what the decoy invited.

SO THE REPAIR SHIPPED IS: delete the decoy, pin the real key with a renderer-level gate, and say
at both ends where the key can and cannot live. It is a clarity + regression-guard change, NOT a
behaviour fix. Nothing in the panel painted or reconciled differently before and after.

TEST DESIGN: `machine-cascade-rows-reach-react-with-distinct-keys` in
tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view_cljs_test.cljs, following the merged
rf2-hxfy precedent in managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs. It does NOT assert `(meta ...)` —
hollow in both directions, since `expand-tree` rebuilds vectors with `mapv` and strips reader
metadata, and a correctly-keyed row reads nil anyway because the key lives in props. It reaches
the rows through the PUBLIC `view/machine-cascade-mini-pipeline`, the same entry the Epoch panel
EVENT HANDLER step and the Machine tab both render through.

VERIFICATION: full CLJS node-test suite 11583 tests / 58095 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors;
compile 0 warnings.

line 1284; static/machines/sim_cljs_test.cljs lines 835 and 869; static/flows/panel_cljs_test.cljs
lines 357 and 367. Not touched — two of those files' panels are held.

Status left in_progress deliberately: the PR is open and the merge is the mayor's call.

=== CENSUS WIDENED AND RE-RUN — SUPERSEDES THE tools/xray/src FIGURES ABOVE ===

The first census in this note was scoped to tools/xray/src, and a follow-up pass found that
scope had missed most of the repo. Re-run over the FULL TRACKED ROSTER
(`git ls-files '*.clj' '*.cljs' '*.cljc'` — 2956 files), classifying each hit by what the
metadata ACTUALLY ATTACHES TO rather than by the regex alone:

    333 `^{:key` hits across 128 files
      271  vector literal   — correct under Reagent; the rf2-twil class at a Fresco boundary
       61  prose / other    — docstrings and comments, several of them documenting prior
                              repairs of this same class (the regex artefacts the brief predicted)
        1  CALL FORM        — see below

Instrument controlled in the positive direction, so a low count means absence rather than a
broken pattern: run against the PRE-FIX copy of this bead's own file it reports
`CALL-FORM 1` at line 3683 alongside 6 vector literals.

So repo-wide there were EXACTLY TWO call-form sites before this change: the one repaired here,
and one other, which REMAINS.

=== THE REMAINING ONE IS A GENUINELY DEAD KEY, AND UNLIKE rf2-wvch HAS NO WORKING KEY UNDER IT ===

    tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/visual_a11y_view.cljs:249

        (for [[i {:keys [kind] :as row}] (map-indexed vector rows)]
          ^{:key (str kind "#" i)}
          (if (= kind :visual)
            [visual-card row]
            [a11y-card row]))

The metadata rides the `(if ...)` FORM, so it is discarded on evaluation and neither branch's
vector carries it. THE FALLBACK WAS CHECKED, and that is what makes this different from

inside a `for`, so sibling keys matter, and the branches are component-head vectors whose
identity is what index-based reconciliation scrambles on a re-order or a filter change.

NOT SWEPT — outside this bead's scope (tools/story, not tools/xray). Worth its own bead, and
the gate pattern shipped here transfers to it directly.

title: docs: two-space nested lists render FLAT under python-markdown, so nested structure is lost on the published site
description:
NESTED LISTS INDENTED BY TWO SPACES DO NOT NEST IN THE PUBLISHED DOCS. They render as FLAT SIBLINGS of their parent, so a two-level structure the author wrote arrives as one undifferentiated list. === MEASURED BY THE MAYOR, ON THIS REPO'S OWN TOOLCHAIN (fact) === Python-Markdown 3.10, the renderer MkDocs uses, with this repo's extension set from mkdocs.yml (`meta`, `admonition`, `footnotes`, `toc`; no `sane_lists`, no `mdx_truly_sane_lists`). Input: - Parent bullet with a two-space child: - two-space child A - Parent bullet with a four-space child: - four-space child A Output:

  • two-space child A

title: api(registry): add (rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f}) and delete the nine clear-* names
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:18:53 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.25 ruling agent (delegated by Mike); parent epic rf2-kuky; discovered-from rf2-kuky.25 (Q2 ruled **E**). The full decision dossier, both reviewers' analyses, the census and the ruling are attached as notes on rf2-kuky.25 — read them there; nothing under `ai/` is tracked._

## Ruling (verbatim from rf2-kuky.25)

> Q2 → **E**: one kind-keyed `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})` on `re-frame.core`, dispatching to each kind's OWNING lifecycle fn and never short-cutting a kind that owns runtime state to `registrar/unregister!`; opts EXACTLY `{:frame f}` and fail-closed, accepted for the two frame-scoped kinds only; unknown kind fails closed; returns the id for every kind; every per-kind public `clear-*` registrar-inverse name is deleted — no shim, no alias, no deprecation. Parity through the EXISTING resource-dispose / route-trace / flow-settle tests is the acceptance bar.

## Problem

The registrar is one map, `(kind, id) → metadata` (`spec/001-Registration.md:89`). The read side already speaks that grammar — `(handler-meta kind id)`, `(registrations kind)`. The inverse does not: nine public names in three shapes, differing on FOUR axes (where the name lives — 7 on the facade, 2 off it; whether a nilary clear-all exists — 3 of 9; how the frame is named — none / tolerant / exact; what comes back — nil for the core five, the id for the other four), and SIX registrar kinds with no public inverse at all (`:cofx :interceptor :view :head :error-projector`, plus per-path app-schemas) although `registrar/unregister!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:713`) already takes `(kind id)` for every registrar kind, forgets provenance, marks the live-frame projection dirty and emits `:rf.registry/handler-cleared`.

**The motivating defect (live at HEAD `13884f326f`).** `re-frame.flows/clear-flow` destructures its opts tolerantly — `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:846-847` is `([id] (clear-flow id {}))` / `([id {:keys [frame] :as _opts}] …)` — so `(flows/clear-flow :cart/total {:fram :session})` binds `frame` to nil, `require-current-frame!` resolves the AMBIENT frame, and the wrong frame's flow is cleared with no signal. That is the exact silent mis-clear rf2-s32bf closed for `clear-http-interceptor` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:231-243`, `valid-clear-opts?` — exactly `{:frame target}`, present, non-nil, no other key, non-map rejected; raises `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` BEFORE any ambient frame is touched), applied to one of two identically-shaped surfaces and not the other. `spec/Principles.md:81` (No silent swallow): a recognised-but-unhonourable input MUST signal. One door with one validator closes it for every frame-scoped kind at once.

## Target API

```clojure
(rf/clear :sub  :cart/total)                       ;; registrar kind → registrar/unregister!; returns :cart/total
(rf/clear :flow :cart/total)                       ;; ambient frame; settles dependents (Spec 013 §Sequencing)
(rf/clear :flow :cart/total {:frame :session})     ;; explicit frame — opts EXACTLY {:frame f}
(rf/clear :flow :cart/total {:fram :session})      ;; THROWS (today: silently clears the AMBIENT frame's flow)
(rf/clear :sub  :cart/total {:frame :session})     ;; THROWS — :sub is not frame-scoped; opts rejected
(rf/clear :cofx :now)                              ;; THE SIX HOLES CLOSE with zero new names
(rf/clear :widget :x)                              ;; THROWS — unknown kind; the message names the closed set
;; (rf/clear :resource :feed) with no resources artefact → the documented :rf.error/resources-artefact-missing

;; HoF position — the only non-test consumer in the corpus, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs
(run! #(rf/clear :sub %)   schema-5-subs-removed)   ;; was (run! rf/clear-sub …)
```

`:rf.fx/clear-flow` is UNCHANGED (it has consumers and takes the same id). `clear-sub-cache!`, `clear-trace-buffer!` and every cache / buffer / test-fixture `clear-*!` are OUT OF SCOPE — this bead is the registrar-inverse arm of the tear-down axis only.

## Closed kind set and dispatch table

`clear`'s kind set is its OWN closed set, documented in `spec/001-Registration.md`'s kind table as a new clear column — it is the registrar's kind set (`registrar.cljc:144-145`) MINUS `:frame` (frames are a live runtime object torn down by `destroy-frame!`, 001:99) PLUS `:http-interceptor` (a per-frame side table owned by the http artefact, not a registrar kind). `:app-schema` is deliberately NOT included (001:112 — not a registrar kind; per-path app-schemas have only `clear-schemas-by-frame!`; nobody has asked — the demand bar).

| kind | routes to | why not `unregister!` | `{:frame f}` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:event` `:sub` `:fx` | `registrar/unregister!` | PARITY BY INSPECTION: `events.cljc:1509`, `subs.cljc:367`, `fx.cljc:162` are literally `(rf.registrar/unregister! kind id)` in their 1-arity | rejected |
| `:cofx` `:interceptor` `:view` `:head` `:error-projector` | `registrar/unregister!` | no owning fn exists today; `unregister!` is the substrate every kind already shares | rejected |
| `:route` | a NEW `rf.core-routing/clear-route` defwrapper → `re-frame.routing.registry/clear-route` (`routing/registry.cljc:594`) | emits `:rf.route/cleared` | rejected |
| `:flow` | `rf.core-flows/clear-flow` (`core_flows.cljc:15`) → `flows/registry.cljc:833` | vacates the output leaf and, outside a drain, SETTLES dependents (rf2-g1zb, PRs #9204/#9257) | accepted |
| `:http-interceptor` | `rf.core-http/clear-http-interceptor` (`core_http.cljc:86`) → `http/middleware.cljc:245` | per-frame chain + `:rf.http.interceptor/cleared` trace | accepted |
| `:resource` `:mutation` `:resource-scope` | `rf.core-resources/clear-resource` / `clear-mutation` / `clear-resource-scope` (`core_resources.cljc:36/96/160`) | `clear-resource` disposes cache entries, timers and in-flight work across ALL frames (`resources/registry.cljc:647-671`) — a `{:frame}` on it is meaningless, hence rejected | rejected |

Artefact-absent still raises the documented `:rf.error/<artefact>-artefact-missing` because the dispatch goes THROUGH the existing defwrappers (the facade row IS the optional-capability mechanism — the manifest's own justification on rows 93-96).

**Two corrections the second reviewer proved against the dossier's sketch, both verified at HEAD — do not copy the sketch literally:**

1. **There is no `rf.core-routing/clear-route` delegate.** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_routing.cljc:15-26` records that the czn2m0 D1 ruling deleted the dormant `clear-route` defwrapper AND its `:routing/clear-route` late-bind hook because nothing consumed them. `rf/clear :route` is now a consumer: add the defwrapper (`:hook :routing/clear-route :artefact routing-artefact :on-absent :throw`), the `set-fn!` in `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc` (beside `:routing/reg-route` at :479), and the directory row in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` (the `:routing/*` block starts :504; the directory test reconciles published hooks against rows, so both go together). Rewrite that :15-26 comment — it will be false.
2. **Omitted opts must reach the owning AMBIENT arity.** `valid-clear-opts?` rejects `nil` and `{}`; the 2-arity `(clear kind id)` therefore calls the owning 1-arity and NEVER normalises an omitted opts to `{}`/`nil` and forwards it into the owning 2-arity. `core_flows.cljc:20`'s `([id] [id {}])` has the same bug in waiting once flows are hardened — make it delegate to the owning 1-arity.

## Opts contract — one validator, three users

- `{:frame f}` is accepted for EXACTLY the two per-frame kinds (`:flow`, `:http-interceptor`), validated with rf2-s32bf's rule (map, sole key `:frame`, value a frame-id keyword or a live frame value — `rf.frame/frame-value?`) BEFORE anything is resolved or mutated. Any opts on any other kind throws. Unknown kind throws.
- LIFT the validator into core (beside `rf.frame/frame-value?`, which it already needs) and use it from THREE places: `rf/clear`, `flows/registry.cljc:847` (harden: the 2-arity becomes exact and fail-closed; the 1-arity stays ambient — it is still the `:flows/clear-flow` hook target and the `:rf.fx/clear-flow` fx reaches it), and `middleware.cljc:231` (replace the private copy). One validator, not two copies.
- ONE new error id for the door's own validation (unknown kind / malformed opts / opts on a non-frame-scoped kind), ex-data carrying `:kind`, `:reason` and the closed set; catalogue it in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` or `python scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` reds (CHECK A). `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` stays for the http fn's own arg validation.
- Return the id for every kind (ends the nil-vs-id split; the `reg-*` return-value convention). Nilary clear-all arities are DROPPED — their only callers are tests, which already have `registrar/clear-kind!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:561`).

## Deletion list (HEAD `13884f326f` line numbers; the dossier's `6d513ba07f` numbers still hold)

title: hygiene: remove-worker-worktree.sh reached CANARY_AFTER but printed no REMOVED=/OK: for a bare-name argument — reproduce and settle the argument contract
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 12:0x AUSEST. This is a CLAIM needing reproduction, not a confirmed defect, and the observation is partly spoiled by my own instrument error — recorded that way on purpose.

WHAT I RAN, from the mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2:
  sh scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh xraygate-a 2>&1 | tail -6; echo "remove exit: $?"
i.e. a BARE WORKTREE NAME, not an absolute path.

WHAT I OBSERVED: six CANARY_AFTER= lines and nothing else in the visible tail. No REMOVED= line and no 'OK: worktree removal complete.' line — and per the script's own CONTRACT block (scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh:55-66) OK: is the last line on success, so the run did NOT report success. The worktree was still registered afterwards (git worktree list showed it) and 'git branch -D worker/xraygate-a' refused with 'used by worktree at ...'. I then removed it myself with 'git worktree remove --force' and the mayor implementation/node_modules canary held at 103 entries either side.

TWO THINGS I CANNOT STATE, and both are my fault rather than the script's:
(1) THE EXIT CODE IS UNKNOWN. I piped the script through 'tail' and read $? — which is TAIL's status, not the script's. That is exactly the failure loops.md and CLAUDE.md both warn about ('never pipe a gate through a filter'; a pipeline's status is its last command's), reached through a maintenance script instead of a gate. So 'remove exit: 0' in my transcript is worthless.
(2) ANY REFUSAL MESSAGE IS UNKNOWN. tail -6 discarded everything above the canary block, so if the script explained itself I destroyed the explanation.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH REPRODUCING: reaching CANARY_AFTER is not the shape of an early usage refusal. An unrecognised argument should be refused before the canary is taken, so a run that canaries and then stops without REMOVED= is either (a) a legitimate refusal that happens late, or (b) a path that does real work and then declines to finish. Those want different remedies and the tail cannot tell them apart.

THE ARGUMENT CONTRACT IS THE LIKELY EXPLANATION AND IS ALSO WORTH PINNING. The script normalises its target by 'cd'-ing to it (scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh:221-223, _np_in=$(cd "$_np_in" && pwd)), which is CWD-relative — so a bare name run from the mayor checkout resolves against the MAYOR CHECKOUT, not the worktree parent, and names a directory that does not exist. If that is the whole story, the script behaved correctly and the repair is documentation plus a clearer refusal, not code.

TO SETTLE IT (cheap, and do it on a scratch worktree, never a live one): create a throwaway worktree under the worktree parent, then run the script THREE ways from the mayor checkout — bare name, absolute path, and a path relative to the worktree parent — each time WITHOUT a pipe, capturing the full stdout+stderr to a file and echoing the script's own exit code on the same command line in the same shell. Compare against the documented exit codes at :64-80 (0 done, 1 refused/nothing destroyed, 2 usage error, 3 PARTIAL). Then either fix the refusal so a bad argument exits 2 BEFORE taking a canary, or document the absolute-path requirement in the script header and in the CLAUDE.md bullet that tells agents to use it.

DO NOT change the canary, the link-disarming order or the exit-code taxonomy — those are load-bearing and were written against two measured node_modules destructions.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 13:0x AUSEST (mayor, hygiene tick) — THE ARGUMENT-CONTRACT HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED AND THE SCRIPT IS NOT AT FAULT.

Three worktrees were reaped this tick with an ABSOLUTE path argument — sh scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh /c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/<name> — run WITHOUT a pipe, with the exit code read directly. All three exited 0 and printed the full documented contract: NO_LINKS=, REMOVED=, and 'OK: worktree removal complete.' The mayor's implementation/node_modules canary held at 103 entries across all three.

That is the discriminator this bead asked for. The earlier bare-name invocation reached CANARY_AFTER and stopped without REMOVED=/OK:, which is consistent with the script normalising its target by cd-ing to it (:221-223, _np_in=$(cd "$_np_in" && pwd)) — CWD-relative, so a bare name run from the mayor checkout resolves against the MAYOR CHECKOUT and names a directory that does not exist. The script behaved correctly; my invocation was wrong.

WHAT REMAINS IS SMALLER THAN THE ORIGINAL BEAD AND IS ERGONOMICS, NOT CORRECTNESS. A bad argument should exit 2 (the documented usage-error code) BEFORE taking a canary, rather than doing canary work and then stopping without a verdict line. The repair is either an early argument-existence check with a clear refusal, or documenting the absolute-path requirement in the script header and in the CLAUDE.md bullet that tells agents to use the script — that bullet currently shows no argument form at all, which is how I got it wrong.

Judge that against the stance before spending a worker on it: this is a one-line invocation habit, the script already fails SAFE (it destroyed nothing), and 'not over-engineering' plus 'don't litigate the minutiae' both point at documentation over code. My recommendation is the CLAUDE.md/header doc fix alone, and to drop the exit-code change unless it falls out for free. DO NOT change the canary, the link-disarming order or the exit-code taxonomy — those are load-bearing and were written against two measured node_modules destructions.

DELIVERED 2026-09-05 (worker hygiene-b) — PR #9279, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9279

REPRODUCTION VERDICT: (a) A LEGITIMATE REFUSAL THAT HAPPENS LATE. Not (b). Run
unpiped against a throwaway worktree created for the purpose, exit code captured
in the same shell: EXIT=1 (not the 0 the piped transcript reported), output in
full = MAYOR_ROOT=, six CANARY_BEFORE=, then on stderr
'REFUSED_UNREGISTERED=<name> (no such directory)' + "Nothing was touched. Check
the path; 'git worktree list' shows what is registered.", then six CANARY_AFTER=.
Nothing disarmed, nothing removed, mayor node_modules unchanged at 103/2933/2.

The observation reproduces exactly and the mechanism is the output ORDER, not a
partial removal: the refusal goes to stderr BETWEEN the two canary blocks while
the canary writes to stdout, so the last six lines of a refused run are the
CANARY_AFTER block and the explanation sits two lines above a tail -6 window.

PREMISES, all checked at source and all held: normalize_path resolves by cd-ing
to the target (line 223, cwd-relative) so a bare name run from the mayor checkout
names <mayor-checkout>/<name>; the CONTRACT block does make 'OK:' the last line
on success; the exit-code taxonomy is as quoted. The line cites in the
description are right to within the enclosing function.

WHAT SHIPPED. The script was right to refuse; what was wrong is WHERE. An
argument fault is knowable before anything is examined, so it now settles at the
top of BOTH scripts: a target that is not an existing directory is refused with
REFUSED_BAD_ARGUMENT= and the documented usage code 2, BEFORE the mayor root is
derived and before the canary, with a message stating the contract and pointing
at 'git worktree list' and 'git worktree prune'. Every bad target is named in one
pass; all-or-nothing is deliberate. Expressed once — the loop's now-unreachable
no-such-directory branch is deleted from both scripts. Mirrored to the .ps1.
CLAUDE.md's bullet now states the argument form (its silence on that is what the
notes identify as how the wrong invocation was reached).

ON THIS BEAD'S OWN RECOMMENDATION. The note recommended the doc fix alone and to
drop the exit-code change "unless it falls out for free". It does fall out for
free: the early gate has to exit something, and 2 is the code the taxonomy
already assigns to argument faults, so no taxonomy was changed — only the
routing of an argument fault into it. Flagged on the PR as a behaviour change
for review: a non-existent target now exits 2 where it exited 1.

THE THREE LOAD-BEARING THINGS LEFT ALONE, as instructed: the canary, the
link-disarming order, the exit-code taxonomy. Nothing new invokes cmd; the
junction is still detected with [ -L ] and unlinked with a plain non-recursive rm.

SAFETY PROPERTIES RE-PROVED, not asserted. A throwaway worktree with the
node_modules junction armed and verified by EFFECT (LinkType=Junction, 103
entries through it) was removed by absolute path: DISARMED= then REMOVED= then
OK:, EXIT=0, and all six mayor node_modules signatures identical either side
(implementation at 103/2933/2). An independent count either side agreed. The
throwaway is removed and deregistered.

TEST HOME: the existing --self-test / -SelfTest, which is where this script's
tests already live (portability.yml runs the POSIX one; the .ps1 has no runner
and was run by hand on Windows). New argument-contract section in both: three
shapes (missing path, existing non-directory, bare name) each asserted to exit 2
with REFUSED_BAD_ARGUMENT=. The load-bearing assertion is that MAYOR_ROOT= was
never printed — exit 2 and a refusal line can both come from a late check; only
"no tree had been examined yet" separates refusing up front from doing the work
and declining after. MAYOR_ROOT= rather than a CANARY_ line deliberately: the
fixtures point --mayor-root at a throwaway repo with no node_modules, so a canary
assertion would pass either way. A positive control proves the marker appears.

GATES (all captured on one command line in one shell, re-run after rebase):
self-test .sh 0, self-test .ps1 0, check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose 0,
check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose 0, check_readme_links.py --ci 0,
check_doc_slugs.py 0, check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh 0. shellcheck is not installed
locally; portability.yml's pull_request trigger is unfiltered so it and the
self-test both run on the PR. report-changed-surfaces.sh arms NO surface for
these three paths (verified non-vacuous against a control). The link gate was
proven to bite: a planted broken target in the edited CLAUDE.md line returned
exit 1 naming CLAUDE.md:99, restored byte-identical by blob hash, green again.

FOLLOW-UP 2026-09-05 (worker hygiene-b) — CI RED ON ONE JOB, FIXED, PR #9279 UPDATED.

THE JOB NAME DID NOT NAME THE SUBJECT. The failing check was "No hardcoded
personal/home paths"; it found no hardcoded path. That job ALSO runs shellcheck,
and shellcheck is what failed — the recorded trap that a gate's name is not its
subject, met here in the wild.

TWO findings, both mine, both SC2016 (info) at scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh
lines 997 and 998: "Expressions don't expand in single quotes." The refusal
message I added quotes the placeholders `<name>` and `<mayor-checkout>` in
BACKTICKS inside single quotes, and shellcheck reads a backtick pair as a
command substitution somebody forgot to let expand. The repo runs shellcheck at
its default threshold, so an INFO grade is a hard failure here — an info finding
is not a pass.

FIX: the message TEXT is unchanged; only the quoting is annotated. Both lines
carry `# shellcheck disable=SC2016` with the reason stated above them — single
quotes are CORRECT there, nothing is meant to expand, and the backticks are the
whole value of the message to a reader, so the warning is answered where it is
raised rather than by rewording the refusal. This matches the file's own
established idiom (it already carries SC2064, SC1003 and SC2015 annotations).

PROVED BYTE-IDENTICAL rather than eyeballed: the refusal path was run before and
after and its combined output hashed —
sha256 d1b72b5d7e69d1aa34cc2aa108cee848ddf7f209d4fca1df76330275ee807aad both
times, diff exit 0, exit code still 2.

WHOLE-FILE AUDIT, not just the two reported lines: a census of non-comment lines
carrying a backtick returns EXACTLY those two sites and no others, and every
added line with a `$` has it inside DOUBLE quotes. That agrees with CI's count,
so nothing was hiding behind a truncated log.

MY EARLIER REPORT SAID SHELLCHECK WAS UNAVAILABLE LOCALLY. That was true of the
system package, but shellcheck 0.11.0 IS reachable via npx, so this round was
verified locally instead of on CI's word. The instrument was controlled both
ways: run against the PRE-FIX committed file it REPRODUCES both CI findings
(exit 1, SC2016 at 997 and 998); run against the fixed file it is exit 0 with no
findings. Local shellcheck is worth using on any future .sh change here.

One local-only artefact worth knowing: shellcheck's default output echoes the
offending source line, and this box's console cannot encode the em-dash in that
line, which truncates the report and returns exit 2. `-f gcc` suppresses the
source echo and reports cleanly. CI (UTF-8 runners) is unaffected.

GATES re-run on the final base after two further rebases (trunk moved three
times during the work): shellcheck 0, self-test .sh 0, self-test .ps1 0,
check_require_alias_dialect 0, check_view_lifetime_residue 0,
check_readme_links --ci 0, check_doc_slugs 0, check-no-hardcoded-paths 0.
Merge-base diff re-read for reverts: three files only, no spec/, skills/ or
ssr-node/ paths carried from the siblings that landed meanwhile.

MAYOR'S RULING RECORDED: the exit-code change STANDS. A non-existent target
exits 2, not 1 — it falls out for free, 2 is the code the taxonomy already
assigns to argument faults, and an argument fault indistinguishable from a
runtime failure is the exact ambiguity this bead exists to remove. The PR body's
flag stays in place so the reasoning is visible at review.

title: reagent-slim sub-cache poison proof is vacuous: the bare js-obj is skipped, never thrown
description:
Found while landing rf2-ss8x (PR #9201).

`reagent_slim_dispose_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs`'s `dispose-adapter-walk-is-best-effort` injects `{:reaction (js-obj "not" "a reaction")}` and claims to pin 'a throwing per-entry dispose'. Nothing throws. The ratom family's claimed-generation disposer is `make-ratom-dispose-dispatch` (spine.cljs), which dispatches `re-frame.disposable/IDisposable` -> the substrate's `IDisposable` -> `:else nil`; a bare js-obj satisfies neither protocol, so the entry is SKIPPED in silence. The test therefore proves visit-and-clear only, and the per-entry failure path it was written for is never reached.

Measured directly: adding a rethrow assertion to that test returned `nil` (no throw) while the stock-Reagent equivalent, rebuilt on a reify of Reagent's real `IDisposable` (methods `dispose!` / `add-on-dispose!`), threw as expected.

Remedy: give the slim test a poison entry that really throws — reify `reagent2.ratom/IDisposable` the way rf2-ss8x's stock-Reagent witness reifies `reagent.ratom/IDisposable` — and assert both the sibling drain AND the post-drain rethrow. Left out of rf2-ss8x deliberately: that bead's non-goals fence reagent-slim redesign, and its reviewed surface is stock Reagent. The vacuity is documented in a comment in place meanwhile.

Note the same shape does NOT apply to `react_shared_suite.cljs`: the React-hook spine passes `rf.disposable/-dispose` directly rather than through the dispatch, so its poison entry genuinely throws (verified green under rf2-ss8x's rethrow assertion).
close_reason: CONFIRMED and FIXED. The bead's finding was exact and is reproduced: dispose-adapter-walk-is-best-effort injected {:reaction (js-obj "not" "a reaction")} and claimed to pin a throwing per-entry dispose, but the ratom family's claimed-generation disposer dispatches re-frame.disposable/IDisposable -> the substrate's IDisposable -> :else nil, and a bare js-obj satisfies neither, so the entry was skipped in silence. What it was PINNING: that a throwing entry does not abort the walk. What it ACTUALLY exercised: that the walk visits an unrecognised entry and clears the cache anyway. Fix follows the stock-Reagent witness already on main (rf2-ss8x) rather than inventing a second approach: throwing-cached-reaction reifies reagent2's own IDisposable (methods dispose! / add-on-dispose!, NOT -dispose, which is precisely why the bare object fell through) and throws a test-allocated sentinel. The test now asserts the disposer was called exactly once, that siblings past it in the same frame and in a later frame were still drained, and the drain-then-rethrow contract via identical? on the sentinel. MAKING IT HONEST REVEALED NO LIVE DEFECT: it passes against current source. Negative control, reverting the witness to the original bare js-obj, fails with attempts reading 0 (the disposer was never called) and thrown reading ::returned-normally - the vacuity reproduced exactly. Test renamed to dispose-adapter-walk-drains-past-a-throwing-entry-then-rethrows and the in-place vacuity comment replaced by an explanation of why the protocol identity is load-bearing. PR #9209.

title: examples(realworld-resources): align host-page base with the /realworld-resources URL/deployment contract
description:
The rf2-do50 census (PR #9155) swept all 31 example index.html files against the route table each example ships. Four examples register routes deeper than one segment AND carry relative asset hrefs, so a deep link or refresh resolves every asset against the route directory. PR #9155 fixed two of them and left these two, which were outside its scope:

  examples/capabilities/resources/resources/  - depth 2, /articles/:slug
  examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/     - depth 3, /profile/:username/favorites

Both are :url-bound? true, so the document URL really is the route.

The fix is the identical one line PR #9155 used, added to <head> BEFORE any
asset reference:

  <base href="/">

Do NOT convert the hrefs to absolute paths instead. check-examples-assets.cjs's
resolveRef special-cases a _shared/-prefixed ref and resolves it against the
examples root; a leading slash falls through to path.resolve(pageDir, '/...')
and misses on disk, turning that gate red. <base> leaves every href untouched.

Measured under rf2-do50 with new URL() over the shipped route shapes: 16 of 28
route x asset combinations resolve wrong without a base, 0 of 28 with one. Note
that main.js is relative too, so the symptom is not merely a lost stylesheet -
the application never boots on a deep-linked route.

The remaining 27 examples ship one-segment routes or none and are correct as
they stand; capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr mentions reg-route only in prose and
is route-free.

Gates: node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs and
implementation's test:examples-compile. Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm) - no
*.spec.cjs under examples/.
notes:
AUDIT PR #9161 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. The plain resources example half is correct; the RealWorld-resources half is not complete.

The landed host page now says `<base href="/">`, but this app's own deployed-URL contract says the opposite: `routing.cljs` defines `(routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy "/realworld-resources")`, and `core.cljs` explicitly says the orchestrator mounts it at `/realworld-resources/`. Its build/stager places `main.js` and `_shared/` under `out/examples/realworld-resources/`. At a shipped deep URL such as `/realworld-resources/profile/bob/favorites`, browser URL resolution with the landed base asks for `/main.js` and `/_shared/css/style.css`; the staged artifacts are `/realworld-resources/main.js` and `/realworld-resources/_shared/css/style.css`. A control with `<base href="/realworld-resources/">` resolves both to those staged paths.

The other advertised posture does not rescue the claim. `npm run dev:example` serves this one output directory at `/`, while the app's URL strategy still emits `/realworld-resources/...`; the shared `http-server` argv has no push-state fallback. A navigation can push that URL in-place, but a deep refresh cannot serve the host page. Thus the PR's claimed deep-link/refresh fix is not demonstrated in either declared posture.

The green gates do not cover this boundary: `check-examples-assets.cjs` resolves source-tree references and never parses `<base>`; the examples compile gate never serves a page; `ADAPTER_SMOKES` contains only the Reagent and UIx testbeds, so the PR body's claimed live-mount coverage does not include this app.

Completion: choose one coherent mount contract and make the host-page base, `with-base-path`, staging root, printed dev URL, and history fallback agree. Pin a deep document request plus `main.js`/`_shared` resolution in the existing script/substrate test surface; keep `examples/` test-free. No open PR currently touches any of these target files.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the .beads checkout/checkpoint race, fifteenth instance today. Payload verified in the WORKING TREE at HEAD==origin/main with controls that fired — examples/capabilities/resources/resources/index.html and examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/index.html each carry exactly one <base href="/">, against a control of 3 script tags per file proving the instrument read them.

Delivered by worker/exfix-b in PR #9161, MERGED.

THE SYMPTOM IS WORSE THAN THE BEAD RECORDED, and that is the part worth keeping. main.js is relative on both pages across six distinct routes, so THE APP NEVER BOOTS on a deep link — not merely unstyled. Chapter 07's warning describes the unstyled case because it assumes an absolute script tag; these two were not that case.

MY RELAYED FIGURE WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER RE-MEASURED. I briefed '16 of 28 route x asset combinations' — that is rf2-do50's figure for the OTHER two examples. The true measurement here is 24 of 64 wrong without a base, 0 of 64 with one.

IT RE-VERIFIED THE WHOLE CENSUS rather than trusting the bead: 8 files under examples/ contain reg-route, exactly 4 are deep-routed, 2 were #9155's. The /api/... hits a naive sweep returns are :request {:url ...} values, and resources_ssr's four reg-route mentions are all comment prose.

ABSOLUTE PATHS WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG, and the brief said so for a reason the worker confirmed at source: examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs special-cases _shared/ in resolveRef, so an absolute path breaks the gate. <base href="/"> is what chapter 07 documents and what #9155 used.

Gates: check-examples-assets 0 (33 pages), check-examples-compile 0 (58 builds, 0 warnings), CLJS compile 0, CLJS suite 0 (11174 tests / 55752 assertions), alias ratchet 0. A planted broken _shared ref reddened the asset gate at exit 1 naming it.

title: hic docs: neither chapter 00's mount section nor chapter 07's routed-root recipe puts an h/error-boundary at the root, so any refusal blanks the whole page
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F19 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to** Decide whether the application root needed an error boundary. I
only asked because P2-F16's induced failure blanked the whole page.

**Expected** The boot recipes to have told me.

**Instead** `h/error-boundary` is a first-class Hiccup head — it is in the
api-reference §Markup with its three options, and chapter 17 owns it — but
**none of the three boot recipes in the corpus uses one**: not
`00-installation.md` §"Mount a first screen", not `cookbook.md` §Boot, not
`07-routing-and-navigation.md`'s routed `app-root`. So the shape a reader builds
by following the guide in order has no boundary anywhere, and a single refused
head — the very mistake chapters 01, 02 and 16 all warn about — takes the
application to a white screen with the error only in the console.

**Looked at** `api-reference.md` §Markup; `17-errors.md` (skimmed for the
boundary's contract); `00-installation.md`, `cookbook.md` and
`07-routing-and-navigation.md` boot/root recipes.

**Resolved by** Left it alone, deliberately: adding a root boundary is a
framework-shaped design decision the brief tells me not to make on my own
initiative, and it would have masked the outcome-5 evidence. Recorded as
friction instead, which is what the brief asks for.

**Bead** Put an `h/error-boundary` in chapter 07's routed-root recipe, or add
one line to chapter 00's mount section pointing at chapter 17. The routed root
is the natural home: it is already the place the corpus teaches you to key and
focus a page region, and it is the last common ancestor of everything that can
refuse.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137, but NOT by the bead's literal remedy - that one collides with chapter 17. Consequence verified rather than asserted: impl/error/fail! THROWS (:recovery :no-recovery on every Hicasso refusal), and React unmounts a root whose tree throws with no boundary above it, which is what ch17's own opening paragraph and troubleshooting row already say. So the blank page is real. What does not hold is 'put an h/error-boundary at the root': ch17 'Place boundaries at useful recovery regions' argues against exactly that - 'a single boundary around the root turns every failure into a whole-page fallback and may remove navigation along with the broken content' - and names the region it wants instead, 'a route's main content while the surrounding shell remains usable'. That region IS ch07's routed root, which had none. The boundary is therefore placed inside <main>, below site-nav, where ch17 asks. It needs no :reset-key: the :key route already on <main> remounts the subtree on a route change, which ch07's own prose already states. Ch00's mount section gets the one-line pointer at ch17 the bead also asked for. Gates: check_guide_samples.py 0 (h/error-boundary resolves), check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs --strict 0.

title: Clarify private locals in reply egress projection conformance
description:
## Finding
The egress projection conformance suite uses terse private helper and loop bindings whose roles are needlessly opaque during review.

## Evidence
implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:109-130 uses [v] in redacted? and large-marker?, and [[k v]] in tree-contains?; lines 299-315 uses [p] for each egress profile and [out] for the projected result; lines 317-338 repeat the out binding. These are test-private lexical names, not exported vocabulary.

## Impact
A reviewer must infer value/map-key/map-value/profile/projected-result roles while validating privacy and projection assertions. This increases ambiguity cost without adding test coverage.

## Recommendation
Rename only the private lexical bindings to role-revealing names (value, map-key, map-value, profile, projected-result or equivalent) and update their local references. Preserve every test name, input/output key, sentinel, payload, profile keyword, assertion, and control flow.

## Compatibility and exclusions
No public API, namespace, file, operation keyword, wire/storage key, or behavior change. Do not alter the projection semantics or the existing rf2-6r9j.88/.90/.91 work: descriptor metadata, matrix gating, stale inventory/path references, and any docs outside this bounded surface are explicitly excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every identified terse binding in lines 109-130 and 299-338 is renamed to a semantically clear role with no missed local reference.
2. The rendered test forms and assertion counts remain unchanged; no test names, keys, sentinels, or profile values change.
3. Focused CLJS/JVM test and lint gates pass, and git diff --check is clean.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in commit 584bd9fd4d: private egress helper/profile/result bindings clarified; JVM, CLJS, kondo, negative-control, and diff-check gates green.

title: Clarify reference and candidate roles in Hicasso shadow diffs
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs` compares reference and candidate DOM/intent state, but the core difference walk uses private helper names `at`, `checkpoint`, and `red` plus repeated `a`/`b`, `x`/`y`, `rt`/`ct` locals.
- In this file those values are not generic pairs: they are reference versus candidate attributes, properties, children, node tags, intent entries, and the resulting checkpoint difference.
- The public `shadow!` API and its result keys are already ledger-settled and must remain stable; the ambiguous names are internal only.

## Actionable insight
Rename private comparison helpers and multi-step locals by side and role, e.g. `path-description`, `checkpoint-difference`, `red-verdict`, `reference-attrs`, `candidate-attrs`, `reference-child`, `candidate-child`, and explicit tag/intent roles.

## Ambiguity cost
A side swap in a differential harness produces a plausible but inverted diagnostic. Single-letter symmetric names make that class of review error unnecessarily easy and make failure reports harder to trace back through the comparison walk.

## Risks / migration
Keep public kit functions, result-map keys, selectors, status/reason keywords, traversal order, and comparison precedence byte-for-byte. Only private names and lexical bindings move; update internal references and any direct test/doc references if found.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Reference/candidate sides and checkpoint/path roles are explicit throughout the shadow comparator.
2. `hm/shadow!` output shape and semantics do not change.
3. Focused test-kit/shadow suites, lint, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Replace opaque machines regression-test filenames with semantic suites
description:
## Locations and evidence

Three tracked test namespaces use provenance/churn names rather than the behaviors they own:
- `machine_remediation_ee38b_test.clj` mixes root `:on` fallback, unhandled/microstep traces, forbidden `:db`, update-snapshot, history placement, and callback-ref validation.
- `trace_enhancements_rf2_82a0u_test.clj` mixes action phase/guard traces with timer cancellation traces.
- `machine_remaining_lifecycle_tail_fence_test.clj` covers destroy continuation fencing, timer subscription release, spawn-all iteration, and classification removal.

All file/namespace mappings are mechanically valid, but the names are opaque to a reader and make test discovery by feature difficult. History shows the first two retain implementation bead/commit labels from their introduction rather than stable behavior names.

## Ambiguity cost

A contributor searching for root fallback, guard failure, timer cancellation, or destroy-incarnation fencing cannot predict which suite owns it. “remediation”, “enhancements”, and “remaining” communicate project history rather than the contract under test, and broad mixed suites become accidental dumping grounds.

## Recommendation

Split/rename by stable behavior, preserving tests and history with moves: root fallback/validation, action+guard traces, timer cancellation traces, and destroy-incarnation fencing. Prefer existing focused suites when a test can be moved without duplication; use semantic namespaces matching filenames. Update any exact path references and test classifier manifests.

## Compatibility / migration risk

Test namespaces/files are not runtime API, but classifier discovery, targeted commands, doc references, and history followability are contracts. Use history-preserving moves, verify every original deftest appears exactly once, and avoid merging behavior changes into the reorganization.
acceptance_criteria:
- No machines test filename/namespace contains `remediation`, `enhancements-rf2`, or `remaining-lifecycle`.
- Replacement suites have semantic filenames/namespaces and every original deftest is retained exactly once.
- Repository exact-path references and classifier enrollment are updated.
- Focused replacement suites plus full machines JVM/CLJS gates pass.
- The reorganization is committed separately from behavioral changes.
close_reason:
PR #9103. No machines test filename or namespace now contains remediation, enhancements-rf2 or remaining-lifecycle; census confirms the three old namespace names 1 -> 0 each and the five new ones 0 -> 1 each, with nested-validation-test as the control that fired and held at 1 -> 1.

Two of the three were renames ONLY, because the bead's split recommendation does not apply to a suite that is already one thing:
  machine_remaining_lifecycle_tail_fence_test -> machine_destroy_tail_incarnation_fence_test (it fences the ordinary :rf.machine/destroy teardown tail to its exact incarnation across three sub-paths, and rejoins the *_incarnation_fence_test family it completes)
  trace_enhancements_rf2_82a0u_test -> machine_trace_payload_shapes_test (it pins the CLOSED payload vocabularies three machine trace events carry — :phase, :outcome, :reason)

The third genuinely was not one thing — 14 deftests over six unrelated Spec 005 rules — so it split three ways along seams a reader can predict:
  machine_root_on_fallback_test (8) — the root :on ancestor fallback end to end: refs resolved at registration, keyword/vector/wildcard targets and guard at runtime, deepest-wins shadowing, and the benign :rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op when even the root misses
  machine_macrostep_snapshot_rules_test (4) — :always microstep traces and the outer :microsteps count, the :db hard-disallow, and the one sanctioned :rf.machine/update-snapshot patch (whose :db key meets the same disallow)
  machine_registration_grammar_validation_test (2) — history placement and :after guard/action refs, both rejected by validate-machine! at registration

Pure move: all 14 deftests verified present exactly once (sorted deftest sets diffed against the pre-split file at HEAD — identical, no duplicates) and none changed. git mv used throughout; the 3-way split falls below git's default 50% rename similarity so the root-on file shows as add+delete in plain status but is detected at -M25. The P1:/P2:/P3: section banners were the same provenance label one level down and now name their sections.

Aliases in the moved files deliberately stay in the machines artefact's current dialect — no machines alias bead existed and a half-migrated artefact reads worse than a uniformly unmigrated one. Filed as rf2-j5or (835 edges, 192 files).

Gates: machines JVM 1241 tests / 4495 assertions exit 0; node bundle 11170 tests / 55749 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo 0 errors. CI on the merge head: 86 checks, 73 success / 13 skipped, 0 failures.

NOT done here: two prose citations of the old name survive in tools/machines-viz (spec/001-Topology-Parity.md:921 and chart/layout.cljc:776), a tree another worker held this tick. Filed as rf2-fti6 with both line numbers and the replacement name.

title: reagent-slim static renderer: name helpers by serialized output role
description:
## Finding

The pure static HTML serializer in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` mixes abbreviated attribute/value names with helpers whose names describe input representation rather than emitted output: `attr-name`, `emit-attr(s)`, `merge-shorthand`, `react-component-comment`, `emit-dom-vector`, and `emit-vector`.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `attr-name`, `named->str`, `style-value->str`, and `attr-value-string` span lines 355-515; each sits in security/parity-sensitive serialization code where spelling out attribute/string roles reduces context switching.
- `emit-attr`/`emit-attrs` at lines 618-694 perform filtering plus mutation of the output buffer, not merely attribute formatting.
- `merge-shorthand` at lines 704-725 merges parsed tag id/class shorthand; the unqualified name does not say what shorthand.
- `react-component-comment` at lines 733-737 is an emitting operation that appends the opaque placeholder.
- `emit-dom-vector` and `emit-vector` at lines 744-890 require readers to remember one emits a DOM element and the other dispatches every Hiccup vector head.
- The serializer's only external surface is `render-to-static-markup`; exact searches show these candidates are private. Targeted history traces them to the original Stage 4-E serializer, with no compatibility consumers.

## Recommendation

Adopt consistent `attribute`/`string` spellings and emitted-shape names: `attribute-name`, `named-value->string`, `style-value->string`, `attribute-value-string`, `emit-attribute`, `emit-attributes`, `merge-tag-shorthand`, `emit-react-component-placeholder`, `emit-dom-element`, and `emit-hiccup-vector`; align private constant names and in-slice comments/spec references where needed.

## Contracts and risk

The names are private; no compatibility aliases should be introduced. The IMPL-SPEC reconciliation owned by `rf2-6r9j.33` must not be broadened here: only mechanically update names directly made stale by this patch.

## Duplicate search

All-status bead data was searched for the old helpers and static-renderer/serializer naming concepts. No naming bead owns this partition. Existing renderer beads concern correctness/performance or the wider stale IMPL-SPEC architecture, not these private names.

title: Test-React inspection API: distinguish components from roots and live children
description:
## Naming finding

The public inspection helpers in `implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:539-554` no longer name the population they return:

- `mounted-roots` returns every live `MountedComponent` in `active-mounts`, including recursively mounted children. Its own docstring calls the result "the whole live forest, parents AND recursively-mounted children." The name predates child mounting (`fefee4a403`); commit `8e3dfe545f` added child roots and broadened the result without changing the original name.
- `children` filters the record's retained `:children` vector to only still-mounted entries. Unqualified `children` can be read as all recorded children, while the function intentionally returns only mounted children.

No tracked code outside this local-only adapter consumes either helper, but both are public vars in the documented test-kit namespace and therefore remain compatibility contracts.

## Ambiguity cost

Tests use the first helper as a leak detector over the entire mounted forest, not a root count. Calling it a root query makes assertions such as "parent + child = 2 roots" conceptually wrong and obscures why an orphaned descendant is visible. The second name hides its liveness filter, so a post-unmount empty result can be mistaken for removal from the record rather than filtering of retained dead child records.

## Proposed change

Add precise canonical helpers `mounted-components` and `mounted-children`. Move the current implementations/docstrings under those names and update the adapter's tests and README to use them. Retain `mounted-roots` and `children` as deprecated delegating compatibility wrappers with explicit historical-name documentation; do not make an unannounced breaking rename.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Preserve return collection shapes/order, `MountedComponent`, the serialized/record `:children` field, public mount/update/unmount names, lifecycle log keys/phases, and React interop. Do not touch the duplicate cache section or stale UIx/CI prose already owned by Phase-1 beads `rf2-6r9j.81` and `rf2-6r9j.85`. All-status searches for `mounted-roots`, mounted components/children, and live-forest Test-React vocabulary found no existing owning bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- New code and documentation use `mounted-components` for the complete live forest and `mounted-children` for one mount's live children.
- Historical public vars `mounted-roots` and `children` remain callable compatibility wrappers, are visibly deprecated, and state their misleading legacy semantics.
- Canonical and legacy helpers preserve the existing lazy-sequence/vector return shapes, order, and mounted-state filtering.
- Exact searches show legacy names only in their compatibility definitions/documentation; no call site continues teaching the ambiguous vocabulary.
- Test-React JVM and CLJS suites pass with the public mount/lifecycle/error and record contracts unchanged.
notes: Implemented mounted-components and mounted-children as canonical helpers; retained mounted-roots and children as ^:deprecated delegating wrappers with precise legacy-semantics docstrings. All production/test teaching uses canonical names except two explicit compatibility tests, which dereference the legacy Vars, assert :deprecated metadata, and verify delegation on JVM and CLJS without compiler warnings or changing the 35/160 count. README updated. Broad CLJS namespace run separately encountered only the pre-existing duplicated sub-cache test failures owned by rf2-6r9j.81; all naming/lifecycle contract selectors passed.
close_reason: Implemented canonical inspection names with deprecated compatibility wrappers, migrated callers/docs, and verified metadata, delegation, shapes, and host behavior.

title: Reader-condition seven SSR definitions and imports to their live host
description:
## Finding

Seven definitions/dependency edges in SSR `.cljc` files are live on exactly one host but are currently compiled on both. Reader conditionals already isolate every call site, leaving the opposite-host copies mechanically unreachable.

## Evidence

Focused clj-kondo runs report host-qualified findings:

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/suspense.cljc:192`: private `subtree` is unused on `:clj`; its only call is inside `boundary`'s `:cljs` arm.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/emit.cljc:20-21`: `clojure.string :as str` and `re-frame.error :as error` are unused on `:cljs`; every `str/` and `error/` call is inside the JVM `ld-json-string` arm, while CLJS uses `js/JSON.stringify`.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc:63`: `re-frame.interop :as interop` is unused on `:cljs`; its only executable read is the JVM-only `with-redefs [interop/debug-enabled? ...]` test arm.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_component_cljs_test.cljc:44-53`: private `card-skeleton`, `card-view`, and `throwing-card` are unused on `:cljs`; every reference is inside JVM-only streaming tests.

Exact source searches confirm each finding has live uses on the stated host and no use on the opposite host. The production `subtree` Var and all three test helper Vars were introduced in `80faa4f2c2` as part of reader-conditional server/client behavior; the definitions themselves were never host-scoped.

This does not classify the public `boundary` component, `re-frame.ssr` facade load, cross-host test namespace, or either host behavior as vestigial. Duplicate searches for "SSR reader conditional", "suspense subtree", "head emit unused namespace", "failed root isolation interop", and "streaming component card-skeleton" found no owning bead.

## Impact

The JVM ships a private Var that can never be called, CLJS carries two irrelevant production dependency edges, and both test targets compile host-inapplicable scaffolding. The seven predictable lint findings also obscure genuinely unreferenced definitions in future audits.

## Proposed disposition

Reader-condition `subtree` to CLJS; reader-condition the `clojure.string` and `re-frame.error` head-emitter requires to CLJ; reader-condition the isolation test's `re-frame.interop` require to CLJ; and reader-condition the three streaming-component test helpers to CLJ. Do not delete or rewrite the live host implementations. Leave the `re-frame.ssr` facade require and other possible registration/side-effect loads unchanged.

## Risks

Malformed `.cljc` require syntax or scoping a helper to the wrong host can break compilation before tests run. Both JVM and CLJS builds must be exercised. In particular, preserve the JVM JSON-LD error paths, the CLJS boundary body/fallback behavior, and the server-side streaming fixture markup exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the seven listed definitions/requires is reader-conditioned to its only consuming host.
- Focused clj-kondo runs no longer report those host-qualified unused findings; unrelated intentional side-effect-load findings are not removed to make lint superficially green.
- The SSR JVM suite passes, including head JSON-LD and server streaming-component tests.
- The Node and browser CLJS builds compile and pass the suspense boundary and failed-root isolation coverage.
- Public facade exports, namespace-load registrations, emitted markup/JSON, error ids, and test discovery are unchanged.
close_reason: PR #9106. All seven reader-conditioned to the host verified as their only consumer. :cljs — suspense/subtree (sole call at suspense.cljc:239, inside boundary's :cljs arm). :clj — head/emit's clojure.string and re-frame.error (every str/ and error/ use at emit.cljc lines 82-181, all inside ld-json-string's :clj letfn; the :cljs arm is js/JSON.stringify), failed_root_isolation_cljs_test's re-frame.interop (sole executable read at line 428 inside the #?(:clj ...) block; line 92 is docstring), and streaming_component_cljs_test's card-skeleton, card-view, throwing-card (all references at lines 104/105/132/133/167/168/176/177, every one inside a #?(:clj ...) deftest). None of the seven is used on both hosts. BOTH hosts run green: implementation/ssr clojure -M:test 623 tests/3172 assertions exit 0; implementation npm run test:cljs 11170 tests/55749 assertions exit 0. Gate liveness proved on each host with a wrong-host plant: #?(:clj (def wrong-host-probe (subtree ...))) gave SSR JVM exit 1 'Unable to resolve symbol: subtree'; #?(:cljs (def wrong-host-probe (card-view ...))) gave node-test compile exit 1 'Use of undeclared Var ... card-view'. Both plants reverted and the restored files verified byte-identical by git hash-object against the committed blobs (b661585278..., 910a8eed6b...). No live host implementation deleted or rewritten; facade exports, registrations, emitted markup and error ids unchanged.

title: Remove the inert status-record source-of-truth constant
description:
## Finding

`status-defect-record-slots` is presented as the closed source of truth from which the production always-on status-defect record is built, but it has never been read. The emitted map is a separate literal and the test compares that literal's output only with its own separate expected set. The constant is inert and several comments/spec statements make a security assurance the implementation does not perform.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:62-88` defines private `status-defect-record-slots`; repository symbol search finds no executable reference. `clj-kondo` reports it as an unused private var.
- `report-non-integer-status!` at lines 90-139 directly constructs the seven-key map passed to `emit-always-on-error!`; it neither selects nor builds keys from the set.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/status_rewrite_always_on_test.clj:67-75` defines a separate `expected-record-slots`, while its assertion at lines 125-130 compares that set with the emitted record's keys. It never resolves or compares the production constant. Its claim that "the two are pinned equal" is therefore false: changing only `status-defect-record-slots` leaves every test green.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` calls the unused var the source of truth, and comments in the pipeline and core catalogue test repeat that characterization. The real behavioral authority is the emitted map plus the exact-key and forbidden-value tests.
- Commit `c2baf05dc4` introduced both the set and literal together and claimed the record was "BUILT FROM" the set, but the diff confirms no use existed even at introduction. Commit `ec6d07b834` added the test-side set without reading the production var.
- The private constant is not part of the façade or API manifest; the observable contract is the seven record keys catalogued in Spec 009.

Duplicate searches for `status defect record slots`, `status-defect-record-slots unused`, and `ssr ring status source of truth` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The dead var creates a lint warning and, more importantly, gives reviewers a false impression that a closed allow-list mechanically constrains egress. There are actually three manually synchronized spellings (dead constant, emitted map, test expectation), so the inert one can drift while the tests remain green and maintenance pays for a source-of-truth that has no authority.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `status-defect-record-slots`. Rewrite its surrounding pipeline/test/spec/core-test prose to state the actual enforcement: the production emit site constructs only the closed seven-key record, and the independent exact-key test plus explicit absence checks guard it. Preserve the emitted record and its privacy contract unchanged; do not add a post-hoc `select-keys` filter merely to make the obsolete constant appear useful.

## Risks

The emitted record is an off-box security boundary. Do not relax the exact key set, add the raw offending `:status`, remove the explicit forbidden-slot assertions, or change the dev-trace/always-on asymmetry. The disposition is removal of a false authority, not removal of the closed-record contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- The unused private `status-defect-record-slots` var is removed and focused clj-kondo no longer reports it.
- `report-non-integer-status!` still emits exactly `#{:error :frame :time :where :status-type :reason :recovery}` on the always-on axis, with raw `:status` confined to the development trace.
- The exact-key and forbidden-slot tests remain independent behavioral checks and still fail if a new production record key is added.
- Pipeline docstrings, `status_rewrite_always_on_test`, Spec 009, and the core catalogue test no longer claim that records are built from or tests compare against the removed constant.
- Production-disabled and development status-rewrite tests plus error-catalogue/channel conformance gates pass with unchanged wire status and record counts.
notes:
NOT DONE - FENCE-BLOCKED (worker/adaptcount-a, 2026-09-03; the rest of that dispatch landed as PR #9112).

PREMISE VERIFIED. git grep -F 'status-defect-record-slots' over tracked files (excluding .beads) returns exactly four hits, and NOT ONE of them is an executable reference:
  * implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:62  - the private def itself
  * implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:97  - a docstring calling it 'the closed [[status-defect-record-slots]]'
  * implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/status_rewrite_always_on_test.clj:69 - a COMMENT naming it, confirming the test does not resolve it
  * spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2126 - the normative row calling it 'the source of truth'
So the bead is right: the var is inert and three manually-synchronised spellings exist where the prose claims one authority.

WHY IT WAS NOT LANDED. Two reasons, either sufficient:

  1. THE ARTEFACT IS IN THE SSR FAMILY. implementation/ssr-ring/ was outside this dispatch's fence (implementation/ssr and implementation/ssr-node named explicitly, and this brief's own instruction was to STOP if the named artefact turned out to sit in a tree another worker holds - security, schemas, http, machines, ssr).

  2. THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CANNOT BE MET WITHOUT A HOT-ZONE EDIT. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2126 is the statement that makes the false assurance normative - it names the var as 'the source of truth being re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline/status-defect-record-slots'. spec/009 is a hot-zone one-toucher file this dispatch was barred from editing. Removing the var while that row stands would leave the spec pointing at a var that no longer exists, which is worse than the current state. There is also a fourth site the description does not list among its evidence bullets: implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj:1282 repeats the characterisation, and implementation/core/test was likewise out of fence.

RECOMMENDATION: dispatch this as ONE bead to a worker holding implementation/ssr-ring PLUS spec/009 PLUS implementation/core/test. It cannot be split - splitting it produces exactly the drift the bead exists to remove. The risk paragraph in the description is the important part of the brief: the disposition is removal of a FALSE AUTHORITY, not removal of the closed-record contract, so the seven emitted keys, the exact-key test, the forbidden-slot assertions and the dev-trace/always-on asymmetry all stay as they are.
LANDED (the non-spec half) — PR #9116, branch worker/resretire-a, head f2ce1d677098b00f68e201bee93e7728d5a62b2c. Worker resretire-a, 2026-09-03.

PREMISE RE-VERIFIED, with a SECOND instrument the note above did not have: clj-kondo on origin/main's pipeline.clj reports `warning: Unused private var re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline/status-defect-record-slots` at line 62. So the inertness is independently attested, not only grep-attested. The five-site census stands.

DONE:
