title: machines: PARKED — [:schemas :events] stays declaration-only; wiring semantics pre-decided (reject-and-report, :rollback? false); un-parks only when a consumer needs the co-located contract (esp. a spawned actor)
description:
*** PARKED 2026-09-08 BY RULING. DO NOT DISPATCH. NOT AN OPEN DESIGN QUESTION. ***

This bead is now the TRACKED RECORD of a deliberately parked feature, not queued work.
Two independent reviews (dossier + Codex, 2026-09-08) plus the mayor §3 check settled it.
READ THE NOTES BEFORE ACTING ON ANYTHING BELOW — the notes carry the ruling, the
pre-decided semantics, and SIX measured findings that CONTRADICT parts of the original
description that follows.

DECISION: `[:schemas :events]` stays DECLARATION-ONLY. No wiring is built now. The
drop-vs-throw question the description below asks is ANSWERED and CLOSED: when the trigger
fires, it is reject-and-report at the delivery boundary, `:rollback? false`, snapshot
untouched, epoch `:ok` — never rollback, never a benign-info-only drop. The "yet" in
spec/005 line 528 STAYS (permanent-declarative was considered and rejected).

TRIGGER TO UN-PARK (consumer-driven, per spec/005:531, sharpened by the ruling): a machine
author who needs the co-located per-event contract — PARTICULARLY on a SPAWNED ACTOR, which
the existing outer-vector `reg-machine` opts `:schema` workaround cannot reach at all — and
who can supply the actual event shapes. No calendar date substitutes for it.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION BELOW, measured and verified — do not re-derive:
- FALSE: that `reg-event`'s `:schema` "cannot reach a machine's internal event vocabulary".
  It can; a passing test proves it (machine_schema_arity_test.clj:159). spec/005:523 and
  :531 repeat the same false claim — that is the split-out doc bead.
- FALSE: "the delivery boundary is after the cofx ensure-step (spec/005 line 444)". It is
  earlier — beside `reject-internal-event-external-dispatch`, registration.cljc:1005.
- FALSE: that the recommended option (i) benign trace is what v6 chose. alpha.50 pairs the
  hook and deadletter with a development CONSOLE WARNING; option (i) over-reads it.
- UNDER-PRICED: an `:rf.error/*` trace does NOT reach the always-on error stream. That is a
  separate router path and must be emitted explicitly. See note finding (3).

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION 2026-09-07, RETAINED FOR CONTEXT ONLY ---

From the 2026-09-07 XState v6 parity review (rf2-2qfi). THIS IS THE MOST ACTIONABLE ITEM IN THAT REVIEW.

=== THE CURRENT STATE ===
spec/005-StateMachines.md accepts a machine-level :schemas map with five sub-keys. Two are WIRED â€” [:schemas :data] validates the :data slot at every macrostep boundary and at bootstrap, rolling the cascade back on failure, and [:schemas :output] validates completion output. Three are DECLARATION-ONLY: :events, :tags and :meta. The spec is explicit at line 528: they "are accepted as part of the single-home machine contract â€” their <schema> values stay abstract â€” but carry no wired behaviour yet."

So an author can declare their machine's event vocabulary and the runtime will not check a single event against it. The declaration is honest about this, and the spec anticipates the gap being closed ("a future addition would re-open it", said of the adjacent :input key).

=== WHAT v6 DID, AND WHY THE DESIGN IS WORTH BORROWING ===
Two v6 alpha entries close exactly this gap, and the SHAPE of the answer is the valuable part, not the feature:

alpha.50: "Invalid external events are now rejected at the delivery boundary instead of erroring the actor or throwing. Rejected events never transition the machine or error it; rejections report through onRejectedEvent hook and @xstate.deadletter inspection events."

Three separable decisions there, all of which re-frame2 would otherwise have to make from scratch:
  1. WHERE â€” at the delivery boundary, before transition selection. Not inside the fold.
  2. WHAT HAPPENS â€” the event is dropped. It does NOT transition the machine, does NOT error the actor, and does NOT throw. A bad event from outside is not a machine bug.
  3. HOW IT IS OBSERVED â€” a dedicated inspection event (deadletter), separate from ordinary traces, plus a hook.

alpha.42: "Add separately declared internal event schemas with schemas.internalEvents. Internal events remain fully typed inside machines while staying out of the public actor event protocol."

That is a real distinction re-frame2 needs too: the events a machine RAISES to itself are not part of the vocabulary an outside caller may dispatch. re-frame2 already has the concept â€” :internal-events landed via EP-0029 A6 â€” so the split maps onto an existing surface rather than inventing one.

=== WHY re-frame2 IS UNUSUALLY WELL-PLACED TO DO THIS ===
Most of the machinery already exists and is spec'd:
  - The delivery boundary is real and named: transition selection happens after the cofx ensure-step, per spec/005 line 444, so there is an identified point "before transition selection runs" to reject at.
  - The observability channel has a precedent with settled semantics: :rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op is already the benign, single-signalled trace for an event that selected nothing (spec/005 Â§Transition resolution). A rejected-event trace is its sibling and should follow the same rules â€” benign grade, single-signalled, and NO accompanying no-change :rf.machine/transition.
  - The failure vocabulary exists: [:schemas :data] failures emit :rf.error/schema-validation-failure with :where :machine-data, and :output uses :where :machine-output. An event rejection has an obvious :where :machine-event slot in the same scheme.

=== THE DESIGN QUESTION THAT NEEDS MIKE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DECISION ===
v6 chose DROP-AND-REPORT for an invalid external event. re-frame2's house posture is fail-loud at the boundary (bad :schemas key, non-map :schemas, malformed :region-order are all registration errors). Those are not in tension â€” registration is authoring time, event delivery is runtime, and dropping a malformed event at runtime is the same instinct as the existing unhandled-event no-op. But it IS a choice, and the two candidate readings differ observably:
  (i) v6's reading â€” drop, trace, machine untouched. Consistent with unhandled-no-op. An invalid event from a misbehaving caller cannot take a machine down.
  (ii) fail-loud reading â€” :rf.error/schema-validation-failure, roll back, as [:schemas :data] does today. Consistent with the machine's own data contract.
RECOMMENDATION: (i), with the error vocabulary available as an opt-in, because the asymmetry is real â€” :data is the machine's own invariant and it authored it, whereas an inbound event is someone else's payload arriving at a trust boundary.

=== SCOPE, DELIBERATELY BOUNDED ===
This bead is [:schemas :events] only. :tags and :meta are the other two declaration-only categories and are NOT in scope: :tags is a closed vocabulary check that would be better served at registration than at delivery, and :meta has no runtime read path at all. Wiring one category is a self-contained change; wiring three is three designs wearing one bead.

DO NOT start implementation before the drop-versus-throw question above is answered â€” it determines the trace vocabulary, the rollback behaviour and the tests, so guessing it wrong costs the whole change.

GATES when it lands: implementation/machines suite (clojure -M:test from implementation/machines/), npm run test:cljs for substrate contract tests, and spec/005 is a hot-zone file so this sequences against any other machine-spec work in flight.

notes:
--- MAYOR §3 CHECK 2026-09-08 22:2x AUSEST — THE SPEC HAS ALREADY RULED ON THIS, AND NAMES THE ACTIVATION CONDITION. IT IS NOT MET ---
I went looking for whether this bead needs Mike or is already answered, and the answer is in the normative
text it is about. spec/005-StateMachines.md carries an SA-4 RECORD immediately above line 531:
    "SA-4 record — declaration-only sub-key wiring is post-v1, untracked. Per SPEC-AUTHORING §SA-4,
     'carry no wired behaviour YET' is a :post-v1 tracked CANDIDATE ... so it remains a post-v1,
     untracked note"
and then it gives a WIRE-WHEN condition for each of the three unwired sub-keys. For this one, verbatim:
    "[:schemas :events] WIRES WHEN a consumer needs send-time payload validation for a machine's internal
     event vocabulary — the [:machine-id [:inner-event <payload>]] inner form — that reg-event's
     outer-event :schema (the :where :event boundary) cannot reach. CONCRETELY: a real machine whose inner
     events carry structured payloads reports a bad-payload bug that only a :where :machine-event check
     would have caught."
SO THIS IS NOT AN UNDECIDED DESIGN QUESTION. It is a post-v1 feature whose activation trigger the spec
already states, and the trigger is CONSUMER-DRIVEN: a real machine reporting a real bad-payload bug. No
such report exists. Dispatching it now would be building ahead of the condition the spec sets for
building it — which is the gold-plating the stance rejects, on a surface the spec explicitly parked.
EVERY PREMISE THE BEAD LEANS ON DOES CHECK OUT, and that is worth recording so nobody re-verifies:
  * :rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op is real — 4 implementation files (registration, parallel, result,
    transition). The sibling-trace design has a live precedent.
  * The :where vocabulary is real and the slot is ALREADY NAMED: :where :machine-data and
    :where :machine-output are used widely, and :where :machine-event ALREADY APPEARS in spec/005 — in
    exactly this wire-when sentence. The spec reserved the slot while parking the work.
  * :internal-events is real — implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/internal_events.cljc, 18
    hits. The public/internal event split the bead wants maps onto an existing surface.
ONE THING IN THE SPEC IS NOW STALE, and it is small: the SA-4 record says this is a candidate "with NO
BEAD FILED". A bead IS filed — this one, 2026-09-07. That does not change the disposition; it just means
the record's parenthetical is out of date.
AND ONE CROSS-BEAD SYMMETRY WORTH KEEPING: I measured §No silent swallow's scope on rf2-dokz an hour ago
and found it does NOT reach a live-actor replacement, because the runtime CAN act on the supplied input.
It DOES reach this case — a dispatched event that fails a declared schema is precisely "a recognised input
that cannot be honoured", so if this is ever wired, dropping silently is not an option and the bead's
deadletter-style trace is required rather than optional. Same principle, opposite answers, both measured.
MY RECOMMENDATION: leave this bead OPEN as the tracked record of a parked feature, and do NOT dispatch it
until the spec's own wire-when condition fires. I have deliberately NOT deferred it on a date — I cleared
exactly that kind of date-standing-in-for-an-event off rf2-fo4ng this same tick, and doing it here would
repeat the mistake. A consumer bug report is the trigger; no calendar entry can stand in for one.
--- RULING 2026-09-08 — DECIDED. DO NOT WIRE [:schemas :events]. NOT DISPATCHABLE. ---

DECISION: `[:schemas :events]` stays DECLARATION-ONLY. No runtime wiring is built now.
The drop-vs-throw question this bead was blocked on is nonetheless CLOSED so it is never
re-litigated: when the consumer trigger fires, the semantics are REJECT-AND-REPORT at the
delivery boundary with `:rollback? false`, snapshot untouched, epoch outcome `:ok` — never
rollback, never a silent benign-info-only drop. The "yet" in spec/005 line 528 STAYS; this is
a parked feature, not a permanently-declarative stance. ONE small piece of work IS warranted
now and is split to its own bead: a documentation correction, because spec/005 currently
asserts something FALSE (finding 1 below).

WHO WON: two independent reviews. The dossier author recommended wiring now (its "Option A").
The Codex reviewer recommended retaining the consumer-triggered deferral, pre-recording the
semantics, and correcting the docs. CODEX WINS ON TIMING; THE DOSSIER WINS ON SHAPE. Codex's
position wins because its measurements destroyed the two pillars of the dossier's urgency
(findings 2 and 3), and because the mayor's own §3 check on this bead (2026-09-08 22:2x, in the
note above) reached the deferral answer independently from the spec text. Where the two reviews
AGREE, unanimously: rollback is wrong; removing `:events` from the closed sub-key set is wrong;
benign-info-only reporting is wrong; `:tags` and `:meta` stay out of scope; and the bead's own
stated premise is false.

=== LOAD-BEARING FINDINGS. RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE THIS SESSION — DO NOT RE-DERIVE. ===

(1) THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE, AND SO IS THE SPEC SENTENCE IT QUOTES.
spec/005-StateMachines.md:523 (the `:schemas` table row) and :531 (the SA-4 wire-when trigger)
both assert that `reg-event`'s `:schema` "cannot reach a machine's internal event vocabulary".
It CAN. The `reg-machine` opts `:schema` validates the whole OUTER vector
`[:machine-id [:inner-event <payload>]]` at the `:where :event` boundary, and the inner event is
element 1 of it. Proven by a PASSING test:
implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_schema_arity_test.clj:159
(`event-schema-arity-validates-outer-vector`) rejects a malformed nested `:auth.login/submit`
payload BEFORE the handler runs, using `[:tuple [:= flow-id] [:tuple [:= :auth.login/submit]
Credentials]]` — `:tuple`, not `:cat`, so the nested inner vector is validated as a vector rather
than flattened by `:cat`'s sequence-regex semantics. Both reviewers found this independently.
The real gap is ERGONOMIC (co-location, per-event keying, tooling legibility) plus ONE genuine
capability gap — finding 4.

(2) THE "ZERO BLAST RADIUS" CENSUS IS FALSE, AND A PASSING TEST ALREADY PINS A VALUE SHAPE THAT
CONTRADICTS BOTH PROPOSED DESIGNS.
The dossier measured zero in-repo declarations on two token axes with a strong positive control
(92 hits / 49 files for the `:data` sibling on the same corpus and instrument). The census misses
a declaration assembled INDIRECTLY:
implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_schemas_grammar_test.clj:45-57 binds a local
`schemas` map containing `:events {:counter/inc [:map [:by :int]]}`, registers it at line 50, and
asserts `(= schemas (:schemas meta))` — the WHOLE map round-trips through the `:rf/machine`
projection. Two consequences: (a) blast radius is small but NOT zero; (b) that fixture pins a
PAYLOAD-MAP interpretation (`[:map [:by :int]]`), whereas both reviewers' designs validate the
WHOLE INNER VECTOR (`[:counter/inc {:by 1}]`). An isolated Malli probe (Codex) confirmed the map
schema ACCEPTS `{:by 1}` and REJECTS `[:counter/inc {:by 1}]`. The validator grammar leaves
sub-key values opaque (lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1398), so the accepted key settles neither
reading. ANY FUTURE WIRING MUST STATE WHICH VALUE IS CHECKED, what an absent event-id entry
means, and must update that fixture.
METHOD NOTE for the next census here: the miss is by CONSTRUCTION, not by token axis — a
structural regex over source text cannot see a value assembled through a let-binding, so two
token axes agreeing is not proof of zero.

(3) THE DOSSIER'S STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR ERROR-GRADE REPORTING DOES NOT HOLD. AN ERROR TRACE IS
NOT AN ALWAYS-ON ERROR RECORD.
The dossier's reason 3 for wiring now was that error grade reaches error listeners, the frame's
`:observability :errors` sink and the console fallback, and therefore avoids the "machine
silently stops transitioning" hazard that data_validation.cljc:134-144 records having already
happened once. IT WOULD NOT. `rf.trace/emit-error!` is the DEV trace path
(implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:900); the always-on error stream is a SEPARATE
router operation (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3127, conditional on the
boundary-rejected marker). Verified structurally this session at
implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/data_validation.cljc:288-294:

    (when (and rollback? (= :machine-data where))
      (emit-machine-data-rejection-record! machine-id frame-id phase))
    (rf.trace/emit-error! :rf.error/schema-validation-failure tags)

and the comment immediately above it states the intent in as many words: promotion is for the
`:rollback? true` MACHINE-DATA arms only, and keying on the boundary too "is what stops a future
promoted arm reaching the always-on axis by default." So a NEW `:where :machine-event` /
`:rollback? false` arm would reach the always-on stream NOT AT ALL unless promotion is added
deliberately. Codex's JVM probe measured exactly that: 0 error-stream records after a schema
error trace, 0 after an ordinary event-schema refusal
(implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:801), and 1 after an explicit
`dispatch-error-record!` — a positive control proving the listener was live. Same for the
`:internal-events` refusal (registration.cljc:840), which calls only `emit-error!`.
CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY IMPLEMENTER: REJECTION AND REPORTING ARE TWO SEPARATE DECISIONS. If visible
reporting is the contract, the structural always-on record must be emitted EXPLICITLY alongside
the rich dev diagnostic, using the existing channel — not assumed to follow from the op name.
This is why the dossier's "small and well-bounded" cost was under-priced, and it is the single
biggest reason not to build this speculatively.

(4) THE ONE THING THAT SURVIVES AS A REAL CAPABILITY GAP: SPAWNED ACTORS.
An opts `:schema` hangs off a `reg-event` registration; opts including `:schema` are stored for
the registered TYPE at registration.cljc:1327. But `handler-meta-for` (registration.cljc:1420)
builds spawned-actor metadata from the spec carrying only the machine discriminator fields — the
type's opts `:schema` is NOT inherited. So a spawned actor cannot be covered by the outer-vector
workaround at all. This is the ONLY non-ergonomic argument for wiring, and it is what the future
trigger should name.

(5) THE INSERTION POINT IS NOT AS EARLY AS THE DOSSIER'S TABLE SUGGESTS.
The dossier correctly relocates the boundary from the bead's "cofx ensure-step" claim (one step
too late) to beside `reject-internal-event-external-dispatch` (call site registration.cljc:1005;
fn defined :821-856), before boot and transition selection. But `prepare-machine-ctx` derives and
reconciles a snapshot BEFORE that check (registration.cljc:478 and :963), and a spawn completion
can invoke the author's on-done fold at :991, also before it. So "before all snapshot derivation
and application callbacks" is FALSE; "before bootstrap entry actions, cofx generation and
transition selection" is TRUE. SECOND TRAP: routed events APPEND outer callback arguments to the
inner vector (registration.cljc:98), so validating merely `(second event)` misses payloads
supplied by HTTP-style replies. THIRD: framework start / timer / completion carriers need
explicit treatment if the event map is ever read as a CLOSED vocabulary — checking only DECLARED
MATCHING entries and letting unknown events fall through to normal unhandled behaviour is the
smaller initial design.

(6) TOOLING AND REDACTION ARE REAL INTEGRATION WORK, NOT FREE.
- Xray: `attach-violations` has NO `:machine-event` case and leaves unknown cases UNATTACHED
  (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:2989). The dossier's "consumers
  route on `:where` and pick it up with one new case" was explicitly taken on trust and is wrong
  as stated.
- Story: a generic selector fallback exists, but the projected record does not preserve the
  proposed actor-id / event-id distinction
  (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/evidence.cljc:119 and :144).
- REDACTION LEAK — verified at source this session: the shared redactor's value-bearing slots are
  `[:value :received :explain :explain-humanized :rf.fx/args :rf.sub/query-v]`
  (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:103). `:event` is NOT among them. The
  dossier's proposed tag map carries the SAME payload three times — in `:event`, `:value` AND
  `:received`. Codex's probe returned `:rf/redacted` for `:value`/`:received` while `:event`
  retained a `{:password {:sensitive? true}}` value verbatim. FIX: do not carry the duplicate
  payload tag; use the existing diagnostic value slots plus structural `:event-id` / `:actor-id`
  identifiers. (This measures the redactor seam, not an end-to-end leak through every projection.)

(7) UPSTREAM v6 DOES NOT ENDORSE QUIET REPORTING. Codex re-fetched primary sources during review:
npm registry dist-tags still report `6.0.0-alpha.52`; changelog read pinned at statelyai/xstate
`2c4eeb4881c7fab607ef2dd410e547c17f1bff87`. alpha.50 pairs the `onRejectedEvent` hook and the
`@xstate.deadletter` inspection event with a DEVELOPMENT CONSOLE WARNING, and keeps
machine-produced schema faults distinct from external rejection. So the bead's option (i) —
benign, info-grade, addressable by nobody — OVER-READS alpha.50. Both reviewers reject it.
Independently: the mayor note above records that spec/005 §No silent swallow DOES reach this case
(a dispatched event failing a declared schema is "a recognised input that cannot be honoured"), so
if this is ever wired an addressable report is REQUIRED, not optional. alpha.42's
`schemas.internalEvents` needs NO new re-frame2 surface — see the rejected list.

(8) STALE BOOKKEEPING: spec/005:530's SA-4 record says this candidate has "no bead filed". A bead
IS filed — this one, 2026-09-07.
=== THE PRE-DECIDED SEMANTICS, so this is never re-argued when the trigger fires ===
Check at the `reject-internal-event-external-dispatch` position (registration.cljc:1005), same
`or`-chain, same short-circuit shape. EXTERNAL DISPATCHES ONLY — an in-macrostep `:raise` drains
inside the macrostep FIFO and never re-enters via `reg-event` dispatch, so it is excluded by
construction and needs no rule. On violation: return the benign `{}` — no snapshot install, no
boot, no transition, no `:fx`; a per-handler refusal, not a drain halt, so the surrounding epoch
outcome stays `:ok` and downstream queued events drain normally. Emit
`:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` with `:where :machine-event`, `:phase :delivery`,
`:rollback? false`, and `:event-id` naming WHICH declared schema failed — AND emit the structural
always-on record EXPLICITLY (finding 3), reusing the existing channel rather than adding a
callback API. Validate the whole ROUTED INNER VECTOR, accounting for appended outer callback args
(finding 5), and update the grammar fixture (finding 2). Check only declared matching entries;
unknown events fall through to normal unhandled behaviour. `:rf.machine/event-received` fires
before the refusal and that is correct — the event WAS received; already true of the
`:internal-events` refusal today. The new `:where` enum member must land in BOTH pinned copies
(spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1119 and spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2665) in the SAME commit.
Acceptance shape, if built: malformed first event (no snapshot, no entry, no cofx generator, no
action); malformed event to an EXISTING SPAWNED ACTOR (same snapshot); a subsequent valid event
still progresses the queue; both nested and outer-appended payload forms; absent schema and absent
matching entry pinned; private external events still get exactly ONE refusal; raises and framework
start/timer/completion traffic keep working; one explicit error-stream record; a sensitive payload
absent from ALL new diagnostic copies; production erasure explicit if the check is dev-gated.

=== DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE — DO NOT RESURRECT ===
- ROLLBACK (`:rollback? true`). Nothing is committed at this position, so it would be a claim
  about a transaction that never existed. Making it true requires moving the check past boot and
  transition selection, which contradicts spec/005:1538's "never reaches transition selection at
  all" and lets a malformed event BOOT A MACHINE. Both reviewers reject it; not a close call.
- BENIGN-INFO-ONLY trace (the bead's option (i) literally, a `:rf.machine.event/schema-rejected`
  sibling of `unhandled-no-op`). Poor feedback when an author explicitly supplied a failing schema;
  over-reads alpha.50 (finding 7).
- REMOVING `:events` from the closed sub-key set. Discards the single-home machine contract that
  motivated `:schemas` (EP-0029 A3: tools learn data, events, output, tags and meta from one
  place), and buys no consistency since `:tags`/`:meta` stay declaration-only anyway.
- PERMANENT DECLARATIVE STATUS (striking the "yet", the SA-4 record's fourth option). Rejected: it
  gives up a useful future contract with no evidence that tooling-only use is sufficient,
  particularly given the spawned-actor gap (finding 4). The "yet" STAYS.
- `:tags` and `:meta`. Unchanged, unwired, out of scope. Both reviewers agree; the bead's original
  scoping instinct here was right.
- A separate `schemas.internal-events` sub-key (v6 alpha.42's spelling). NOT NEEDED and it would
  violate the closed sub-key set for no gain: because the check runs only on external dispatches,
  an event listed in `:internal-events` is refused on the VISIBILITY axis before its schema is ever
  consulted — alpha.42's semantics reached with no new declaration surface. Do NOT touch
  `:internal-events` itself (the set form, the reserved-`:rf/*` check, the refusal error); it is
  settled and shipped (EP-0029 A6).
- Production-validation knobs, retries, a second rejection protocol, nag diagnostics, a callback
  API.

=== WHAT HAPPENS NOW ===
This bead is RE-SCOPED and RE-TITLED as the parked record, and dropped to P4 because it is not
queued work — it was appearing in `bd ready` as a dispatchable feature and that is exactly how a
worker gets briefed to build a thing the spec parked. DO NOT DISPATCH IT. Its trigger stays
consumer-driven (spec/005:531) and is SHARPENED by this ruling: a machine author who needs the
co-located per-event contract — PARTICULARLY on a spawned actor, which the outer-vector workaround
cannot reach at all — and who can supply the actual event shapes. That need alone justifies
implementation; it does NOT require waiting for a production incident. No calendar date substitutes
for it, per the mayor note above.
The one piece of actionable work is split out as a documentation-correction bead (see
discovered-from children): correct the false "cannot reach" claim, make the declaration-only status
author-visible with the working alternative, and refresh the stale "no bead filed" parenthetical.

--- MAYOR 2026-09-08 23:2x AUSEST — THE RULING LANDED AND MATCHES MY RECOMMENDATION; BUT A PREMISE I QUOTED IS FALSE ---
A sibling process ruled on this bead while I was working, and filed rf2-e0x7 out of it. The ruling: this
bead STAYS PARKED, do not implement any runtime validation — which is what my §3 note above recommended,
and rf2-e0x7's own text points back here for "the full measured analysis". Good.
BUT ONE PREMISE I QUOTED FROM THE SPEC IS ITSELF FALSE, and it is the load-bearing half of the wire-when
sentence I reproduced. spec/005-StateMachines.md asserts at BOTH :523 and :531 that reg-event's :schema
"cannot reach a machine's internal event vocabulary". IT CAN. I verified the refutation at source rather
than relaying it: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_schema_arity_test.clj:159 carries a
PASSING test, event-schema-arity-validates-outer-vector, whose own docstring says the :schema opts key
"validates the dispatched OUTER event vector at the :where :event boundary — a malformed :submit payload
is rejected BEFORE the handler runs". It works because the schema is written with :tuple rather than :cat,
so the nested inner vector is validated as a vector instead of being flattened by sequence-regex semantics.
WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. It does NOT change the disposition: the wire-when condition is still
consumer-driven and still unmet, and the ruling parks this bead. What it changes is WHY the question kept
re-opening — rf2-e0x7 says the false sentence is the reason, and I can see how: a reader is told the outer
:schema cannot reach the inner form, concludes only [:schemas :events] can, and re-files the gap. The
answer available today is to write the outer schema with :tuple.
SO MY NOTE ABOVE QUOTES A TRUE SPEC SENTENCE THAT SAYS A FALSE THING, and I am flagging it here rather
than editing that note, because the note is an accurate record of what the spec said when I read it. The
correction goes to rf2-e0x7, which I have dispatched.

--- MAYOR 2026-09-08 23:5x AUSEST — THE RESIDUAL GAP IS NOW NAMED, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE SPEC SAID ---
rf2-e0x7's worker (PR #9500) established what [:schemas :events] would ACTUALLY close, and I verified the
load-bearing half at source rather than relaying it. This matters here because the parked status is better
founded with a real gap than with the false one.
THE FALSE SENTENCES CONTRADICTED THEIR OWN FILE, which nobody had noticed: spec/005:965 ALREADY states the
truth — "Its :schema key is the validator for the dispatched OUTER EVENT VECTOR — the :where :event
boundary" — while :523 and :531 asserted that same schema "cannot reach a machine's internal event
vocabulary". One file, both claims, roughly 440 lines apart. I read :965 myself to confirm it.
THE GENUINE GAP IS SPAWNED ACTORS. registration.cljc:1327 stores the whole opts map for the registered
TYPE, but handler-meta-for at :1395 builds the handler-meta from a machine SPEC and stamps only
{:rf/machine? true :rf/machine machine}. I read its docstring: it is "the surface the lazy-actor-handler
resolver drives a SPAWNED ACTOR's cascade through". So the opts :schema is never inherited by an actor —
the :tuple outer-vector workaround covers SINGLETONS and cannot reach spawned actors at all.
WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS BEAD'S PARKED STATUS: it strengthens it rather than reopening it. There IS a
capability gap, so the feature is not pointless — but the gap is narrower and more specific than the spec
claimed, and the wire-when trigger the SA-4 record states (a real machine reporting a bad-payload bug) is
still the right trigger and still unmet. Three lesser residuals were also named: per-event keying rather
than one alternation for the whole machine, co-location in the single-home contract, and per-event tooling
legibility.
AND MY OWN §3 FINDING WAS CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY: the SA-4 record's "no bead filed" parenthetical was
stale, and the worker found this bead's own id already on main at spec/005:4543. The record's title also
said "untracked", which the worker deleted as a fresh self-contradiction now that this bead exists.

--- MAYOR 2026-09-09 AUSEST — WHY THIS RULED/PARKED BEAD STAYS `open`, RECORDED ONCE SO THE NEXT §3 PASS STOPS RE-ASKING ---
Every backlog reread meets this bead in the ready view, reads a title beginning RULED or PARKED, and has
to re-derive whether it should be closed. Here is the answer, and it is not the obvious one.

**CLOSING IT WOULD DELETE IT.** `bd gc`'s decay phase removes closed beads past a 14-day retention, and it
runs regularly here — the commit log names each run in its own subject (`a37a5bf5ac` 2026-08-21, 618
deleted; `42ea359b1e` 2026-09-02, 851 deleted, Mike; `5e22f68194` 2026-09-08). Measured today: **no closed

That is not hypothetical for beads of THIS kind. **20 of the 39 bead ids `CLAUDE.md` cites no longer
resolve**, and 1018 distinct dangling ids are cited in `spec/` or `docs/` prose. Full measurement,
options and my recommendation are on **[[rf2-nj0c]]**.

**SO THE DISPOSITION IS DELIBERATE: this bead is a tracked RECORD, and `open` is currently the only status
that preserves a record.** It is not queued work, it must not be dispatched, and its title says so. The
cost is one line in the ready view; the cost of the alternative is losing the ruling.

**THIS BECOMES REVISITABLE THE MOMENT rf2-nj0c IS ANSWERED.** If retention is raised or cited beads are
exempted from decay, then closing this bead is safe and it should be closed — that is the cheaper resting
place for a record nobody must act on. Until then, leave it open.

=== RELEASE CONDITION MET 2026-09-12. The note above holds this bead `open` for ONE stated reason, and that reason is now false. Closing it. ===

THE NOTE ABOVE SAYS, verbatim: "CLOSING IT WOULD DELETE IT ... a close is a deletion on a fortnight's
delay", and then names its own release: "THIS BECOMES REVISITABLE THE MOMENT rf2-nj0c IS ANSWERED. If
retention is raised or cited beads are exempted from decay, then closing this bead is safe and it
should be closed -- that is the cheaper resting place for a record nobody must act on."

rf2-nj0c IS ANSWERED. Closed 2026-09-09, and its close reason is unambiguous: "Routine bead decay is
OFF permanently; the sanctioned invocation is `bd gc --skip-decay --force` and `--older-than` is never
passed again." It records the operator changing the recurring GC prompt himself, in his own words:
"Compact the beads store. Do not delete any closed beads -- their close reasons are normative records
here." And it states the effect in terms: "THE CLOCK IS NOW STOPPED ... Under the new instruction no
run deletes anything, ever."

DECAY BEING OFF ENTIRELY IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN EITHER CONDITION THE NOTE NAMED. It asked for
retention raised, or cited beads exempted; it got the whole phase retired. So the cheaper resting
place the note points at is now available, and by its own instruction this bead takes it.

I CHECKED WHETHER ANY SIBLING IS HELD BY THE SAME FALSE PREMISE, rather than assuming this bead was

NOTHING ABOUT THE RULING CHANGES. The feature stays PARKED, the pre-decided semantics stand, the six

RECORDED IN NOTES AS WELL AS IN THE CLOSE REASON, deliberately: reopening a bead ERASES close_reason
and closed_at with no copy kept, and this bead exists to be a durable record. The reasoning therefore

title: spec(011): write the JVM-vs-Node full-document server pipeline discriminator once beside the :renderer seam
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 by the ruling on rf2-kuky.44 (sub-question iii — flagged to the Hicasso owner, not ruled there). Not blocked on anything._

## Problem

Two complete full-document server pipelines ship: the JVM `re-frame.ssr.ring/ssr-handler` (hiccup emitter + Ring envelope) and the Node `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:~294`; `react-dom/server` + CLJS envelope). The second is the TAUGHT Hicasso Node SSR door — `docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md:50-81`, `skills/reagent-migration/references/ssr-hydrate.md:36-54`, the MIG-23 fixture `skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs:73-87` — not test-only, as the wave-3 fable doc first said. Two review passes re-counted it as duplication because the discriminator is written nowhere: `spec/011-SSR.md:416-418` writes the `:renderer` seam contract (`(fn [{:keys [frame-id request opts]}] → {:body-html :render-hash})`) but not "one full-document pipeline per substrate — JVM hiccup vs Node React".

## Target

One paragraph (or a two-row table) beside the `:renderer` seam paragraph in `spec/011-SSR.md` (~:416-418) — or in 004B §The SSR consumption boundary if the Hicasso owner prefers — naming the two pipelines, the substrate each serves, and that they are one contract with substrate-forced realisations (the discriminator the fable doc's own Non-goals section reached). Cross-link from `docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md` if it helps. No code change. rf2-323z (the request-frame platform bug on `server/render`) is CLOSED at tip — do not re-file it.

## Hot zone

Neither `spec/011-SSR.md` nor 004B is on the hot-zone list. Gates: `mkdocs build --strict` (covers `spec/` via the staging hook) and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for anchors; verify anchors and any table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.

## Acceptance

The discriminator sentence exists once, in spec, and the hicasso guide links to it (or vice versa); both gates green.
notes:
2026-09-06 — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9321 (open, ready for review). One paragraph added to spec/011-SSR.md at line 422, immediately after the ssr-node recipe pointer and beside the :renderer seam (416-420), as the target section asked. Bead left OPEN; the close is the mayor's.

WHAT IT SAYS. JVM pipeline = re-frame.ssr.ring/ssr-handler (ring.clj:101), whose DEFAULT body renderer is Spec 011's own hiccup emitter (pipeline.clj:547 local-renderer -> :583 ssr/render-to-string; emit.cljc:836) and which owns the whole Ring response — head, __rf_payload, :html-shell, status, headers, cookies, redirects, error projection, teardown (pipeline.clj:615-620 is the code's own list), with stream-handler as its chunked counterpart (ring.clj:62). Node pipeline = re-frame.hicasso.server/render (server.cljs:295), where a view resolves to a React element so the body can only come from react-dom/server renderToString (server.cljs:56, :387, :390-391), and the page returned is its own small envelope (server.cljs:106-127) with no status/headers/cookies/redirects/error projection because it is not an HTTP host (server.cljs:47). Shared: one :platform :server frame per request destroyed in a finally (pipeline.clj:295,:304 + ring.clj:329-332; server.cljs:351,:381,:428-437), one fail-closed :payload policy (both via payload-policy/apply-policy — ring/payload.clj:81-82, server.cljs:404-409), one pinned __rf_payload id (shell.clj:46-51, server.cljs:52,:102). Substrate-forced difference: hiccup-tier render hash on the JVM (pipeline.clj:582,:586) vs adoption tier and NO hash for Hicasso (server.cljs:44-46,:412-414; payload_policy.cljc:746-748); streaming JVM-only (server.cljs:31-37 gives the reason). Door-scope difference, stated as such: the Node payload carries neither :rf/runtime-db nor :rf/head-hash (server.cljs:400-415), both of which the JVM projects (pipeline.clj:634,:638-639,:645; ring/payload.clj:93). And explicitly NOT the ssr-node crossing, which is the JVM pipeline with a remote body (node.clj:393,:378; server.cljs:443-449) — 011:418 already describes it.

BEAD-VS-CODE. Two differences, both resolved for the code. (1) server.cljs:~294 in the description; (defn render is at 295. (2) 'hiccup emitter + Ring envelope' is true of the DEFAULT renderer only — with a :renderer supplied (pipeline.clj:621) the same handler serves a React body across the ssr-node crossing, so the prose says 'default'. Every other premise held at tip, including that 011 names Hicasso only at :849/:853 and never names server/render.

ACCEPTANCE. Met by the 'vice versa' arm: 011 links OUT to docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md#render-a-page-from-a-snapshot, so the change stays inside one file and clear of the skills/guide surfaces other workers held this tick.

Two near-misses that are NOT residue: the :ssr.streaming/render-shell / render-continuation / build-final-payload strings in spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-streaming*.edn are conformance trace :call labels (the deleted hooks carried a trailing !), and re-frame.ssr.streaming/build-final-payload (streaming.cljc:684) is a live fn 011:93 correctly cites.

HAND-CHECKS. The paragraph is prose, not a fence — 18 fence markers precede it, an even count, so both link gates did inspect it; links were hand-checked anyway by resolving all five against the BUILT site (four in-page anchors each match exactly one id= in site/spec/011-SSR/index.html; the cross-tree link emitted href="../../core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration/#render-a-page-from-a-snapshot" whose target carries that id). Nothing parses 011's prose. Control: the same script returns ssr_node=true for implementation/ssr-node/src/service.cjs.

OBSERVATION, not actioned: 011:849's adoption-tier bullet is titled 'Native UIx roots', but a Hicasso root is adoption-tier too (server.cljs:44-46, payload_policy.cljc:746-748) and :853 states the rule generally. Widening that title is a different edit on a different paragraph.

`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md` is 318 lines / 63,758 bytes — 4x the 16 KB per-leaf byte ceiling in `skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline (1.3x the 250-line ceiling; the byte ceiling exists precisely for long unwrapped table rows like this file's). The catalogue exemption there is a test, not a pass: "would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?"

## APPLYING THE CATALOGUE TEST HONESTLY

ops.md is two things stapled together:

**Catalogue (keep together, locked):** §Read, §Frames, §Write, §Trace, §Live watch, §Signal recording, §Hot-reload coordination, §Time-travel, §Dropped from v1 — op tables plus the protocol sections that `spec/design.md:134` and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:33` explicitly LOCK into ops.md ("The hot-reload protocol and v1 → v2 surface-map both live in ops.md as sections rather than separate leaves"), and that `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` reads from ops.md by anchor (`ops.md#hot-reload-coordination`, `section-from @ops-md "Hot-reload coordination"`). Roughly 42 KB.

**Not catalogue (split candidate):** lines 108–203, ~22 KB — §DOM source bridge, §Reading what's on screen (`read-dom` vs `read-ui`), and §Hicasso evidence (mounted boundaries / read attribution / render cause). This is a self-contained "what is on screen and why did it render" concern: the Hicasso block alone is ~10 KB of honesty-marker prose (added under rf2-6c12m, `3043d1aca4`, AFTER the file-structure lock was written), not op rows. SKILL.md's loading map already routes to it as its own task shape (`SKILL.md:186-188`: two rows pointing at `ops.md#view--rendered-content…` and `ops.md#hicasso-evidence…`), and `mcp-transport.md:84-88` links the five screen/evidence tools to those anchors.

Token test, both directions: an agent doing a read/dispatch/trace/time-travel session loads 64 KB and never reads the 22 KB screen block; an agent answering "why did this boundary render?" loads 64 KB for a 10 KB section. A split reduces tokens-per-session for every session that is not both — which is nearly all of them. That is the opposite of the "multiplies file handles without reducing tokens" case the exemption protects.

## RECOMMENDATION (one PR)

- New leaf `references/screen-reads.md` (~22 KB — itself still over the ceiling, but one concern; name is a suggestion) holding ops.md lines 108–203 verbatim: DOM source bridge, read-dom vs read-ui, Hicasso evidence.
- ops.md keeps a one-line row per moved section in its §Contents pointing at the new leaf; its own size drops to ~42 KB, and everything the design lock and the prompt-regression test name stays where it is.
- Update the anchors: `SKILL.md:186-188` (loading map), `mcp-transport.md:84-88` (five rows' "Semantics home"), `recipes.md` wherever it links `ops.md#dom-source-bridge` / `#read-dom…` / `#hicasso-evidence…` (grep before moving), and `spec/design.md:119` + `spec/authoring-prompt.md:34` file-structure listings (add the new leaf; the lock is on hot-reload + v1 map, which do not move).
- Do NOT split hot-reload or the v1 map (locked + tested), and do not split the op tables (that is the catalogue the exemption is for).

If the maintainer would rather keep ops.md whole, the honest alternative is to record ops.md as an accepted exception in `skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline with the reasoning — the current state is neither.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose` (mcp-transport.md rows survive; 29 = 29); `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (every moved anchor resolves — skills/ is in its roots; this is the gate that catches a broken `ops.md#hicasso-…` link); `bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` (`skill-router-still-points-at-hot-reload`, `hot-reload-*`, `ops-md-raw-eval-rows-carry-privacy-carveout` all read ops.md and must stay green — they will, since nothing they name moves). Verify by hand that SKILL.md still loads at most two leaves for the screen-read task shapes (it does: SKILL.md + the new leaf).

title: ci(classifier): no skills/re-frame2/* arm in report-changed-surfaces.sh — flagship skill arms 0 of 29 surfaces
description:
The surface classifier `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` carries arms for `skills/re-frame2-pair/*` and `skills/reagent-migration/*`, and **no general `skills/re-frame2/*` arm** — only the single pinned leaf `story-mcp-loop.md` is routed. So a change confined to the flagship authoring skill classifies as **0 of 29** surfaces true, `skills_structural` included.

MEASURED, not inferred, by the `rf2-ikbgk.4` worker on PR #10153 (9 files, 8 of them under `skills/re-frame2/`): the classifier was handed PATHS, never revisions — which is the documented misuse that reports every surface false at exit 0 — and a control whose arming was already known was taken beside it (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/assertion_strip.cljs` arms 6). So the 0 is the classifier answering correctly about its own arms, not an instrument misused.

**WHY IT COSTS NOTHING TODAY, WHICH IS ALSO WHY NOBODY HAS NOTICED.** The gates that actually grade this surface are UNGUARDED and run on every PR regardless of the classifier: `test.yml`'s "Repo invariant checks (skills, MCP, catalogues, namespaces)" job carries no `if:` guard and hosts the `check_skill_*` gates, and `verify-readme-links` likewise runs unconditionally. PR #10153 was graded green by exactly those jobs. So the classifier gap is latent rather than live, and a reader who checks whether the skill is covered will correctly find that it is — by a different mechanism than the one they are looking at.

**THE RISK IS A FUTURE ONE AND IT IS THE ORDINARY DIRECTION OF DRIFT.** Any job that is LATER put behind `skills_structural`, or any new skills gate wired to a surface guard rather than left unguarded, silently will not run for the flagship skill — the largest skill in the tree at 62 files, 47 leaves. The failure would present as a green PR, with nothing on screen naming the arm that did not fire. That is the "gates nobody nominated" class recorded in the memory `gate-rostering-by-name-grep-over-a-glob-is-wrong-in-both-directions`, reached through the classifier rather than through a gate roster.

**NOT YET A DECISION ABOUT WHAT TO DO.** Adding a `skills/re-frame2/*` arm is the obvious repair, but `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` is a CLAUDE.md hot-zone file with a mirror test (`implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`) that pins the classifier's outputs — so a change altering what the classifier OUTPUTS must move both halves in ONE commit, and that pairing is one-toucher by construction. It also needs someone to decide whether the flagship skill SHOULD arm `skills_structural`, or whether the deliberate design is that the unguarded invariant job covers it and the classifier arm would be redundant. Both readings are defensible and neither is recorded anywhere.

Ask before changing anything: which jobs would a `skills/re-frame2/*` arm newly schedule, and is that wanted? A wrong repair here adds CI time to every skills PR for no coverage gain.

Filed from `rf2-ikbgk.4`'s close reason; `.github/**` was outside that worker's fence, so it recorded the finding and stopped, which was correct.
notes: Audit #10153 revalidated this exact open finding against the current classifier and workflow. A general authoring-skill arm would newly schedule those unrelated suites/CLJS fixtures; its own Python skill gates and link checks already run unconditionally. No current coverage loss was established. close_reason:
DECIDED ON MEASUREMENT — DO NOT ADD THE ARM. No code change; the bead asked a question before anything was to be touched, and the answer is that the obvious repair is the wrong one.

## THE GAP IS REAL AND I REPRODUCED IT RATHER THAN RELAYING IT

Measured at trunk `23be281e07`, handing the classifier PATHS (never revisions — CLAUDE.md item (v)), with controls both ways:

| Path handed to `report-changed-surfaces.sh` | Surfaces true |
|---|---|
| `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md` (flagship) | **0 of 29** |
| `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md` | `skills_structural=true` |
| `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md` | `skills_structural=true` |

So the classifier is answering correctly about its own arms, and the two controls prove the instrument bites. The finding as filed is confirmed.

## WHAT THE ARM WOULD ACTUALLY BUY, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THE BEAD SAID TO ASK FIRST — NOTHING

Exactly three jobs are gated on `skills_structural` (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, `if: needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.skills_structural == 'true'` at lines 6176, 6369, 6466):

1. `skills-structural` — "Skills structural tests (changed skill paths only)"
2. `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure` — re-frame2-pair shipped-preload pure-core node-test (rf2-etsj8p)
3. `reagent-migration-fixture-cold-start` — reagent-migration MIG-23 SSR cold-start node-test (rf2-vpdrf)

Jobs 2 and 3 are fixture tests for **other skills** by their own names, so arming them on a flagship-skill PR is pure CI cost.

**And job 1 is the one that settles it. Its display name is misleading: "changed skill paths only" describes the JOB'S GATE, not a discovery loop.** Its body is a HARDCODED ROSTER of `working-directory:` steps — `skills/re-frame2-pair`, `skills/re-frame2-setup`, `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro`, `skills/re-frame2-improver` — each running that skill's own `bb tests/…`.

**The flagship skill has NO `tests/` tree at all**: `git ls-files "skills/re-frame2/**"` matching `tests/` reads **0** across its **62** tracked files, against a live control of five sibling skills that do carry one (`re-frame2-pair` 25 files, `reagent-migration` 6, `re-frame2-setup` 4, `re-frame2-improver` 2, `re-frame2-pair-retro` 2).

So adding the arm would schedule a job that runs four OTHER skills' suites and nothing of the flagship's, plus two unrelated node-test jobs. **Coverage gain for `skills/re-frame2/`: zero. Cost: three jobs on every flagship-skill PR.** That is precisely the "wrong repair adds CI time for no coverage gain" the bead itself warned about.

## THE ARM AND THE ROSTER STEP ARE TWO HALVES, AND THIS IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING

The reason the obvious repair fails is structural rather than incidental: because `skills-structural` dispatches by a fixed `working-directory:` roster, **a skill is covered only if BOTH its classifier arm AND its roster step exist.** Adding the arm alone is worse than nothing — it buys CI time and, more expensively, it makes the flagship LOOK covered to anyone who checks the classifier, which is the reassuring direction. Adding a roster step alone would be inert for the same reason in mirror.

**The flagship is nonetheless GRADED TODAY, by a different mechanism**, which is why nothing is broken: `test.yml`'s "Repo invariant checks (skills, MCP, catalogues, namespaces)" job carries no `if:` guard and hosts the `check_skill_*` gates, and `verify-readme-links` likewise runs unconditionally. The bead established that and I have not disturbed it.

**Band impact of the rejected change, recorded so nobody re-derives it**: none. A job gated off by `if:` still contributes a `COMPLETED`/`SKIPPED` row, so the arm would have flipped three rows from skipped to running without moving the count.

## THE TRIGGER THAT REOPENS THIS

**If `skills/re-frame2/` ever gains its own `tests/` tree, the arm becomes correct and must land WITH a `working-directory: skills/re-frame2` step in `skills-structural`, in one commit.** Until then the deliberate-design reading is the right one — and it is now recorded, which the bead correctly observed it was not.

The latent-drift risk the bead names is unchanged and is NOT dismissed: a future skills gate wired behind `skills_structural` still will not fire for the flagship. What this close changes is the repair — it is two halves, not one, and whoever adds that future gate needs to know that.

## WHY THIS IS CLOSED RATHER THAN HELD FOR MIKE

The bead asked for a decision between two defensible readings and said neither was recorded. The measurement above decides it without taste entering: one reading buys zero coverage. Holding a P3 open for a question already settled by measurement is the minutiae-litigation the project stance rules out — the item dies here with its reasoning recorded, and the reopening trigger is named above.

`.github/**` was outside the `rf2-ikbgk.4` worker's fence, so it recorded the finding and stopped. That was right, and the finding was good: the gap is real, it is simply not worth the repair it invites.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.

- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.

- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: skills/re-frame2-setup

Reviewer persona: senior CLJS/shadow-cljs build engineer reviewing a scaffolding skill as if an AI agent ran it verbatim on a clean machine today
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: skills/re-frame2-setup in full — SKILL.md (129), references/{first-counter,deps-versions,shadow-cljs,entry-namespace}.md (885), spec/{design,inputs,authoring-prompt}.md (265), tests/*.clj (1,920, read not run), evals/evals.json (67), README.md (229), package.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, LICENSE — ~3,550 lines

Gates run (from the frozen worktree root, PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8): check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py exit 0; check_skill_description_budget.py exit 0; check_skill_eval_docs.py exit 0; check_skill_eval_packaging.py exit 0; check_skill_package_refs.py exit 0; check_skill_redirect_anchors.py exit 0

Overall: the derived core of this skill is in very good shape. Every version pin, every `day8/re-frame2*` coordinate and `:local/root` directory, every API name, error id and event/fx id the leaves teach resolves at trunk, and the thirteen files match the template's emission on spot-check (the derivation locks pin the rest). What has drifted is the HAND-WRITTEN prose around the derived blocks — the two leaves that "explain" the build config and the npm/deps roster describe an older, pre-Story scaffold, and one of those descriptions produces a compile failure if followed.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. `shadow-cljs.md` explains a build config that is not the one the scaffold writes — its alias list drops `:dev`, which makes `compile app` / `watch app` fail  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: self-contract] [size: S]
- Where: skills/re-frame2-setup/references/shadow-cljs.md:22 (item 1), :24 (item 3), :26 (item 5); skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:28 (id 4, expectation 2)
- What: The "key by key" leaf teaches `:deps {:aliases [:shadow]}` (and the pure-JVM spelling `clojure -M:shadow -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli watch app`), while the scaffold it claims to explain is `{:deps {:aliases [:shadow :dev]}}` (first-counter.md:78), and the `:dev` alias is what puts Story on the classpath for the `stories/init` entry the dev build boots.
- Evidence: first-counter.md:86-87 / template `_shared/shadow-cljs.edn:21-22` carry `:dev {:modules {:main {:init-fn acme.my-app.stories/init}}}`; shadow-cljs 3.4.10 merges that build-level `:dev` map in dev mode (`shadow/build.clj:172-173 config-merge … (get config mode)`), and the template's own comment (`_shared/shadow-cljs.edn:9-10`) says `watch` and `compile` boot `stories/init`. `stories.cljs` requires `re-frame.story`, which is only on `deps.edn`'s `:dev` alias (first-counter.md:35). So a `[:shadow]`-only alias list fails the terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app` with exactly the error SKILL.md:110 catalogues ("The required namespace \"re-frame.story\" is not available"). The template's gated proof compiles with both aliases (`clojure -M:shadow:dev … compile app test`, emitted_test_run_test.clj:617, 1080). Two more divergences in the same leaf: item 5 (:26) spends a paragraph on a `:source-paths ["src" "test"]` key "the template emits" — the template's `_shared/shadow-cljs.edn` carries no `:source-paths` at all (13 lines: `:deps`, `:dev-http`, `:builds`); and item 3 (:24) says `:init-fn acme.my-app.core/init` is the fn called at bundle load without mentioning that under `watch`/`compile` it is `acme.my-app.stories/init` (the `:dev` override), which is the first thing an agent will meet when it wonders why `core/init` did not run in dev. evals.json:28 pins the wrong shape too: the id-4 (empty-shadow conversion) expectation reads "replaces shadow-cljs.edn's :dependencies with {:deps {:aliases [:shadow]}}", contradicting SKILL.md:82, which correctly says `[:shadow :dev]`. Where an agent reads it: the conversion route (SKILL.md:80-82) sends the agent to "the leaf's shapes" and any agent asked to explain or debug the build reads shadow-cljs.md.
- Action: Rewrite items 1, 3 and 5 of shadow-cljs.md against first-counter.md's `shadow-cljs.edn` — alias vector `[:shadow :dev]` with one sentence on what `:dev` carries (Story) and the pure-JVM spelling `clojure -M:shadow:dev -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli watch app`; item 3 gains the `:dev {:modules …}` override (dev boots `stories/init`, which hands every page but `#/stories` to `core/init`; release boots `core/init`); item 5 shrinks to "the scaffold carries no `:source-paths`; under `:deps` shadow ignores that key and warns, so add source dirs to `deps.edn`". Change evals.json:28 to `[:shadow :dev]`. One worker, one PR.

### 2. `deps-versions.md` §`package.json` says the scaffold declares "exactly three packages" — the recovery path SKILL.md routes through it drops Story's two npm packages  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: self-contract] [size: S]
- Where: skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md:123 (and :84-94, the `:local/root` table)
- What: The section reads "the scaffold's `package.json` declares exactly three packages — `shadow-cljs` … and `react` + `react-dom`", while the scaffold declares five (first-counter.md:51-59: `@xyflow/react 12.4.2` and `elkjs 0.11.1` beside them), as SKILL.md cardinal rule 2 (:53), the Done checklist (:98) and the skill's own spec/design.md L3 (:36) all say.
- Evidence: The two extra packages are not optional: Story's `:dev` alias pulls `day8/re-frame2-xray` (tools/story/deps.edn:525), Xray pulls `machines-viz` (tools/xray/deps.edn:75), and `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:36-37` requires `["@xyflow/react"]` and `["elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js"]` — a JS-require sweep over everything the dev classpath reaches finds exactly {react, react-dom, react-dom/client, react-dom/server, @xyflow/react, elkjs}, i.e. the five packages and nothing else. SKILL.md:114's npm-side troubleshooting row sends the agent to precisely this section: "restore the entries in `package.json` to the pinned versions the leaf carries (§`package.json`), then plain `npm install`" — an agent that restores the roster this section names ends with three packages and the next `compile app` fails with shadow's `The required JS dependency "@xyflow/react" is not available` (shadow/build/resolve.clj:471). Same leaf, same blind spot: the `:local/root` table (:84-94) lists every pay-as-you-go artefact plus Xray but has no row for `day8/re-frame2-story` → `tools/story`, although SKILL.md step 2 (:87) requires that rewrite on every route (the template's gated proof rewrites it too, emitted_test_run_test.clj:185-187). Nothing gates this: `check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py` pins counter keywords, the hot-reload wording, adapter-key vocabulary and the schemas single-require; `setup_drift_test.clj` pins the derived blocks, pins and ABSENCES (no schemas/Xray/CSP) but never compares the hand-written roster prose to the derived `package.json`.
- Action: Rewrite §`package.json` (:123) to name the five packages with their roles — three build/runtime (`shadow-cljs`, `react`, `react-dom`) plus two that Story's embedded machine canvas needs (`@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`) — "at the versions `implementation/package.json` ships", and add a `day8/re-frame2-story (tool, `:dev` alias) | tools/story` row to the `:local/root` table. title: False: #10169 unanswered-save ledger permanently suppresses later isolated settings saves
description:
PR #10169 (3093a0db1c389af5f35c9f19312a28e0b077896f) correctly refuses the occupied-name cross-account success, but its new ledger retains a completed request forever. This is beyond the documented loss of the currently ambiguous updates: future uncontended saves for that username can never complete in the same app lifetime.

Reproduction using the exact merged submit/success/failure handlers and ledger helpers: Alice submits a save under alice; logout and Bob submits an occupied-name rename to alice. Ledger is [alice alice]. Alice success arrives first and is correctly refused by settings.cljs:595-596, but retires nothing. Bob's own 422 then settles his form and retires one entry (:641-663), leaving [alice]. BOTH actual requests have now delivered their only terminal reply. Sign back in as Alice and make a new ordinary settings save; the ledger becomes [alice alice], so her fresh successful reply is discarded. Repeating the attempt grows the count and never restores progress. Neither route load nor logout clears this top-level ledger by design.

The file describes entries as saves still unanswered/on the wire, but the remaining Alice entry represents a callback already consumed. Its KNOWN LIMIT paragraph discusses ambiguous concurrent lost updates, not permanently preventing future non-overlapping saves after both requests have settled. RealWorld's normal one-reply-per-request contract does not provide another callback that could retire the stale entry.

Independent Babashka source-function probe: ai/probe-settings-audit-sep21-monitor-10169-1.clj, absolute path, correct gate root, captured exit 0 in gate-settings-audit-sep21-monitor-10169-1.log/.exit. Uses actual merged auth session helpers, machine seed/begin actions, submit, success, failure and ledger helpers. HTTP request construction and readable error formatting are stubbed because this probe covers app-state transitions, not transport or the full CLJS runtime. Positive controls: a fresh-ledger save succeeds, and a distinct-name Bob save succeeds beside Alice's outstanding save. The original cross-account reply remains refused and Bob's rejection still settles.

Correction: permit later isolated saves to recover after settled ambiguous requests, preserving cross-account refusal and the one-map classified success payload. Use a bounded app-level ownership/recovery mechanism that works in both live HTTP and canned demo mode. Do not merely clear ambiguous entries while older replies can still arrive. Extend the existing implementation-side settings overlap test with the full terminal-callback sequence followed by a fresh save; keep examples test-free. No literal-open Bead already records this persistent recovery defect. No existing status or closure was changed.
acceptance_criteria: After an ambiguous Alice success is refused and Bob occupied-name failure settles, a later isolated Alice save completes without reloading the app. Preserve cross-account auth/form/navigation isolation, normal own replies, valid renames, canned-mode parity and token classification.

Nine slices, one reviewer and one child bead each, cut along examples/README.md's concept map and sized so one reviewer reads the whole slice. Reviewers run at most three at a time after the 2026-09-17 session-limit incident.

Each child bead's description is the reviewer's report verbatim under the stance, prefixed with the worker rules (re-verify every cite at trunk; fences are full repo-relative paths; the shadow-cljs lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor; examples stay test-free). description:

The source-preservation guard is incomplete on Windows: scripts/install-skills.ps1 Resolve-RealDir inspects only whether the final directory itself is a reparse point. A junction to the repository parent leaves <junction>/skills looking like an ordinary directory with a different FullName, although it is the same maintained source directory. The guard at lines 83-86 therefore passes; -Force deletes skills/demo, then New-Item fails because the source was just removed. Git Bash delegates to this same PowerShell path.

Reproduced at the exact merged tree using the existing installer test fixture, with all source and junctions inside this audit worktree ai/ disposable directory: create repo/skills/demo/SKILL.md; create parent-alias junction to repo; run install-skills.ps1 -Target parent-alias/skills -Force (and separately install-skills.sh --target parent-alias/skills --force). Both exit 1 at New-Item after deletion; original skills/demo and SKILL.md are absent. The standard seven tests pass because they cover only skills/ itself and a junction directly to skills/, not an alias in an ancestor. Fixtures were disarmed before cleanup; no maintained checkout source was touched.

Before any force replacement, compare the physical source and destination directories with ancestor junctions resolved, so an alias to the checkout cannot bypass source identity. Extend the existing disposable regression with the parent-junction case for both Windows entrypoints and assert source bytes survive refusal. Keep separate destination force behavior; no broad installer redesign needed. No open Bead explicitly recorded this defect/correction at audit time.

Measured directly: with a junction to the fixture repo's PARENT, <alias>/skills reports Attributes = Directory (no ReparsePoint) and a FullName under the alias, while the real directory's FullName is under the repo -- so Resolve-RealDir returned two different spellings for ONE directory and the guard compared them unequal. Running the unmodified installer at <alias>/skills with force: install-skills.ps1 exited 1 at New-Item (line 161) with skills/demo and its SKILL.md GONE and skills/ empty; install-skills.sh exited 1 with the identical New-Item error raised from the delegated PowerShell script, source likewise gone. Both Windows entrypoints destroy the source, as recorded.

FIX: Resolve-RealDir now walks the WHOLE path -- it rewrites the deepest reparse point on it and restarts, so a junction whose target itself lives under another junction resolves too; a 32-hop cap stops a cyclic pair from spinning. Starting from (Get-Item ...).FullName also keeps a relative -Target resolving against PWD rather than the process CWD. Nothing else moved: the separate destination force behaviour is untouched and Test-IsLink still routes a reparse-point destination to the non-recursive unlink. No installer redesign.

SCOPE DECISION, recorded because a future reader will ask: no second per-entry guard was added beside the destructive Remove-Item. With ancestors resolved, a destination can only BE a source skill if the target directory is physically the source directory (the top-level guard catches that) or if the destination is itself a reparse point (already routed to the non-recursive unlink). No shape was found that reaches the recursive delete past those two, so a third comparison would be a guard with no case.

POSIX NEEDED NO CODE CHANGE, and this was verified rather than assumed: install-skills.sh's resolve_dir uses pwd -P, which already yields the physical path with ancestors resolved. That is why the defect was Windows-only. A comment now says so in the file, so the next reader does not "fix" what is not broken.

The installer was reverted to its committed pre-fix blob for the control run and the revert confirmed BY EFFECT first -- the working file's git hash-object equalled the pre-fix blob exactly, and a token unique to the new code read 0 while a sibling token present in both versions read 3, so the zero was the plant and not a broken search. The restore of the fixed installer was verified against the committed blob: git hash-object default form matched git rev-parse HEAD:<path> exactly, with git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path> at exit 0 as a second independent instrument.

## Recommendation

**B, with R.** Argued from the stance: this is not a library-ergonomics question at all — the programmer never meets it — so the only thing being bought is less friction for the mayor and the AI workers, and the stance says to buy that cheaply. C is defensible because the file was never wrong, but it leaves in place exactly the pair of instruments (a stale docstring and a true zero) that produced two wrong briefs in one wave, and "trust the programmer" cuts the other way here: the workers did the right thing and were sent to do redundant work by a brief that trusted a census. A is the thorough option and that is the reason not to choose it — clause (3) is a lesson `CLAUDE.md` already teaches three times, and adding a second worked instance of it to a 7,081-character line is litigating the minutiae. B is one sentence stating what is gated and what is not, in the paragraph whose job is precisely that, and it keeps the in-repo / site-URL distinction the mayor's note requires. R costs five minutes, needs no ruling, and fixes the sentence that actually exists.

What would change my mind: if Mike would rather the script's own docstring be the authority and keep `CLAUDE.md:151` from growing at all, then **C with R** — the docstring fix alone removes the false instrument, and the residual risk is a brief-writer who reads neither the script nor the bead, which is the risk C already accepts.

| Bead | P | Type | Title |
|---|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.13.1 | P2 | bug | render-to-string/render-shell emit hiccup prop names and values verbatim (`read-only`, `tab-index`, `view-box`, `html-for`, `className`; `:type :button`, `:class [..]`) where the client adapter paints the DOM attribute, and React never repairs it. Executed. |
| rf2-3x7nj.13.2 | P2 | bug | The streaming client finalises on the `__rf_payload` element's PRESENCE, so a payload (or resolved template, or delta) split across network reads is read half-parsed: `hydrate!` fails closed and the canonical state is never installed. Inspected. |
| rf2-3x7nj.13.3 | P3 | task | The hydration payload and streaming deltas carry JVM-only numbers (Long > 2^53, BigDecimal, BigInt, Ratio) that the browser reads back as different values. The manifest and render-state wires refuse exactly these; the payload wire does not. Executed server side. Decision needed. |

### Considered and rejected

Each line says what looked wrong and why it is not a finding.

**Isolation and hydration contract**

- **Per-request frame isolation (the P1 axis): no leak found.** The request, response and pending-error-trace side channels are keyed by frame address and cleared by `on-frame-destroyed!`. The tag-name cache is a dynamic binding per `render-to-string` call. The head registry holds registration-time data only.
- **Suspense failed-boundary record** (`suspense.cljc:144-163`). It is process-global and additive, and only the test surface ever clears it, so a boundary that failed during SSR renders its fallback for the whole page lifetime, including after client navigation. Not filed: Spec 011 §Failed boundaries on the client specifies a frame-free, page-level record written once at finalisation, and recovery is an unspecified feature rather than a contract break.
- **Hydrate handler guards and install ledger** (malformed payload, non-map partitions, frame-id mismatch, claim atomicity): correct and fail-closed as Spec 011:400 requires.
- **An explicit `:version` opt produces a client version-mismatch warning.** This is spec-consistent: 011:64 makes the caller's opt the source of truth.
- **Multi-root: the first root's hash is compared against a whole-body hash.** No server producer emits multiple hashed roots.

**Emitter and escaping**

- **The escape set is correct:** `escape-edn-script-body` (EDN-aware `<`), `escape-raw-text` (React's closing-sequence rewrite), and the text and attribute escapes (values are always double-quoted, and `escape-attr` handles `&` and `"`).
- **Attribute-name grammar gate, tag grammar, `strip-prop?` roster** (`on*` case-insensitive, fn values, `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`, key/ref/children, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`): correct, and closed both ways per 011:321.
- **`emit-ui-tree` has no attribute/tag grammar gate and no strip roster.** Nothing in-tree produces a v1 structural tree since re-frame.ui was retired (rf2-0yp7w).
- **An `ifn?` head that is a map, set, vector or symbol renders oddly instead of raising the structured error.** It is rare, and the Reagent client errors on it too.
- **A raw-text `script`/`style` with a nil child falls back to escaping.** An edge case with no correctness impact.
- **`read-boundary-id` misreads exotic string ids** ("42", ids containing spaces). An edge case, since boundary ids are author keywords by convention.

**Streaming and diagnostics**

- **The server-side `:rf.ssr/suspense-boundary-failed` is dev-only.** Documented as such in Spec 009, where only the client arms are always-on.
- **JSON-LD `clj->js` drops keyword namespaces on CLJS while the JVM keeps them.** An edge case: JSON-LD keys are conventionally strings.
- **The dev React warning about `data-rf-render-hash`** is the host's `emit-hash?` concern and outside this slice.

**Response gates**

- **safe-redirect bypass attempts** (backslash, tab, `///`, `https:evil`, userinfo, underscore hosts) are all rejected by the five-step gate. rf2-gwye.18 covers this area.
- **Header, cookie and status gates** in `response.cljc` are correct: CR/LF/NUL and `;` refusal, and status range.

### Could not verify

- **rf2-3x7nj.13.2** needs a browser and a server that splits one chunk across network writes. The analysis rests on the WHATWG parser's progressive insertion and on microtask-timed MutationObserver delivery, and the existing DOM tests append chunks whole, so they cannot show it either way.
- **rf2-3x7nj.13.3, browser half.** I did not execute the CLJS reader. The narrowed values are the ones Spec 011:546-551 and the `manifest.cljc:257-263` table record as measured.
- **rf2-3x7nj.13.1** was executed on the JVM only. The CLJS compilation of the same `.cljc` path (`npm run test:cljs`) was not run, and the touched code carries no reader conditional.
- **Tracker search reach.** The export search may miss beads written to Dolt after the last checkpoint; I mitigated this with a live `bd list` of the wave label. The rf2-x76af2.* and rf2-v4foc ids cited in source comments no longer resolve in the tracker, so their close reasons could not be read.

No tracked file was edited and no git write was made. The only tracker writes were the three finding beads above, this note, and the close.
