title: core-pipeline: a per-event cofx/chain-assembly hard error escapes the drain and strands the rest of the frame's queue until an unrelated dispatch
description:
## Defect

A per-event hard error thrown while the router assembles an event's context or chain escapes `process-event!` and the whole drain. That covers `:rf.error/unregistered-cofx`, `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`, `:rf.error/cofx-value-invalid`, interceptor-ref resolution errors and `:rf.error/interceptor-override-invalid`. The router's panic path, `drain-emergency-release!`, clears `:scheduled?`, drops the drain lock and rethrows. It does not re-arm a drain for the events still queued behind the failing one. So every other event already in that frame's queue, including the failing event's own `:fx [[:dispatch ...]]` siblings, sits unprocessed until some unrelated dispatch happens to arrive and schedule a new drain. In an idle app that can be indefinitely.

The router's own contract is that a per-event failure aborts that event only and keeps the drain alive. Spec 002 says "`process-event!` already traps per-event handler / fx / interceptor throws internally ... anything reaching this level is outside that contract". The router already follows that rule for a legacy runtime root, whose docstring says a throw "would escape `process-event!` into `drain-emergency-release!` — which re-throws, abandoning the rest of the drained queue. So we emit in-band and abort THIS event only". The cofx and chain-assembly throws were left on the abandoning path.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3930-3938`, `drain-emergency-release!`. It runs `(swap! router assoc :scheduled? false :in-drain? nil)` and `(reset! drain-lock false)`. It does not clear the queue and does not reschedule.
- `router.cljc:3940-3969`, `drain-try!` (the async entry). It catches, calls `drain-emergency-release!` and rethrows (3966-3968).
- `router.cljc:3971-4026`, `drain-block!` (the `dispatch-sync!` entry). Same pattern (4022-4024).
- `router.cljc:4061-4064`, `drain-reentrant!`. Same model, without even releasing the lock, which the cold holder owns.
- `router.cljc:4068-4101`, `ensure-drain-scheduled!`. It schedules a drain only when `:scheduled?` was false, so the stranded tail waits for the next dispatch.
- The throw sites reached from `process-event!`, via `run-handler-pipeline!` (2951), then `prepare-handler-ctx` (2408), then:
  - `assemble-initial-ctx` (843), which calls `rf.cofx/deliver-declared-cofx` at `router.cljc:960-962`. That rethrows every hard cofx error while the frame is live, at `cofx.cljc:1197-1201`. The emitters are `emit-unregistered-cofx!` (`cofx.cljc:493-516`), `emit-missing-required-cofx!` (518-544) and `emit-cofx-value-invalid!` (587-656).
  - `resolve-chain` at `router.cljc:2450`.
  - `apply-icpt-overrides` at `router.cljc:645`.
- The contrasting in-band abort is the `emit-legacy-runtime-root!` docstring at `router.cljc:1998-2016`.
- Spec: `spec/002-Frames.md:2038-2044`.
- Public entry points are `rf/dispatch` and `rf/dispatch-sync` (`core.cljc:223-224`). The event in the queue behind the failing one can be any `:dispatch` fx sibling or any externally queued event.

## Failure scenario

Executed on the JVM at 034d0c8fc8, with the plain-atom adapter and one frame `:p/f`.

1. Synchronous case (probe p1). `:p/bad` declares `{:rf.cofx/requires [:p/token]}`, where `:p/token` is `reg-cofx`'d `{:recordable? true :provided? true}`. `:p/parent` returns `{:fx [[:dispatch [:p/bad]] [:dispatch [:p/good]]]}`. Run `(dispatch-sync! [:p/parent] {:frame :p/f})`.
   - Result: `dispatch-sync!` throws `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx` to the parent's caller, even though the parent committed.
   - After 500ms the log is `[:parent]` and the router is `{:queue [[:p/good]], :scheduled? false, :drain-lock false}`. `:p/good` never ran.
   - Only a later unrelated `(dispatch! [:p/other])` drains it: the log becomes `[:parent :good :other]`.
2. Async case (probe p2). `:p/typo` requires an unregistered `:p/no-such-cofx`. Registration succeeds, because there is no registration-time registered check. `:p/parent` queues `[:p/typo]` then `[:p/good]`, sent with async `dispatch!`.
   - Result: `Exception in thread "pool-1-thread-1" ... [:rf.error/unregistered-cofx]`, with a stack of `drain-try!`, then `drain-loop!`, then `run-one-pass!`, then `process-event!`, then `assemble-initial-ctx` (router.cljc:960).
   - After 800ms the log is `[]` and the router is `{:queue [[:p/good]], :scheduled? false}`.
   - Only an unrelated `dispatch!` runs `:p/good` (log `[:good :other]`).

Reachability on normal paths:

- A typo'd or not-yet-loaded cofx id is "at first processing" per `spec/001-Registration.md:449`.
- A `:provided?` fact on a child `:dispatch`: the child never inherits `:rf.cofx` (`fx.cljc:582-587`).
- A generator minting a non-EDN value, such as a `Date`, or a value failing its `:schema`. That error is always-on in production.
- Under the `:test` preset the mint policy is `:strict` (`spec/002-Frames.md:927`, 1285-1288). There, any cascaded child that requires a generator-backed fact is `missing-required-cofx` by design.

## Evidence

- Executed:
  - p1 and p2 as above. The scripts and outputs are in the reviewer scratch (`review-wave/core-pipeline/probe/p1_cofx_strand.clj`, `p1.out`, `p2_async_strand.clj`, `p2.out`).
  - They ran from a scratch deps project with `:local/root` pointing at the frozen core. The frozen tree read `git status --porcelain` 0 lines afterwards.
  - Controls in both probes:
    - The same `:p/good` runs immediately once any later dispatch arrives, so the handler itself is healthy.
    - In p1 the parent's own commit landed (`:parent` in the log), so only the tail after the throw is lost.
- Inspected:
  - Both `drain-emergency-release!` call sites (`drain-try!`, `drain-block!`).
  - `drain-reentrant!`'s own catch, which follows the same model.
  - `try-release-on-empty!` / `force-release-on-halt!`, the only other re-arm seams. Neither runs on the throw path.
- Pinned behaviour: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/interceptor_overrides_test.clj:109-112` and `:199-202` pin that a bad override THROWS out of `dispatch-sync`. They do not pin the queue state afterwards. No test in `implementation/core/test` asserts on the queue after a thrown per-event error.
- Tracker:
  - `bd search` found nothing for `drain-emergency-release`, `emergency`, `missing-required-cofx` or `unregistered-cofx`. As a control, `stranded` returns 3.
  - A full-text scan of all 2109 issue records in the export for `emergency-release`, `strand...queue`, `abandon...queue` and cofx-error-plus-drain found 0 related beads. As a control, `drain-lock` found 5.
  - No ruling says this is deliberate.

## Smallest fix

Two options, either sufficient:

- (a) In `drain-emergency-release!`, when the queue is non-empty after the release, re-arm one next-tick `drain-try!`. This keeps the crash-loud rethrow for the failing event and stops the stranding.
- (b) Trap per event, which is what spec 002 already claims. Catch around `process-event!` in `run-one-pass!` (or around `prepare-handler-ctx`), emit the already-emitted error in-band and continue the pass, as `emit-legacy-runtime-root!` does.

(b) changes whether `dispatch-sync` throws. That contradicts the interceptor-override pin, so (a) is the smaller change.

Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`, plus a JVM test in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/`. Not a hot-zone file. Option (b) would also want a sentence in `spec/002-Frames.md`, which IS a hot-zone file. Option (a) needs no spec edit.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/core` (a JVM probe-style test asserting that the queue drains after the throw).
- `router.cljc`'s drain entry points are shared `.cljc` outside any reader conditional, so the CLJS arm is compiled by `npm run test:cljs` (node lane). Note that `rf.interop/next-tick` differs per host.

## Decision needed

Yes, a small one:

- Should a hard cofx or chain-assembly error keep THROWING to the `dispatch-sync` caller and merely stop stranding the queue (option a)?
- Or become an in-band per-event abort like the effect-map and legacy-root defects (option b)?
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 22:23:40 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.1.1.drain-error-strands-queue.md in the mayor checkout. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own.

Read at trunk 4b627ee9e2 (= origin/main). git diff 034d0c8fc8 4b627ee9e2 -- implementation spec tools = 0 lines, so the bead's cites hold.

RECOMMENDATION: option (a) — keep THROWING to the dispatch-sync caller and re-arm the drain. drain-emergency-release! (router.cljc:3930-3938) snapshots the queue under the router lock and, if it is non-empty, keeps :scheduled? true and schedules one next-tick drain-try!. No spec edit, no public-contract change, no test pin moves.

Decisive findings:
1. |---|---|---|

- **.35.2 (executed).** `cap.cljc:330-340` reports chars whenever the char gate trips, including when the token gate also tripped. A dual-coded 19,990-char payload reports 9998; a 20,100-char payload reports 40214. `cap_test.clj:357-374` claims the token count is reported, yet its own fixture reports 4010 chars (1002 tokens), and the assertion is tautological.

**Considered and rejected** (one line each, so nobody re-litigates them)

- *Cursor/marker EOF-sentinel reproduction* (`{map} :re-frame.mcp-base.cursor/cursor-eof-sentinel] junk` decodes to the map; executed). Already ruled a non-goal in rf2-fzbj.9. The payload must still pass `valid?`, so nothing is gained over sending the map directly.

title: ssr-ring: stream-handler leaks its writer thread, request frame and side-channel slots for ever when middleware drops the body unread (Ring wrap-head / HEAD) on a page over 16 KiB
description:
## Defect

`stream-handler` returns a `PipedInputStream` body and pumps the page into it from a per-request daemon writer thread; the frame is torn down only in that thread's `finally`. If anything between the handler and the server DROPS the body without reading or closing it, and the page is larger than the 16 KiB pipe buffer, the writer blocks in `PipedInputStream.awaitSpace` for ever: the reader side never read (so the JDK's "read end dead" check, which keys on the reader thread, is never armed) and was never closed (so "pipe closed" never fires). The writer thread, the request frame and its request/response/pending-error side-channel slots are all retained permanently, one set per such request. Ring core's own `ring.middleware.head/wrap-head` does exactly this for every HEAD request (`(assoc response :body nil)`, no close — unchanged in ring-core 1.15.3), so an externally triggerable request type leaks unboundedly. This contradicts the documented no-leak contract: "every writer thread terminates and is reclaimed once its request completes or its client disconnects".

## Where

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:602-619` — 16 KiB `PipedInputStream`, daemon writer, frame destroy only in the writer thread's `finally`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:119-121` — `write-chunk!` is an unbounded blocking `.write`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:707-719` (docstring: "no-LEAK ... the live count decays to zero") and `spec/011-SSR.md:1808` (the no-leak contract).
- Public entry: `re-frame.ssr.ring/stream-handler` (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:62`), composed as `(ring.middleware.head/wrap-head (ssr-ring/stream-handler opts))` and hit with a HEAD request.

## Failure scenario

`(def app (wrap-head (ssr-ring/stream-handler {:initial-events [] :root-view (fn [] ((rf/view :app/root))) :payload [:x]})))`, root rendering more than 16 KiB of HTML. Send `HEAD /` three times (an uptime monitor, a link checker, a crawler). Each returns 200 with `:body nil`; each leaves one `rf2-ssr-streaming-*` thread parked in `PipedInputStream.awaitSpace` plus one live `:rf.frame/*` frame and one request slot, for the life of the JVM. Repeated HEADs exhaust threads/heap. The host's request-concurrency knob (the spec's stated ceiling) does not bound this, because each HTTP request has already completed.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — bounded process-local JVM probe (`probe1_wrap_head.clj` in the reviewer scratch dir), real `stream-handler` + real `ring.middleware.head/wrap-head` from ring-core 1.12.1 on the ssr-ring `:test` classpath, `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- baseline: live-writer-threads 0, request-frames 0, request-slots 0.
- CONTROL 1 (body read fully with `slurp`, as Jetty does): 94,352 body bytes, then threads 0 / frames 0 / slots 0.
- CONTROL 2 (small page, below 16 KiB, body dropped by `wrap-head`): threads 0 / frames 0 / slots 0 — the writer fits the whole page in the buffer and exits.
- CASE (big page, body dropped by `wrap-head`, 3 HEAD requests): after 4 s AND after 8 s, live-writer-threads 3 (all `TIMED_WAITING`, top frames `Object.wait` <- `PipedInputStream.awaitSpace` <- `PipedInputStream.receive`), request-frames 3, request-slots 3.

Ring-core source inspected in the local Maven repo: `ring.middleware.head/head-response` sets `:body nil` without closing in 1.12.1 and 1.15.3, whereas `ring.middleware.not-modified` DOES `close!` the body — so this is a known-shaped gap in Ring, not a misuse. Compojure's GET routes are understood to drop HEAD bodies the same way (not measured here). The 2026-09-12 surface review (rf2-fzbj.24) explicitly left "every server's response-close behavior" unverified rather than ruling it deliberate. Tracker search over all fields (export at trunk) for wrap-head / awaitSpace / head-response: 0 hits.

## Smallest fix

Bound the writer's WRITE STALL on the writer thread itself (no pool, no new thread): write only what fits (`(- buffer-size (.available pipe-in))`) and poll, aborting through the existing catch/finally (`:rf.error/ssr-streaming-writer-failed`, pipe closed, frame destroyed) when no byte has been consumed for N seconds; or equivalently close `pipe-in` from the writer when the stall bound expires. Fence: `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj` (+ a regression next to `streaming_robustness_test.clj`), and a one-sentence refinement of `spec/011-SSR.md` §Writer concurrency model. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM only: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/ssr-ring` (a wrap-head regression belongs in the default lane — it is fast and needs no Jetty); the burst tests are `clojure -M:slow-test`. No CLJS lane involved (`.clj` files).

## Decision needed

Yes. The stall bound also caps slow-loris clients, which the spec currently leaves to the host server: choose (a) a fixed stall bound (e.g. 30-60 s) in the writer, (b) the same as an opt, or (c) no code change and a documented rule that `stream-handler` must not sit behind body-dropping middleware such as `wrap-head`.

(a) "Harmless overlap". The dossier called cutting a zero-progress live client at 60 s benign; Codex said unsupported. Codex is right about what "progress" measures: the IMMEDIATE BODY CONSUMER (Jetty, or a middleware) draining the pipe, not the browser receiving bytes. A live consumer that deliberately pauses 60 s is truncated. RULED: accept it as a DOCUMENTED finite-resource policy for streamed HTML, not as "harmless". On ring-jetty defaults a consumer that drains nothing is now cut at 60 s where the host cut it at 200 s.
(b) WAKEUPS. The dossier said "a read wakes the writer"; Codex said too strong. Codex is right. (c) Codex's CONTRACT LIMITS, adopted into the spec text. title: ssr: streaming client finalises on the __rf_payload element's PRESENCE - a payload (or resolved template / delta) split across network reads is read half-parsed, so hydrate! fails closed and the canonical state is never installed
description:
## Defect

The streaming client (`re-frame.ssr.streaming.client/install!`, re-exported as `ssr/streaming-install!`) treats a chunk element as complete the moment the element EXISTS in the DOM. The HTML parser does not work that way.

The parser INSERTS a `<script>` or `<template>` element at its start tag. It then appends the element's text (for a script) or its content (for a template, into the detached `.content` fragment) progressively, as network data arrives. A MutationObserver callback runs at the next microtask checkpoint, which falls after any parser task that ended mid-element. So when a chunk is split across network reads, the observer can see a half-parsed element.

Three consequences follow:

- **The final payload.** When the `<script id="__rf_payload">` element appears, `finish!` runs. It calls `on-ready`, and the documented bootstrap calls `ssr/hydrate!` from `on-ready`. `hydrate!` reads the payload's `.textContent`, which is only a prefix of the EDN, so it records `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` and returns nil. `hydrate-root` then adopts the DOM against speculative, delta-merged state instead of the canonical server state.
- **Resolved templates.** A resolved `<template>` is swapped using a CLONE of its partial `.content`, and the template is then removed. The parser keeps filling the detached template, so the rest of that boundary's markup is lost.
- **Delta scripts.** A delta `<script>` can likewise be read partially, and it is then dropped.

## Where

Cites are at `034d0c8fc8`, under `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/`.

- `streaming/client.cljs:700-710` `final-payload-present?` is `(some? (element-by-id root payload-id))`, a presence test only.
- `streaming/client.cljs:888-902` `on-mutations`: `(when (final-payload-present? root payload-id) (finish!))` at 901. `streaming/client.cljs:907-917` is the same test at install time, where `finish!` runs synchronously.
- `streaming/client.cljs:726-766` `finalize!`: sweep, `record-failed-boundaries!`, `unwrap-mounts!`, `stop!` (disconnect), then `on-ready`. The observer is disconnected, so nothing re-reads later bytes.
- `boot.cljc:53-105` `read-server-payload`: `(reader/read-string (.-textContent el))` at 88. A parse failure emits malformed and returns nil (fail closed, per Spec 011 §The :rf/hydrate event).
- `streaming/client.cljs:179-185` `template-content-fragment` is `(.cloneNode (.-content template) true)`. `streaming/client.cljs:247-265` `replace-mount-content!` appends the clone and removes the template. `process-resolved-template!` (525-628) records the outcome, so the swap never retries.
- `streaming/client.cljs:461-523` `apply-ready-deltas!` reads `(.-textContent script)` at 517 through `read-delta` (388-426), then removes the script whatever the outcome.
- **Public entry.** `install!` with the `:on-ready` bootstrap its own docstring prescribes (client.cljs:770-855) and Spec 011 §Streaming SSR requires ("from HERE — not on a timer, not by polling").

## Failure scenario

A streamed page ends with a large `__rf_payload`, for example a 100 KB `:rf/app-db` slice. It is written as one server chunk but reaches the renderer in several network reads, which TLS record and TCP segment boundaries make routine.

1. The parser handles the first read. It inserts `<script id="__rf_payload" type="application/edn">` holding the first N KB of text, and the parser task ends.
2. The MutationObserver microtask fires. `final-payload-present?` is true, so `finish!` runs, then `on-ready`, then `ssr/hydrate!`.
3. `read-server-payload` reads `{:rf/version 1 :rf/app-db {… truncated`, and `cljs.reader` throws. The code emits `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload`, `hydrate!` returns nil, and the frame is never seeded with the canonical state.
4. `hydrate-root` adopts the server DOM against a frame holding only whatever the per-boundary deltas merged. Every view that reads un-delta'd state renders its empty state, and React either reports a hydration mismatch and client-renders, or silently keeps server markup bound to wrong state.
5. The remaining payload bytes arrive after the observer has disconnected, so nothing ever reads them.

The resolved-template variant is the same story. A large resolved boundary (a long list) split across reads is swapped in truncated, and its tail is parsed into a detached template that has already been removed.

## Evidence

**Inspected, not executed.** Reproducing this needs a browser and a server that splits a chunk across network writes, both of which this review wave forbids.

- **Why I am confident.** The WHATWG tree-construction rules insert the script and template elements at their start tags (the "in head"/"in body" start-tag steps), and "text" insertion mode inserts each character token as it is tokenised. Template contents go to the template's content fragment. Mutation observers are notified at microtask checkpoints, which fall after the parser task.
- **The code has no other completeness signal.** It never checks for a following sibling, `document.readyState`, `DOMContentLoaded`, or a sentinel.
- **Why the tests cannot see it.** The DOM tests append each chunk WHOLE through `innerHTML`, so an element always arrives complete. See `test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_hydration_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (`payload-chunk` at 213-222; the chunk appender at 238-244 parses each chunk whole through a `<template>` `innerHTML` and appends its content) and `streaming_client_dom_cljs_test.cljs`. No test splits one element across two appends.
- **The design already knows the neighbouring race.** The `sweep!` docstring (630-660) handles a template and its delta landing in separate observer batches, but it assumes each element arrives whole.
- **Tracker.** A search of the tracker export for `MutationObserver`/`final-payload-present` with `partial|truncat|incomplete` found no bead on this (the control hit on `MutationObserver` alone was rf2-fn0kx.6, which is unrelated). rf2-3x7nj.14.x are server-side ssr-ring findings and do not cover it.

## Smallest fix

Treat a chunk element as complete only once the parser has CLOSED it:

- **For `__rf_payload`, when observing `js/document`:** finalise on `DOMContentLoaded`, or immediately if `document.readyState` is not `"loading"`. The payload is the last chunk, so the document finishing parsing is exactly "stream complete".
- **For resolved templates and delta scripts:** process an element only once it has a following sibling node. The server writes the delta script after its template and further chunks after that. Alternatively, have the server emit a tiny terminator after each chunk, which is an ssr-ring change.

A detached test `:root` keeps working, because an element appended by `innerHTML` is complete. The fence is `streaming/client.cljs` plus a DOM test that appends one element's markup in two pieces, or drives a real incremental parse through `document.write` into an iframe. No hot-zone file is involved.

## Gates

`streaming/client.cljs` is CLJS-only, so no JVM lane compiles it. The streaming client tests are `*_dom_cljs_test.cljs` and are graded by the browser lane, `npm run test:browser` (shadow-cljs, so CI or the build-lane holder only).

## Decision needed

No, unless the terminator-sentinel route is preferred over the parser-state checks. That route changes the wire protocol in Spec 011 §Streaming SSR and touches ssr-ring's writer.
notes:
FIXED in PR #10306 (worker/ssr2-3x7nj), 2026-09-24. Parser-state route, as the bead said; the wire protocol and ssr-ring's writer are unchanged.

- `streaming/client.cljs`: `parser-closed?` counts a chunk element as whole once a node follows it, or once the root Document is no longer `"loading"`. Resolved templates and delta scripts are processed only when closed. `stream-complete?` (which replaced `final-payload-present?`) requires the payload to be closed too. `install!` also re-sweeps on `DOMContentLoaded` while the root Document is still parsing, and `stop!` removes that listener.
- The payload also counts as closed once a node follows it. A classic bundle `<script>` after the payload, or a deferred or module bundle, therefore still finalises synchronously inside `install!`.
- An Element root reports no parse state, so it behaves as before. This is the test-harness contract; it is documented on `:root`.
- Spec 011's client-side hydration semantics gain one sentence (item 2) and one clause (item 3).

Control: two browser tests in `streaming_client_dom_cljs_test.cljs` drive an incremental parse through `document.open` + `document.write` into a same-origin iframe. The tests-first commit went RED in CI's browser lane with 6 failures, all in the new tests:

Merged-PR audit #10306 (f643984683a7b9fd913ba97a7eaa36dd2e84108f; merged 2026-09-23T20:48:01Z). Completeness: Resolved chunks, deltas and payload wait for parser completion; Ring refusal pins, nullish Node failures and nil-value docs are covered. Initial fallback templates remain ungated; separately tracked in rf2-5yj03. Correctness: Accepted reported Node nine-suite run, Ring 256/1343 and browser red/green evidence; CI 59 successful checks. title: xray-epoch-panel: FLOW step :db diff is not scoped to the flow's path — with two flows in one epoch, each FLOW step shows every flow's change (contradicts 021 §9.1.10.8)
description:
## Defect

A FLOW step's `:db` diff is meant to show only that flow's slot. With two or more flows in one epoch, every FLOW step instead shows every flow's change. The view builds the diff from two different snapshots:

- `diff-before`: `(assoc-in db-pre-flow path before)`
- `diff-after`: `(assoc-in db-post-flow path after)`

`db-pre-flow` is the post-handler db. `db-post-flow` is t2, a single snapshot taken after ALL flows ran. Setting this flow's path on both sides isolates nothing, because every OTHER flow's write is still present in `db-post-flow` and absent from `db-pre-flow`. So flow A's step also paints flow B's output as `~ modified`, and the reverse.

The docstring and the spec both claim the opposite. The spec's own recipe is the defective construction. It says `value = :db-post-flow with the flow's post-write value at :path`, which cannot meet the goal it states in the next clause.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:4489-4490`: the two diff endpoints in `render-flow-step`. The docstring at `:4446-4451` claims "Scoped to the flow's `:path` so each FLOW step shows only its own slot's reshape".
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:4284-4300`: `project` puts the SAME `:db-pre-flow` / `:db-post-flow` on every flow step. That part is correct as a data contract.
- Spec: `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §9.1.10.8, `:4079-4083`. It says the diff "is **scoped to the flow's `:path`** ... so each FLOW step shows ONLY its own slot's reshape even when several flows rode the same pre→post transition".
- Producer: t2 is `:rf.event/db-pending-post-flow`, one snapshot after all flows ran (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1713` and `:1907`).

## Failure scenario

An app has two flows. `::total` derives `[:cart :total]` from `[:cart :items]`, and `::badge` derives `[:ui :badge]` from `[:notifications]`. One event updates both inputs. In Epoch, the `::total` FLOW step's diff shows `[:ui :badge]` changing, and the `::badge` step shows `[:cart :total]` changing. A programmer reading the `::total` step concludes `::total` wrote the badge. That is a wrong-attribution lie in the one place meant to answer "what did this flow change?".

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe, from the scratch dir against the frozen tree's `tools/xray` as a `:local/root`, with no writes into the tree (`probe1.clj` section P4). The probe ran a real two-flow epoch:

- `::fa` wrote `[:fa]` from `[:a]`, and `::fb` wrote `[:fb]` from `[:b]`.
- The handler changed both `:a` and `:b`.

`project` produced the flow steps. The view's two `assoc-in` endpoints were then evaluated verbatim, in JVM Clojure, on each step's data:

```
flow :user/fb path [:fb]
  diff-before {:a 2, :b 11, :fb 1000, :fa 100}
  diff-after  {:a 2, :b 11, :fb 1100, :fa 200}
  top-level keys the step's diff shows as changed: #{:fa :fb}
flow :user/fa path [:fa]
  diff-before {:a 2, :b 11, :fb 1000, :fa 100}
  diff-after  {:a 2, :b 11, :fb 1100, :fa 200}
  top-level keys the step's diff shows as changed: #{:fa :fb}
```

What was EXECUTED is the endpoint algebra on real projection output. What was INSPECTED is the rest of the chain: `view.cljs` is CLJS-only, and the render was not run in a browser. The claim that the edn-inspector diff paints every differing key is also inspected.

The existing flow tests are single-flow only, so they cannot see this:

- `projection_cljs_test.cljc:2422-2567`
- `real_substrate_projection_cljs_test.cljs:162-204`

Tracker search for `flow step`, `render-flow-step` and `flow-db-diff`: no existing bead.

## Smallest fix

In `view.cljs:4489-4490`, diff against ONE baseline:

```clojure
diff-before (when db-diff? db-pre-flow)
diff-after  (when db-diff? (assoc-in db-pre-flow path after))
```

Only this flow's slot then differs. This keeps the rf2-48oc4 "handler returned no :db" behaviour, because `db-pre-flow` is still the effective post-handler db.

Amend the §9.1.10.8 recipe in `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:4079-4083` to match. Add a two-flow case to `view_cljs_test.cljs`.

Fence:

- `panels/epoch/view.cljs`
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md`
- `test/.../panels/epoch/view_cljs_test.cljs`

No hot-zone file.

## Gates

This change is CLJS-only, so it needs `npm run test:cljs` (node lane, `view_cljs_test.cljs`). A JVM green is not evidence about this fix. For the spec edit, `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` is the link gate (its roots include `tools/*/spec`). `mkdocs build --strict` does not see `tools/`, and no gate checks the prose itself.

## Decision needed

No.

title: pair-mcp: past-epoch markers carry a live-path handle (no :as-of-epoch) and get-path cannot read an epoch, so a followed handle returns NOW's value as that epoch's
description:
## Defect

A `:rf.size/large-elided` marker inside a past epoch's `:db-before` / `:db-after` carries a live-path handle, `[:rf.elision/at <path>]`, with no `:as-of-epoch`. `get-path` also has no way to read an epoch at all: its `path` is a plain `get-in` against the frame's *current* app-db. The contract says otherwise. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3024 and :3063, and Spec-Schemas.md:3659, say a marker riding a past-epoch payload carries `[:rf.elision/at <path> :as-of-epoch <epoch-id>]`, and that "`get-path` resolves against the existing epoch-record's `:db-after` snapshot so the agent sees that-epoch's value, not now's". Neither half exists in pair-mcp. So an agent that follows a handle out of `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `snapshot :epochs` / `dispatch :trace` gets the value as it is **now**, in a response that looks like the answer for that epoch. On a default launch it gets the marker again instead (see the elision-gate sibling, rf2-3x7nj.32.4).

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs:140-199` (`egress-opts-edn` renders `{:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool}`, plus `include-sensitive?` when opted in, and never `:as-of-epoch`) and `:325-375` (`project-page-src` maps ONE opts map over every record in the page).
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1427-1433`: `:as-of-epoch` is only *selected* through from the caller's opts. The epoch arm does not derive it from the record's own id.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:652-656` (`handle-of` emits the `:as-of-epoch` variant only when the opt is present).
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:82-124` (`single-path-form`): the singular form is `(get-in db path)` over `(snapshot <frame>)`, the live app-db. `args/parse-path-arg` (`tools/args.cljs:324-349`) has no `:rf.elision/at` / `:as-of-epoch` syntax, so a handle passed as `path` is read as a literal key vector and reports `:path-not-found`.

Entry points: MCP `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`, `snapshot` (`:epochs` slice) or `dispatch` (`:trace` / `:settle` modes) produce the marker. `get-path` is the documented follow-up.

## Failure scenario

1. The app declares `{:large [[:doc :body]]}`. Epoch 7 stores draft A (60 KB) at `[:doc :body]`, and a later epoch 12 replaces it with draft B.
2. The agent investigates epoch 7 via `trace-window` and sees `[:doc :body]` elided with `:handle [:rf.elision/at [:doc :body]]`, with no epoch qualifier.
3. On a launch with `--allow-sensitive-reads`, the agent follows the handle with `get-path {:path "[:doc :body]" :elision false}` and receives draft **B**. It reports it as epoch 7's state. Nothing in the reply says the read was of the live db. On a default launch the same follow-up returns a marker (see the elision-gate sibling, rf2-3x7nj.32.4).

## Evidence

**Executed**: a bounded JVM probe, run from the scratch dir with `implementation/core` and `implementation/epoch` as `:local/root`, with no tree writes (`git status` 0 lines, and no `.cpcache` created under `implementation/epoch`). It projected an `:rf/epoch-record` standing in for epoch 7 (`:frame :p/main`, `:db-after {:blob {:payload <50000 X>}}`, frame declaring `:large [[:blob :payload]]`) through `rf/project-egress`.

- With the opts pair-mcp renders (`{:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool}`), the `:db-after` marker handle is `[:rf.elision/at [:blob :payload]]`.
- Control, with the same call plus `:as-of-epoch 7`, the handle is `[:rf.elision/at [:blob :payload] :as-of-epoch 7]`.

So core supports the spec'd shape, and pair-mcp never asks for it.

**Inspected**: the `get-path` eval forms (live `snapshot` read only) and `parse-path-arg` (no handle syntax). A Grep for `as-of-epoch` over `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src` finds 0 hits. As a control, the same Grep over `implementation/**/src` finds 14, in elision.cljc, projection.cljc and tool_pair.cljc, so the term is findable.

Tracker: rf2-kuky.9 (closed, the one-door egress ruling) lists `:as-of-epoch` among `project-egress`'s pass-through opts but does not rule on pair usage. rf2-ealv5 (open) concerns descendant reads, and rf2-3x7nj.17.1 (open) concerns `:halted-depth :last-event`, so neither covers this. No bead names the missing epoch handle.

## Smallest fix

Two parts.

- Stamp the handle: have `project-page-src` pass each record's own id, `(project-egress r (assoc opts :as-of-epoch (:epoch-id r)))`, or have the epoch arm in `tool_pair.cljc` default `:as-of-epoch` from the record it is projecting. The latter fixes every consumer at once.
- Honour it in `get-path`: accept either a handle vector or an `:as-of-epoch` argument, read `(:db-after (epoch-by-id id frame))` instead of the live db when it is present, and refuse with `:epoch-aged-out` when the record is gone.

Fence: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../tools/{epoch_egress,get_path,args,descriptors_data}.cljs`, and optionally `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc`. No hot-zone file, unless the ruling is instead to drop the `:as-of-epoch` promise, which would edit spec/009 and Spec-Schemas (**both hot zone**).

## Gates

`npm test` in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` (CLJS only). If `tool_pair.cljc` changes, run `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/epoch` for the JVM half and `npm run test:cljs` for the CLJS half. The spec edits need `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.

## Decision needed

Yes. Should past-epoch handles be resolvable? (a) Stamp `:as-of-epoch` and teach `get-path` to read the epoch's `:db-after`, as spec 009 describes. (b) Drop the promise, and have spec/009:3024/:3063 and Spec-Schemas:3659 say that a handle always addresses the live db.

title: xray-domain-panels-a: Resources live-work and stale-races join the cross-frame trace buffer on the frame-LOCAL work-id, so another frame's outcome labels this frame's running work
description:
## Defect

The Resources panel's "what is still running" list and its stale-races view join trace rows on `:work/id` alone. But Xray's trace buffer merges every host frame's ring, and a resource work-id is frame-LOCAL. It is `[:rf.work/resource <scoped-key> <generation>]`, and the generation allocator is per frame, so two frames that load the same resource at the same generation mint the SAME work-id.

The result is that another frame's trace rows are joined onto the observed frame's work:

- **Live-work.** A work item still `:running` in the observed frame gets its "latest phase/op" from a different frame's arc. For example, it is labelled `phase completed`, `op :rf.resource/succeeded` while it is still running here.
- **Stale races.** The same key merges two frames' attempt arcs into one, taking the phases and the terminal status from both.
- **Stale tally.** It counts suppressions across every frame.

rf2-qqi7u fixed exactly this frame-collision class for the optimistic indexes in `resources_helpers.cljc`. The reply-envelope joins beside them were left on the bare key.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc`
  - `:874-884`: `latest-phase-by-work-id`, which indexes by `(:work-id row)` only.
  - `:886-914`: `live-work`, which joins the observed frame's ledger rows (`(get phase-by-id (:work-id row))`) to that cross-frame index.
  - `:743-778`: `races-by-work-id` does `(group-by :work-id)`.
  - `:733-741`: `stale-tally-by-kind`.
  - The rows already carry `:frame` (`work-event-row`, `:566-650`).

- **Runtime:**

- **Entry point:** the Xray Resources tab on any app with two or more frames that load a shared resource. Examples are a story or workspace hosting several frames, an SSR-style per-request frame, or `make-frame` twins.

## Failure scenario

1. Frames `:app/a` (observed) and `:app/b` both load `:article/by-slug {:slug "x"}` with global scope, first load in each. Both mint work-id `W = [:rf.work/resource [... :article/by-slug {:slug "x"}] 1]`.
2. Frame B's request completes. Frame A's request is still in flight.
3. The Resources tab, observing A, shows A's running row with `phase completed`, `op :rf.resource/succeeded`. That is frame B's outcome.
4. In the stale-races section, if A's attempt is later superseded, one arc for W holds both frames' rows (`frames #{:app/a :app/b}`), with B's `:completed` phase merged in.

## Evidence

**Executed.** A bounded JVM probe (`probe_reply.clj`, reviewer scratch dir) loaded the frozen tree's `reply_envelope.cljc`. It used hand-built trace rows in the runtime's tag shape (`:rf.frame/id`, `:rf.reply/work-id`, `:rf.reply/work-kind`, `:rf.reply/status`).

| Function | Input | Result | Control (frame A's rows only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `live-work` | A's ledger holds W `:running`; buffer = A issues W, B issues W, B completes W | `status :running latest-phase :completed latest-op :rf.resource/succeeded` | `latest-phase :issued latest-op :rf.resource/work-started` |
| `races-by-work-id` | Buffer adds A's stale-suppression | one arc, `suppressed? true`, `terminal-status :ok`, `frames #{:app/a :app/b}` | `terminal-status :stale` |

**The weaker half.** With real runtime rows the `:rf.resource/succeeded` row may not carry `:rf.reply/status`, in which case the races arc's terminal status could stay `:stale` while its phases still merge. The live-work mislabel does not depend on that and is the load-bearing half.

**Inspected only:** the views (`resources.cljs:471-504`, `:543-565`). No CLJS run was allowed in this review.

**Tracker.** A full-text export search for `latest-phase-by-work-id` hits 0 beads. `races-by-work-id` hits only review prose: rf2-y8doi.12's perf note and rf2-y8doi.6 #8. rf2-y8doi.6 #8 is a different defect, a bare `:rf.http/aborted` arc read as still in flight, and was dismissed as plausible. Neither raises the frame collision. rf2-qqi7u fixed the same class for the optimistic indexes only (`resources_helpers.cljc:1655-1732`, `:2032-2148`).

## Smallest fix

Key the three joins on `[frame work-id]`, since the rows already carry `:frame`. Alternatively, have the Resources composite hand them the buffer filtered to the observed frame. That still keeps them cross-FAMILY, which is what the `:1514` comment protects.

`live-work` then looks up `[(:frame ledger-row) (:work-id ledger-row)]`, or the observed frame if the ledger row carries none.

**Fence:** `reply_envelope.cljc`, `resources.cljs` (only if filtering at the caller) and `reply_envelope_cljs_test.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- **`reply_envelope.cljc`:** the tools/xray JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`) and `npm run test:cljs` (`reply_envelope_cljs_test.cljc`).
- **`resources.cljs`, if touched:** `npm run test:cljs` (`resources_cljs_test.cljs`) only. A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No.

title: routing: :rf.nav/scroll touches the DOM in the navigating event's fx phase, before the new pane commits — a cross-route :fragment lands at the top and Back :restore clamps to the old page's height
description:
## Defect

`:rf.nav/scroll` touches the DOM synchronously, inside the navigating event's fx phase: it calls `getElementById(fragment)` then `scrollIntoView` for `:top`, and `scrollTo(saved-pos)` for `:restore`. That happens before the view substrate has committed the NEW route's pane, which is after the drain (spec 012 line 2079). So the effect reads and scrolls the OLD page.

For a fragment-only navigation this is harmless, because the target element is already on the page. For a cross-route navigation it defeats the feature in the two cases scroll handling exists for:

- A cross-route fragment link, spec 012's own `{:to :route/docs … :fragment "scroll-restoration"}` example, looks the id up in the old DOM, finds nothing (or a same-id element on the old page), and falls back to `scrollTo(0,0)`. The user lands at the top instead of the section.
- `:restore` on Back to a page taller than the one being left calls `scrollTo` against the shorter old document. The browser clamps it, and the new page then renders at the clamped offset.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc:457-469`: `scroll-fx-handler`, whose `:top` and `:restore` branches touch the DOM immediately.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:329-352`: the commit returns `:rf.db/runtime` plus `:fx`, with `scroll-fx` last and inside the same event.
- The URL-driven and fragment doors emit the same fx.

Public entry points: `[:rf.route/navigate {:to … :fragment …}]`, `route-link` with `:fragment`, and Back/Forward (`:rf.route/handle-url-change` cause `:popstate`) with the default `:restore`.

## Failure scenario

1. The user is on `:route/home`. The app dispatches `[:rf.route/navigate {:to :route/docs :params {:page "routing"} :fragment "install"}]`, and the docs view renders an `[:h2 {:id "install"}]`. The scroll fx runs before the docs pane commits: `getElementById("install")` returns nil, so `scrollTo(0,0)` runs, and the docs page then renders at the top instead of at `#install`.
2. The user scrolls a long list to y=3000, opens a short detail page (default `:top`), then presses Back. `:restore` runs `scrollTo(0,3000)` while the short detail page is still mounted, so the browser clamps it to the detail page's maximum, and the list re-renders at that offset instead of 3000.

## Evidence

INSPECTED, not executed; this needs a browser. Confidence rests on three things in the tree.

1. The fx is synchronous and last in the commit's own `:fx` (the cites above). No routing or substrate path flushes a render inside a drain: the only `flushSync` sites are mount / `render!` / `flush-render!` tooling and controlled inputs.
2. The repo's own browser witness states the ordering for the adjacent recipe: `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:149-150` says "`:on-match` dispatches during the navigation cascade, before the substrate has committed the new pane, so resolving now would answer the OLD pane's heading". That is why its focus effect defers one `requestAnimationFrame`. The scroll fx runs even earlier than `:on-match`.
3. Both browser witnesses that pass for scroll restoration hold page height constant on purpose. The routing one gives both panes a 4000px filler "so the document does not shrink out from under a saved offset on a navigation" (same file, line 209). The fresco one keeps the offset "well inside the shell's height so nothing is clamped" (`implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/examples/navigation/conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:511`). Neither exercises a cross-route fragment or a taller destination.

Related, not a duplicate: rf2-pk4i6.7 finding #3 (`history.scrollRestoration` left at `auto`, so the browser's traversal restore races `:rf.nav/scroll`) was DISMISSED as plausible-unconfirmed pending a browser check. That is a different mechanism and covers Back only. The cross-route fragment case above involves no browser restoration at all; it is re-frame2's own ordering. One browser session confirms or refutes both.

## Smallest fix

Defer the DOM half of `scroll-fx-handler` until after the substrate commits: one `requestAnimationFrame` hop, the same move the conduct witness's focus recipe makes, or the substrate's after-render seam if one is preferred. The fx args and their ordering relative to `:rf.nav/capture-scroll` / push stay as they are. Update the reference handler in `spec/012-Routing.md` §Scroll restoration to match.

The fence is `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc`, `spec/012-Routing.md`, and a browser row with DIFFERENT pane heights plus a cross-route fragment. There is no hot-zone file.

## Gates

The change sits in the `#?(:cljs …)` branch of `scroll.cljc`, so only the CLJS lanes grade it: `npm run test:cljs`, plus the browser lane (`routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, a `-dom-cljs-test` namespace) for the new witness row. JVM tests see only the `:clj` skip branch.

## Decision needed

Yes. (A) defer the scroll one frame after commit (recommended; small), or (B) keep synchronous scrolling and state in spec 012 that `:top`-with-fragment and `:restore` only work when the target is already rendered and page height is stable. Take rf2-pk4i6.7 #3's `scrollRestoration = "manual"` in the same browser pass if it reproduces.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 23:17:55 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.12.3.scroll-before-commit.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot. The findings below stand on their own.
Read at trunk 51494841d9, which equalled origin/main. git diff 034d0c8fc8..51494841d9 -- implementation/routing spec is 0 lines, so every frozen-tree cite holds.

RECOMMENDATION: option A, deferring through the adapter's post-render hook (A-ii). In scroll-fx-handler's CLJS branch, move the :top / :restore DOM calls into (rf.interop/after-render f), falling back to one requestAnimationFrame when that returns nil (Test-React or headless). The fx id, args, closed vocabulary and ordering relative to capture and push stay unchanged. Add one spec 012 sentence stating the limit: the scroll waits for the commit, not for still-loading resources. B (stay synchronous and document the limits) documents the feature not working in the two cases it exists for. Waiting for route readiness was considered and ruled out as over-engineering.

DECISIVE FINDINGS (inspection; no browser):
1. scroll.cljc:457-469 touches the DOM inline (getElementById / scrollIntoView / scrollTo), and events.cljc:352 emits scroll-fx LAST in the committing event's :fx, before the queued :on-match events and before the substrate renders. Spec 002:1881 says the drain is decoupled from rendering, and 002:1883 names after-render effects as THE post-render seam. routing/src contains zero after-render or requestAnimationFrame uses (rg exit 1).
2. The repo's browser witnesses hide the defect by design. routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:209 gives both panes a 4000px filler "so the document does not shrink out from under a saved offset". Fresco's conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:511 keeps the offset "well inside the shell's height so nothing is clamped". Neither covers a cross-route fragment. The same routing file at :149-150 records that :on-match runs "before the substrate has committed the new pane", and the scroll fx runs earlier still.
3. All three shipped adapters publish :adapter/after-render (Reagent, UIx, reagent-slim, each with its own test). rf2-cdoo (PR #9209) made slim's hook genuinely post-commit. Test-React deliberately does not publish it (test_react.cljc:615-621), hence the rAF fallback.

STANDING RIDE-ALONG: rf2-pk4i6.7 #3 (history.scrollRestoration left at auto) was dismissed under Mike's 2026-09-16 ruling of the rf2-pk4i6 shortlist, with the condition "confirm in a browser ... and take the two-line scrollRestoration = manual plus a 012 sentence in the same routing PR if red". This fix is that PR. Verification: the node lane (npm run test:cljs) can pin that the handler defers, using stubbed hook / scrollTo / getElementById / rAF. Landing offsets, clamping and the scrollRestoration race need the browser lane (routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test, npm run test:browser), in a row with UNEQUAL pane heights plus a cross-route fragment. A JVM green says nothing about this change. No hot-zone file.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 00:18:04 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option A. Defer the DOM half of :rf.nav/scroll until the destination has committed, using the adapter's post-render seam, rf.interop/after-render.
- Test for the hook's PRESENCE, never its return value.
- Use no requestAnimationFrame fallback. A host that publishes no after-render hook scrolls immediately, which is today's behaviour.
- A deferred scroll whose navigation has been superseded by the time it fires does nothing.
- The fx id, its args, its closed vocabulary, and its order relative to :rf.nav/capture-scroll and the push all stay exactly as they are.
- Carry out the rf2-pk4i6.7 #3 scrollRestoration check in the same routing PR, as that bead's disposition already says.

WHY
- The defect holds at trunk 8e65232c40, and the routing tree is unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8. Four facts establish it:
  - scroll.cljc scroll-fx-handler (:457-472) touches the DOM inline. :top calls getElementById then scrollIntoView, falling back to scrollTo(0,0). :restore calls scrollTo(saved-pos).
  - events.cljc commit-navigation (:329-352) emits (when scroll-fx [scroll-fx]) as the LAST :fx of the committing event. That is before the queued :on-match events and before any render.
  - Spec 002:1881 says the drain is decoupled from rendering, and 002:1883 names after-render effects as the post-render seam.
  - Nothing in routing defers. grep -c "after-render|requestAnimationFrame" reads 0 in every file under implementation/routing/src (exit 1). The control is the same grep, which reads 5 on core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs and 1 on routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs.
- So the handler reads and scrolls the page being LEFT. A cross-route fragment misses and lands at the top; this is spec 012's own example at :1475, {:to :route/docs ... :fragment "scroll-restoration"}. Worse, if the old page has an element with the same id, it scrolls to that. And Back :restore to a page taller than the one being left is clamped. The CSSOM scroll algorithm bounds the requested position by the current scrollable area, so the offset is lost. These are the two cases scroll handling exists for.
- The repo's own browser witnesses hide the defect by design:
  - routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:202-209 gives both panes a 4000px filler "so the document does not shrink out from under a saved offset".
  - fresco/.../navigation/conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:509-513 keeps the offset "well inside the shell's height so nothing is clamped".
  - Neither has a cross-route fragment.
  - The routing file itself records the ordering at :147-152: :on-match runs "before the substrate has committed the new pane, so resolving now would answer the OLD pane's heading". That is why its focus recipe defers. The scroll fx runs earlier still.
- B (stay synchronous and document the limits) loses. It documents the feature failing in exactly its two use cases. The only workaround is :scroll false plus a hand-written after-render scroll, which is the deferral A does once, rewritten by every app. Trust the programmer means not nagging them. It does not mean shipping a default that fails silently.
- Two other options are ruled out. Waiting for route readiness couples scrolling to Resources and turns a visual effect into a readiness consumer. flushSync inside the drain contradicts 002's render decoupling and 012:2079's single render pass.

DOSSIER vs CODEX: both chose A, and both chose after-render as the seam. They DIFFER on the fallback, and Codex wins on a fact I verified at trunk.
- The dossier's A-ii read "(after-render f); if that returns nil, use one requestAnimationFrame". But rf.interop/after-render (core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:54-59) returns WHATEVER THE HOOK RETURNS. UIx's hook, spine.cljs make-after-render-hook (:1589-1618), returns nil AFTER it has successfully scheduled. Codex reports that Reagent 2.0.1's batching and slim's scheduler can also return nil when a drain is already scheduled. So the return value is not a presence test, and the dossier's fallback would double-scroll on supported adapters.
- RULED: test presence explicitly, with (rf.late-bind/get-fn-cached :adapter/after-render) or a tiny interop predicate. With a hook, schedule through it. With no hook, run the DOM half IMMEDIATELY.
- Why immediately, and not rAF and not skip:
  - The hookless hosts are Test-React, whose after-render is deliberately unpublished (test_react.cljc:615-621 says production paths reaching for it are a misconfiguration that should surface), plus headless and non-React hosts. None of these has a commit boundary for a rAF to certify, as Codex argues.
  - Skipping would silently drop a scroll.
  - Immediate is exactly today's behaviour, adds no new timing primitive, and cannot double-run.
- Codex's other points are ADOPTED:
  (1) STALE-CALLBACK GUARD. Deferral creates a new failure mode that did not exist while the scroll was synchronous. Navigation A emits its deferred scroll. Before the render, an :on-match or other redirect commits navigation B. If B uses :preserve or :scroll false, B emits no corrective scroll, so A's callback would scroll B's page. FIFO order does not save this case.
     Fix: capture the navigation identity the commit allocated, the frame's current [:rf.runtime/routing :current :nav-token], when the fx runs. The fx runs after the commit's runtime-db write (spec 002 §:fx ordering, rule 1). In the callback, skip the DOM half if the token has moved.
     If the implementer finds the read awkward, carry the token in the fx args instead; nav_fx_schemas and 012 §:rf.nav/scroll integration then move with it. Expose no cancellation API.
  (2) "All adapters publish it" is weaker than "the destination DOM is committed". Slim's rf2-cdoo repair, with its ordinary-path DOM witness, is real evidence for slim. For UIx I found a concrete reason to check, and recorded it under NOT SETTLED.
  (3) The stated limit is a scope choice, not an industry inevitability. React Router's restoration does wait for loaders. Content that arrives after the relevant commit, through a still-loading resource, is outside this repair. Say so in one spec sentence and add nothing else: no readiness observers, no retry timers, no new strategies, no settings.

WHAT TO BUILD
- implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc, CLJS branch only, about 10 lines:
  - :top and :restore close over their args. At fx time they capture the nav-token, then run through the hook when one is present, or immediately otherwise. The callback re-checks the token first.
  - :preserve stays nil.
  - The unsupported-strategy rejection (emit-unsupported-strategy!) stays SYNCHRONOUS, because it is not a DOM call.
  - The :clj skip trace is unchanged.
- spec/012-Routing.md:
  - Update the reference handler at about :1244-1262 to match.
  - Add one sentence to §Scroll restoration / §:rf.nav/scroll integration (:1451-): the DOM half runs after the commit that installs the new route, through the adapter's after-render hook. A host with no hook applies it immediately. A superseded navigation's scroll is dropped. The scroll waits for the commit, not for data that arrives later.

That disposition stands under Mike's ruling of the rf2-pk4i6 shortlist "as your recommendation" (2026-09-16).
  - This fix IS that routing PR.

  - Keep the two findings distinct. #3 is the browser's native traversal restore racing the runtime on Back only. This bead is re-frame2's own ordering, and it bites forward navigation too.
  - The same close reason names two other "ride along with any routing PR" items, #1 and #6. Take them if cheap; they are not part of this ruling.
- NO hot-zone file, and no public-contract change: the same fx id, args and vocabulary. This assumes the token is read from the slice rather than added to the args.

REGRESSIONS AND ACCEPTANCE
- Node lane (npm run test:cljs), a -cljs-test namespace, using a stubbed :adapter/after-render hook plus the existing window/document stub:
  - The handler makes NO DOM call during the fx, and makes EXACTLY ONE when the hook fires.

  This is honest evidence about the deferral and nothing more.

  1. From home, navigate to docs with :fragment "install", where #install exists only on the arriving page. Read scrollY as within a few px of #install's offset. RED today: 0.
  2. Scroll a tall list to 3000, go to a SHORT :top page, press Back, and read scrollY as 3000. RED today: clamped. Run this row with history.scrollRestoration set to "manual" in the test itself, OR run the #3 check separately. Browser auto-restore can mask or override the runtime, so a Back-only green does not isolate this fix.
  3. The #3 check itself: a route with :scroll :top; scroll, push, Back, read scrollY. If it is red, set scrollRestoration = "manual" where the listener installs, and add one 012 sentence claiming scroll ownership.
  4. Cover each shipped adapter's NORMAL mount path: Reagent, UIx and reagent-slim. For UIx this includes the native mount's FIRST after-render use (see NOT SETTLED).
- Controls that stay green unchanged:
  - the existing constant-height rows;
  - the fragment-only jump;
  - the conduct focus recipe (its rAF still runs after the deferred scroll, and :preventScroll still composes);
  - routing_scroll_test.clj on the JVM, which pins fx vectors and ordering (26 :rf.nav/scroll mentions). This is a regression control only: its :clj branch is untouched, so it is not evidence about this change.
- LANE: the change sits in the #?(:cljs ...) branch of scroll.cljc, so only the CLJS lanes grade it: the node lane for the unit rows, the browser lane for the witness. A JVM green says nothing about it. Both take the machine-wide shadow-cljs exclusive, so the mayor must grant the lane.

title: mcp-base: overflow marker :token-count reports the CHARACTER count for every overflow over ~2x the cap
description:
## Defect

The overflow marker's `:token-count` switches to the CHARACTER count whenever the secondary char gate trips, even when the primary token gate also tripped. For a single payload string the char gate (`chars > 8 x cap`) trips as soon as the payload is about 2x over budget. So on the ordinary big-overflow path, every shipped marker reports characters under a key named `:token-count`: about 4x the token estimate, with a discontinuous jump at the 8x-cap boundary. The char-count arm was added (commit `4d017069d3`, rf2-ih7g4) for the case where the token heuristic MISSES: many sub-4-character slots whose per-string floors sum to about 0. The docstring still says so ("an actionable number for the payload that escaped the token heuristic"). But the selector tests only the char gate, so it also fires when the token estimate is perfectly usable. The brief's cap question is "does it say how much?". Here the marker says how much in the wrong unit for most real overflows.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc:330-340`: `reported-count` is `(if (> chars (* cap byte-cap-multiplier)) chars tokens)`.
- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc:385`: its result becomes the marker's `:token-count`.

Contract that says tokens:

- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/overflow.cljc:51`: ":token-count - estimated token count of the over-budget payload".
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/Principles.md:278`: "estimate of the original (over-budget) payload".
- `tools/mcp-base/spec/cap.md` §Algorithm step 3 describes the implementation as written, so it is spec-stale with it.

Public entry: `apply-cap`, which runs on every `tools/call` of both servers (story-mcp `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:406`, pair-mcp `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/cap.cljs:197`). Both servers dual-code results into `:content[*].text` and `:structuredContent`, so the char sum is about 2x the payload.

## Failure scenario

Default cap 5000 with a dual-coded result:

- An agent asks for a snapshot whose payload is 19,990 characters and gets `{:rf.mcp/overflow {:token-count 9998 :cap-tokens 5000 ...}}`.
- A payload of 20,100 characters instead gets `:token-count 40214` for a response the same heuristic estimates at 10,052 tokens.

The agent then sizes its next move against a number 4x too large. It may raise `max-tokens` far past what it needs, or decide the response cannot fit its context and abandon or over-narrow a read that was only about 2x over.

## Evidence

EXECUTED: a bounded JVM probe against the frozen `src`, using a story-shaped dual-slot ResultIO and the default cap:

```
payload-chars= 12000  measured tokens=  6002 chars= 24014  -> :token-count=6002
payload-chars= 19990  measured tokens=  9998 chars= 39994  -> :token-count=9998
payload-chars= 20100  measured tokens= 10052 chars= 40214  -> :token-count=40214
payload-chars= 60000  measured tokens= 30002 chars=120014  -> :token-count=120014
```

Control: a 2,400-char single-slot payload at cap 500 trips only the token gate and reports 600, the token estimate.

The suite does not catch this, and one test states the opposite of what it does. `cap_test.clj:357-374` (`over-cap?-and-reported-count-agree-with-apply-cap`) says "A token-gated over-budget response reports the token count" and "the token gate is the one that trips". Its own fixture measures tokens=1002 and chars=4010 against a char ceiling of 4000, so both gates trip and the marker carries `:token-count 4010` (executed). The assertion only compares `reported-count` with the marker, which is tautological, so it cannot fail. Every other test asserts only `> cap`. rf2-6r9j.105 said to "preserve the reported-count behavior" while cleaning up comments, but it never examined the case where both gates trip. No bead rules that case deliberate.

## Smallest fix

Report a token-unit number in every case, for example `(max tokens (quot chars 4))`, or tokens when the token gate tripped and `(quot chars 4)` otherwise. This keeps the original goal (a non-zero, actionable number when many short slots floor the estimate to 0). It still satisfies the conformance invariant `:token-count > :cap-tokens` (`tools/mcp-conformance/lib/overflow-marker.cjs:127-133`), because `chars > 8 x cap` implies `quot chars 4 > 2 x cap`.

Fence:

- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc`
- `tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/cap_test.clj`: the `reported-count` boundary cases, the live char-gate case that pins 9000 (becomes 2250), and the tautological test, which should assert the token value.
- `tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/cljs_branches_cljs_test.cljs:129` (pins 801).
- One sentence in `tools/mcp-base/spec/cap.md`.

No hot-zone file. Pair's `wire_cap_test.cljs:277` (`> 200 x cap` on a 5 MB payload) still holds with the token value.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `tools/mcp-base` (JVM; `cap_test`). The change is not in a reader conditional.
- The CLJS pin at `cljs_branches_cljs_test.cljs:129` is compiled only by the shadow-cljs lane (machine-wide exclusive), so declare reliance on CI or take the lane.
- story-mcp `tools_test` overflow cases (JVM).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== NOTE FOR THE FIXING WORKER (mayor, relayed from the mcp-conformance review rf2-3x7nj.36, 2026-09-24) ==

This bug is live on the exact path the live overflow conformance test drives (tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-overflow.cjs). That test asserts only `:token-count > :cap-tokens`, so it passes whether the count is in tokens or characters. When you fix the count, add a range assertion to that test so the regression becomes visible, for example that the reported count is close to floor(chars / 4) for the payload the test sends. Do NOT run the live test yourself unless you hold the shadow-cljs build lane; it drives a shadow-compiled server. Add the assertion, and let CI grade it.
== FIX LANDED ON PR #10322 (worker mcp-3x7nj, 2026-09-24 09:50 AUSEST) ==

Verdict: FIXED. The premise held at trunk 23f1406306. Reproduced with story's real `result-io` at the default cap 5000 on a dual-coded payload:

| payload chars | tokens | chars | `:token-count` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12000 | 6001 | 24007 | 6001 |
| 19990 | 9996 | 39987 | 9996 |
| 20100 | 10051 | 40207 | 40207 (characters) |
| 60000 | 30001 | 120007 | 120007 (characters) |

Fix (the second option the bead offered): `reported-count` in `mcp-base/cap.cljc` is now `(if (> tokens cap) tokens (quot chars 4))`.
- It keys on the TOKEN gate, so when both gates trip the marker carries the token estimate.
- When only the char gate tripped (many sub-4-char slots floor the per-string estimate toward 0), it reports chars/4. The char gate implies chars > 8*cap, so that value is still > 2*cap.
- The marker is now always in token units, and the conformance invariant `:token-count > :cap-tokens` holds on both arms.
- The docstring and the §Algorithm step 3 sentence in `tools/mcp-base/spec/cap.md` were updated to match.

Tests:
- `cap_test.clj`: the boundary cases are now `reported-count-is-always-in-token-units` (both gates → tokens, token-only → tokens, char-only → chars/4, tokens = cap → chars/4, and the chars/4 arm > cap).
- The tautological `over-cap?-and-reported-count-agree-with-apply-cap` now asserts that both gates trip, and that `:token-count` equals the token sum (1002, not the 4010 characters).
- The live char-gate pin moved from 9000 to 2250.
- The CLJS pin in `cljs_branches_cljs_test.cljs` moved from 801 to 200, and it gained a token-only row and a both-gates row.
- The live pair overflow conformance test (`tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-overflow.cjs`) gained the range assertion the mayor's note asked for. `:token-count` must lie in [floor(25000/4), cap*8] = [6250, 40000], and a character count can only land above that ceiling. The pair wire response here is well over 40,000 characters, so the pre-fix code reported one.

Control, shown red: with the old selector planted back (`(if (<= chars (* cap byte-cap-multiplier)) tokens chars)`), mcp-base `clojure -M:test` exited 1 with 5 failures in `cap_test`:
- `over-cap?-and-reported-count-agree-with-apply-cap` :380
- `reported-count-is-always-in-token-units` :350 :354 :357
- `apply-cap-many-short-strings-trips-char-gate` :408

The run stayed at the same 295 tests / 1052 assertions as the green run. After the restore, the default-form blob hash matched the committed blob.

The CLJS pin and the live `.cjs` range assertion run only in shadow-cljs-backed lanes, which were not granted. They were NOT run locally; CI grades them. `node --check` on the `.cjs` exits 0.

Gates: mcp-base `clojure -M:test` exited 0 (295/1052), and story-mcp exited 0 (308/1794).

Brief and item differed on one point: the brief's fence did not list `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-overflow.cjs`, but this item's note (relayed by the mayor from the rf2-3x7nj.36 review) asks for the assertion there. The item governed.
Merged-PR audit #10322 (eec6b9a6c4a77a8ecf9ee3882f7c03b1eef374e3; merged 2026-09-24T00:03:11Z). Completeness: All four MCP findings are addressed in both consumers and the shared wire layer: over-cap failure flag, token units, sequential collection-kind changes including map keys, and an unencodable Instant marker preserving the verdict. Correctness: Checked both ResultIO adapters, token selector, wire equality recursion, ordered dissoc/assoc key replacement, and JVM/CLJS scalar predicate branches. Accepted mcp-base 295/1052, Story-MCP 308/1794, wire-vocab 92/1038, negative controls and CI pair 1236/4581 plus live overflow conformance. Implementation quality: Shares the existing dedup equivalence and narrows scalar admission to encoder capability. Focused fixes preserve the existing wire protocol and caps; no actionable new finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: xray-shell-views: edn-inspector presents a lazy seq longer than 1001 as exactly 1001 elements, with no truncation marker
description:
## Defect

The EDN inspector silently truncates a finite lazy sequence that is longer than `count-bound` (1001) and presents it as a 1001-element sequence. The header count, the `(…1001 items)` summary and the expanded body all agree on 1001, and the body closes its `)` after row 1000 with no marker that the sequence continues. A 5000-row `(map ->row resp)` in app-db reads as exactly 1001 rows; an infinite `(iterate inc 0)` reads as a finite 1001-element seq. The inspector's own docstring concedes that over the bound "the header is therefore a FLOOR rather than a promise" (edn_inspector.cljs:943-944), but nothing on screen says so. The diff path already refuses this lie: past a capped side it paints `::unrealised` as an explicit unknown. The browse path has no equivalent.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:926-957`: `count-bound` (1001) and its FLOOR admission at :943-956.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:959-973` `bounded-count*` and `:975-997` `bounded-vec`. A value that is not `counted?` is taken to 1001, and its count stops at 1001.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:1537-1538`: `children-of`'s `(:vector :list :seq)` arm walks `bounded-vec`.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:2132-2142`: `child-count` for `:list`/`:seq` is `bounded-count*`.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:1429-1436` (`inline-scalar-str`) and `:1453-1461` (`inline-preview-string` fallback) print `(…1001 items)`. `collapsed-summary` at :2685-2693 shows that text.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:3538-3542`: the close bracket is painted straight after the last realised row.
- Public entry: the App-DB panel mounts `ei/edn-inspector-view` over `(f/display-value value)` (`panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:401-416`). `display-value` passes sequences through unchanged (`panels/app_db_diff_format.cljs:98-120`). Trace payloads and sub values reach the same renderer through `edn/inspect`.
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md:770-778` says realisation is bounded and that "a slot past a capped side paints `::unrealised` — an explicit unknown". That line covers the diff path only.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-event :rows/loaded (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ resp]] {:db (assoc db :rows (map ->row resp))}))` with a 5000-element `resp`. Open App-DB and expand `:rows`. Rows 0 to 1000 render, then `)`. Nothing indicates 3999 more rows. When the row maps are wide, the collapsed summary reads `(…1001 items)`. An infinite `(iterate inc 0)` under a key renders identically to a genuine 1001-element seq.

## Evidence

- **Executed** (bounded JVM probe, scratch `probe2.clj`, mirroring `count-bound`, `bounded-count*` and `bounded-vec` verbatim):
  - `(map inc (range 5000))` reads true count 5000, header 1001, rows 1001.
  - `(filter even? (range 10000))` reads 5000 / 1001 / 1001.
  - Controls: `(vec (range 5000))` reads 5000 / 5000 / 5000, and `(map inc (range 10))` reads 10 / 10 / 10.
  - CLJS `bounded-count` and `counted?` share these semantics: `LazySeq` is not `ICounted`.
- **Inspected**: no browse-path code emits an unknown-tail marker. A search of the file for `truncat|at least|+ more` finds only docstrings.
- **Prior rulings**: rf2-jh12f fixed the COUNTED case by rendering it whole. Its own brief asked to "explicitly surface and make accessible any omitted tail; keep the guard for unbounded lazy input", and the lazy tail was never surfaced. rf2-y8doi.11#9 (dismissed) was about paging LARGE counted collections, not this unknown tail.

## Smallest fix

When a sequence that is not `counted?` hits the ceiling, the widget should say so. Realise one more element (`bounded-count` already looks one ahead) to tell "exactly 1001" from "more". Then render a trailing muted row such as `… (not realised past 1001)` and print the count as `1001+` in `inline-scalar-str` and `inline-preview-string`. This is parity with the diff path's existing `::unrealised` statement. It is not virtualisation or paging.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs` and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_cljs_test.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs`, the node lane. The file is `.cljs`, so no JVM lane compiles it. The existing rf2-jh12f realisation-counter tests must stay green, because the marker must not realise more than the bound plus one.

## Decision needed

No. spec/004's "no `… N entries …` row" rules out windowing, not a statement that a tail was never realised.
notes:
## Worker verdict (ednins-3x7nj, PR #10323) — FIXED

Reproduced at trunk 63e118215c: cljs.main probe on clojurescript 1.12.145, `(bounded-count 1001 (map inc (range 5000)))` = 1001 and `(counted? …)` = false. The browse path had no marker.

title: mcp-conformance: the hermetic suite's SKIP/sentinel verdict has no test that can fail - inner-test-close-grading case 4 is a tautology and main() is unexported
description:
## Defect

The hermetic live suite's per-test verdict has no test that can fail. The check that turns an exit-0 inner run into a pass sits inline in `main()`: an exit 0 that printed a `SKIP ` banner fails, and so does an exit 0 that never printed the test's success sentinel. `main()` is not exported, so no unit test can reach that code. The one test that claims to cover it cannot fail. `inner-test-close-grading.test.cjs` case 4 ("still surfaces a sentinel-less stdout...") asserts only that its fake child, which never prints the sentinel, did not print the sentinel. Its header (item 4) says this proves "the caller's sentinel-check in `main()`'s INNER_TESTS loop still fails it", but the test never runs that check. So the guard behind the README's promise ("A skipped inner test therefore cannot pass the hermetic suite") can be deleted or broken and the whole Node unit cluster stays green.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`, under `tools/mcp-conformance/`:

- `scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:1752-1793`: the inline verdict in `main()`. Non-zero exit rethrows the child's code. The SKIP guard is at 1774-1783 and the sentinel guard at 1784-1792.
- `scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:1940-1956`: the export list. It has `spawnAndGradeInnerTest` (stdio capture only) but not `main` or the verdict.
- `test/inner-test-close-grading.test.cjs:48-53` (the header claim) and `:186-211` (case 4, a tautology).
- `README.md:69-74` states the guarantee.

Public entry: `npm run test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite`, which runs in three places: the per-PR `mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (surface `mcp_live`, graded on the step's exit code), the nightly `mcp-live` / `mcp-live-windows` jobs in `expensive-tests.yml`, and `npm --prefix implementation run test:mcp-conformance -- --live`. The regression net that should protect the verdict is `npm run test:unit` in `tools/mcp-conformance`.

## Failure scenario

1. A refactor of the inner-test loop drops or breaks the two guards. Examples: grading on the exit code alone, or a condition edit such as matching `'\r\nSKIP '`.
2. `npm run test:unit` stays green, because nothing in it runs `main()`.
3. Later, a setup regression leaves every live test on its SKIP path. For example, `testEnv` stops carrying `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT`, or the inventory path resolves elsewhere. Each inner test prints `SKIP ...` and exits 0.
4. The hermetic suite then prints `RE-FRAME2-PAIR-MCP live hermetic conformance passed (7 inner tests).` and exits 0 without exercising a single live row. The per-PR CI step and the repository runner (`implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:563-577`) both grade the step on exit code alone, so both read green.

## Evidence

EXECUTED, as a mutation probe in scratch. Nothing was written to the tree, and nothing spawned a server, shadow-cljs or a browser: the test drives `spawnAndGradeInnerTest` with a fake `spawnFn`, and requiring the orchestrator does not run `main()`. I made three copies of the orchestrator and pointed a copy of `inner-test-close-grading.test.cjs` at each, then ran `node --test` (Node v24.13.0):

- `baseline` (unmodified logic): 5 pass, 0 fail.
- `noguard` (the SKIP guard at 1774 and the sentinel guard at 1784 both replaced with `if (false)`): **5 pass, 0 fail**. Case 4 passes too.
- Positive control `exitgrade` (grading moved from `'close'` back to `'exit'`, a regression this file does pin): 3 pass, **2 fail**. The instrument can go red.

INSPECTED: a tree-wide search for the guards' message text (`SKIPped inside`, `did NOT print its success sentinel`, `rf2-ybiz0`) matches only the orchestrator itself, at 1774-1789. The other harness self-tests exercise `finalizeConformance`, `makeCleanup`, `readPortFile`, `wipeStalePortFileCandidate` and `runTrusted`, and none of them reaches `main()`. The guard is correct today; the problem is that nothing tests it.

## Smallest fix

Lift the verdict into a pure exported function, for example `gradeInnerTestOutcome({ code, stdoutText, sentinel, testFile })`. It returns pass, or throws the same errors with the same `exitCode` attribution (inner code for non-zero, orchestration 2 for SKIP or a missing sentinel), and `main()` calls it. Replace case 4 with RED and GREEN cases against it: a SKIP banner at the start and after a newline, exit 0 with no sentinel, exit 0 with the sentinel, and a non-zero exit keeping its code. The last is optional. Consider failing loudly when an inventory row has no `sentinel`, because `test.sentinel &&` currently skips the check.

Fence: `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs` and `tools/mcp-conformance/test/inner-test-close-grading.test.cjs` (or a new `*.test.cjs` plus its `scripts/test-all.cjs` row). No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:unit` in `tools/mcp-conformance`: pure `node --test`, no server, no shadow-cljs. The changed guard itself is exercised end to end only by the hermetic live suite (the shadow-cljs build lane plus Chromium; the per-PR `mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair` job and nightly `mcp-live`), so say that the live half relies on CI.

## Decision needed

No.
