title: spec/docstrings: the keyword-interning rationale says JVM keywords are never GC'd — Clojure 1.12.4 holds them by reference; restate the reason, keep the defences
description:
## Defect

The keyword-interning rationale in the spec and in several docstrings says JVM keywords live in a process-global table that is never garbage-collected, so every interned hostile key is a permanent leak. That is not what the pinned Clojure does. On Clojure 1.12.4 (the version the routing artefact resolves), `clojure.lang.Keyword.table` is declared as `ConcurrentHashMap<Symbol, java.lang.ref.Reference<Keyword>>`. It was read by reflection on 2026-09-24 in a bounded JVM probe against trunk f6bb999d6e. The table holds keywords through references and `Keyword.intern` clears dead entries through a ReferenceQueue. An independent review (the Codex section of the rf2-3x7nj.12.1 dossier) cites WeakReference plus that cleanup in Keyword.java at tag clojure-1.12.4, lines 25-48. A keyword that nothing references can therefore be reclaimed. On CLJS there is no global keyword table at all. Nobody measured resource exhaustion either way.

The defences themselves still hold, and this bead does not ask to remove them:
- routing's selective keywording (only declared `:query` / `:query-defaults` keys become keywords);
- the `:keyword`-value enum gate;
- HTTP's `:rf.http/max-decoded-keys` cap.

Declared vocabulary as the keyword universe is still the right design, because it is author intent and it separates typed from untyped keys. rf2-3x7nj.12.1 was ruled on those merits alone. What is wrong is the stated REASON, which is written as a categorical fact. A false premise in normative text is a hazard for future rulings: in rf2-3x7nj.12.1 it was nearly the whole case against one of the options.

## Where (at trunk 8e65232c40)

- spec/012-Routing.md:1390 ("JVM keywords intern into a process-global, never-GC'd table ... permanently extends that table"), :1394 ("refuses to permanently extend the JVM keyword table") and :1398
- spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:277 ("never garbage-collected ... would permanently burn N keyword slots per response")
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/json.cljc:29 (docstring: "never GC'd")
- implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:988 (coerce-query docstring: "permanent JVM keyword slots")
- spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-query-keyword-discipline.edn:32 and implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_registry_test.clj:1611 (comments)

## Smallest fix

Restate the rationale in each place, and change no behaviour. The honest cost of promoting attacker-chosen keys is transient: allocation and table churn for each unique key, plus retention for as long as a slice or reply holds the keyword. The design reasons stand without the leak claim: declared vocabulary is the trust boundary, keys are typed only where declared, and the behaviour is the same on both hosts. If the fixer concludes that one of the three defences has no remaining justification once the premise is corrected, that is a separate question for its own bead. It is not part of this one.

## Gates

This is prose and docstring only. A docstring edit in a .cljc file sits outside reader conditionals and is graded by the JVM lane of that artefact (clojure -M:test from implementation/routing, and from implementation/http). The spec pages are covered by check_doc_slugs.py and the mkdocs strict build. Ratchets grade the paths touched, so run them.

## Decision needed

No. Correct the rationale. Removing a defence is out of scope.

title: machines-viz: SCXML export does not region-scope targets declared inside a parallel region - the emitted target ids dangle
description:
## Defect

`spec->scxml` path-qualifies every state id with its region (`<region>___<state>`), but it resolves transition targets declared INSIDE a parallel region as though the region were a machine-root state. Spec 005 drives each region as a synthetic single machine, so a region-local vector target is an in-region absolute path, and a region body's own root `:on` / `:after` keyword target names a top-level state of that region. The exporter resolves both against the machine root instead:
- a region-local vector target `[:c :d]` emits `target="c___d"`, when the state id is `r___c___d`;
- a region-root `:on {:reset :idle}` emits `target="idle"`, when the state id is `a___idle`.

Either way the `target` names no element in the document. If the region also has a state named after a sibling region, the target would name that sibling REGION instead. The local round trip still compares equal, because `decode-target` inverts the same mistake, which is why the round-trip tests are green. But the export is invalid SCXML for exactly the external tools it exists to serve. API.md claims "transition targets reference those same unique ids — valid SCXML a strict external consumer accepts". The chart and Mermaid both region-scope these targets correctly, so the three emitters disagree.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/scxml.cljc:383-404`, `resolve-target-path`: a keyword resolves as `(conj (parent-path source-path) target)` and a vector as `(vec target)`, both from the machine root.
- `scxml.cljc:797-802`: `emit-parallel` emits each region through `(emit-state [region-id] region-node ...)`, so the region body's own `:on` sees `source-path [region-id]`, and inner states get region-prefixed paths while their vector targets do not.
- `scxml.cljc:541-553`: `emit-history` has the same shape for a vector `:default-target` inside a region.
- The contract: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1808` ("every target declared inside a region ... resolves strictly within that region"), and `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2311-2316`.
- The correct siblings: `chart/layout.cljc:1099-1173` (`project-flat` per region plus `region-scoped-id`) and `mermaid.cljc:140-152` (`root-path` = region).
- Entry point: `scxml/spec->scxml` (:809).

## Failure scenario

1. `{:type :parallel :regions {:r {:initial :a :states {:a {:on {:go [:c :d]}} :c {:initial :d :states {:d {} :e {}}}}} :q {:initial :x :states {:x {}}}}}` exports `<transition event="go" target="c___d" .../>`. The document's ids are `{r, r___a, r___c, r___c___d, r___c___e, q, q___x, rf2_parallel_root}`, so `c___d` is dangling.
2. `{:type :parallel :regions {:a {:initial :idle :on {:reset :idle} :states {:idle {:on {:go :b}} :b {}}} :b {:initial :x :states {:x {}}}}}` exports `<transition event="reset" target="idle" .../>`, which is dangling too. The chart projects the same edge as `region__a -> region__a__idle`.

## Evidence

Executed with bounded JVM probes (`p1.clj`, `p4.clj`, frozen tree, scratch `deps.edn`). Both printed the emitted XML, the id set, and "dangling targets: (c___d)" / "(idle)", with `round-trip equal? true` in both, which shows why the existing round-trip oracle cannot see it. Control: in the same documents the in-region keyword target `:b` correctly emits `a___b`. Both definitions pass `grammar/valid-definition?`. Tracker: no bead on SCXML region scoping (searched "scxml", "machines-viz").

## Smallest fix

Thread a region `root-path` through the region's emit, as `mermaid.cljc` does. Resolve a vector target (and a vector `:default-target`) as `(into root-path target)`, and resolve a keyword target on the region body itself against the region, not the machine root. Make `decode-target` the inverse: strip the region prefix off an in-region absolute target when the source sits in that region. Add a test asserting that every emitted `target` token is a declared `id`. Fence: `scxml.cljc`, `scxml_cljs_test.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`tools/machines-viz`: `clojure -M:test` (JVM; `scxml_cljs_test.cljc`, `cross_emitter_agreement_cljs_test.cljc`).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict (worker/mviz-3x7nj, PR #10333) — 2026-09-24 AUSEST

FIXED. Premise reproduced at trunk 82dbed92a7 with a JVM probe: scenario 1 emitted target="c___d" (dangling), scenario 2 target="idle" (dangling), and a vector history :default-target [:c :e] inside a region emitted "c___e" (dangling). In all three the local round trip still read equal, as the bead said.

Fix (tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/scxml.cljc): emit-state carries the scope root ([] for flat/compound, [<region>] for a region body and everything under it). A vector target, and a vector history :default-target, resolve as (into root-path target). A region body's own :on / :after / :always keyword resolves among the region's top-level states (sibling-scope). decode-target is the exact inverse: it takes the same root and sibling path and strips the region prefix back off.

Deliberately unchanged: a region body's own :on-done keeps the plain sibling rule (a keyword names a SIBLING REGION). That is the existing three-emitter convention the chart and Mermaid share, and cross_emitter_agreement_cljs_test pins it. A vector on it is now region-scoped, which matches the chart and Mermaid. Spec 005's "every target inside a region resolves within it" sentence names a region STATE-NODE's :on-done and the region root :on, not the region root's own :on-done, so no ruling was made here.

Regression (scxml_cljs_test.cljc): region-targets-are-region-scoped (exact ids r___c___d, a___idle, r___q___y for a head that shadows a sibling region's name, and r___c___f___g for a region history default, plus the declared-id guard), region-scoped-targets-round-trip, and scxml-parallel-fixtures-targets-declared. The declared-id helper now splits a space-separated W3C target list.

Control: with scxml.cljc reverted to the pre-fix blob, the machines-viz JVM suite went to exit 1 with 10 failures, all in the new tests. The shadowing case is caught only by the exact id, because pre-fix it named the sibling region's DECLARED state q___y. The round-trip test stayed green pre-fix, as predicted. Restored and verified by blob hash against HEAD. Final: machines-viz clojure -M:test exit 0, 667 tests / 2981 assertions / 0 failures, post-rebase onto 401b33174d.
Merged-PR audit #10333 (44f5c986c9aaf70b1fb852d720c02c26460ce273; merged 2026-09-24T01:31:08Z). Completeness: Region roots now thread through SCXML transition/history emit and inverse decode, with the existing region-completion convention preserved. Viz grammar mirrors unaddressed inline-spawn refusal and parity corpus includes addressed controls. Share sanitization drops the four non-topology record fields while preserving identifier keys; unencodable residuals return documented value-free encode-failed. Correctness: Accepted machines-viz JVM 667 tests/2981 assertions, local CLJS 878/3983 and CI 31 successes. Controls produce 10 SCXML failures, 2 grammar/parity failures, 3 share failures plus the RegExp error. Exact shadowed-target ids and declared-id checks supplement roundtrips. title: xray-domain-panels-b: App-DB diff mode drops whole-instance, area and top removals, so a destroyed machine, a cleared pending-nav or a reset user db renders as nothing
description:
## Defect

In diff mode, the App-DB tab's section model is built from the post-state alone. Anything removed at section granularity vanishes without trace:

- **A destroyed machine instance or spawn.** `instances-of` maps only over the after-area's entries, so an id present only in `before` never becomes a row.
- **A reserved area emptied by the epoch** (the last machine destroyed, a pending navigation cleared). The area is filtered out by `:when (not (:empty? entry))`, so its before-state is never rendered.
- **A user-domain app-db cleared to `{}`.** `top-section` takes the empty branch and renders the "no user-domain keys yet" placeholder without passing `before`, although the model carries a non-empty `:before-top`.

Spec 004 says the tab shows the post-state "with its pre-state carried into the shared inspector for added, modified and removed annotations". It also says that removed slots must still be visible, rendered "in place struck-through". Removals INSIDE a surviving instance do render, because the shared inspector unions before and after. It is only removal of a whole instance, area or top that disappears. Added and modified instances are handled, including the rf2-227cz `added` sentinel. The removed side is simply missing.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:364-397`. `instances-of` does `(->> area-value (map ...))`. Ids only in `before-area` are never visited.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:399-552`. In `current-state-sections`, the `:empty?` of an instances area is computed from the after-side instances only (line 533). For a singleton it is the after value only (lines 541-545). Line 551 filters on it.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:481-522`. In `top-section`, `empty?` (line 515) makes the body `(empty-body ...)` (line 521), and `before` is dropped on that branch.
- Public entry: the App-DB tab (`:rf.xray/app-db-state`, `app_db_diff_subs.cljs`) in diff mode, on any epoch that destroys an actor, clears a routing slot, or resets the user db.

## Failure scenario

1. A machine `:door/main` is destroyed by an event while `:other` survives. The App-DB tab's machines area lists only `:other`, with no struck-through `:door/main`.
2. If `:door/main` was the only machine, the machines area disappears entirely.
3. A navigation guard continues or cancels, so `:pending-navigation` goes from `{:to :app/settings}` to absent. The route area shows the current route with no removed pending-navigation.
4. A logout handler returns `{}` as the user db. The top card reads "app-db has no user-domain keys yet.", which suggests the db was always empty rather than that the user and cart were just cleared.

In each case the operator asks "what did this event remove?" and the tab answers "nothing".

## Evidence

The section model (`.cljc`) was **executed** in a bounded JVM probe against the real helpers:

```
A1 machine :door/main destroyed, :other survives
   areas: [:rf/machines]  instance ids shown: [:other]  any trace of :door/main in model? false
A2 the only machine destroyed
   areas: []              any trace of :door/main in model? false
A3 pending-navigation cleared
   areas: [:rf/route]     any trace of pending (:app/settings) in model? false
A4 control: ADDED machine  instances: [[:door/main :ADDED-SENTINEL]]
A5 control: MODIFIED machine  instances: [[:door/main {:state :closed} {:state :open}]]
A6 top cleared to {}      :top {}  :before-top {:user {:name "a"}, :cart [1 2]}
```

The controls A4 and A5 show the model does diff the added and modified sides.

The A6 renderer behaviour is **inspected**, not executed: `app_db_diff_state.cljs` is CLJS and shadow-cljs is out of bounds for this review. The empty branch visibly never reads `before`.

Spec quotes:

- `tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md:23-25`: "the focused epoch's post-state, with its pre-state carried into the shared inspector for added, modified and removed annotations".
- `004-App-DB-Diff.md:343-348`: "The diff renders the union of before ∪ after — a slot present in before but absent from after ... must still be visible, rendered in place struck-through with the :removed chrome".

Tracker search found no bead ruling instance-level removals out of scope. rf2-227cz fixed the added side only, and rf2-jcdvo's empty-area filter was about "No X" placeholder cards, not diff mode.

## Smallest fix

In diff mode:

- iterate the union of after-ids and before-ids in `instances-of`, and tag before-only ids with a removed marker (for example `:value` set to the existing absence sentinel, with the real `:before`);
- compute `:empty?` over both sides, so an area emptied this epoch survives the filter;
- in `top-section`, take the value-body path when `before` is a non-empty map.

The shared inspector already has the `:removed` idiom for slots (004:343-348). How it presents a removed ROOT, that is a whole instance, was not checked here, so the fix should confirm it.

- Fence: `app_db_diff_helpers.cljc`, `app_db_diff_state.cljs`, and their tests.
- No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- The helpers are `.cljc` with no reader conditional at these lines, so they are graded by the `tools/xray` JVM suite (`clojure -M:test`, `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh`).
- The `top-section` change is `.cljs`, so only the CLJS lane grades it: `npm run test:cljs`, plus the DOM tests in the browser lane if a dom test pins the empty card.

## Decision needed

No.

title: examples-scripts (out-of-tree doc): docs/ssr/streaming.md:105 'nil => fresh root' implies a payload-less page renders; :on-ready never fires without a payload
description:
## Defect

This is OUT-OF-TREE DOC PROSE about an example, not a file in `examples/`. It sits outside every slice of this wave and is filed here at the coordinator's request.

The streaming-SSR guide's client bootstrap snippet comments its render call `;; payload ⇒ adopt the streamed markup; nil ⇒ fresh root`. That reads as if the bootstrap degrades to a client-rendered fresh root when there is no SSR payload. It does not. `:on-ready` fires only after the final `__rf_payload` node is in the DOM. So a nil `payload` inside it means the payload script was present and the fail-closed EDN read REJECTED it, and a page served without a payload never reaches the callback and renders nothing.

The 2026-09-21 wave rewrote exactly this implication in the example itself (rf2-fn0kx.6 finding 3, commit `c383969c5f`). Its report and worker notes both name `docs/ssr/streaming.md:105` as carrying "the same 'nil ⇒ fresh root' comment", out of fence and handed to the docs owner. It never became a bead.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `docs/ssr/streaming.md:105`, inside the `ssr/streaming-install!` `:on-ready` example, above `(reagent-adapter/render! app-root tree el {:hydrate? (some? payload)})`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming/client.cljs:901` and `:908`: both `finish!` call sites are gated on `(final-payload-present? root payload-id)`.
- `client.cljs:726-766`: `finalize!` is the only caller of `on-ready`.
- `client.cljs:798-823`, the `:on-ready` docstring: "called EXACTLY ONCE when the stream has FINALISED … and above all not by falling through to `create-root`".
- The example's corrected comment is at `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:451-466`.

## Failure scenario

A reader copies the guide's bootstrap. They take "nil ⇒ fresh root" to mean the same entry point also serves an un-streamed load, such as a client-only route, a static dev serve with no baked payload, or a server that streamed nothing. They then ship it for a page that sometimes has no `__rf_payload`. On that page `:on-ready` never fires and the app never renders. The page is blank with no error, because the observer simply keeps waiting (the example's comment at `core.cljc:457-459` states this outright). The guide's own warning box (`:124-131`) covers only "don't fall through before the payload arrives". It never says the payload-less case renders nothing.

## Evidence

Inspected; the control flow is short and fully gated.

- `on-ready` is invoked only from `finalize!`, and `finalize!` only through `finish!`, whose two call sites both require `final-payload-present?`. So a nil payload at `:on-ready` can only mean a rejected payload.
- rf2-fn0kx.6's close reason and notes record the same reading, and its merged commit `c383969c5f` corrected the example on it.
- Tracker: `bd search "fresh root" --status all` and `bd search "streaming.md" --status all` each return 0. The control search `suspense-boundary` returns rf2-fn0kx.6, so the instrument finds beads. rf2-fn0kx.6's notes name this line only as an out-of-fence pointer.

## Smallest fix

Reword the one comment to what is true, for example: `;; payload ⇒ adopt the streamed markup. nil here means the payload arrived but was rejected (a page with no payload never reaches :on-ready) ⇒ fresh root`. Optionally add one sentence after the snippet: a page that must also work un-streamed checks for the payload BEFORE `streaming-install!`, or uses the non-streaming recipe. That mirrors `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:462-466`.

Fence: `docs/ssr/streaming.md` only. Not a hot-zone file.

## Gates

The edit is confined to a fenced code block, so neither link gate inspects it. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` both skip fenced content, per CLAUDE.md § Build & Test. Verify the rendered snippet by hand and say so in the PR body. A strict build confirms only that the page still builds.

## Decision needed

No. The example's comment was already corrected on the same reading; this brings the guide into line.
notes:
WORKER VERDICT (PR #10338, branch worker/ssrstream-3x7nj), 2026-09-24 AUSEST: FIXED.

The premise held at trunk 757ece5afd. In client.cljs, `on-ready` is called only from `finalize!`, and both `finish!` call sites are gated on `stream-complete?`, which is #10306's renamed final-payload check and now also requires the parser to have closed the payload. The comment inside the fenced snippet in docs/ssr/streaming.md now reads, over three comment lines: payload => adopt the streamed markup; nil here means the payload arrived but was REJECTED => fresh root; a page with no payload at all never reaches :on-ready. title: INCOMPLETE: Story schema reads still disappear when setup or scripts use ambient args
description:
PR #10315 (43bf4ee37ce115e4cfae1382989dc8c5f9df00ab) claims the shared Controls/Schema-validation resolver is arg-independent, but it still calls variant-plan without :run-args and recovers only :rf.error/story-view-args-invalid. A valid variant whose setup or script uses [:arg k], with k supplied by its story or globals, throws :rf.error/story-missing-arg earlier in compilation. No schema rides that exception, so compile-schema still returns nil and schema-derived Controls and Schema-validation disappear.

Source: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/view_args.cljc:compile-schema; plan.cljc:1413-1426 substitutes setup/script before resolving the view schema at 1610-1617. Concrete shape: a story supplies :args {:label "Go"} and a component with :rf/props [:map [:label :string]], while its variant has :setup [[:dispatch [:app/set-label [:arg :label]]]]. The actual run and the fixed Docs reader supply the ambient layer; the schema reader does not.

The implementation notes on closed rf2-3x7nj.28.3 explicitly acknowledge this remaining case but leave it solely in notes. No exact open Bead exists. This combines supported story args and ordinary arg substitution.

Correction: resolve the effective component's schema without compiling arg-dependent execution steps, or supply the correct run-arg layers while keeping memoisation valid and preserving schema visibility for invalid current values. Reuse existing component/plan resolution rather than introduce a second inheritance policy. Add a regression for story/global-only args referenced in setup/script, plus the existing invalid-prop control.

Evidence is source flow and the implementer's explicit residual, not a new test run. Accepted the PR's reported JVM/CLJS suites and controls.

title: story xray-preset :focus arm dispatches :rf.xray/focus-event with a map where Xray takes <dispatch-id> <frame> — silent no-op
description:
Follow-up noted (and deliberately not fixed) under rf2-dsbob, PR #10264.

The Story xray-preset `:focus` arm, `apply-focus!` in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/xray_preset.cljc (inside `#?(:cljs ...)`), dispatches `[:rf.xray/focus-event {:event-pos n}]` into `:rf/xray`. Xray registers that event at tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs (`(rf/reg-event :rf.xray/focus-event (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ dispatch-id frame-id]] ...))`, verified at trunk 828abaf938), so the preset's map lands as the `dispatch-id` and `frame-id` is nil: the handler runs without error and focuses nothing meaningful. Same silent-no-op shape as rf2-dsbob. The contract per tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/focus.cljc is `[:rf.xray/focus-event <dispatch-id> <frame>]`, so a cascade POSITION has to be resolved to a dispatch-id (or the preset's shape changed) before dispatching; that is a design call rather than an id rename, which is why it was left out of rf2-dsbob.

Do: decide how `:event-pos` resolves to a dispatch-id (or whether the slot should carry something else), fix `apply-focus!`, and pin it with a node-lane test that reads Xray's focus state (as `panel-preset-selects-the-xray-tab` in tools/story/test/re_frame/story/xray_preset_cljs_test.cljs does for `:rf.xray/selected-tab`), not merely that a dispatch happened.

The preset slot `{:event-pos N}` is documented only as "the Nth event in the current cascade" (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc `XrayPreset`; tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md §Xray preset slot), and nothing defines (a) which list N indexes — the variant frame's `rf/epoch-history`, or Xray's L2 `:rf.xray/event-bundles` in `:rf/xray` — (b) which frame, since a variant can own more than one (story frames.cljc `variant-frames`), and (c) what happens when the preset applies at the selection edge before the variant's setup events have settled, so N does not exist yet. == RULING (mayor, 2026-09-24, under the project stance; small call, not escalated) ==

DECISION: the Story xray-preset :focus {:event-pos N} slot has no defined meaning. The earlier STOPPED note on this bead names three unanswered questions: which list N indexes, which frame, and what happens before setup settles. And the slot has never worked: apply-focus! dispatches a map where Xray's :rf.xray/focus-event takes [dispatch-id frame-id], so it is a silent no-op. Define it, or retire it?

RULING: RETIRE the :focus slot.

WHY:
- Measured at trunk 46ef83f136: no story, testbed or example in the tree uses it. Its only carriers are its own schema (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc XrayPreset, about :429-441), its dispatcher (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/xray_preset.cljc, the ns-doc example about :15 and apply-focus! about :499-506), its own test (tools/story/test/re_frame/story/xray_preset_cljs_test.cljs about :564), and one row in tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md (:653). That row already says "Rare — usually you want LIVE to track head".
- Designing index, frame and timing semantics for a slot nobody uses, and which never worked, is exactly the gold-plating the stance rejects. Pre-alpha, so there is no back-compat cost. If a real need for pre-focusing appears, it can be designed then, against a real use.

title: xstate-parity: an :entry / :exit / :action VECTOR passes reg-machine and kills the first drain with a generic :rf.error/handler-exception; the engine's :rf.error/machine-bad-action-form never surfaces at registration
description:
## Gap

XState v6 authors `entry` / `exit` as ONE transition function; an array is not a valid shape and the actor errors at start (`TypeError: transitionFn is not a function`) — loud, if generic. re-frame2's spec is stricter still: spec/005:256 — "`:entry` and `:exit` are single fns or single keyword references into the machine's `:actions` map — never vectors" — and :461-470 says the same for `:action`; §Testing Level 1 (:4270) promises that a guard or action "that is neither fn nor keyword" throws the same `:rf.error/*` ex-info the registration validators throw. The engine does own that id — `transition.cljc:265` throws `:rf.error/machine-bad-action-form`, pinned on the pure path by `machine_pure_error_contract_test.clj`.

But `reg-machine` / `make-machine-handler` does NOT run that form check. A vector `:entry`, `:exit` or transition `:action` registers `:ok`; the first drain that reaches the vector throws inside the handler, the router reports it as the generic `:rf.error/handler-exception` with no `:rf.error/machine-*` id, and the machine is left either never booted (`:entry` — the installed snapshot is the empty map `{}`) or stuck (`:exit` / `:action` — the event is swallowed, state unchanged). This is a fail-loud promise that fails generic, one drain late. Handed off by dimension D (D-j1b §1/§1b); re-measured here at source.

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/E-7b-handoffs.mjs` -> `E-7b-handoffs.out`: `entry as ARRAY of fns | ERROR TypeError: transitionFn is not a function`, `entry array ran: []`; control: a single-fn entry ran (`control ran: ["single"]`). Docs: `xs-docs/actions.md:9-11` (`entry: (_, enq) => {...}`), `configuration.md` state-node table (`entry` — "transition function or named action"). "documented, not reproduced" for `exit` arrays (same shape, not separately probed).

## re-frame2 evidence

Executed at trunk fe8de195bd, `jvm/E/E7_handoffs.clj` -> `E7_handoffs.out`:
- §1 `:entry [fn fn]`: `reg: :ok`, `start: {}` (snapshot is the EMPTY MAP), `log: []` (neither fn ran), `error traces: [[:rf.error/handler-exception ...]]`.
- §1b `:entry [:k1 :k2]` (keyword vector): identical — `start: {}`, `:rf.error/handler-exception`.
- §1c transition `:action [fn fn]`: `reg: :ok`, start fine (`{:state :a}`), `go: {:state :a}` — the event is SWALLOWED, `:rf.error/handler-exception`.
- §1d `:exit [fn]`: `reg: :ok`, start fine, `go: {:state :a}` swallowed, `:rf.error/handler-exception`.
- §1e Level-1 control: `(machine-transition ...)` with the vector `:entry` throws `{:threw :rf.error/machine-bad-action-form}` — the engine has the precise id; only the registered path loses it.
- §1f control: a single-fn `:entry` runs on start (`log: [:ran]`, no errors).
- Source: `transition.cljc:265` is the only site raising `:rf.error/machine-bad-action-form`; `validation.cljc` (1930 lines) has no `:entry` / `:exit` / `:action` FORM check (its `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` covers a dangling KEYWORD only — `E1_graph.out` `unresolved-action-ref | REJECTED`).
- Dimension D's independent measurement agrees: `jvm/D/D-j1b-silent-accepts.out` `[1 entry-vector-runtime] {:reg :ok, :state nil, :log [], :errors [:rf.error/handler-exception]}`.
- Tracker: `bd search` "entry vector", "bad-action-form", "action vector", "handler-exception" — 0 each.

## Why it matters

Coming from XState (`entry: [a, b]` is the v4/v5 idiom that v6 dropped) or from re-frame's own `:fx` vectors, a vector of actions is the first thing an author or an AI writes. The spec says it is refused; the runtime says `:ok` and then the machine silently fails to boot — the snapshot is `{}`, so even `[:rf/machine id]` reads as "alive". The generic `:rf.error/handler-exception` names no machine, no slot and no state, so the diagnosis is a stack trace into `transition.cljc`. This is precisely the "silent swallow" Conventions §No silent swallow forbids, arrived at through a grammar rule the engine already knows how to name.

## Options

1. Registration: add the form check to `validate-machine!` — every `:entry` / `:exit` / transition `:action` (in `:on`, `:always`, `:after`, `:on-done`, `:on-error`, `:on-timeout`, choice candidates) must be a fn or a keyword; reject with the EXISTING `:rf.error/machine-bad-action-form` (and the symmetric `:rf.error/machine-bad-guard-form` for `:guard`, which `transition.cljc` also owns). Runtime-only; no spec change (spec already says "never vectors"); breaks no valid machine.
2. Widen the grammar to accept vectors (run in order) and update spec/005:256, :461-470, Spec-Schemas `:rf/state-node`, the skill page's "no action-vector" row, machines-viz emitters. Rejected by the spec's own reasoning (one named compound action is richer for tooling than an anonymous list) and by EP-0029 C3's posture; do not take.
3. Do nothing. Not acceptable: the spec promises a registration-time refusal.

## Recommendation

Option 1. The error id, its message shape and its pure-path test already exist; this is one walker over the action slots in `validate-machine!` plus one registration test per slot (entry, exit, transition action, guard). Type `bug` because spec/005:256 and :4270 promise the refusal and the code does not deliver it.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc`
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/` — registration pins (a `machine_registration_action_form_test.clj` or an addition to the existing grammar test)
- optionally `spec/conformance/fixtures/machine-reg-error-*.edn` (capability `:fsm/registration-validation`)
- No hot-zone file: spec/005 already states the rule; spec/009's error catalogue already lists `:rf.error/machine-bad-action-form` / `-bad-guard-form` (grep count: present in `implementation/machines/src` outside `validation.cljc`).

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` only if the change lands in a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch (not expected); conformance corpus only if a fixture is added.

## Decision needed

no

This finding's fix edits implementation/machines/src, so do NOT dispatch it until PR #10357 has MERGED; the fix then also follows the present-tense rule of epic rf2-tv5ac for any comment it writes. Cleared by: PR #10357 merging.
## Guard and map forms — dimension A handoff merged (2026-09-24, jvm/E/E8_a_handoffs.out §2; A/gap-2-transition-keys.md)

The same hole admits every non-fn / non-keyword GUARD form and the map ACTION form, not only vectors. Re-measured at trunk fe8de195bd (E8 §2, each beside its control) and independently by A at 20d5050bdc (`jvm/A/A-5.out` §guard shapes / §action shapes):

- `:guard [:g 10]` (vector), `:guard {:id :g :params {}}` (map), `:guard {:and [:g :h]}` (combinator), `:guard "g"` (string): all `reg=:ok`, and the first `[:go]` wedges the machine on that event — state unchanged, generic `:rf.error/handler-exception`, no `:rf.error/machine-*` id. Control `:guard :g` (g false) stays `:a` with no error.
- `:entry {:type :a1}` (the XState `{type, params}` object): `reg=:ok`, throws at BIRTH — `state=nil`, the snapshot never installed, `:rf.error/handler-exception`. Control `:entry :a1` runs (`ran=[:a1]`).
- The ENGINE owns the precise ids for every one of these: pure `machine-transition` throws `:rf.error/machine-bad-guard-form` for the vector and the map guard (`transition.cljc:238`) and `:rf.error/machine-bad-action-form` for the map entry (`transition.cljc:265`). Only the registered path loses them.

Record: `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2763` `GuardRef` is `[:or :keyword fn?]` — "one fn or one keyword reference … No compound data form ({:and ...})" — and `:2770` `ActionRef` likewise; `spec/005:222-224` transition shape row. So the closed VALUE grammar is normative and pure-path-enforced, and unchecked at registration.

Option 1 above already names the symmetric `:rf.error/machine-bad-guard-form` for `:guard`; this note is the measurement that it is needed, and widens the walk to the map form. The message should name the XState spellings it will meet: `{:type ..}` / `[..]` -> a fn or a keyword into `:actions`; `{:and ..}` / `{:id :params}` -> compose fns or name a guard in `:guards`. Priority: A's draft groups this with the foreign-key half (rf2-2n6uv.1.3) as one P2 "transition-map closed-key + value-shape check"; the two beads stay separate here because this one is a BUG against a promised registration refusal (spec/005:256, :4270) and .1.3 is a consistency task, but one PR can close both — the walk over transition maps is shared.

title: xstate-parity: :spawn :on-done in the transition-map shape EP-0029 A8 teaches registers without error and is silently inert
description:
## Gap

XState v6 `invoke.onDone` is a TRANSITION: `onDone: { target: 'authenticated' }` (optionally with a function body reading `event.output`) moves the parent when the child completes. It is the one-line spelling every XState machine uses to advance on a child's result.

re-frame2's `:spawn :on-done` is a `:data`-only fold — `(fn [{:keys [data result]}] new-data)` (spec/005 D2, line 3327 at fe8de195bd) — and the parent advances through a SEPARATE spelling: an explicit `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/done {:target …}}` arm or an `:always` guarded on the folded data (both measured working, `jvm/C/c7.out` A/B/C). The parity EP itself, however, teaches the XState shape as the re-frame2 expression: `docs/EP/EP-0029-xstate-v6-machine-parity.md` A8 (lines 377-423) shows `:on-done {:target :loaded :action :store-user}` on the parent's `:spawn`. That map form is ACCEPTED by `reg-machine` without error and is silently INERT at runtime: the child finishes and is destroyed, the parent stays in the spawning state, no `:data` changes, the named action never runs. Two defects in one: a registration-time hole (every other bad `:spawn` shape fails loud) and a stale record in the document an AI reads first when porting from XState.

## XState evidence

- Executed: `xs/C-4.mjs` → `xs/C-4.out`: `after child final: parent authenticated {"token":"T","err":null,"events":["xstate.done.actor"]} … kid status done kid output T` — `onDone: ({ context, event }) => ({ target: 'authenticated', context: {…token: event.output…} })`.
- Docs: `xs-docs/invoke.md` §Invoke properties (`onDone` — "Transition taken when the child completes. `event.output` holds its output.").

## re-frame2 evidence

- Executed: `jvm/C/c7.clj` → `jvm/C/c7.out` (trunk fe8de195bd):
  - A (fold + explicit arm): parent `:authenticated`, `:token "T"`, the arm saw `(nth ev 2)` = `{:result "T", :error? false, :completed-at …}`.
  - B (explicit arm only): parent `:authenticated`, carrier map captured.
  - C (fold + `:always` on data): parent `:authenticated`.
  - D (`:on-done {:target :authenticated :action :store}` — the A8 shape): `[:accepted {:state :authenticating, :data {:token nil}}]` — registered, child finished and was destroyed, parent did not move, no `:stored` key, no error trace.
- spec/005 D2 (line 3327): "The parent-notification hook is `:on-done` on the parent's `:spawn` map. Signature `(fn [{:keys [data result]}] new-data)`". §Spec-spec keys row `:on-done` (line 3003) — fn only. §`:on-error` (3337-3396) — the failure counterpart IS an `:on`-shaped transition.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:667` (`apply-spawn-on-done`) applies the fold; the validator (`lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc`) does not refuse a non-fn value.
- Documented spellings that DO work: `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md:89`, `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:281`, `docs/machines/actors.md:280`.
- No test pins the map form either way (searched `implementation/machines/test` for `:on-done {`).

## Why it matters

An AI or programmer porting an XState chart writes `:on-done {:target …}` because EP-0029 A8 — the document titled "XState v6 Machine Parity" — shows exactly that, and `reg-machine` says nothing. The machine then hangs in the spawning state after every child completion, with no error anywhere; the only clue is the absence of a transition. This is the silent-wrong-behaviour class (P1 shape) contained to P2 only because the correct spelling is one grep away in the skill docs.

## Options

1. **Fail loud + fix the record (spec-only + validation, no behaviour change).** Reject a non-fn `:on-done` at registration with `:rf.error/machine-spawn-bad-shape` (or a dedicated id) whose message names the two working spellings; correct EP-0029 A8's example to the fold + `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/done {:target …}}` pair. Breaks no existing machine (the map form does nothing today).
2. **Honour the map as sugar (runtime + spec).** Let `:on-done` accept the same `:on`-shaped transition spec `:on-error` accepts — keyword / vector target, `{:target :guard :action}`, guarded vector — resolved at the `:spawn`-bearing state's level, with `:result` reachable as `(:result (nth ev 2))`, and keep the fn form as the data-only fold. The carrier already flows into the parent's macrostep, so this is desugaring the map onto the existing `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/done …}` arm. Re-rules D2 (fn-only) into "fn = fold, map = transition", which is the `:on-error` symmetry and the XState shape. Breaks nothing existing.
3. Leave the runtime, delete A8's example — smallest diff, but leaves a registration hole that swallows a plausible spelling.

## Recommendation

Option 2, with option 1's validation as the floor if D2 is retained: symmetry with `:on-error` removes a rule to teach ("success is a fold, failure is a transition"), matches the gold standard's shape, and costs one desugar onto machinery that already exists. Either way the A8 example must stop teaching a shape that does nothing.

## Fence

- `docs/EP/EP-0029-xstate-v6-machine-parity.md` (A8 example)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT ZONE — D2 at 3327, §Spec-spec keys 3003, §`:on-error` 3337) and `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (HOT ZONE — `:rf/invoke-spec` `:on-done` shape) if option 2
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` (reject or admit the map), `registration.cljc:667` (`apply-spawn-on-done`) and `transition.cljc` (the `:on {:rf.machine.spawn/done …}` resolution) if option 2
- `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md`, `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md` (row `invoke` → `:spawn`), `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:281`
- new test beside `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machines_on_error_cljs_test.cljc`

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` (JVM); `npm run test:cljs` if a `#?(:cljs …)` branch moves; `spec/conformance` corpus if `final-state-child-fires-on-done.edn` is extended.

## Decision needed

Yes. Keep D2 (fn-only `:on-done`, reject the map at registration, fix A8) — or widen `:on-done` to the `:on`-shaped transition `:on-error` already accepts (fn = fold, map = transition)?

## What

PR #10407 (rf2-2n6uv.5.1, merged at trunk abc2be08ce) made the machine ROOT honour `:entry`, `:exit` and `:tags`. ## Required correction (in tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/grammar.cljc)
- Add a root-slot check with the engine's refused set, returning `{:category :rf.error/machine-root-slot-not-supported :path [] :keys <sorted>}`:

  - accepted on a PARALLEL root: `:after`, `:timeout` / `:on-timeout`, and an action-only `:on-done`, because the runtime reads them there;
  - a flat root's `:after` / `:timeout` keep the existing `machine-non-parallel-root-after-not-supported`.

- Call it in `flat-defect` and `parallel-defect`, right after `(node-keys-defect [] d true)`.
- Root `:entry` / `:exit` / `:tags` need no grammar change. If the chart or Mermaid projections render root actions or root tags anywhere, check them; the worker did not.
- Add parity rows to `engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc`: rejects for a root `:spawn`, a root `:final?` and a flat root `:on-done`; accepts for root `:entry` / `:exit` / `:tags`. Red first.

## Fence
tools/machines-viz/src and tools/machines-viz/test only. The engine is the reference.

title: machines-viz parity 3: choice grammar unchecked on ordinary states; region-body :after nil refused by viz but accepted by engine
description:
## What

Worker vizparity2-8pfog found both of these while fixing rf2-8pfog (PR #10451, merged at trunk 3729603038). That PR made the viz grammar refuse region-body `:after` and `:choice` exactly as the engine does. Both findings were measured by running the engine's `validate-machine!` beside the viz grammar. Re-verify each at your trunk.

1. **The viz checks no choice grammar on ORDINARY states.** Two examples:
   - The engine refuses a stray `:choice` without `:type :choice`, as in `{:a {:choice [{:target :b}]}}`. The viz accepts it.
   - The engine refuses a choice state with no unguarded default. The viz accepts that too.

   PR #10451 applied the engine's six choice rules to region bodies only.
2. **A region body's `:after nil` is accepted by the engine but refused by the viz** as `machine-bad-after-spec`. Here the viz is stricter than the engine.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-26, under the stance)

Mirror the engine in both directions. The viz grammar's whole purpose is to agree with the engine about what a machine may say.

- **Item 1.** Apply the same choice validation #10451 built for region bodies to every state node, reusing that code. Refuse with the engine's categories. Controls:
  - a valid choice state, and a choice state nested inside a compound and a region, are accepted on both sides;
  - an ordinary state with no `:choice` is unaffected.
- **Item 2.** Accept `:after nil` wherever the engine accepts it, treated as absent.
  - Check the class, not just the instance: every `:after nil` position (state, region body, machine root). Make the viz agree with the engine at each one.
  - If the engine itself is inconsistent across those positions, do not touch the engine. Report it.
- Each gets engine-grammar parity rows in `engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc`, with both directions controlled.

title: Present-tense comments, docstrings and spec prose, repo-wide: remove change-narration and bead/PR/date provenance
description:
**Mike's instruction, 2026-09-24:** make comments, docstrings and `spec/` prose describe the code as it is now, across the whole repo. **All code is reviewed**, tests included, and `spec/` too.

This description is THE RULE for every child. Before you edit, read it together with the newest `== CALIBRATION` note below it. The pilot child writes that note, and where the two differ the note wins.

## The rule

Comments, docstrings and spec prose describe the code and the contract **as they are now, and why**. They do not tell the story of how they got here. Git history, PRs and beads hold that story.

**The test, applied to each sentence:** would this sentence still be true and worth saying if the code had been written this way on day one?
- **Yes:** keep it. Touch its wording only where a removal next to it leaves it broken.
- **It is only true because of history:** rewrite it as a present-tense reason. If it carries no reason, delete it.

Rewrites look like this:
- "We used to X, which broke Y, so now Z" becomes "Z, because X breaks Y."
- "Previously this returned nil; now it throws" becomes "Throws when …".
- Delete provenance tags outright: "(rf2-4dra9)", "per PR #10351", "added 2026-08-12", "fixed in the 2026-09-23 review wave", "EP-0026 (rf2-dlvmpc) removed …".
- Delete a retirement story, keeping only a present-tense constraint if one survives. For example, `;; validator-install wrappers — RETIRED (rf2-kuky.39) … rf2-wad2fl had already removed their re-exports …` becomes nothing, or becomes "There is no per-fn install wrapper; register schemas with `reg-app-schema`."
- A comment whose ONLY content is a bead id: if the reason it points at matters, `bd show <id>`. If that resolves, write the reason in present tense. Otherwise delete the comment.
- Audit and process narrative inside code ("a worker measured …", "the audit found …", "the mayor ruled …", "the rf2-3x7nj review wave") goes. Keep the property it established, stated as a property.

## In scope

- **Code comments** in every tracked code file (`.clj .cljs .cljc .edn .js .cjs .mjs .ts .py .sh .ps1 .yml .yaml .bb`): `;` and `#` and `//` and `/* */` comments, and the prose inside `(comment …)` and `#_` forms.
- **Docstrings:** ns, def, defn, defmacro, defmethod and schema `:doc`/`:description` strings, JSDoc, and Python docstrings.
- **Human-readable test prose:** `testing` descriptions and assertion messages.
- **Spec prose:** every `spec/*.md` page, `spec/conformance/**` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`.

## Out of scope — leave it, or report it

- **Identifiers of every kind:**
  - var, fn and ns names, and test names (`deftest …-rf2-xxxx` stays);
  - keywords, CSS classes and `data-*` attributes — `data-rf2-source-coord` is NOT a bead id;
  - JS test titles in `it(…)` / `describe(…)`, because runners and filters match on them.
- **Strings the program emits or a test asserts on:** error messages, diagnostics, ex-data, trace payloads, CLI output. Those are behaviour.
- **Present-tense contract that merely uses a history word.** "`:rf.adapter/ui` is reserved and never recycled" stays, and so does "retired keys are rejected loudly with …", which describes current behaviour. Only the provenance around such sentences goes.
- **Cross-references a reader can open, which hold the current contract or rationale:** spec section references (`spec/011-SSR.md §…`), and `docs/EP/EP-00NN` references used as a POINTER ("see EP-0026 §Image Keys"). EP *narration* ("EP-0026 removed X") is history.
- **Spec headings:** do not rename one. Its anchor is its slug, and inbound links break. If a heading is itself historical, report it.
- **Generated files:** a file whose header says GENERATED is fixed at its generator and regenerated, never hand-edited. `spec/api-manifest.edn` is regenerated from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`.
- **Other trees:** `docs/`, `migration/`, CHANGELOG, markdown beside code (READMEs), `**/findings/**`, `.beads/` and `ai/`. History is their purpose, or they are a separate campaign.

## Why bead ids go, even as pointers

Measured 2026-09-24 at trunk `fe8de195bd`:
- **In scope:** 3,877 tracked files and ~1.60M lines. ~46k lines of tracked code carry a bead-shaped id: 18.4k library-source lines in 1,260 files, and 27.5k test lines in 1,972 files.
- **Most ids resolve to nothing.** Of 6,793 distinct `rf2-`-prefixed tokens in tracked files, 1,280 name a bead in the tracker export. A few of the rest are not bead ids (`rf2-source` is the tail of `data-rf2-source-coord`). Most are ids the tracker does not hold: `bd show` answers "no issue found" for the three most cited, rf2-d2841 (642 lines), rf2-o5dbf (287) and rf2-2rtt6.2 (124). Control: rf2-30a8k resolves.
- **Library source ships in jars**, and its readers cannot resolve any bead id at all.

So in practice an id points somewhere no reader can follow.

## Supersedes

rf2-wppza (2026-08-21) recorded the retirement references in `spec/` as deliberate and to be kept. Examples are the dated statements naming rf2-0yp7w and the struck-through retirement rows in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`. Their history goes under THIS epic. The contract they protected stays, stated in the present tense: `:rf.adapter/ui`, `:rf.adapter/freehand` and `:rf.adapter/helix` are reserved and never recycled. CLAUDE.md's Architecture Overview still states the old disposition; the standing-rule child updates it. Until that merges, this epic governs where the two disagree.

## Mechanics every child must respect

- **Comments and prose only, with no behaviour change.** If a code token needs changing, that is out of scope: report it.
- **Prove it** with `scripts/present_tense.py`, which the pilot builds: `verify` over every changed file, having first shown it RED on a planted code change. Use its `census` for the before and after counts.
- **Docstrings are code in Clojure.** A stray `"` breaks the namespace.
  - An edit inside `#?(:cljs …)` is compiled only by the CLJS lanes (CLAUDE.md, rf2-z0pma), so a JVM green says nothing about it. Rely on CI's `CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)` and say so.
  - The shadow-cljs lane is NOT granted by any child here.
- **Tests that read docstrings or `:doc` metadata move with the text.** Run the artefact's suite.
- **Line endings.** Nearly every file is `w/crlf`.
  - Never `sed -i` (CLAUDE.md item (u)). Use the Edit/Write tools, and never pass backslashes through the Bash tool's command text (item (o)).
  - After editing, take item (e)'s three numbers with Python for every changed file.
  - `spec/011-SSR.md` is the one `i/crlf` blob (item (r)).
- **Hot-zone files** (CLAUDE.md §Workflow) take one worker at a time. Each appears in exactly one child here, marked HOT, and the mayor dispatches that child only when no other live worker holds the file.
- **Keep the diff to comment, docstring and prose lines.** Do not re-wrap untouched paragraphs, reformat, or tidy anything else.
- **Do not delete tests. Do not edit any bead a comment names.**

## Census patterns (so every child measures the same thing)

- **Bead-id line:** matches `(?<![A-Za-z0-9-])rf2-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[0-9]+)?(?:\.[0-9]+)*`. The lookbehind excludes `data-rf2-*`.
- **History-word line** (case-insensitive): matches `\b(previously|used to|no longer|formerly|was renamed|were renamed|historically|originally|retired|superseded|replaced by)\b`.

Both are CANDIDATE FILTERS, never verdicts. A history word inside a present-tense contract is correctly kept. History with none of these words is still in scope, which is why every comment gets read, not only the hits.

## Structure

- **Pilot child (P2): `implementation/machines/src`.** It calibrates this rule on real text and builds `scripts/present_tense.py`. Every other child is blocked on it. When it merges, the mayor appends a `== CALIBRATION` note here, and the fan-out starts.
- **Standing-rule child:** puts the rule into CLAUDE.md so new work does not grow it back, and updates the Architecture Overview paragraph.
- **76 surface children**, disjoint by path so they run in parallel. Each is about one dispatch: ≤ ~35k lines of code, or ~5–8k lines of spec prose. The smallest may be clustered up to four per dispatch.

## Done, per child

1. **A PR, comment- and prose-only:** `present_tense.py verify` exits 0 over the changed files, having been shown red on a plant.
2. **The surface's gates are green.** CLJS verdicts are CI's.
3. **The report states:**
   - before/after census counts for the fence;
   - which census hits were deliberately kept, grouped by reason;
   - everything reported rather than changed: identifiers, emitted strings, headings, generated files.
notes:
== CALIBRATION (mayor, 2026-09-24, from the pilot rf2-tv5ac.1, PR #10357 merged at trunk a0a49022ca) ==

READ THIS BEFORE EDITING. It amends the rule above; where the two differ, this note wins.

The pilot reviewed every comment and docstring in implementation/machines/src (34 files, 23k lines). Census: 361 -> 2 bead-id lines and 88 -> 53 history-word lines. The survivors are present-tense contract, identifiers or emitted strings. Its full report is on rf2-tv5ac.1. The mayor's rulings on it follow.

R1. THE TEN KINDS BELOW ARE THE STANDARD. Apply them as the pilot did, including the counterfactual "would" (kind 4) and the plain present tense for narration that uses no census word (kind 6).

R2. BEAD IDS WITHOUT THE rf2- PREFIX ARE IN SCOPE, AND THE CENSUS DOES NOT SEE THEM. Examples: emz8l, mle6e.2, x4s9t, bz0ox.2, h3wca.1, and labels such as (m-reply). Sweep for 4-6 character mixed letter+digit tokens with an optional .N, and read each hit. The sweep is noisy (snap2, 10ms, step3); a reviewer's eye settles it. Report the count you removed.

R3. CHANGE NARRATION WITH NO CENSUS WORD IS MOST OF WHAT REMAINS once the ids are gone. Reviewer word list, not a pattern: now, still, existing, unchanged, preserved, retained, additive/additively, continue(s) to, today, the old, the fix, remains, kept, was chosen.

R4. "used to" IS NEARLY ALWAYS PURPOSE ("Used to detect …"). Only "used to be" and "used to <past-tense verb>" are history. No tool change.

R5. NO NEW TOOL CHECK FOR STRINGS. `verify` blanks every string, so an edited emitted string passes it; that is known and accepted. Instead, each child's report states how many strings changed and confirms each is a docstring or human-readable test prose (a `testing` description or an assertion message), saying HOW it checked. A docstring-position rule would misfire on test children, where test prose is legitimately in scope. The suites catch asserted text.

R6. SCOPE EXTENSION — USER-FACING EMITTED STRINGS THAT CARRY PROVENANCE. This is a mayor ruling under the stance, and Mike may reverse it.
- Error messages and diagnostic text that carry a bead id, PR number, date, or ruling/process vocabulary ARE in scope. Examples: "rf2-wvh95f F2 …", "operator-ruled divergence", "EP-0029 A4" used as narration.
- Rewrite such a message to state the present rule. Keep its meaning, and change NO keyword, ex-data key or identifier. Every test that asserts the text moves with it: run the suite.
- History that genuinely helps a user stays, as a present-tense instruction. Example: "`:timeout-ms` is not a spawn key; use `:timeout`".
- A `do-not-rename` sentinel string is an identifier: leave it.
- The pilot's machines/src instances are filed separately as a child of this epic.

R7. SIZE — COMMIT AND PUSH AFTER EVERY FILE. The pilot needed about 1.4M tokens and one compaction for 23k dense lines, and several children are about 35k.
- Do not split your bead.
- Commit each finished file as `docs(<area>): present-tense comments in <file>` and PUSH it immediately. A compaction or an allowance stop then loses nothing, and a resume costs one message.
- Expect one or two compactions on dense source. After one, re-read this note and the files you have already committed; your commits are the record of progress.

R8. STALE PROSE FOUND WHILE REWRITING (kind 9): fix it ONLY where the code verifies the new sentence. A BEHAVIOURAL contradiction between comments is REPORTED, never settled in prose. The pilot's one, about synchronous versus post-drain listener delivery in machines/src, is filed separately.

R9. KEEP these pointers: Spec D-labels (D3/D5/D7), spec line references, EP A-labels used as pointers, and version pins (xstate@5.32.0). "XState v6" is the documented baseline, not a typo.

R10. EVERY CENSUS HIT IS A QUESTION, NEVER AN INSTRUCTION. In machines/src, 55 surviving hits were runtime-state words ("no longer on the active path"), attempt semantics ("superseded"), a rejected-input category ("retired", tied to an identifier), purpose ("Used to"), or emitted strings.

---- The pilot's ambiguity kinds, verbatim ----

--- Ambiguities, one before/after per kind ---
1. Parenthesised bead tag -> delete.
   "restarts too (rf2-3x7nj.8.1)." -> "restarts too."
2. Bead id as sentence lead -> drop it and keep the sentence.
   "rf2-3x7nj.9.3 / .8.2 — every entry also bumps this invoke's ATTEMPT token" -> "Every entry also bumps this invoke's ATTEMPT token"
3. Bead ids without the rf2- prefix, which the census does NOT see -> delete.
   "(the emz8l shape)" -> deleted; "Spec 009 (mle6e.2)" -> "Spec 009"; "(m-reply)" -> deleted; "(bz0ox.2 / x4s9t.2)" -> deleted.
4. Bug story -> present-tense reason, written as a counterfactual "would".
   "the declarative allocator previously read :machine-id unconditionally, so an author who supplied the documented :id-prefix was silently ignored" -> "Reading :machine-id unconditionally would silently ignore an author's documented :id-prefix"
   "Previously this recur passed cascade unchanged, which DISCARDED …" -> "Passing cascade unchanged would DISCARD …"
   "a second copy … is what drifted out of sync with the executable cond before (rf2-xkr5r3)" -> "a second copy … would drift out of sync with the executable cond"
5. Retirement story -> "There is no X", keeping the constraint.
   "No :machines/machines hook: the retired enumerate alias (rf2-kuky.31) had no consumer at all … Removed from the directory with it." -> "There is no :machines/machines hook: enumerating machines is a filter over the generic registrar query any caller can write."
6. Change narration that uses NO census word -> plain present tense. This is most of what is left once the ids are gone.
   "so this preserves today's behaviour for both cases" -> "so they behave identically"
   "ride ADDITIVELY on the trace, preserving its public shape" -> "ride on the trace alongside its public shape"
   "The 2-arity is retained for callers …" -> "The 2-arity serves callers …"
   "continue to call" -> "call"; "still select-then-apply" -> "select-then-apply"; "(today rejected at registration)" -> "(registration rejects it)"
7. Past-tense design statement -> present or conditional.
   "a direction flag obscured the unifying rule" -> "would obscure"; "Flat machines used :state :foo" -> "Flat machines use :state :foo"
8. Process and ruling vocabulary -> delete it or name the reason.
   "per the XState-v5 alignment ruling." -> "per the XState-v5 alignment."; also removed RULED, "security-audit finding F1", PR numbers, slice-N, "the wave".
9. Stale prose found while rewriting -> fixed ONLY where the code verified it.
   spawn.cljc had a sentence cut short: "the :rf.machine.spawn/spawned trace and the\n trace.". git log -S traced the missing half to the deletion of the system-id family. Rewritten to name the single emission that remains.
   transition.cljc had a comment labelling the spawn-all-init fx as step "(2)" while the docstring calls it step 4 -> "(4)".
   Also fixed: the destroy.cljc example, the join :rf/join-attempt wording, and a "two spawned traces" reference.
10. Pointers that look like provenance but are not -> KEPT: Spec 005 D-labels (D3/D5/D7), spec line refs (spec/005:3568), EP-0029 A-labels, xstate@5.32.0.

--- History words that turned out to be present-tense contract (kept) ---
"no longer", "superseded", "replaced by" and "previously" mostly describe RUNTIME states and events, not code history (see the groups above). "retired" names a category of user input that the validator rejects with its own message, bound to an identifier. "Used to" is nearly always purpose. Treat a census hit as a question and never as an instruction to edit.

---- The pilot's tool ----
scripts/present_tense.py (merged): `census [--hits] <paths>`, `verify <base-rev> <paths>`, `self-test`. Show `verify` RED on one planted one-token code change before trusting its green.
MAYOR NOTE (2026-09-25), merge mechanics for large sweep branches; R7 is unchanged.
R7 (commit and PUSH after every file) stays: surviving a compaction or an allowance stop is worth more than per-commit history on trunk.
But a child with more than about 100 files produces a branch GitHub refuses to rebase-merge: "This branch can't be rebased". Measured on PR #10375: 111 commits, CLEAN, and a local replay onto trunk exited 0.
The mayor squash-merges such a PR with --match-head-commit pinned to the graded head, then verifies the landed tree against that head over the squash commit's FULL file list. That check means git diff --name-only, because gh pr view --json files stops at 100.
No worker action is needed. Workers keep R7 as written.
== STATUS (mayor, 2026-09-26): all 81 children are CLOSED.

The collector, rf2-tv5ac.81 (PR #10452, trunk 269ad7ff24), was the last child. The only present-tense residue it left is in rf2-escwk item 7 (bead ids in the tools/xray persistence_cljs_test testing strings), alongside unrelated truth fixes.

Close this epic when rf2-escwk merges.

title: spec/005: the quorum idiom has a guard read runtime-db (:rf.runtime/machines ... :done) and names :done-guard; state the achievable :data-count form
description:
spec/005-StateMachines.md prescribes a quorum idiom that a guard cannot evaluate. In section Composition with hierarchy and :after (about line 3998 at c456e717e9), and in the quorum notes near lines 3833 and 3876, a guard reads [:rf.runtime/machines :spawned ... :done]. That path lives in runtime-db, and a guard's context is only #{:data :event :state :meta :rf.cofx}, measured on the JVM at c456e717e9 by the correctness pass of rf2-ahrss. A :done-guard key is also named, but it appears only in code comments (join.cljc:240, validation.cljc:354) and is not a key the grammar accepts.

The achievable pattern: each child's :on-done keeps a count in the parent's :data, and an ordinary guard reads that count. The spec should state that form.

The guide (docs/machines/actors.md, base 460-462 and 482) carried the same impossible pattern; the rf2-ahrss PR corrects the guide. spec/005 is a hot-zone file, so this is its own change.
notes:
== VERDICT (worker spectruth9-feyyp) — FIXED in PR #10477, head 7d8d7b6a2b ==
Premise reproduced at trunk 2e5cb8da8d, in three places in `spec/005-StateMachines.md`:
- `:3833`, the `:join` key row: "Quorum uses the data-only `:after` + `:done-guard` idiom".
- `:3876`, the quorum note: "an `:after` (or `:always`) ... guarded by a `:done-guard` that reads the live join-state `:done` count".
- `:3998`, §Composition with hierarchy and `:after`: an `:always` checking `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent> <invoke-id> :done]`.
`:done-guard` appears only in code comments (`join.cljc:240`, `validation.cljc:354`), and the grammar has no such key.
Guard context re-measured at source. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` `callback-ctx` (364-372) builds `{:data :event :state :meta}`, plus `:rf.cofx` when the handler threaded it, plus `:tags` / `:all-state` on a parallel region. It includes no runtime-db.
A second finding changes the idiom's timing. A `:spawn-all` join child's completion folds into the join and short-circuits WITHOUT running a parent macrostep. See `registration.cljc` 1067-1105 ("the parent's macrostep is driven by the join's own resolution event, not by each child's arrival") and `join.cljc` 623-630. A non-resolving fold returns `:fx []` (`join.cljc` 570-574). So an `:always` on the `:spawn-all`-bearing state is NOT re-checked as each child arrives, and "fire the moment K of N complete" cannot be built from `:always`. The achievable quorum is decided at a step the parent actually takes, i.e. the `:after` deadline.
JVM probe against this branch, run from `implementation/machines`: 3 children, each with `:on-done (fn [{:keys [data]}] (update data :done-count (fnil inc 0)))`, a `:quorum?` guard of `>= 2`, and `:after {60000 [{:guard :quorum? :target :degraded} {:target :failed}]}`.
- 2 of 3 done, then a synthetic `:after` fires: `:degraded`.
- 1 of 3: `:failed`.
- 3 of 3: `:ready` via `:on-all-complete`.
- With an added `:always [{:guard :quorum? :target :early}]` on the `:spawn-all` state, the parent stayed `:hydrating` after 2 completions. It moved to `:early` only when an unrelated event made it step.
- The guard saw keys `#{:data :event :meta :rf.cofx :state}`, and `(get-in ctx [:rf.runtime/machines :spawned])` returned `nil`.
Changes, spec/005 only:
- The `:join` row and the quorum note now state the `:data`-count form.
- §Composition now carries a sample: per-child `:on-done` count, `:guards {:quorum? ...}`, and a guarded `:after` candidate-vector. The prose explains why the guard reads `:data` and not runtime-db, why the count is read at the deadline and not by `:always`, and that `:on-done` counts successes only and the count outlives the state.
- `:done-guard` count in the file is now 0, both line-wise and whitespace-flattened; the control `:on-all-complete` reads 13.
For the rf2-ahrss guide PR: its step 2 had not written the `:data`-count form when this landed; the machdocs-review branch was still at its step-1 commit. If the guide says "`:after` / `:always` plus a guard over the `:data` count", the `:always` half is wrong for the reason above, so mirror the `:after`-deadline form.
Gates, run on 7d8d7b6a2b:
- `check_doc_slugs.py`: exit 0.
- mkdocs `--strict`: exit 0.
- The 84 fast-PR static checks: all exit 0.
- Control: a planted `#value-shape-plantedfault` anchor at `005:3998` turned `check_doc_slugs.py` red, naming `spec\005-StateMachines.md:3998`. Restore verified: the file's blob hash equals the committed blob.
- CI: 88 of 88 green.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10477 (merged 2026-09-26, rebase).

Guard context re-measured at transition.cljc:364-372 as {:data :event :state :meta} plus :rf.cofx. A guard cannot see runtime-db, and :done-guard exists only in code comments.

In spec/005-StateMachines.md, the :join row, the quorum note and §Composition now use the :data-count form, with a sample: each child's :on-done counts into the parent's :data, and a guarded :after entry reads that count at the deadline.

The :always variant was refuted and left out. A join child's completion does not step the parent (registration.cljc:1067-1105), so an :always guard is not re-checked as each child finishes. The worker's JVM probe: 2 of 3 done then the deadline gave :degraded; 1 of 3 gave :failed; the :always guard fired only on an unrelated parent step. The docs/machines guide review (rf2-ahrss) is told on its bead to use :after, not :always.

Gates: check_doc_slugs and mkdocs --strict at exit 0 with red plants; CI 88/88.

title: Shipped SSR example's root view hashes to a constant, so hydration-mismatch detection never fires
description:
From GitHub issue #10500 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** P2 · **Surface:** `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc`

## Description
The render hash walks the tree as given and writes any fn head as the constant token `#fn[]`. A root view whose body is only another view therefore hashes to the same value for every app state, whether the root is `:app/root` → `[(rf/view :pages/articles)]` or the vector-form `:root-view`. The Ring handler emits no hash at all for that shape. The shipped SSR example has this shape, so its mismatch detection compares nothing.

## Evidence (reported by the review editors; verify)
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hash.cljc:256-272`: fn heads hash as one fixed token.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:120-135` and `lifecycle.clj:199-244`: an unresolved root carries no hash.
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:271-272`: the root returns `[(rf/view :pages/articles)]`.
- The same example waits for its data by hand (`await-page-load!`, `core.cljc:278-300, 368`), because `:rf.http/managed` fetches from `:rf/server-init` are not awaited.

## Acceptance
- The example's root view returns element content, so the render hash is meaningful. Its `:root-view` uses the fn form.
- A planted server/client divergence trips `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` (a test, or the example's own demo).
- Optionally, the example loads data through a route resource with `:blocking? true` instead of a hand-rolled wait.
- The SSR guide (`docs/ssr/`, being corrected in `claude/ssr-docs-review-b8ik2s`) points at the fixed example.

Discovered by: the SSR guide review (branch `claude/ssr-docs-review-b8ik2s`).
notes:
== FIXED in PR #10514 (worker/ssrfix-kz6ki) — 2026-09-26 17:10:32 AUSEST

Reproduced at trunk d260199251: the ssr example's `:app/root` returned `[(rf/view :pages/articles)]`, so `render-tree-hash` (which writes every callable head as the fixed token `#fn[]`) read `f1d63f7e` for two frames holding different articles, while their rendered HTML differed. resources_ssr had the same shape and the same constant.

Fix (the example's shape, not the hasher): both examples' `:app/root` now return the page's elements themselves; `:pages/articles` is gone. After the fix the same two states hash `81541bfd` / `9c7d4542`. The static index.html pages are re-baked to the root's dev annotations and match a fresh JVM render byte for byte (the ssr page's old `pages:articles:251:1` coordinate was already stale against its reg-view at line 254).

`:root-view` premise: neither example passes a Ring `:root-view`; each has its own `handle-request`, which already hashes the called root `((rf/view :app/root))`, the fn form. Nothing to change there.

Detection, end to end through the example's own `handle-request` and client `:render-tree-fn` idiom on an `:on-mismatch :hard-error` client: a faithful payload verifies clean; a payload with one article dropped throws `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` (server `89b40c6c`, client `7795db4b`). resources_ssr likewise (faithful clean; tampered entry server `472d78a9` vs client `c9dbe256`).

Regressions:

title: skills state-machines/cancellation.md: says destroy unregisters the machine handler; registration survives destroy
description:
skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md line ~84 says a destroyed machine's handler is unregistered ("before unregistering the handler"). That is wrong. Per spec/005 §Liveness is derived from runtime-db, a reg-machine registration is a DEFINITION that no actor teardown clears, and lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc step (8) unregisters only an entry with no machine definition. docs/api/re-frame.machines.md was corrected the same way by PR #10509 (rf2-yocd0), which also pins the behaviour with a JVM regression (singleton_destroy_registration_test.clj).
Fix: reword the sentence to say that destroy removes the actor's snapshot while a singleton's registration survives, and that rf/clear removes a registration for good. Re-verify the line at tip, and grep the rest of skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/ for the same claim.
Found by the rf2-yocd0 worker.
notes:
== WORKER PASS 2026-09-26 17:29:21 AUSEST (PR #10520, branch worker/speclinks-wogka, branch base e5931d99cd)

Premise HOLDS. skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md:84 read "... runs the standard exit cascade on the actor's current configuration before unregistering the handler." The claim is wrong for BOTH actor kinds, and most plainly so for the paragraph's own subject, a parent destroying a spawned child:
- A spawned actor has NO per-instance registrar entry (spec/005 §Liveness is derived from runtime-db; the spawn fx is a pure runtime-db write). There is nothing to unregister.
- A singleton's reg-machine entry is a DEFINITION. lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc step (8) calls unregister! only when spec-from-registry returns nil, i.e. it never clears a machine definition.
- rf/clear is the permanent removal.

Grep of the rest of references/state-machines/ found the same claim ONCE MORE: spawn.md:100, a code comment on a self-destructing singleton, ";; <- machine handler unregisters on :end". This is the :final? auto-destroy case.

Census: line-oriented, whitespace-flattened and comment-marker-stripped passes over all 8 files. Before the fix, "unregist" matched cancellation.md:84 and spawn.md:100 in all three modes; after, 0. Other hits were read and are correct or unrelated: xstate-translation.md:43 already says a registered singleton is re-born from :initial.

FIX in PR #10520:
- cancellation.md:84 now says destroy removes the actor's snapshot, ends the instance and never the definition, that a spawned actor has no per-instance handler, that a singleton's registration survives, and that only rf/clear removes a registration for good.
- spawn.md:100 comment now reads ";; <- snapshot removed on :end; the registration survives".

Behaviour pinned on the JVM by existing tests, run on the branch (exit 0, 10 tests / 55 assertions / 0 failures):
- implementation/machines/test/re_frame/singleton_destroy_registration_test.clj: explicit destroy, from PR #10509.
- machine_definition_survives_teardown_cljs_test.cljc: its final-auto-destroy-of-a-singleton-leaves-the-address-restartable test is exactly the spawn.md case.

title: Attribution guard passes an italic-wrapped '_Generated by [Claude Code](…session…)_' PR-body line
description:
The PR-body arm of scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh (step "PR guards (no tracker database, no AI attribution)" in test.yml's beads-pr-boundary job) PASSED PR #10515, whose body's last line was:

  _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01JrjwcM69LAsZe6qE2cyEBq)_

CLAUDE.md § Git Conventions refuses "a marker line with nothing but decoration in front and its own link at the end". This line is exactly that marker wrapped in markdown italics, and the TRAILING "_" after the link defeats the "link at the end" shape. So the one line CLAUDE.md most plainly means to refuse passes whenever it is italicised, which is how a platform commonly emits it. Found by the mayor's attribution grep on #10515 (the PR was superseded by #10516 without the line).

Fix: allow decoration on BOTH sides of the marker line (e.g. leading and trailing _ * spaces), keeping the rf2-uo5f rule that a line merely MENTIONING the trailers in prose passes. Add layer-10 tests in scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh (or wherever the detector's tests live) both ways:
- the italic-wrapped line above is refused;
- a prose sentence naming "Generated with Claude Code" passes;
- the bare session URL alone on its line stays refused.
Check whether the commit-msg hook shares the detector, and cover it too. Hot zone: .github/workflows/* only if the job wiring must change; the detector script and its tests are not hot.
notes:
== CLUSTER (mayor, 2026-09-26)
Dispatch together with rf2-jp9on, which Mike ruled on 2026-09-26: enforce the attribution check on the commit author/committer field. Both change scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-commit-attribution.sh, the CI script and the layer-10 tests.

== FIXED (worker attrguard-jp9on, 2026-09-26), PR #10527 — CAUSE DIFFERS FROM THE DESCRIPTION
Reproduced at trunk a00ac45e0f: the exact #10515 line passed check-commit-attribution.sh --pr-body at exit 0.
The trailing "_" is NOT the cause.
- The tail anchor extracts the URL's HOST and cuts at the path, so ")_" touching the link is harmless.
- Measured at that trunk, "_Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_" was already refused.
- The line passed because rule 3 opened only on "generated with" and the line says "Generated by". The un-italicised "Generated by [Claude Code](<session link>)" passed too.
- The description's "decoration on both sides" gap is real in a second shape: a closing mark written APART from the link ("... (link) _") becomes the last blank-separated word and hides the link.
Fix, in the shared detector scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-commit-attribution.sh:
- rule 3 opens on either verb, with the same no-letters head anchor;
- a new rf2_attribution_ends_on_tool_link sets aside trailing words carrying no letters before testing for the tool's link, mirroring the head.
- A trailing word with letters still makes the line prose.
The commit-msg hook sources the same detector, and tests drive it through a real git commit.
Tests, scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh layer 10r:
- the italic line and the separated-decoration line are refused by the PR-body arm, the commit-message detector and a real git commit (italic);
- permitted: "This change was not Generated with Claude Code, ...", "Generated by scripts/api-manifest ...", and "Generated by [Claude Code] was declined per CLAUDE.md. _";
- a mixed body quotes only the marker;
- the bare session URL alone on its line is still refused.
Each was shown red with its fix removed: dropping the verb reds 4, disabling the decoration loop reds 2, and a bare-substring rule 3 reds the permitted prose. Suite: 141/0 before, 170/0 after.
CLAUDE.md's existing rule-3 wording ("decoration in front and its own link at the end") was left as is, because the CLAUDE.md edit was limited to one sentence for rf2-jp9on.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10527, merged 2026-09-26T08:41:11Z at trunk 86e90d3130. The defect reproduced, but the cause differed from the bead's premise. The trailing "_" touching the link was harmless; the italic "_Generated with […](…)_" form was already refused. #10515's line passed because the rule matched only "generated WITH", and the line said "Generated BY". A second gap was real too: a closing mark written apart from the link ("… (link) _") hid the link. Both verbs are now matched, and trailing words with no letters in them are set aside, so decoration on either side no longer hides a marker line. Prose that merely names the marker still passes. The commit-msg hook shares the detector, and a test drives it through a real git commit. Every new test was shown red with its fix removed.
Noted, not filed (minutiae): CLAUDE.md's description of the marker rule ("decoration in front and its own link at the end") now slightly understates what is refused.
