title: Examples review: realworld_resources flagship (7 findings: a logged-out visit to the following feed fails the whole home plan and the page then lies; README claims a Form-3 reaction the code does not have; a skill leaf says a favourite stales global tags where the example's lesson is that they are viewer-scoped)
description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-fn0kx (report realworld-resources.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: RealWorld (Conduit) on Resources — `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources`

Reviewer persona: senior reviewer for behavioural correctness under the Resources model — every user flow traced route → plan → ensure → request → entry → subs → view, and every write event → mutation → consequences → settle, with each option/consequence key checked against `implementation/resources/src`, `implementation/http/src`, `spec/016-Resources.md` and `spec/API.md`.

## THE DELIVERABLE

A logged-out visit to `/?feed=following` — reload, bookmark, expired token — failed the whole home plan, and the page then LIED about it: articles and tags were never ensured either, so their `:idle` projection rendered as "No articles are here… yet." plus a permanent "Loading tags…". A partial failure presenting as success is worse than an error, which is why the lying half was treated as part of the defect rather than as cosmetics.

The worker traced it end to end at trunk rather than taking the report's word: scope resolves at PLAN time inside `materialize-occurrences`, a nil `{:from-db :realworld/session}` throws fail-closed, and the plan boundary commits a failed activation with **no ensures at all**. `home-page` now reads `:rf.route/error` and renders a new `home-plan-error` view.

**The gate on that render is load-bearing and the worker argued it rather than asserting it**: it fires only when `:rf.error/id` is `:rf.error/resource-route-plan`, because a *blocking read* failure also sets `:error` — and there the plan did form, so `article-list` reports it better. Verified at trunk after merge: `home-plan-error` present (5 sites), the error-id gate present (1).

Findings 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 also landed. Finding 3 lives in `skills/` — out of fence, verified still live and still stale, untouched.

## CORRECTIONS TO THE MAYOR AND THE REPORT — FOUR

1. **Finding 1's "decide A or B" was NOT a live choice, and the worker proved it rather than guessing.** Option (B)'s `:auth/clear-session` half is **already the case at trunk** — `navigate.cljc:331-334` takes a destination's `:query` literally, and the EP-0037 R5 comment records that the router deliberately stopped folding ambient query state into a fresh destination. (B) also **cannot reach the cold-bookmark case at all**: with no token, `:auth/initialise` routes through the `:has-token?` guard into the no-op `{:target :idle}` branch, so neither handler ever runs. And the one remaining half would contradict `:abandon-restore`'s documented "stay put" design. **(A) is the floor, not the alternative.** A brief that says "this is Mike's call" is satisfied by demonstrating the call does not exist — that is better than either choosing or holding.
2. **Finding 7 had a THIRD site the report missed** — `core.cljs:384` attributed the base-path strategy to a non-existent orchestrator's mount point. Fixed, without touching the base-path design, which remains the cross-fence decision below.
3. **The brief's "11 tracked test files" reads 13** at trunk.
4. **THE HARNESS AND THE CAPTURED EXIT CODE DISAGREED, LIVE, ON THE SABOTAGE SWEEP.** The harness reported "exit code 0" while the worker's captured exit file read **1**. Believing the harness would have inverted the plant's conclusion — a red sabotage read as green, i.e. "the gate cannot see my fault", which is the reassuring direction. This is the quality-gates block's capture rule earning its keep in the one place where the two numbers can differ and only one is right.

**And one near-miss it reported rather than buried**: it re-checked the report's finding-7 instrument at the report's stated scope, found it CORRECT (1 hit), and did not write it up as a defect — having nearly done so after running a wider pattern of its own. title: api(observability): delete re-frame.emit, the re-frame.trace listener aliases and the unconsumed :trace.tooling listener hooks
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Three dead spellings of the listener registries survive beside the one app-facing verb `rf/register-listener!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2135-2168`) and the home namespaces:

1. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/emit.cljc` (77 lines): six `def` re-exports of `re-frame.event-emit` / `re-frame.error-emit`. Its docstring (:5) calls itself "the single public registration facade", contradicting `core.cljc:2224-2238` (the registries are reached through `register-listener!`'s `:events` / `:errors` streams and the home namespaces). No manifest row (`grep '"re-frame.emit"' spec/api-manifest.edn` → 0), no `docs/api` page. Consumers: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:13,388`; `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:43,204`; one test, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_r1_purge_test.clj:31,80,98,132,158,185`.
2. `re-frame.trace/register-listener!`, `unregister-listener!`, `clear-listeners!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:951-953`): `def` aliases of `re-frame.trace.tooling/*` (`trace/tooling.cljc:81,88,95`). rf2-ic1sv pick c called them "the canonical app-facing names" (`trace.cljc:21-26`, `:943-949`); the facade `:trace` arm superseded that, and `spec/API.md:596-606` and the manifest (0 `"re-frame.trace"` rows) know only the facade. Non-test consumers: 0 (`core.cljc:2164,2178` call the alias for the `:trace` arm; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:27` and `drop_in.cljc:73` mention it in prose). Test consumers: 97 files (`git grep -lE "(rf\.trace|re-frame\.trace)/(register-listener!|unregister-listener!|clear-listeners!)" -- 'implementation/*test*' 'tools/*test*' 'testbeds/*' 'skills/*'`), of which 49 register/unregister and the rest call `clear-listeners!` in fixtures.
3. Late-bind hooks `:trace.tooling/register-listener!` / `:unregister-listener!` (`trace/tooling.cljc:1300-1301`; directory entries `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:1114-1121`). The directory entry itself says the hook is "retained for the directory contract" and that every live consumer calls `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` directly; the one real consumer moved to `:error-emit/register-error-listener!` under rf2-87f7fb (`directory.cljc:907-914`). `git grep -n "get-fn :trace.tooling/\(un\)\?register-listener!"` → 0.

Plus `routing.cljc:195-204`: an idempotent purge, on every façade load, of the `:rf.route/on-match-error-trap` listener id retired with EP-0037 R1 — a shim for an HMR session spanning a change that landed months ago; no shipped code registers that id.

## Evidence

Measured at HEAD as above. Also: `trace.cljc:39-49` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally on both platforms, so the aliases buy no elision the facade lacks (the `trace.cljc:28-34` DCE note is about the buffer/configure surface at `:955-957`, which stays and belongs to `@trace-epoch.1`). `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:338-347` describes the aliases as "thin late-bind shells whose `:trace.tooling/*` lookups resolve to nil" — stale; they are `def`s, and the `trace-events` sentinel reads 0 in the counter bundle because Closure drops the unreachable buffer fns, not because the namespace is absent from the graph.

## Target API

One home per verb, nothing else names a registry:

- `rf/register-listener!` / `rf/unregister-listener!` — the only app-facing spelling (unchanged).
- `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` / `clear-listeners!` — the `:trace` registry's home: core's `:trace` arm, SSR's own listener (`ssr.cljc:404`), the test-support bracket (`test_support.cljc:1221`), fixture clears (`test_support.cljc:552`).
- `re-frame.error-emit/*` / `re-frame.event-emit/*` — the always-on registries' homes: framework-internal consumers and the late-bind hooks (`frame.cljc:2810,3909`).

```clojure
;; core.cljc:2164 / :2178 — before
:trace (rf.trace/register-listener! id f)
;; after (add [re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace.tooling] to core's requires;
;; trace.cljc:49 already requires it on both platforms, so reachability is unchanged)
:trace (rf.trace.tooling/register-listener! id f)

;; ssr.cljc:388 — before
(rf-emit/register-error-listener! ::error-projection error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener)
;; after
(rf.error-emit/register-error-listener! ::error-projection error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener)
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer; codex: "Remove proven unused aliases independently; internal fan-out and late binding need not become public synonyms." Grok's retirement bead lists all three. Independent of the observability.6 ruling.

## Deletion list

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/emit.cljc` — whole file.
- `trace.cljc:943-953` (section comment + three defs); trim the pick-c paragraphs at `:21-26` and the require comment `:41-48` to what remains true (tooling is required for the buffer/configure defs at `:955-957`, which `@trace-epoch.1` owns — do not touch `:955-957` here; sequence with that bead since both edit `:940-957`).
- `trace/tooling.cljc:1291-1301` (comment + two `set-fn!`), `:57` docstring bullet.
- `directory.cljc:1114-1121` (two entries) — `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj` pins both directions (`every-published-key-has-a-directory-entry`, `every-directory-entry-is-actually-published`), so entry and publication go together.
- `routing.cljc:43` (require) and `:204`; the comment `:195-201` says "exactly these three" → two (the two `clear-event` purges at `:202-203` are routing's and stay).
- `check-bundle-isolation.cjs:338-347` comment — rewritten to the measured mechanism (aliases gone; tooling reachable via `re-frame.trace`; sentinel held by DCE of unreachable fns).

## Consumers to migrate

- `core.cljc:2164,2178` → `rf.trace.tooling/*` (+ require).
- `ssr.cljc:13,388` → `re-frame.error-emit`.
- `routing_r1_purge_test.clj`: `::user-probe` / `::channel-probe` registrations (:98,132,158,185) → `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!` / `unregister-error-listener!`; the `retired-trap` arm (:10, :51, :80, the three `error-listener-registered? retired-trap` assertions, the deftest title "three") deleted; acceptance criterion 2 (`::channel-probe`) kept.
- 97 test files: `rf.trace/clear-listeners!` → `rf.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!` in fixtures; `rf.trace/register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` → `rf/register-listener! :trace` / `rf/unregister-listener! :trace` where the file already requires `re-frame.core`, else `rf.trace.tooling/*`; require aliases per `spec/Conventions.md`'s canonical `rf.*` dialect. `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machines/test_support.cljc:115-140` is a shared helper — migrate it once. Mechanical; `git grep` the two regexes above until both read 0.
- `test_support.cljc:1127` comment (names the tooling verb — still right; touch only if the sentence reads wrong).
- Prose: `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:331` (`re-frame.trace/register-listener!` → `rf/register-listener! :trace`); `install.cljs:27` and `drop_in.cljc:73` comments.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- HOT-ZONE `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2222-2223` — the hook-rename table rows `:trace.tooling/register-trace-cb! → :trace.tooling/register-listener!` / `remove-trace-cb! → unregister-listener!` name a target hook that no longer exists → "removed (no consumer; call `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` directly, or `rf/register-listener! :trace`)". Same table in `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md:135-136`.
- `spec/API.md:606` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:657-660` already name `re-frame.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!` — no change.
- Manifest: no rowed var changes; run `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` (no regeneration expected).
- Examples: 0 consumers. Conformance: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj:236-238` uses the alias — part of the test migration; `spec/conformance/fixtures` name no listener verb.
- Tests to add: none beyond the migrated ones; `late_bind_drift_test` is the hook-roster gate.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

One hot-zone file (migration README, one row) — serialise with observability.5's one-line edit there. Sequence with `@trace-epoch.1` on `trace.cljc:940-957` (whichever lands second rebases a ten-line region). Independent of observability.1/2/4 and of the ruling.

## Risks

Breadth, not depth: ~97 test files, all mechanical. The `core.cljc` require of `re-frame.trace.tooling` looks like the thing the bundle-isolation comment warns against — it is not (trace already requires it); the gate proves it. A downstream consumer using `re-frame.emit` or `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` gets a compile-time unresolved-var error naming the old symbol — pre-alpha, no shim; the migration README's M-26 table already routes v1 names to the facade.

title: Present-tense: settle the R8 comment contradictions the surface sweeps report
description:
Collector for the present-tense campaign (epic rf2-tv5ac).

Under ruling R8, a surface sweep that finds two comments contradicting each other about behaviour REPORTS the contradiction and does not settle it: the sweep changes prose, not behaviour, and choosing a side means reading the code. This bead gathers those reports in one place, so one worker can settle them all against the code at the end of the campaign, rather than each sweep guessing.

The mayor appends each report to this bead's NOTES as `R8 REPORT (<source bead>, <PR>)`. The list is the notes, not this description.

## What settling means

For each report:
1. Read the code the two comments describe.
2. Decide which is true, and make the false one agree, in the present tense.
3. If the code itself looks wrong, meaning neither comment describes intended behaviour, STOP on that item and report it as a possible defect. Do not change behaviour under this bead.

## Dispatch

Dispatch this once the campaign's sweeps are done, or earlier if the list grows past about eight entries.
- Fence: exactly the files named in the reports, each only for the contradicting comment.
- Each file must be free of any live sweep at dispatch.

## Gates

- For each changed file, the artefact's JVM suite and clj-kondo run plainly, with before and after counts equal.
- `scripts/present_tense.py verify` against the merge base, with the three line-ending counts.
- CI for the CLJS lanes.

title: Incomplete: Story fidelity upgrades retain pins from composed fragments
description:
Merged-PR audit of #9803 at f626f7709255815395d9880c61bd8d87c889fc50. The closed rf2-mw9th claim that the completed upgrade carries no :sub-overrides is incomplete: when the source has its own pin AND composes a pinning fragment, upgrade-snippet strips the direct pin but re-emits :compose unchanged, so the fragment pin survives. The dialog explicitly promises no pins and the spec says the completed upgrade has no :sub-overrides rung.

Reproduced with the real landed upgrade-snippet and variant-plan (JVM, explicit raw lookup maps): source :story.audit/pinned = {:sub-overrides {[:audit/own] "own pin"} :compose [:fragment.audit/pin] :args {:heading "context"}}; fragment = {:sub-overrides {[:audit/email] "PINNED"}}. Read the generated form, complete :setup with [[:dispatch [:audit/set-email "REAL"]]], and compile the child. It contains :compose [:fragment.audit/pin], yields :fidelity #{:sub-overrides :real-setup}, and retains {[:audit/email] "PINNED"} under [:world :render :sub-overrides]. Removing :compose in a diagnostic control yields #{:real-setup} and {}. The shipped 17 tests/99 assertions still pass. Artifact: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-merged-pr-audit-a-pr9803-probe-2.clj and matching .log/.exit, exit 0, worker root printed. Probe 1 with ONLY a composed pin did not reproduce because :compose is child-only; do not use that case as evidence. The generator is unchanged through fetched main at audit time.

Cause: view_state.cljc upgrade-snippet only finds direct :sub-overrides on the raw :extends chain. When any layer pins, own retains :compose. The compiler correctly applies the copied child composition. No compiler merge change or public deletion API is needed.

Correction: make this scaffold account for pinning composed fragments, or emit an explicit author completion recipe that removes those pin sources before calling the result an upgrade. Preserve useful non-pin context and keep the boundary local to authoring. Add a regression that compiles the COMPLETED generated artifact for this mixed direct/composed-pin shape, including a pin-free control. The existing direct/inherited-pin cases must stay green. Notes on the closed source mention an untested composition residual; that does not separately track the required correction. No exact open finding existed in the 13-item open inventory.
acceptance_criteria: Completed generated upgrade of a source with direct and composed pins compiles without the sub-overrides rung, or explicitly requires removal of the remaining pin sources before claiming completion; preserve relevant context, retain direct/inherited regressions, add a completed-artifact composition regression.

title: hicasso: the fused reader array costs 91-92 B/read — the largest term this page has attributed to a container rather than a value
description:
MEASURED, NOT SPECULATED. rf2-zei9w's ablation attributes 91 B/read (Reagent segment) / 92 (UIx) to the cell's fused reader array — the container itself, not the membership it holds. Per-round bands are disjoint across all six rounds, the R=0 shell does not move, and donors moved 0.05/0.19 B/read, so this is a per-KEY term and the attribution is solid. Published in docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md (2026-08-04 section), PR #7452.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. rf2-dabt3's fusion banked -60 B/read in both segments — real, and it won — but that is only ~40% of the ~151 B/read the old reverse edge cost, because the replacement array is ~2x what ONE PersistentHashSet membership costs (+46/+47 B/read, PR #7418 run D). The design predicted the surviving array would be cheap residue; it is not. It is now the largest single term this page has attributed to a CONTAINER rather than to a value.

THE OBVIOUS SHAPE, and it is only a sketch. At the fan-out this table actually sees, the overwhelmingly common case is ONE reader per key. A scalar slot that holds the single reader directly and promotes to an array on the SECOND reader would retain a pointer instead of a JSArray-plus-backing-store for that case. arm1/runtime.cljs's own section header already argues a JS array beats a persistent set here; this asks the next question down, which is whether a container is needed at all in the common case.

THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first, for three reasons:
• release-cell!'s .indexOf, arm-cell-reaper!'s alength and stats's alength all read .-readers directly, and cell-readers/stats are witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against — a polymorphic slot touches all of them.
• It is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm, and the stance is explicit that not every measured term needs actioning.
• The bill it would attack is +331 B/read against Reagent; 91 of that is this term. Worth knowing the size before deciding it is worth the branch in a hot path.

Precondition if it is ever taken: a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder 6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and the same ablation discipline rf2-zei9w used — attribute, do not infer.

write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside tools/xray top-level test files. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
tools/xray top-level test files to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in tools/xray top-level test files; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If tools/xray top-level test files plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside tools/xray top-level test files that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: Contract text: FormAction GET arm, CP-5 singleton row, duplicate spec/005 headings, http stub docstrings, Conventions flows-nil example
description:
Five places where contract text contradicts the spec or the code. The re-frame2 skill review (rf2-osu7l, PR #11163) found them; each was checked at trunk 728a17f52b. All are text fixes: no behaviour changes, and no decision is needed.

1. spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:219: the GET arm dispatches `[:page/load route]`. Spec 011 (spec/011-SSR.md:1330-1340) feeds a URL through `[:rf.route/handle-url-change uri]`. The skill's form-action leaf now uses that. The reviewer also cited :212 and :511 for the same pattern; re-derive every site at tip.

2. spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md:217: the creation-modes row reads "singleton via `reg-event`". A singleton machine is registered with `reg-machine`.

3. spec/005-StateMachines.md:2991 and :3806: two headings read "### Spec-spec keys". They sit under the `:spawn` and `:spawn-all` maps (the text after each reads "The map under `:spawn` accepts..." and "The map under `:spawn-all` accepts..."), beside a separate "### Spawn-spec keys" at :2817. That makes duplicate anchors. Give each heading an accurate, unique name, and move every inbound `#spec-spec-keys` / `#spec-spec-keys-1` link in the same commit (search spec/, docs/, skills/, tools/ and implementation/).

4. implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:547 and :675: the docstrings give `stubs` as `{[method url] {:reply <:ok|:failure>}}`. The code takes a map under `:reply`, `{:ok v}` or `{:failure m}` (see the comment at :498, `{:reply {:ok v :meta {...}}}`). Correct both docstrings to the shape the code reads.

5. spec/Conventions.md:866 gives "flows exclude `nil` output segments" as an example of a spec narrowing the shared segment domain as a stated policy. Spec 013 records no such narrowing, and the flows registry accepts nil: implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:354-357 checks `:output-path` against the shared domain, nil included, and its error text says so. The minimal fix is the Conventions example: replace it with a narrowing a spec actually records, or drop it. If you find that Spec 013 does record the narrowing, the code is what is wrong; then stop and report rather than adding a registration check. If the example goes, check the flows wording in skills/re-frame2/ (its review states nil-free output paths as policy) and keep it as advice.

title: Dev-only hot-reload sweep: at the end of a reload cycle, a namespace loses registrations it did not make again (ruled (e) under rf2-bmrh9)
description:
Filed 2026-10-13 23:11:15 AUSEST at HEAD 2579b6b410. This is part (e) of Mike's ruling on rf2-bmrh9 (read that bead's `== RULING ==` note first). It is BLOCKED on rf2-bmrh9, which makes the default frame resolve the store live.

## Problem

Hot reload cannot remove a registration. The source store is keyed kind → id → provenance-namespace → descriptor (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_store.cljc:82-90`). A namespace that re-registers an id replaces its own leaf, but when a namespace STOPS registering an id (the handler moved to another namespace, was renamed, or was deleted), its old leaf stays, because core has no notion of a reload cycle ending.

Consequences:
- After rf2-bmrh9, a moved handler leaves two provenances for one id, so using it raises `:rf.error/ambiguous-registration` until someone runs `(rf/clear kind id)` or reloads the page.
- A deleted handler stays callable.

## Ruling

Add a dev-only reload sweep. At the end of a hot-reload cycle, every namespace that registered anything during the cycle loses each older registration it did not make again.

## Fix direction

- **Boundary.** The documented setup re-calls `init!` from a `^:dev/after-load` hook (see the `init!` docstring, core.cljc about :3050-3063). Treat that re-call as the end of a reload cycle, or provide an equivalent explicit dev entry if that reads better, and document it. The first boot has no previous cycle, so it sweeps nothing.
- **Tracking.** Record which `[kind id]` leaves each namespace wrote since the last boundary.
- **Sweep.** At the boundary, for each namespace that wrote anything in the cycle, forget its leaves that it did NOT write in the cycle. Use the existing per-id forget path (`registrar/unregister!` → `source-store/forget-id!`, registrar.cljc about :768-779), narrowed to the one provenance leaf. Then mark the live projection dirty so frames re-resolve.
- **Dev only.** The sweep must not exist or run in production builds (gate it on `rf.interop/debug-enabled?`, or keep it in a dev-only path). The JVM has no after-load boundary, so it is out of scope there.
- **Known edge, accepted by the ruling.** A namespace whose LAST registration moved out registers nothing during the cycle, so the sweep cannot tell it was reloaded, and its stale leaf surfaces as rf2-bmrh9's one-id ambiguity error. Document that, and the `rf/clear` remedy, in the hot-reload docs.
- **Spec.** Add a short "Hot reload" paragraph to 002 §Image resolution and composition (next to "Registrations made after a frame exists") and 001 §Re-registration. Both are hot zones (002 especially), so sequence this after rf2-bmrh9.

## Verification (CLJS; needs `npm run test:cljs`, and the shadow-cljs build lane granted by the coordinator)

Simulate cycles by calling the boundary directly:
- **Move:** ns A registers `:x/ev`, then a cycle where A re-registers nothing for `:x/ev` but registers something else, and B registers `:x/ev`. After the boundary, `:x/ev` runs B's code with no ambiguity error. Red before the fix (ambiguity), green after.
- **Delete:** A registers `:x/gone`, then a cycle where A registers other ids but not `:x/gone`. After the boundary, dispatching `:x/gone` reports no-such-handler.
- **Untouched namespace:** a namespace that registered nothing in the cycle keeps all its leaves.
- **Explicit images:** a frame with explicit `:images` is unaffected except through normal reprojection.
- **Production:** the sweep is absent from release builds, for example via a check in the advanced-production lane or `debug-enabled?` gating.
notes:
GUIDANCE FROM rf2-bmrh9's WORKER (mayor relaying, PR #11235): frames made without `:images` resolve through `rf.live-frame/live-view`, once per event cascade. Their frame record carries `:live-store? true`, which `make-frame` sets internally (it is not a user option). The registration hook `reproject-on-registration-change!` now receives `{:kind :id :was}`, and it invalidates first-time `:sub` registrations for the frames in `live-store-frame-ids`. These frames no longer seal or cache a generation, so reprojection concerns only frames with explicit `:images`. The reload sweep this bead implements therefore works on the store itself, and live frames see its result on their next cascade with no reprojection step.
PITFALL FROM rf2-bmrh9's WORKER (mayor relaying, PR #11235): a frame made without `:images` is not "image-loaded", so `rf.live-frame/live-frame` returns nil for it. Code that treats "image-loaded" as "the frame exists" will re-make such a frame, and the re-make invalidates every cached sub on it. Xray's `xray-frame-seated?` does exactly that; it is safe in production only because Xray always seats `:rf/xray` with its own image. Ask whether a frame EXISTS by a frame-existence query, never by `live-frame`.

title: Unit-test pruning: ssr
description:
Apply Mike's pruning prompt to implementation/ssr/test recursively in an isolated worker worktree. This is a distinct cluster in rf2-0wcq5. Push a test-only draft PR, babysit all checks until green, then mark ready; do not merge. Report no-op with evidence instead of manufacturing changes.

Simplify the unit tests under implementation/ssr/test. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside implementation/ssr/test. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
implementation/ssr/test to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in implementation/ssr/test; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If implementation/ssr/test plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside implementation/ssr/test that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: A queued resource GC check bypasses the final-release warm window
description:
Audit of PR #11261, merge 089c98b3ddd6673528fb8a756026c34d3c84f179, discovered from rf2-yna4r.

The final-release re-arm does not invalidate a GC re-check that the old timer already queued. In implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/timers.cljc, schedule-kind!'s fire claims and removes its timer slot before asynchronously dispatching the advisory re-check (around lines 317-331). release-owner-from-identities now arms a fresh GC timer (events.cljc around 2057-2068), but gc-fired-handler checks only the live owner/in-flight facts. An older queued check delivered after that release sees an idle, owner-free entry, deletes it immediately, and cancels the fresh timer. This violates the full warm window this PR adds for ordinary route bounces/remounts.

Confirmed locally on the current merged production code using this PR's virtual host-clock fixture and the real production timer thunk, with router delivery queued rather than forced synchronous:
1. Settle an owned entry at t=0 with gc-after-ms=1000.
2. Queue its final owner release at t=900; before draining, let the original GC timer fire at t=1000. FIFO is [release-owner, gc-fired].
3. Deliver release-owner: the entry remains and one fresh timer is armed for t=2000.
4. Deliver the older queued gc-fired: the entry disappears at t=1000.

The JVM probe exited 0 and printed:
:fifo-events [:rf.resource/release-owner :rf.resource.internal/gc-fired]
:after-final-release true :new-gc-timer-count 1
:after-older-queued-gc false :clock 1000 :new-window-end 2000

Keep an obsolete queued GC check from collecting an entry whose final release established a newer window, using the existing timer ownership/lifecycle mechanism where practical. No new public knob or general scheduling framework is needed. Preserve stale/poll sibling timers, ownerless prefetch collection, :never, server gating and normal collection after the current window.

Acceptance: a regression with the FIFO above keeps the entry through t=1999 and collects at the current t=2000 check. Exercise queued delivery, because the new timing tests force the re-check dispatch synchronous and cannot expose this interleaving.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY 2026-10-15 23:55 AUSEST (PR #11299, branch worker/resource-gc-queued; head 3b3ea4b20a)

Reproduced at tip e24514bce0, which already carries the #11280 rule that only an in-flight skip re-arms. The test uses a virtual host clock, the real timer thunk and the real router, with next-tick captured so delivery is queued. The owned entry settles at t=0 with gc-after-ms 1000, the final release is queued at t=900 and the settle timer fires at t=1000. The FIFO is [:rf.resource/release-owner :rf.resource.internal/gc-fired]. On trunk, the entry was gone after the t=1000 drain.

Fix:
- timers.cljc: schedule! records whether the entry had an active owner when a GC timer arms. It reads this from the frame's runtime-db after the arming event's commit. The fire stamps :armed-while-owned? true onto the gc-fired payload.
- events.cljc: gc-fired-handler skips a stamped check whose entry is owner-free, with reason :superseded, and arms nothing. The last owner's release has already armed the window that collects the entry.
- The skip order is no-entry, has-owner, superseded, in-flight, then collect. The decision is a pure function of the payload and runtime-db, so replay stays sound.
- Nothing else changes. No knob and no new durable entry field. Stale and poll timers are unstamped, ownerless prefetch is armed unowned, and :never and server frames arm nothing. An owned skip still arms nothing and an in-flight skip still re-arms. A direct gc-fired dispatch without the stamp behaves as before.

Evidence (resources JVM lane):
- New namespace resources_gc_queued_check_cljs_test: 2 tests, 6 assertions.
- Scoped red on trunk source: exit 1, 2 failures. The entry was collected at t=1000.
- Scoped green with the fix: exit 0. The entry is kept through t=1999 and collected at t=2000.
- Full lane: 537/1531 at baseline, 539/1537 on the branch, exit 0. The +2/+6 matched the prediction.
- clj-kondo exit 0, and a planted fault went red. The ratchet scripts all exit 0.
- CLJS is covered by CI test:cljs. The change is common .cljc code, in neither reader branch.

Spec 016 is unchanged, because no sentence in it describes the window wrongly.

Residual, not fixed:
1. A timer armed while the entry was owner-free can still collect early. This needs its check queued behind both an owner attach that re-arms nothing (adopt-owner) and the final release. A fresh-skip attach does re-arm, while owned, and so is covered.
2. A sibling race of the same shape exists with a settle in place of the release. An ownerless entry's timer fires while a refetch is in flight. Its check is queued behind the success reply, the settle re-arms, and the check then collects at once. This is outside this bead's scope.
Merged-PR audit #11299: follow-up rf2-p5prg — A queued GC check armed unowned can collect a newly released resource immediately. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
close_reason: Merged in PR #11299. When a GC timer arms, schedule! records whether the entry had an active owner, and the gc-fired payload carries :armed-while-owned? true. A flagged check that finds the entry owner-free skips as :superseded and arms nothing, because the final release already armed the newer window. The decision reads only the payload and runtime-db, so replay is deterministic. Reproduced on tip with held router drains (FIFO [release-owner, gc-fired]): the entry was collected at t=1000 on trunk; it is kept through t=1999 and collected at t=2000 with the fix. Resources lane 537/1531 -> 539/1537. The two residual interleavings are filed as rf2-mxjjn. Merge check: rollup 88 (58 pass, 30 skip, 0 bad), 0 live runs, 0 workflow drift.

title: Test support: restore-registrar! does not roll back the source store that frames without :images read
description:
The public test bracket `snapshot-registrar` / `restore-registrar!` no longer rolls back what a frame made without `:images` actually runs. Since the live-default ruling (rf2-bmrh9), such a frame resolves registrations through the SOURCE STORE. The public pair captures and restores only the registrar's latest-writer map. So registrations made inside a hand-rolled bracket probably survive the restore and stay runnable. This was traced in source and has not been run.

## Evidence (trunk 89517e8f54)

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:~188-210`:
  - `snapshot-registrar` returns `@rf.registrar/kind->id->metadata`, and `restore-registrar!` resets only that atom.
  - The docstring promises: "Any registrations made since the snapshot are dropped".
- The internal fixture restores the store as well, through the PRIVATE `restore-source-store!` (`test_support.cljc:~177-186`). It resets `rf.source-store/kind->id->ns->descriptor`, so `make-reset-runtime-fixture` is fine. Only the public hand-rolled bracket is exposed.
- A frame without `:images` resolves through `live-view`, which reads only the source store (`live_frame.cljc:~338-373`).
- The public pair is still documented as dropping registrations:
  - `spec/API.md:834`: "dropping registrations made since";
  - `spec/008-Testing.md:279-280` teaches the pair as rungs L1 and L2;
  - `spec/008-Testing.md:1027`.

## Change

Make the public pair capture and restore both tables. The simplest route is for `snapshot-registrar` to return both values and `restore-registrar!` to reset both, reusing `restore-source-store!`. Keep the docstrings and Spec 008 / API.md wording true.

## Related

The decision dossier `one-registry-top-level-reg.md` proposes collapsing the registrar into one registration table. That would fix this by construction, and its acceptance case reads: "a frame made without `:images` after `restore-registrar!` cannot run a registration made inside the bracket". If that bead lands first, close this one against it. Otherwise this is the small standalone fix.

`spec/API.md` is a HOT ZONE, together with its manifest sidecars, if its row wording changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a test that is red at base and green after the change. It takes `snapshot-registrar`, registers an event inside the bracket, calls `restore-registrar!`, then dispatches that event on a frame made without `:images`. The handler must not run.
2. `make-reset-runtime-fixture` keeps its current behaviour, and its suite stays green.
3. The docstrings, `spec/008-Testing.md` and the `spec/API.md` row describe what the pair actually restores.
close_reason: Folded into rf2-uwsy0 (one registration table). That bead's acceptance criterion 1 is this bead's failing-first test verbatim: snapshot, register inside the bracket, `restore-registrar!`, dispatch on a `make-frame` frame without `:images`, and the handler does not run. Its criterion 7 makes Spec 008 and `spec/API.md` describe what `restore-registrar!` restores. Collapsing the registrar to one table fixes the rollback by construction, so a separate two-table patch here would be thrown away.

title: Machines: a fixed-actor-id single :spawn reuses one work id across attempts; mint one per attempt as :spawn-all does
description:
A single `:spawn` child with an explicit `:fixed-actor-id` gets the same reply work id on every attempt. A `:spawn-all` child with a fixed id gets a distinct work id per attempt. The two spawn kinds therefore disagree about work identity, and the docstring promising a fresh work id per re-spawn is untrue for fixed-id single spawns. This was read in source and has not been run.

## Evidence (trunk 89517e8f54)

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/reply.cljc:93-110`. The machine work-id head is `[:rf.work/machine actor-id work-bearing-path generation]`.
  - For a generated `<type>#<n>` actor, the generation is `n`, "so a re-spawn under the same declaring path lands on a fresh work id (one ATTEMPT, one `:rf.reply/work-id`, per EP-0007)".
  - For an explicit `:fixed-actor-id` with no `#n` suffix, the generation is `1` for an ordinary `:spawn`. A `:spawn-all` child instead reuses that slot for its join-attempt token, so its fixed-id attempts stay distinct (Spec 005 ~L4051).
- The single-spawn path builds its work id from the actor-id suffix through the 2-arity (`reply.cljc:~156-158`; `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:~438-443`).
- Example: two attempts of `{:spawn {:machine-id :uploader :fixed-actor-id :uploader}}` at `[:loading]` both report `[:rf.work/machine :uploader [:loading] 1]`. The child still carries a `:rf/invoke-attempt` that tells the attempts apart.

Stale-completion suppression has other fences, so this is a correlation and identity defect, not a known correctness failure. But EP-0007's "one attempt, one work id" is what Xray and the pair MCP use to correlate replies and traces.

## Change

For a fixed-id single `:spawn`, use the spawn's attempt as the work-id generation, as `:spawn-all` already does with its join-attempt token. Correct the `reply.cljc` docstring to match.

## Related

The decision dossier `machine-fences-to-entry-stamp.md` proposes one region-qualified entry stamp. That stamp would become the work-id generation for timers, spawns and joins, which fixes this as a side effect. If that bead is filed and lands first, close this bead against it. Otherwise this is the small, standalone fix.

`spec/005-StateMachines.md` is a HOT ZONE if the spec text needs adjusting near L4051.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A test respawns a fixed-id single `:spawn` at the same path and asserts that the two attempts' replies carry different `:rf.reply/work-id`s. It is red at base and green after the change.
2. The fixed-id `:spawn-all` and generated-id single `:spawn` work-id tests stay green.
3. The `reply.cljc` docstring states one rule that holds for both spawn kinds.

title: Region-qualify the :rf/spawned mirror and delete the region spawn-path refusal
description:
## Ruling

Key the parent's `[:data :rf/spawned …]` mirror by the region-qualified invoke-id `[<region> & <in-region-path>]` inside a `:type :parallel` machine, the same key the runtime registry slot `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent-id> <invoke-id>]` and the child's `:rf/invoke-id` already use. Then delete the registration refusal that forbids two regions from declaring a `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` at the same in-region path. Regions become true scopes: two regions may both have a spawning `:loading` state. A region action that reads its own mirror names its region, `(get-in data [:rf/spawned [:upload :loading]])`. Non-parallel machines are unchanged, because their invoke-id has no region head.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both reviews chose this option (B) as the thing to do now. The wider "one region-qualified entry stamp for `:after`, `:spawn` and `:spawn-all`" (option C) is NOT ruled. The original recommendation wanted it as a second bead after this one. Codex wanted it deferred until a concrete need appears. It stays open for Mike in the dossier `machine-fences-to-entry-stamp.md`. This bead stands alone and is a strict prefix of C, so it does not wait on that call.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. The mirror alone drops the region. The pure reducer writes `(assoc-in snap [:data :rf/spawned invoke-id] …)` with the in-region invoke-id (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:595-632`, called at `:2662` for a single spawn and `:2765` for a join). `spawned-mirror-path` strips a region head for every install, reject-clear and teardown (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/paths.cljc:93-114`). Meanwhile the attempt key is already region-qualified, `(if region (into [region] invoke-id) invoke-id)` (`transition.cljc:2641`), and so is the registry slot. The conformance fixture pins the split side by side: `{:data {:rf/spawned {[:loading] :fetcher#1}} … :rf/spawn-attempts {[:data :loading] 1}}` (`spec/conformance/fixtures/parallel-spawn-scoped-to-region.edn:57-59`).
2. The refusal exists only because of that key. `validate-region-spawn-paths!` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1869-1903`, called at `:2525`) throws `:rf.error/machine-parallel-bad-shape` saying "Rename the spawning state in one of the regions". Its own docstring says "The runtime registry slot is region-qualified and would still tell them apart; the mirror cannot."
3. The stated reason for the in-region key, "a region name is not addressable from inside a region", is about transition targets (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:1805`, `:3451`), not data keys. A region callback's context already receives region names as data, through `:all-state`, a map keyed by region name (`transition.cljc:341-371`).

Rejected options:
- A (keep the in-region key and the refusal): it keeps a registration refusal whose only cause is an internal key choice, so parallel regions cannot reuse an ordinary state name. That is a wart under rf2-29hkz ("excellent statecharts implementation").
- C now (the entry stamp, folded in here): not agreed by both reviews. It is left open for Mike and is not part of this bead.
- D (C plus an owner-token helper for the frame-incarnation rechecks): both reviews leave that to the separate frame-lifetime decision (dossier `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`). Nothing to build here.

Supersedes: the mayor's 2026-09-25 ruling recorded on rf2-tbh0z ("OPTION (A), the documented IN-REGION key", which explicitly said "the operator may reverse"). Its option (B), region-qualify the key everywhere, is this bead. Leave rf2-tbh0z itself untouched; it is closed.

## Work

Code (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/`):
- `transition.cljc`: `bind-spawned-id-into-parent-data` (`:595-632`) keys by the region-qualified invoke-id. `handle-spawn-decl` (`:2618`) already receives `region`, so pass the attempt-key form at `:2662`. `handle-spawn-all-decl` (`:2665`, arity `[parent-id s acc-fx prefix n event]`) does not, so thread `(:rf/region machine)` into it from its call site at `:3756`, as the single-spawn call at `:3753` already does. Rewrite the docstring at `:609-614`.
- `paths.cljc`: `spawned-mirror-path` (`:93-114`) becomes the plain `(conj (snapshot-path parent-id :data :rf/spawned) invoke-id)`. Delete the region-strip branch and its docstring rationale. Its callers keep working unchanged: `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:153`, `:570`, `:1494` and `lifecycle_fx/teardown.cljc:92`. Update their comments at `spawn.cljc:140`, `:1479` and `teardown.cljc:21`, `:68`, which describe the in-region key.
- `lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc`: delete `validate-region-spawn-paths!` (`:1869-1903`) and its call at `:2525`. Remove the sentence about it from the registration docstring at `:2382-2385`. The error id `:rf.error/machine-parallel-bad-shape` stays, because it still covers the other parallel-root shapes.

Spec and docs (all `w/crlf`, so edit with the Edit tool or Python bytes and never `sed -i`; see CLAUDE.md instrument hazard (u)):
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:88` (the `:rf/spawned` reserved-key row): the key is the invoke-id, region-qualified inside a parallel region, exactly like the registry slot. Delete the refusal sentence and show a region read example.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1895` (§Per-region scoping, `:spawn` bullet): delete the refusal clause and say the mirror uses the same region-qualified key.
- `spec/Conventions.md:652` (the `:rf/spawned` row): the same change.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2377` (the `:rf.error/machine-parallel-bad-shape` row): drop the shared-spawn-path clause, its fix hint and its `:regions` / `:state-path` payload note.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2720`: drop the clause "including two regions that declare a `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` at the same in-region path …".
- `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:136`: drop "or two regions declare a spawn at the same in-region path".

Fixtures and tests:
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/parallel-spawn-scoped-to-region.edn:44-59`: expect `{:rf/spawned {[:data :loading] :fetcher#1}}`, and rewrite the "Documented asymmetry" comment to say the mirror, registry, attempt key and `:rf/invoke-id` agree.
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/parallel_spawned_mirror_test.clj` (111 lines): rewrite it. `regions-sharing-a-spawn-path-are-refused` (`:77`) becomes a positive test in which two regions spawn at one in-region path. The in-region-entry tests at `:39` and `:46` assert the region-qualified key.
- Grep the machines tests for in-region mirror keys and for comments citing the refusal, for example `spawn_on_done_transition_cljs_test.cljc:153-154` and `join_parallel_attempt_select_test.clj:20`. The `spawn_on_done` test can now use a genuine same-path pair. Leave the state renames the refusal forced in `join_parallel_attempt_select_test.clj` and `spawn_all_test.clj`; they are harmless.

Deliberately stays:
- The `:rf/spawned` value shapes: a bare id for a single spawn, a `{child-id spawned-id}` map for `:spawn-all`.
- The non-parallel key.
- The registry slot, `:rf/spawn-attempts`, `:after` epochs and join attempt tokens. Those belong to the undecided entry-stamp question.
- `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:109` reads `[:rf/spawned [:active]]` on a non-parallel machine, so it is unchanged.
- Xray reads the registry, not this mirror (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:223`), so it is unchanged.
- machines-viz does not mirror this refusal.

No region-name key is added to callback context. Add one only when an example needs a reusable region body.

## Sequencing

- Hot-zone files touched: `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`. Sequence this against every other bead editing those files, never in parallel. It does not touch `spec/011-SSR.md`, `spec/API.md` or the manifests.
- Bead dependencies: none.
- Cross-dossier:
  - It shares `spec/005-StateMachines.md` with the work from `machine-after-delays-from-subscriptions.md` and `machine-snapshot-before-first-event.md`, if those are filed, so land one before the other.
  - If Mike later rules the entry stamp in `machine-fences-to-entry-stamp.md`, that work follows this bead.
  - It is independent of `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`.
- Out of scope, noted for the stamp work: repeated single spawns with a fixed `:fixed-actor-id` appear to get the same work id on every attempt. The work id comes from the actor-id suffix (`reply.cljc:156-158`, `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:438-443`), although the child carries a distinguishing `:rf/invoke-attempt`. The coordinator is filing that bug separately; do not fix it here. Any entry-stamp work, if ruled, should check it.

## Evidence

- Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54: every `path:line` above, including the mirror write, its two call sites, `spawned-mirror-path` and its four callers, the refusal and its call, the region callback context, the conformance fixture, and the spec, docs and test lines.
- Predicted, not yet run: that the change is local (Codex: "one local change in the reducer's mirror write"; rf2-tbh0z's worker said the same of its option (B)), and that no other reader depends on the in-region key.
- Confirm with the machines JVM tests and `npm run test:cljs`, which needs a shadow-cljs lane grant from the coordinator, plus the conformance runner, `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec and docs edits.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A `:type :parallel` machine in which two regions each declare a `:spawn` at the same in-region path (for example both `:loading`) registers without error. The same holds for a `:spawn-all` pair, and for a `:spawn` in one region beside a `:spawn-all` in the other.
2. Each region's spawn writes its own mirror entry under the region-qualified key (`[:rf/spawned [:upload :loading]]` and `[:rf/spawned [:download :loading]]`). Each entry equals the invoke-id of the registry slot `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent-id> <invoke-id>]` for the same child.
3. Exiting, then re-entering, one region's spawning state clears and rewrites only that region's entry. The sibling region's entry and child are untouched.
4. A spawn the spawn fx rejects in one region clears only that region's entry. This holds for a single spawn and for a rejected `:spawn-all` invoke.
5. A non-parallel machine's mirror key is unchanged. `examples/patterns/websocket` still reads `[:rf/spawned [:active]]`.
6. `validate-region-spawn-paths!` no longer exists. A search of `implementation/` for `in-region path` finds no mirror or refusal prose. `:rf.error/machine-parallel-bad-shape` is still thrown for the other parallel-root shapes.
7. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (the `:rf/spawned` row and the §Per-region scoping `:spawn` bullet), `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` and `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md` describe the region-qualified key and carry no same-in-region-path refusal. Each edited `w/crlf` file still has CR == CRLF and zero bare LF, measured with Python over the bytes.
8. The conformance fixture `parallel-spawn-scoped-to-region.edn` expects the region-qualified mirror key and passes.
9. The machines JVM tests, `npm run test:cljs` (run under a lane grant), `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` are green. The PR body quotes each runner's own exit code and the test and assertion count delta.
10. Fixed-id work ids, `:rf/spawn-attempts`, `:after` epochs and join attempt tokens are untouched by this PR.

title: Docs playground pre-creates :rf/default, so interactive cljs-rf2 cells cannot adopt the conventional app-frame id
description:
## Problem

The guide's interactive `cljs-rf2` cells cannot adopt `:rf/default`, the conventional single-app frame id (the rf2-x8nh8 ruling), without breaking.

The docs playground creates `:rf/default` itself before every cell runs. `renderLast` calls `ensure-init!`, which calls `ensure-app-frame!`, which runs `(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default})` when that frame is not live (`docs/tools/playground/sci/src/rf2_playground/sci.cljs`, `app-frame` / `ensure-app-frame!` / `renderLast`). A cell root such as `[rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default :initial-events [[:initialise 3]]} [counter]]` then meets a live frame. Re-mounting under a live id is idempotent replacement, and `:initial-events` are re-recorded but not replayed (Spec 002 §`frame-root` "`:initial-events` fire once per committed frame-id lifetime" and §Duplicate id). So the cell renders unseeded: the introduction's counter would show no count, and `app-db.md`'s stepping counter would add `nil`.

No gate covers this. The playground smoke (`docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs`) runs its own synthetic page with non-`:rf/default` ids, never the docs pages' cells.

## Where it stands

rf2-x8nh8's sweep (PR #11418) left every interactive cell, and the three prose lines describing a live cell (`docs/core/introduction.md` "creates the `:app` frame", `docs/core/views.md` "mount under the same `:app` frame", `docs/core/flows.md` "the example passes `:frame :app`"), on `:app` / `:app/main`. At the PR head that is 40 cell lines across about 30 pages: `docs/core` (app-db, coeffects, errors, flows, introduction, observability, subscriptions, views, how-to/validate-with-schemas), `docs/core/fresco` (14 chapters and the cookbook), `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md`, `docs/resources/concepts.md` and six `docs/routing` pages. Non-interactive blocks and REPL lines on the same pages now say `:rf/default`, so those pages show both ids.

## Decision needed

Either the playground stops pre-creating the conventional id, or the cells keep a page-local id on purpose.

- A: the playground's implicit frame for frameless cells gets its own reserved or descriptive id (its README promises `:rf/default`, `docs/tools/playground/README.md` §Rules "Frames are optional"), after which cells can name `:rf/default` and seed it. Then rename the cells.
- B: the playground creates `:rf/default` lazily, only when a cell's tree establishes no root of its own. Harder: evaluation runs under `(rf/with-frame app-frame …)` so a top-level `dispatch-sync` in a cell resolves.
- C: leave the cells on `:app`, and say once in the playground README why a live cell names its own frame.

Gate: none reads frame ids. A run of the docs site with the playground bundle rebuilt is the only witness; check the introduction counter shows 3 and `app-db.md`'s stepper increments.
notes:
== MAYOR 2026-10-16 21:45 AUSEST: OPTION A FOLLOWS FROM THE RULING; DISPATCHABLE ==
Not held for Mike. The destination is already ruled (rf2-x8nh8 / rf2-are72: every teaching surface converges on :rf/default as the single-app frame id); the playground's implicit frame for frameless cells is plumbing serving that ruling. Option A removes the obstacle with the smallest change: give the playground's implicit frame its own descriptive id, update docs/tools/playground/README.md's Rules to match, then rename the live cells and the three prose lines to :rf/default. Option C (cells keep :app on purpose) is the fallback only if A turns out to break frameless cells or the top-level dispatch-sync path under (rf/with-frame app-frame ...); if so, say why in the PR and take C. Option B is not wanted. The playground's rf2 bundle is a shadow-cljs build (docs/tools/playground/sci) built and smoked in CI by test.yml's tools-playground job and rebuilt from main by docs.yml; a local build needs a lane grant.

== WORKER rf-default-cells 2026-10-16 22:05 AUSEST: IMPLEMENTED, DRAFT PR #11424 (branch worker/rf-default-cells, commits 0d3d9ce65e playground, e183296b46 cells) ==
OPTION A, as the mayor's note rules. title: Make MCP app-schema enumeration accept mixed-type schema paths
description: PR #11422 (79b966d981) adds app-schema to MCP list-handlers, but the runtime accessors it now exposes still sort path-vector ids with the ordinary compare order. skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:658-662 registrar-list and :970-980 frame-registrar-list both use keys -> sort -> vec. App-schema paths explicitly permit concrete mixed-type segments (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:168-196). Registering [:todos 0] and [:todos :filter] therefore makes the new list-handlers {:kind "app-schema"} fail with the comparison error instead of returning both paths; the explicit-frame listing takes the same failing sort. handler_meta.cljs:432-449 routes directly to these accessors, while the two new MCP tests stub the runtime result and cannot exercise this failure. The worker reports the same concrete repro. Existing in-progress rf2-b6py7 already owns the preload correction and has been read in full; this new open audit finding preserves independent tracking as requested, without changing that work. Small correction: use a deterministic total ordering for path ids in both runtime listing accessors, preserving existing keyword-id output order. Pin two equal-length mixed-type paths through the real listing path, including an explicit frame, and confirm handler-meta can still inspect either returned path. No new kind, fallback result, or public API is needed.

title: Make the app-db REPL read address the live counter it accompanies
description:
Merged-PR audit #11418 (b5fcd82d22c2c16a0e4fda7461e1223159259c4b), discovered from rf2-x8nh8.

docs/core/app-db.md:109 changes the reader's REPL instruction to (rf/app-db-value :rf/default), but the interactive stepping counter on that same page still constructs :app at lines 50-52. Interacting with that counter changes :app, so following the new read does not show the counter's state. The playground separately pre-creates :rf/default (sci.cljs ensure-app-frame!/ensure-init!), so the read addresses the playground's implicit frame instead. The previous instruction addressed the displayed counter.

The runtime and naming ruling are sound; this is a concrete mixed-id teaching gap left by the migration. Read complete follow-up rf2-sqdrq: it is in_progress and already owns moving the playground's implicit frame and then converging live cells on :rf/default. That existing work may resolve this observation, but this audit finding has its own open tracker as requested rather than a note on a closed source.

Small correction: when the live-cell migration lands, ensure this page's interactive root, explanatory REPL read and actual displayed counter all address the same frame.
